Overview

HVL Interaktiv lets a teacher take one learning outcome and turn it into a short, accessible, interactive activity in under 30 minutes. The teacher can place it in Canvas, and walk into the next seminar knowing which misconceptions to address.

Everything in this specification serves that sentence. If a proposed feature does not shorten the path to a good activity, make it more accessible, or close the feedback loop between asynchronous and synchronous teaching, it is out of scope.

What it does for teachers and students

For teachersFor students
Start from nine learning-design patterns for forarbeid, mellomarbeid and etterarbeid, not a blank editorShort, focused activities with explanatory feedback
Use ten curated H5P content types, chosen for pedagogical value and accessibilityResume on any device; unlimited retries in practice activities
A pre-publish check catches missing alt text and captions, and nudges towards good designWorks with keyboard, screen readers and 320 px phones (WCAG 2.2 AA)
Before-the-seminar insight: hardest questions, most common wrong answers, anonymisedNynorsk by default, plus Bokmål and English
Place activities in Canvas with one click (LTI 1.3 Deep Linking); optional formative gradesPrivacy: pseudonymous; teachers never see individual answers
Pedagogisk mappe export documents designs and their reasoning for merit and promotion applications

How asynchronous work fits around the seminar

HVL Interaktiv supports the asynchronous phases of a course. The synchronous session (samling) happens in the classroom or online; the activities prepare for it and consolidate after it.

PhasePedagogical purposeRecommended patterns (§4)Canvas placement and attempt policy
ForarbeidActivate prior knowledge; meet threshold concepts; surface misconceptions before teachingfa-video, fa-slides, fa-hotspots, ea-diagnoseIn the module before the seminar. Unlimited retries; Show solution on. The teacher reviews Før samlinga insight the evening before.
Mellomarbeid (underveis)Deepen integration; practise professional judgement (profesjonell dømmekraft, didaktisk skjønn) on realistic casesuv-case, uv-module, uv-columnOne or two interactive items per Canvas page. Resume enabled.
EtterarbeidConsolidate through spaced retrieval; check the learning outcomes (læringsutbytte)ea-retrieval, ea-terms, ea-diagnoseGraded through AGS with the mastery or best policy (LTI-012), unlimited attempts. Suggested repetition dates (PROD-014).

How to read this site

  • Teachers and learning designers: start with 00 Product and pedagogy, then 04 Læringsdesign studio.
  • Evaluators and reviewers: read the Evaluator guide, then use Requirements to check any promise against its acceptance criteria.
  • Developers: the Documentation standard says how every file must explain itself.
  • Norwegian terms are explained in the Glossary.

Requirements

Every requirement in the specification, with its acceptance criteria and how it will be verified. Filter by area, priority, build session or status, or search the text. Click an ID anywhere on this site to jump to its definition.

Showing all 126 requirements.

PROD-001 Must S5 Create an activity from a learning-design pattern ● Tested

An author can create a new activity by choosing a phase (Forarbeid, Mellomarbeid, Etterarbeid) and then a pattern. The H5P editor opens pre-filled with a pedagogically sound skeleton and guidance.

  • Acceptance: Every pattern in 04 §4 can be instantiated. The created content passes validateContent with zero errors before the author edits it, apart from placeholders that are deliberately flagged as needing input. Choosing blank activity is still possible.
  • Verify: Integration test that creates each pattern; e2e for J1.
  • Amended (D-101, 2026-11-05, S6 step 8): SPEC-DEVIATION: "e2e for J1" is J1's portal half (patternToPublish.e2e, publishWithReason.e2e); creating from a pattern in Canvas's Deep Linking picker passes to HVL's bachelor students (docs/handoff/canvas-studio.md).

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-001 · Product

PROD-002 Must S2 Exactly ten authorable content types ● Tested

Authors can create only the ten content types in 01 §3.

  • Acceptance: See H5P-002.
  • Verify: Covered by H5P-002 tests.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-002 · Product

PROD-003 Must S4 Check-and-publish quality gate ● Tested

Activities have the states draft and published. Publish runs the universal design validator (UD-020) and the pedagogical hints (PED-020). Findings are listed in plain language with a Go to field link.

  • Acceptance: An error blocks publishing unless the author records an acknowledgement with a reason (e.g. "captions are being produced in Panopto"). Acknowledgements are stored, appear in insight and in the portfolio export, and are raised again on the next publish after 14 days. Warnings and hints never block.
  • Verify: Unit tests for state transitions; e2e for J1 step 5.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-003 · Product

PROD-004 Must S3 Learners only see published activities ● Tested
  • Acceptance: A learner request for a draft returns a friendly "not yet available" page (HTTP 404 to avoid revealing its existence). Authors can preview drafts.
  • Verify: Integration test.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-004 · Product

PROD-005 Must S3 Place activities in Canvas ● Tested

Authors can place an activity in a Canvas module, assignment or rich-content editor through LTI Deep Linking. See LTI-005.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-005 · Product

PROD-006 Must S3 Share outside Canvas with Feide ● Tested

An author can share an activity link that works outside Canvas. Viewers log in with Feide. Visibility is one of: only me / co-authors, everyone at HVL, or anyone with a Feide login.

  • Acceptance: Visibility is enforced by the permission system (H5P-006). Changing visibility takes effect immediately.
  • Verify: Integration tests per visibility level.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-006 · Product

PROD-007 Should S5 Co-authoring and an institutional content bank ● Tested

Authors can add co-authors (HVL staff found by name or Feide ID) and can publish an activity to the HVL content bank so that colleagues can duplicate and adapt it.

  • Acceptance: A duplicate keeps a link to its source and the original author's attribution. It never copies learner data.
  • Verify: Integration tests.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-007 · Product

PROD-008 Must S2 Resume where you left off ● Tested

A learner who leaves an activity and returns on any device resumes with their previous answers and position. See H5P-005.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-008 · Product

PROD-009 Must S5 Formative defaults ● Tested

For all patterns, Retry and Show solution are enabled, there are no time limits, and pass thresholds are informative rather than gatekeeping.

  • Acceptance: Pattern skeletons set the relevant behaviour fields. The hint rule PED-H07 flags activities where an author has turned these off.
  • Verify: Unit tests on skeleton parameters.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-009 · Product

PROD-010 Must S6 Teacher insight before the seminar ● Tested

Authors see aggregated, anonymised results per activity, designed to prepare the next synchronous session. See INS-* in 05.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-010 · Product

PROD-011 Must S4 Formative-use notice ● Tested

The editor and the Deep Linking picker show a short, dismissible notice. It says H5P activities are scored in the browser and are meant for formative work (undervegsvurdering), not exams.

  • Acceptance: Notice text exists in nn, nb and en. Dismissal is remembered per user.
  • Verify: Component test.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-011 · Product

PROD-012 Must S1 Three languages, Nynorsk first ● Tested

All UI is available in Nynorsk (default), Bokmål and English. H5P strings fall back from nn to nb to en. See H5P-008.

  • Acceptance: A test fails if any key is missing in a locale file.
  • Verify: Unit test for key parity.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-012 · Product

PROD-013 Should S5 Safe editing of a published activity ● Tested

When an author edits an activity that already has learner state, the editor warns that structural changes (adding, removing or reordering questions) reset saved progress. It offers Save as new version.

  • Acceptance: Existing learner state is invalidated only when the author confirms. Insight separates results by version.
  • Verify: Integration test.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-013 · Product

PROD-014 Could S6 Spaced-retrieval suggestion ○ Planned

After publishing an Etterarbeid activity, the author is shown suggested repetition dates (for example +7 and +21 days) and a one-click copy to place in a later Canvas module.

  • Verify: Component test.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, PROD-014 · Product

NFR-001 Must S6 Performance ● Tested

An activity page (player plus content) becomes interactive in ≤ 3 s at p95 on a simulated "Fast 4G" profile with 200 concurrent learners on one application node. API p95 is ≤ 300 ms excluding file downloads.

  • Verify: k6 or Artillery load test script in tools/load/; Lighthouse CI on the player route.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, NFR-001 · Non-functional

NFR-002 Must S6 Availability and recoverability ● Tested

99.5 % monthly availability during the semester. Database backups run daily with 30-day retention. A documented restore is tested once per semester.

  • Verify: Operations runbook in docs/ops/; restore drill log.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, NFR-002 · Non-functional

NFR-003 Must S4 Mobile and assistive technology ● Tested

Works on the last two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on iOS Safari and on Android Chrome, and with NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver. See 03.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, NFR-003 · Non-functional

NFR-004 Must S1 Maintainability ● Tested

Source files are ≤ 200 lines and each has a single responsibility. Every file follows DOCUMENTATION-STANDARD. CI runs typecheck, lint, tests and the traceability check.

  • Verify: npm run check:filesize, npm run spec:trace in CI.

Defined in 00 Product and pedagogy, NFR-004 · Non-functional

NFR-005 Must S1 Open source licence ● Tested

The repository is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. This is required because @lumieducation/h5p-server is GPL-3.0-or-later. Dependencies must be GPL-3.0-compatible (for example MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC).

  • Verify: A licence check in CI against a GPL-3.0-compatible allow-list (npm run check:licences, D-029).

AUTH-001 Must S3 Feide OpenID Connect login (Authorization Code + PKCE) ● Tested

The server is a confidential OIDC relying party, registered in the Feide Customer Portal (kunde.feide.no) under HVL (realm hvl.no (verify realm)). It uses openid-client 6 with discovery from issuer https://auth.dataporten.no (document /.well-known/openid-configuration), plus PKCE (S256), state and nonce. ID tokens are RS256-signed. Scopes: openid profile email userid-feide groups-org groups-edu. All six are valid Feide scope (attribute-group) names. Always send the scope list explicitly: a request with openid alone releases every attribute group configured for the client. In the Customer Portal, authorise only the attribute groups userinfo-name, email, userid-feide, groups-org and groups-edu; never userinfo-photo or userid-nin.

  • Acceptance: The full flow works against a mock OIDC provider in tests. ID tokens with a wrong iss, aud, nonce or an expired exp are rejected. The client secret is read from an environment variable or secret store and is never logged.
  • Verify: Integration tests with oauth2-mock-server (or equivalent); test names [AUTH-001] ….

AUTH-002 Must S3 Map Feide affiliation to roles ● Tested

After login, call GET https://groups-api.dataporten.no/groups/me/groups with the user's Feide access token (Authorization: Bearer). Find the organisation group (type: "fc:org", id: "fc:org:<realm>", for HVL fc:org:hvl.no (verify realm)) and read its membership.affiliation array. Feide's values are faculty, student, staff, alum, member, affiliate, employee and library-walk-in. Course groups for AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS come from groups-edu as FS groups, e.g. fc:fs:fs:emne:<realm>:<course-code>:<version>; they require HVL's FS integration in Feide (verify).

AUTH-003 Must S3 Portal session ● Tested

The server keeps the session in Redis and gives the browser an opaque ID in a cookie (__Host-hvli_sid; HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/). The session expires after 2 h idle or 12 h absolute. State-changing requests require a CSRF token (synchronizer pattern). Logout clears the session and redirects the browser to Feide's end_session_endpoint (https://auth.dataporten.no/openid/endsession) with post_logout_redirect_uri (registered in the Customer Portal) and id_token_hint. Feide requires both, so the raw ID token is kept in the server-side session only, encrypted at rest and deleted at logout or expiry (D-021).

  • Verify: Integration tests (expiry, CSRF rejection, logout).

Defined in 02 Feide, LTI and grades, AUTH-003 · Feide login

AUTH-004 Must S3 Data minimisation at login ● Tested

Request only the scopes listed in AUTH-001. Never request userid-nin or read the claim https://n.feide.no/claims/nin (national identity number), or other extended attributes. Feide releases name and email for every user once those attribute groups are authorised, so the claims mapper drops them for learners before anything is stored. Store a display name and e-mail only for authors and admins, who need them for co-author search and attribution. Feide never verifies e-mail addresses (email_verified is always false), so e-mail is never used as an identifier; use sub or the Feide ID.

  • Verify: Unit test asserts the scope string. Integration test asserts that no learner row has a name or e-mail.
  • Amended (D-090, 2026-10-29, S5 review): SPEC-DEVIATION: the e-mail is no longer stored for anyone. Co-author search matches the display name or the Feide ID's hash, and the bank and copies show the name only, so a stored address had no use; each staff login now clears User.email.

LTI-003 Must S3 Cookie-less ltik transport ● Tested
  1. onResourceLink and onDeepLinking call context.redirect(res, '/app/…'), which appends ?ltik=….
  2. The Next.js page reads ltik once and keeps it only in memory (React context, never localStorage or sessionStorage). It removes it from the address bar with history.replaceState.
  3. All API calls send Authorization: Bearer <ltik>. H5P iframe URLs carry it through HvlUrlGenerator (H5P-007).
  4. Server middleware resolves provider.getLaunchContext(ltik) into a Principal. Invalid or expired → 401 with a "please reopen from Canvas" page.
  5. Pages that receive an ltik send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. The logger redacts ltik in query strings and headers.
  6. Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors lists only the configured Canvas origins (config CANVAS_ORIGINS, e.g. https://hvl.instructure.com, plus TeCopp's test instance and any vanity domain). sso.canvaslms.com is not an ancestor and is not listed. X-Frame-Options is not sent.

Defined in 02 Feide, LTI and grades, LTI-009 · Canvas LTI and grades

LTI-010 Must S6 Capture xAPI in the player ● Tested

The injected client script (packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.ts, H5P-009) subscribes with H5P.externalDispatcher.on('xAPI', …). It POSTs each statement to /api/h5p/xapi, batched every 2 s and flushed on pagehide, with the ltik or CSRF token. Failed posts are retried from an in-memory queue. They never block or slow down the activity.

  • Verify: Unit test of the batching queue; Playwright test that statements arrive.
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION: the bridge is plain JavaScript, packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.js, like the theme's other client scripts (there is no browser build for TypeScript). It runs once in the top player document (h5p/render/playerPage.ts: /h5p/play/:contentId in the portal, /lti/play in Canvas), not inside H5P's iframes (H5P-009 as amended), and queues each statement once, also one that H5P Core relays from its own iframe. The player page loads it only for a learner principal, so previews and teachers' plays are never sent. It makes a random attemptId for the root activity when the page loads and a new one after the root's scored completed or answered statement (probe P1 checks the real attempt boundaries). Credentials: in Canvas the ltik as Authorization: Bearer from the page's memory, in the portal the session cookie with the X-CSRF-Token header; never an ltik in the query. On pagehide it flushes with fetch and keepalive: true (not sendBeacon, which cannot carry those headers); nothing goes to browser storage. It adds no ✓/✗ text (UD-003 as amended).
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from "It POSTs each statement": the bridge sends only what the server stores (LTI-011 as amended): the page load's first root attempted, every answered and a root completed; never interacted, progressed, or a sub-content attempted or completed. Each statement is cut down to the fields the server reads, with no actor, question text, choices or feedback, and answers capped as DATA-012 (as amended) stores them. Each carries a statementId (crypto.randomUUID(), one per dispatched event) and an attemptId <viewId>:<n>: viewId is made once per page load, and n starts at 1 and goes up by one right after a root result with score.max above 0, so a retry, which H5P does not announce, is a new attempt at its next result. A batch names its content and the version the page was rendered with, and holds at most 50 items and 60 000 bytes of JSON, one request in flight; after a network error, a 5xx or a 429 it goes back to the head of the queue, after any other 4xx it is dropped. On pagehide everything not yet acknowledged, the request in flight included, goes in one keepalive request within the same limits, oldest first. The bridge is the last script in the player's global assets, never the editor's. It registers only in a document that is not one of Core's iframes, and at event time does nothing in a document that H5P marks as one (H5P.isFramed with H5P.externalEmbed === false), so each statement is queued once, by the parent document's bridge, also if H5P's iframe embedding is used.

Defined in 02 Feide, LTI and grades, LTI-010 · Canvas LTI and grades

LTI-011 Must S6 Validate and store statements ● Tested

/api/h5p/xapi validates statements with a zod schema. It accepts only verbs it uses (answered, completed, attempted, interacted, progressed). It checks that the object belongs to content the principal may view, and that 0 ≤ score.raw ≤ score.max and 0 ≤ scaled ≤ 1. It rate-limits each learner and activity to 120 statements per minute. Then it stores the minimal fields defined in DATA-012 and drops the rest of the statement (including actor.name and actor.mbox).

  • Verify: Unit tests for the schema; integration test for rate limiting.
  • Amended (D-102, D-103, 2026-10-30): statements are stored only from a learner principal; anyone else's request stores nothing. In Canvas the content must also be the launched activity. The stored contextId is the platform-scoped <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103, null for a portal play), and the stored timestamp is when the server received the batch, not what the browser claims.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from "Then it stores the minimal fields": all five verbs are still accepted, but not every accepted statement is stored. Stored: a root attempted; a root answered that is a root result (LTI-012 as amended), and a sub-content answered with a subContentId; a root completed that is a root result and not a replay. Accepted and not stored: interacted, progressed, a sub-content attempted or completed, a sub-content statement without a subContentId, a root answered or completed whose category does not name the activity's main library (DATA-012 stores no category, and insight and the grade queue read every stored root answered and completed as a root result), and a replay: a root completed after no stored answered since its page load's previous root result (or since the load), whose raw score and maximum equal the learner's latest stored root result for the same content, context and version (CoursePresentation re-sends its result on resume; BranchingScenario is exempt). A statement is root when object.id is the content ID with no ?subContentId=, it has no h5p-subContentId extension and no contextActivities.parent (LTI-012 as amended). Each item is checked on its own: an invalid one, including one about another activity or whose scaled differs from raw / max by more than 0.0001, is discarded and counted in the log without its content, so it never blocks its batch. Besides a request without a valid session and CSRF token or ltik (401) and the rate limit (429), a whole batch is refused only when it is about an activity the principal may not view (403; in Canvas, any but the launched one), is over 64 KiB (413), or is no batch envelope, holds no item or over 50, or names a version above the activity's current one (400; a page keeps the version it was rendered with). The schema ignores actor (the learner comes only from the principal), and accepts a bare UUID as object.id, a missing context, a numeric response (stored as text) and a score without scaled when its maximum is 0. The item's statementId becomes the row's ID and is inserted once, so a batch sent twice (the pagehide flush, a request retried after a lost answer) stores nothing twice; the stored timestamp is the receive time plus the item's place in the batch in milliseconds, which keeps the batch's order. A 429 carries Retry-After, and nothing from that batch is stored. The answer is 202, with no detail per item. Not deviated: the five verbs, the score checks, the View check and the rate limit.
  • Amended (D-103, 2026-11-04, step 3 integration): a learner's batch from a Canvas launch whose context claim cannot form <platformId>:<contextId> (empty, over 255 characters, or with a line break) is answered 202 and stores nothing; the log counts it as noCourse. Such a play is neither a portal play (null) nor stored under a made-up course.

Defined in 02 Feide, LTI and grades, LTI-011 · Canvas LTI and grades

LTI-012 Must S6 Publish scores to the Canvas gradebook (AGS) ● Tested

When a statement concerns the root content (no subContentId), has the verb completed or answered, and carries result.score, the server applies the activity's attempt policy:

Policy (author setting)Score sent to Canvas
best (default)highest scaled score so far, ×100
latestlatest scaled score, ×100
mastery100 once the scaled score ≥ threshold (default 0.8), otherwise latest ×100

The result goes to a durable GradeSyncJob queue. A worker calls context.grading.submitScore(lineItemUrl, { userId: sub, scoreGiven, scoreMaximum: 100, activityProgress: 'Completed', gradingProgress: 'FullyGraded', timestamp }) with exponential backoff (up to 8 attempts in 24 h). Jobs are idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId). If the line item no longer exists, the job is marked orphaned and is not retried. The developer key needs the scopes …/lti-ags/scope/score and …/lti-ags/scope/lineitem.readonly (the latter detects orphaned line items). ltijs's grading service works from a LaunchContext, which lives as long as the ltik (24 h); a job still failing after that window stores what it needs to request a new client-credentials token itself, or is marked failed for the author to retry from a fresh launch.

  • Acceptance: Learning never waits for grade sync. Authors see a per-activity sync status (counts of sent / pending / failed) and can retry failed jobs.
  • Verify: Integration tests with a mock AGS endpoint (success, 5xx retry, 404 orphaned, idempotency).
  • Amended (D-104, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION from the sentence "A worker calls context.grading.submitScore(…)" only: that method works only from a live ltik, which a background worker does not hold and must not store. AgsScoreClient (apps/server/src/grades/) requests the client-credentials token itself, from the first attempt, with a JWT assertion signed by the tool key ltijs stores for the platform, and posts the same score body to the line item's /scores URL. A job is written only for a learner in a Canvas launch, a root statement with completed or answered and a score, and a placement with a lineItemUrl; jobs stay idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId), so a later scored statement of the same attempt updates its job. The worker (one node at a time, about every 15 s) coalesces due jobs per (placement, learnerKey), applies the placement's attempt policy to that learner's attempt scores, sends one current score and settles the coalesced jobs together. Outcomes: 2xx succeeds; a 404 confirmed with a lineitem.readonly read marks the job orphaned, not retried; a 429, 5xx or network error is retried with exponential backoff and jitter, at most 8 attempts, the last within 24 h of the first, then failed; a 401 fetches a new token once; any other 4xx fails at once. The encrypted sub is removed 30 days after the job stops, whatever its outcome. Authors see sent, pending, failed and orphaned counts per placement on the activity page and in /app/play and retry failed jobs there. Not deviated: the score body, the policies, the retry limit, idempotency, orphaned and the developer key's scopes.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from the root as "no subContentId": no single test finds the root (that one takes DragText's context-less interacted inside a QuestionSet, and every child of content saved without subContentIds; H5P's own, no contextActivities.parent, takes InteractiveBook's chapter completed). A statement is root when object.id is the content ID with no ?subContentId=, it has no h5p-subContentId extension and no contextActivities.parent. A grade job is written only for a gradable root result: a root answered or completed whose category[0].id names the activity's main library (http://h5p.org/libraries/<machineName>-<major>.<minor>), with score.max above 0, and not a replay (LTI-011 as amended). scoreGiven is scaled × 100, never success. An attempt holds at most one result (LTI-010 as amended), so each job is one attempt; latest, and mastery below its threshold, send the score of the job whose result was stored last, by GradeSyncJob.resultAt (that result's stored timestamp), then by the attempt number n of <viewId>:<n>, then by the attempt ID as text (D-115's step-3 amendment). Which result each type sends is D-115's table: MultiChoice, Blanks and DragText an answered at every «Sjekk»; QuestionSet, Column, CoursePresentation and BranchingScenario a root completed; InteractiveBook at «Send inn rapport», which the player page offers a learner by setting H5P's reportingIsEnabled (Q18), and only a learner, never an author's preview; InteractiveVideo only with a submit screen its author added; BranchingScenario nothing gradable when its scoring is no-score; ImageHotspots no statement at all. An activity that sends no score never gets a job, and the Deep Linking picker says so for assignment_selection. Not deviated: the two verbs, result.score, the policies and their table.
  • Amended (D-104, two amendments of 2026-11-04, the step-3 security review): jobs are one per (placement, learnerKey) (idempotencyKey <placementId>:<learnerKey>), so one learner can never flood the queue; idempotency per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId) holds a fortiori. Each new gradable result updates the job, and a stopped job is reopened with a new window of 8 attempts in 24 h. The score is computed when it is sent, by the placement's policy over the learner's stored gradable results of that activity in that course, in D-115's result order. Claiming is fair (one place per learner a run); a job that takes in a result while its score is in flight is due again at the next run; each run first reopens a stopped job whose learner stored a newer result 15 to 1 minutes earlier (the reconcile pass). The line item URL must parse, use https in production, hold no credentials and have an origin in CANVAS_ORIGINS or among the platform's own (issuer, authorisation and token endpoints); it is checked when a launch records the placement (refused: stored as none, the link is ungraded) and again by the worker before any request (refused: the job fails as line-item-url). Not deviated: the score body, the policies, the retry limit, orphaned and the scopes.

LTI-013 Must S6 Score integrity is honest ● Tested

H5P computes scores in the browser, so a determined student can forge them. The system therefore (a) labels AGS scores as formative in the line-item label suffix "(formativ)", (b) shows the formative notice (PROD-011), and (c) never presents these scores as exam evidence. Server checks in LTI-011 reduce accidental and casual manipulation. They are not claimed to prevent deliberate manipulation. On assignment_selection, Canvas uses the line-item label as the assignment name and overwrites the teacher's own name. Whether "(formativ)" belongs in the assignment name, or in the content item's description instead (with Canvas's preserveExistingAssignmentName extension), is a decision for HVL and ALU (verify).

  • Verify: Review item in the evaluator guide; unit test for the label suffix.
  • Amended (D-105, 2026-10-30): AGS_LABEL_MODE chooses: suffix (the default, as written above: the label is «Tittel (formativ)», the title cut when needed so the suffix is never lost) or preserve (the label is the title, the content item carries Canvas's preserveExistingAssignmentName, and its description says the score is formative). The suffix is «(formativ)» in every language. Q8 stays open; HVL and ALU's answer changes the setting, not the code, and a change affects new placements only. The insight views, the INS-009 CSV and the grade-sync status also say that the scores are formative, computed in the browser and not exam evidence. The unit test checks the label in both modes.

UD-020 Must S4 Validator engine ● Tested

apps/server/src/validation/validateContent.ts exports a pure function:

/**
 * Inspects authored H5P parameters for universal design and pedagogical problems.
 * Pure and deterministic: no I/O, so it can run on save, on publish, and in tests.
 */
function validateContent(input: {
  mainLibrary: string;            // e.g. "H5P.InteractiveVideo 1.28"
  params: unknown;                // content.json
  metadata: H5PMetadata;          // h5p.json-style metadata
  locale: 'nn' | 'nb' | 'en';
}): Finding[];

interface Finding {
  ruleId: string;                 // e.g. "V-IMG-ALT"
  severity: 'error' | 'warning' | 'hint';
  requirement: string;            // spec ID, e.g. "UD-021"
  path: string;                   // JSON path into params, for "Go to field"
  message: string;                // localised, plain language, says what to do
}

The walker visits nested sub-content recursively (any object with library: "H5P.X a.b" and params). Each rule is a separate file under validation/rules/, ≤ 100 lines, with its own test. Pedagogical hint rules (PED-H*) are specified in 04 §5 and plug into the same engine.

MAPPE-002 Should S5 Dossier structure ● Tested

Headings come from content/mappe/template.{nn,nb,en}.md and criterion texts from content/mappe/criteria.{nn,nb,en}.yaml, keyed by criteria set (default hvl-merittering-2025). HVL revises the merit criteria for every call (next call 2027), so a new set is a content change only. The proposed Nynorsk template is docs/reference/proposals/mappe-template.nn.md ↗ (opens external site). The default structure follows HVL's three-part merit portfolio:

  1. Reader's guide: a table mapping each 2025 criterion (1.1–1.4, 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.3) to the chapter and attachment that address it, as in published HVL portfolios.
  2. Del 1 – Samanhengande framstilling: chapters ordered by the criteria, each with a pre-filled writing prompt. The teacher's learning-design approach opens the text. For each selected activity (under 2.3, varierte læremidler): title, content type, phase, course, learning outcomes, didactic rationale, universal design status (validator result plus any acknowledgements with reasons), a link, and anonymised aggregates (participants, completion rate, median attempts, change between first and last attempts). A live word count shows Del 1 against the limit (default 7 500 words, references excluded).
  3. Del 2 – Pedagogisk CV: entries HVL Interaktiv can document (digital learning resources developed, with dates), to paste into HVL's own CV template.
  4. Del 3 – Suggested attachments (default limit 11, including the manager's letter, which the tool never produces): documentation of developed learning resources, and an anonymised summary of student feedback.
  5. References, pre-filled from the patterns' research keys (§3).

The word limit, attachment limit and criteria set are content values marked (verify) until ALU confirms them. A promotion mode (opprykk, rules in force from 13 June 2025) uses the same three parts; its Del 1 headings wait for ALU.

  • Acceptance: Switching the criteria set changes every criterion text and the reader's guide with no code change. The word count excludes the references and the reader's guide.
  • Verify: Integration test with two fixture criteria sets.

INS-001 Must S6 Participation overview ● Tested

Shows: learners who started, learners who completed, completion rate (denominator from NRPS when available, LTI-008, otherwise "of those who started"), median time on task, and median number of attempts.

  • Acceptance: Numbers match a hand-calculated fixture of 30 synthetic learners.
  • Verify: Unit tests of the aggregation queries.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): what each number reads, since H5P marks no attempts. A learner has started with any stored statement for the activity (InteractiveBook without a cover counts at load, Column from its first answer; no statement is made up). Completed is a stored root result (LTI-012 as amended), and attempts are the stored root results. Time on task comes from the stored timestamps of each page load, from its first to its last stored statement, never from durationMs. Where a type cannot send a root result, completed, the completion rate and attempts are shown as not available, never as 0; ImageHotspots sends no statement at all, and its tab says that it sends no learning data. Residuals, named in the DPIA input and the students' checklist: attempts count each Column re-check and each CoursePresentation summary slide reached after new answers; a learner who opens a Column and never checks is not counted as started; and reading before the first stored statement and time after the last are not counted.

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, INS-005 · Teacher insight

INS-006 Must S6 Minimum group size and no individual view ● Tested

Any cell, bar or list item that represents fewer than k = 5 distinct learners is shown as "< 5" and its value is suppressed. k is configurable, with a minimum of 3. If suppression of one cell would let a hidden value be worked out from the totals, the next-smallest cell is suppressed too. The insight API has no endpoint that returns per-learner rows.

  • Amended (D-106, 2026-10-30): applied as written: a value about fewer than k learners is shown as «< k» and the API answer carries no value for it. The mappe's two-sided rule (D-095, a rate of 0 % or 100 % hidden) is not added for insight. The grade-sync status counts are exempt (§3), and the property tests cover the insight endpoints and the CSV.
  • Amended (D-106, 2026-11-04): SPEC-DEVIATION: a count of 0 is shown, since it is about no learner; it is hidden only as a complement or in a hidden group. "The next-smallest cell" becomes the rule that leaves no hidden value to work out: in a group with a shown total, when one cell is hidden (or several, all 1 or all k − 1), every shown 0 is hidden, or, without a 0, the smallest shown count and each next one less than k above it. When the learners who started are hidden, every question cell is. An exhaustive test checks every group of two to five cells for k = 3–6.
  • Acceptance: Property-based test: for random datasets, no API response contains a group smaller than k.
  • Verify: fast-check property test [INS-006] ….

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, DATA-001 · Data protection

DATA-002 Must S1 Pseudonymous learners ● Tested

learnerKey = HMAC-SHA256(PSEUDONYM_SECRET[academicYear], source), where source is feide|<feide-id> or lti|<iss>|<sub>. The secret is held in the secret store, rotated per academic year, and destroyed when that year's data is purged. Learner rows store no names, e-mail addresses, Feide IDs, national ID numbers or raw LTI sub values. The one exception is the encrypted ltiSub in GradeSyncJob, which AGS needs; it is deleted 30 days after a successful sync.

  • Verify: Unit tests for key derivation; schema test asserting no PII columns on learner tables.
  • Amended (D-104, 2026-10-30): the encrypted ltiSub is deleted 30 days after the job stops, whether it succeeded, failed or was orphaned, so a job that never succeeds keeps it no longer.

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, DATA-002 · Data protection

DATA-003 Must S6 Annual retention purge ● Tested

A scheduled job runs on a configured date (default 15 August), for the academic year that has ended. It deletes XapiStatement, H5PUserData, GradeSyncJob and learner Identity rows older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days, then learner User rows that have no Identity left (D-034), and destroys that year's pseudonym secret. Only aggregate snapshots that already satisfy k-suppression are kept, for the pedagogisk mappe.

  • Acceptance: A dry-run mode reports counts without deleting. Each run writes an audit event with the counts.
  • Verify: Integration test with time travel.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION in three points. (1) The default date: the job runs by default on 31 August, Oslo time, for the academic year that ended on 31 July, because the boundary plus 30 days ends on 30 August; the date is configurable, but not to a day before 31 August, so the 30 days always pass first. (2) Which rows go: XapiStatement, H5PUserData and GradeSyncJob store an academicYear, set, when a row is written, to the year of the secret that made its learnerKey (DATA-012 as amended, §4), and the purge deletes the ended year's rows by that stored year, in batched transactions, then the learner Identity rows created before that year ended, then learner User rows left without an Identity (D-034); not every row "older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days", which, read on the run date, would also take the new year's first 30 days. The 30 days after the boundary are kept as the time before the purge may run. (3) Who destroys the secret: not the job. The secrets are an environment value (PSEUDONYM_SECRETS) that the server cannot destroy, so HVL operations remove the year's secret in a runbook step after the real run, and DATA-002's rule holds through that step; at start-up the server names, by year only, any secret still configured for a purged year, so a forgotten step shows. Before anything is deleted, the year's InsightSnapshot rows are written per activity, context (D-103) and content version, already suppressed with the configured k (D-106); only they outlive the purge, and the values the mappe reads from them follow D-095's rules. The dry run (counts per table, nothing deleted) and the audit event of every run are as written. A leased job runs the purge on one node, and a CLI runs the same code by hand.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-11-04, the purge built): PURGE_RUN_DATE names a day from 31 August to 31 December (a day in spring would keep a year's rows for most of another year); the job checks hourly and runs once the date is reached and no completed run for the ended year is audited. A run deletes every stored year before the current academic year, so a year a missed run left behind goes too. A snapshot holds the mappe's figures for the year (MAPPE-002) under the mappe's group rules. The runbook is docs/ops/yearly-purge.md.

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, DATA-003 · Data protection

DATA-004 Must S6 EEA residency and encryption ● Tested

PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible storage are hosted in Norway or the EEA. All traffic uses TLS 1.2 or later. Storage is encrypted at rest. Backups are encrypted and retained for 30 days.

  • Verify: Deployment checklist (docs/ops/).
  • Amended (D-109, 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05): in production the server refuses to start with a DATABASE_URL whose sslmode is not require, verify-ca or verify-full, a redis:// REDIS_URL, an http: S3_ENDPOINT, either of the AWS SDK's own endpoint variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL), or file storage outside the EEA allow-list in apps/server/src/config/storageResidency.ts. These checks catch a wrong setting, not where a server stands: the EEA location, encryption at rest and backups stay the deployment checklist's evidence (Q5), and the start-up log names the database and Redis hosts and the storage region for it (docs/ops/database-roles.md).

AuditEvent(at, actorUserId, action, targetType, targetId, details jsonb) records: insight views, exports, library installs and updates, permission changes, data-subject actions and purge runs. The audit log itself has no free-text personal data. It is kept for 2 years.

DATA-008 Must S6 Data-subject requests ● Tested

An admin-only tool takes a Feide ID or an (iss, sub) pair. It derives the learner keys for the retained academic years, then exports (JSON) or deletes that learner's data. Every use is audited.

  • Verify: Integration test of export and erasure.
  • Amended (D-108, 2026-10-30, and its amendments of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05): the tool is a CLI on the server host, with no web page or HTTP route, that HVL operations run on the instruction of HVL's data protection officer, naming an HVL admin as the operator. The identifiers come on standard input, never in the arguments; the CLI derives the learnerKey for every year in PSEUDONYM_SECRETS and the identity hash under every identity key; erase is a dry run unless it is given --confirm; learner H5P state is deleted through our own storage, because Lumi 10.0.4's deleteAllContentUserDataByUser deletes the acting user's state. The audit target is a random request ID. The export also lists the person's portal login events (AuthAuditEvent), which the erasure keeps for their 2 years; a staff member's own data and Canvas's own data are outside the tool (Q6). Runbook: docs/ops/data-subject-requests.md.

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, DATA-011 · Data protection

DATA-012 Must S6 Minimal xAPI storage ● Tested

For each statement, store only: contentId, subContentId?, contentVersion, contextId?, learnerKey, verb, scoreRaw?, scoreMax?, scaled?, success?, completion?, response? (choice indices or short gap text), durationMs?, attemptId, timestamp. Everything else is dropped, including actor names, mailboxes and extensions.

  • Verify: Unit test of the mapper.
  • Amended (D-102, D-103, 2026-10-30): contextId holds the platform-scoped <platformId>:<contextId> (null for a portal play; one module builds and parses it), attemptId is made by the xAPI bridge, since H5P sends none, and timestamp is when the server received the batch. Only learner principals' statements are stored.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION: XapiStatement also stores academicYear, a field outside the list above, set when the row is written. It holds no statement data, only the academic year of the secret behind the row's learnerKey, which the key cannot reveal and a timestamp can misstate (a portal session made before 1 August can keep its learnerKey for up to 12 hours after it, D-057); the annual purge (DATA-003 as amended) deletes by it. H5PUserData and GradeSyncJob store it too (§4).
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): the field list is unchanged; what fills it is made exact. Which statements become rows is LTI-011 as amended: a root attempted, a root answered or completed only as a root result (LTI-012 as amended; a root completed only when it is not a replay), and a sub-content answered with a subContentId. Every stored root answered and completed is therefore a root result, which INS-001 counts without a category field. A row's ID is the bridge's statementId, inserted once, so a batch sent twice stores nothing twice; a content hash is never an identity, because identical statements are normal. timestamp is the receive time plus the item's place in its batch in milliseconds, so the batch's order survives; the browser's clock is never read. attemptId is <viewId>:<n> (LTI-010 as amended). subContentId comes from the h5p-subContentId extension, else from object.id. response is kept only for the interaction types choice and fill-in: each gap (between [,]) is cut to 100 characters, enough to group the answers k learners share, and a response still over 1 000 characters is not stored, since a shortened list would shift its gaps; a numeric response is stored as text. durationMs is parsed from result.duration (null when absent, unreadable or over 24 hours), and no insight reads it, because H5P's durations mean different things by type.
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-11-04, the step-4 privacy review): SPEC-DEVIATION: XapiStatement also stores testUser, true for a statement of Canvas's Student View test student (the LTI TestUser role), set from the launch, never from the statement; database default false. Like academicYear it holds no statement data. Insight, the mappe and the yearly purge's snapshots never read a flagged row, so k − 1 test students cannot make a group of k around one real learner; the grade worker does read them, so a teacher can test the score passback.

Defined in 05 Insight and privacy, DATA-012 · Data protection

DOC-001 Must S1 Every source file starts with a module header ● Tested

Use exactly these labels. Omit a label only when it truly does not apply, never "TODO".

/**
 * SvgSanitizer — removes executable content from SVG files that authors upload.
 *
 * Why: @lumieducation/h5p-server up to and including 10.0.4 is affected by
 *      CVE-2025-7062 (stored XSS through uploaded files) and no fixed release
 *      exists, so HVL Interaktiv sanitises every SVG itself (decision D-003).
 * Spec: SEC-001
 * Invariants:
 *   - Output never contains <script>, on* attributes, <foreignObject>,
 *     <!DOCTYPE> or <!ENTITY>.
 *   - Never throws on malformed input; returns NotSanitized and the file is rejected.
 * Collaborators: registered in H5pEditorFactory via `fileSanitizers`.
 * Tests: apps/server/test/security/SvgSanitizer.test.ts
 */

Checked by: tools/doc-lint (added in Session 1). It fails if a file under apps/, packages/ or tools/ lacks a header, or if a Spec: ID does not exist in docs/specs/. React components and CSS files use the same header in their language's comment syntax.

Add an @example for anything with more than two parameters or a non-obvious call order. Add @spec <ID> when the symbol directly implements a requirement.

export function deriveLearnerKey(source: LearnerSource, secrets: PseudonymSecrets, at: Date = new Date()): string { … }

(From apps/server/src/privacy/deriveLearnerKey.ts.)

Class methods that implement a documented interface, such as Lumi's storage interfaces, may rely on that interface's documentation. DOC-003 Must S1 Explain non-obvious code with tagged rationale comments ● Tested

Comments explain why, never restate what. Use one of these tags so reviewers can grep for them:

TagUse whenMust contain
WHY:The obvious alternative is wrong for a reasonThe reason
SECURITY:The line defends against a threatThe threat and how this line mitigates it
PRIVACY:The line limits personal dataWhich data, and which DATA-* requirement
A11Y:The line exists for accessibilityThe WCAG criterion or user need
PEDAGOGY:A threshold or default comes from learning researchThe reference key from spec 04 §3
UPSTREAM:A workaround for a bug in H5P, Lumi, ltijs or CanvasLink to the upstream issue, and when it can be removed

// SECURITY: the ltik grants access to a learner's launch for 24 h. Strip it from the URL

window.history.replaceState(null, '', withoutLtik(window.location.href));

Spec 00 — Product, Users and Pedagogical Intent

StatusApproved for build (v1.0, 2026-10-16)
Load in sessionsAll sessions read §1–§4. Feature details (§5) are loaded when a session implements them.
Owns requirement IDsPROD-*, NFR-*
Related01 H5P core · 02 Auth/LTI · 03 Universal design · 04 Læringsdesign · 05 Analytics & privacy · Glossary

How to read the requirements: each one has an ID, a priority (MUST, SHOULD or COULD, with the RFC 2119 meanings), the session that delivers it (S1–S6), a statement, acceptance criteria that can be tested, and a verification method. Code and tests refer back to these IDs (see DOCUMENTATION-STANDARD), so an evaluator can follow any ID from spec to code to test.

1. Problem and product promise

1.1 The problem we are solving

Asynchronous study at HVL often means students watch a 45-minute lecture recording or read a PDF that was uploaded to Canvas. This is passive. Research on multimedia learning and retrieval practice (see §4) shows that students learn more from short segments with frequent low-stakes questions. They also learn more when feedback explains why an answer is wrong, not just that it is wrong. Teachers face three practical barriers:

  1. Authoring friction. Interactive tools such as H5P have dozens of content types and many settings. Most of the settings do not help pedagogically, and several content types are not accessible. Teachers have little time and no guidance on which design actually works.
  2. No feedback loop. After setting asynchronous pre-work (forarbeid), a teacher cannot see what students struggled with before meeting them. The synchronous session therefore cannot respond to it.
  3. Institutional obligations. Universal design (WCAG / forskrift om universell utforming av IKT), GDPR, Canvas integration and documentation for the pedagogisk mappe are each solved separately, by hand, if at all.

1.2 Product promise

HVL Interaktiv lets a teacher take one learning outcome and turn it into a short, accessible, interactive activity in under 30 minutes. The teacher can place it in Canvas, and walk into the next seminar knowing which misconceptions to address.

Everything in this specification serves that sentence. If a proposed feature does not shorten the path to a good activity, make it more accessible, or close the feedback loop between asynchronous and synchronous teaching, it is out of scope.

2. Users and personas

Personas are composites. They exist to make requirements concrete; they are not real people.

PersonaRoleContextWhat success looks like
IngridAssociate professor, nursing (Bergen)Prepares students for clinical placement (praksis); 90 students; uses Canvas and Panopto daily; little time for tooling.Creates a three-decision clinical case in a branching scenario. Students practise judgement before placement. In the seminar, Ingrid discusses the choice most students got wrong.
LarsLecturer, engineering (Haugesund)Runs a flipped first-year course with 200 students; records short videos.Students answer embedded questions in an 8-minute video. On Wednesday evening Lars sees that 62 % chose the same wrong option on question 2, and opens Thursday's lecture with it.
AminaPart-time student, social educationWorks days; studies on a phone in the evening; often interrupted.Can stop halfway through a module and resume at the same place the next evening. Gets feedback that explains the misconception.
JonasStudent, teacher education (PPU)Blind; uses a screen reader (NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on iPhone).Completes every activity with keyboard and screen reader alone. Feedback is announced with text, not only colour.
KariLearning designer, ALU (Avdeling for utvikling av læring og undervisning)Supports teachers across faculties; curates templates.Can point teachers to the studio's patterns and planner instead of repeating the same advice in one-to-one meetings.
OlaPlatform administrator, TeCoppApproves LTI tools for Canvas; responsible for library updates and incident response.Only vetted H5P libraries run. Updates are controlled. Logs contain no personal data, and the accessibility statement is easy to keep current.

Roles in the system (used throughout the specs):

RoleWhoCan
learnerStudents (Feide affiliation student, or LTI role Learner)Play published activities; resume their own state.
authorStaff and faculty (Feide employee/faculty/staff), LTI Instructor/TeachingAssistant/ContentDeveloper, plus allow-listed student-author courses (e.g. PPU)Create, edit, share and publish activities; view aggregated insight for activities they own or co-own; export pedagogisk mappe.
adminNamed platform administrators (allow-list in config, Feide login only)Everything an author can do, plus: install and update H5P libraries, manage platforms, run data-subject requests, view audit log. Never granted through an LTI launch.

3. Core user journeys

These journeys are the end-to-end acceptance tests of the product (Playwright, Session 6). Each step names the requirements it exercises.

J1 — Create from a pattern and place it in Canvas (Lars).

  1. In a Canvas module, Lars chooses Add item → External tool → HVL Interaktiv (Deep Linking, LTI-005).
  2. The picker shows Lars's activities and Create new. Lars chooses the phase Forarbeid and the pattern Short video with retrieval checks (PROD-001, PED-010).
  3. The H5P editor opens with an Interactive Video skeleton. It contains three question placeholders at 2–3 minute spacing, a summary task at the end, and guidance text in Nynorsk (H5P-002, H5P-008).
  4. Lars pastes a Panopto link, writes the questions and adds feedback for each wrong option.
  5. Lars clicks Check and publish. The quality check reports one error, a missing caption track, and one hint, that question 3 has no feedback for option C (PROD-003, UD-020, PED-020). Lars fixes both.
  6. The activity is published and returned to Canvas as a graded resource link (LTI-005, LTI-012).
  • Amended (D-101, 2026-11-05, S6 step 8): SPEC-DEVIATION: the picker of step 2 offers no Create new and no content bank; both pass to HVL's bachelor students (docs/handoff/canvas-studio.md). J1 is tested in two halves: steps 2–5 in the portal (patternToPublish.e2e, publishWithReason.e2e) and steps 1 and 6 in Canvas with an activity made in the portal (journeyPlaceInCanvas.e2e).

J2 — Study asynchronously on a phone and resume (Amina, Jonas).

  1. Amina opens the activity from Canvas on a phone. It loads in under 3 s (NFR-001) and reflows to 320 px width (UD-008).
  2. Amina answers two questions. Wrong answers show ✗ Feil: and an explanation (UD-003).
  3. Amina closes the app and, the next evening, resumes at the same point (PROD-008, H5P-005).
  4. Jonas completes the same activity with NVDA and the keyboard only (UD-006, verified manually per UD-031).

J3 — Prepare the seminar from evidence (Lars, Ingrid).

  1. Wednesday evening Lars opens Innsikt → Før samlinga for the activity (INS-001).
  2. Lars sees that 148 students started and 131 completed. Question 2 had 38 % correct on the first attempt, and 62 % chose option B (INS-002, INS-003). Cells with fewer than five students are hidden (INS-006).
  3. Lars adds question 2 to the Bring to seminar shortlist and opens Thursday's session with it.

J4 — Document practice for the teaching portfolio (Ingrid).

  1. Ingrid tags each activity with phase, learning outcomes and a short didactic rationale (PED-030).
  2. Ingrid chooses Pedagogisk mappe → Export and receives a Markdown file and an accessible PDF. They contain the designs, each design's universal design status and anonymised aggregate results (MAPPE-001…MAPPE-004).

J5 — Govern the platform (Kari, Ola).

  1. Kari edits pattern guidance text in the studio's content files and opens a pull request; no code changes are needed (PED-011).
  2. Ola installs a new library version in staging, verifies it, then promotes it. Non-admins cannot install or update libraries, even through an uploaded .h5p file (H5P-006, SEC-003).
  • Amended (D-101, 2026-11-05, S6 step 8): step 1 is an end-to-end test (journeyGovernance.e2e). Step 2 has no page: who may install is tested over HTTP (packageImport.int, ajax.int), and installing in staging and promoting is the procedure A new content-type version in docs/ops/runbook.md §2, which no test runs.

4. Design principles and the pedagogy behind them

#PrincipleWhat it means in the productEvidence base (verify citations with ALU before publishing on the studio page)
P1Pedagogy before featuresUsers start from a learning-design pattern, not from an empty list of content types.Biggs (1996), constructive alignment, Higher Education 32
P2Short segments, frequent retrievalVideo patterns default to 6–9 min with checks every 2–3 min.Guo, Kim & Rubin (2014), L@S '14; Szpunar, Khan & Schacter (2013), PNAS 110(16); Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Psychological Science 17(3)
P3Feedback that explainsWrong-option feedback is prompted, checked and highlighted in insight.Shute (2008), Review of Educational Research 78(1); Hattie & Timperley (2007), RER 77(1); Nicol & Macfarlane-Dick (2006), Studies in Higher Education 31(2)
P4Formative by defaultRetry and Show solution are on; no timers; scores are low-stakes.Dunlosky et al. (2013), Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1)
P5Close the async → sync loopInsight is designed for the evening before a seminar.Novak, Patterson, Gavrin & Christian (1999), Just-in-Time Teaching
P6Practise professional judgement safelyBranching scenarios with 3–4 decision points, explanations and retry paths.Schön (1983), The Reflective Practitioner; van Manen (1991), The Tact of Teaching
P7Accessible by default, not by auditTheme, validator and patterns prevent barriers before publishing.WCAG 2.2; Norwegian forskrift om universell utforming av IKT-løysingar
P8Privacy by designPseudonymous learners, aggregated insight only, yearly purge.GDPR Art. 5 and 25
P9Nynorsk firstUI and H5P strings default to nn, with nb and en as fallbacks.HVL language policy; mållova
P10Less is moreExactly ten content types; sensible defaults; settings hidden unless they help learning.Sweller (1988), cognitive load, Cognitive Science 12(2)

5. Functional requirements

PROD-001 Must S5 Create an activity from a learning-design pattern

An author can create a new activity by choosing a phase (Forarbeid, Mellomarbeid, Etterarbeid) and then a pattern. The H5P editor opens pre-filled with a pedagogically sound skeleton and guidance.

  • Acceptance: Every pattern in 04 §4 can be instantiated. The created content passes validateContent with zero errors before the author edits it, apart from placeholders that are deliberately flagged as needing input. Choosing blank activity is still possible.
  • Verify: Integration test that creates each pattern; e2e for J1.
  • Amended (D-101, 2026-11-05, S6 step 8): SPEC-DEVIATION: "e2e for J1" is J1's portal half (patternToPublish.e2e, publishWithReason.e2e); creating from a pattern in Canvas's Deep Linking picker passes to HVL's bachelor students (docs/handoff/canvas-studio.md).

PROD-002 Must S2 Exactly ten authorable content types

Authors can create only the ten content types in 01 §3.

  • Acceptance: See H5P-002.
  • Verify: Covered by H5P-002 tests.

PROD-003 Must S4 Check-and-publish quality gate

Activities have the states draft and published. Publish runs the universal design validator (UD-020) and the pedagogical hints (PED-020). Findings are listed in plain language with a Go to field link.

  • Acceptance: An error blocks publishing unless the author records an acknowledgement with a reason (e.g. "captions are being produced in Panopto"). Acknowledgements are stored, appear in insight and in the portfolio export, and are raised again on the next publish after 14 days. Warnings and hints never block.
  • Verify: Unit tests for state transitions; e2e for J1 step 5.

PROD-004 Must S3 Learners only see published activities

  • Acceptance: A learner request for a draft returns a friendly "not yet available" page (HTTP 404 to avoid revealing its existence). Authors can preview drafts.
  • Verify: Integration test.

PROD-005 Must S3 Place activities in Canvas

Authors can place an activity in a Canvas module, assignment or rich-content editor through LTI Deep Linking. See LTI-005.

PROD-006 Must S3 Share outside Canvas with Feide

An author can share an activity link that works outside Canvas. Viewers log in with Feide. Visibility is one of: only me / co-authors, everyone at HVL, or anyone with a Feide login.

  • Acceptance: Visibility is enforced by the permission system (H5P-006). Changing visibility takes effect immediately.
  • Verify: Integration tests per visibility level.

PROD-007 Should S5 Co-authoring and an institutional content bank

Authors can add co-authors (HVL staff found by name or Feide ID) and can publish an activity to the HVL content bank so that colleagues can duplicate and adapt it.

  • Acceptance: A duplicate keeps a link to its source and the original author's attribution. It never copies learner data.
  • Verify: Integration tests.

PROD-008 Must S2 Resume where you left off

A learner who leaves an activity and returns on any device resumes with their previous answers and position. See H5P-005.

PROD-009 Must S5 Formative defaults

For all patterns, Retry and Show solution are enabled, there are no time limits, and pass thresholds are informative rather than gatekeeping.

  • Acceptance: Pattern skeletons set the relevant behaviour fields. The hint rule PED-H07 flags activities where an author has turned these off.
  • Verify: Unit tests on skeleton parameters.

PROD-010 Must S6 Teacher insight before the seminar

Authors see aggregated, anonymised results per activity, designed to prepare the next synchronous session. See INS-* in 05.

PROD-011 Must S4 Formative-use notice

The editor and the Deep Linking picker show a short, dismissible notice. It says H5P activities are scored in the browser and are meant for formative work (undervegsvurdering), not exams.

  • Acceptance: Notice text exists in nn, nb and en. Dismissal is remembered per user.
  • Verify: Component test.

PROD-012 Must S1 Three languages, Nynorsk first

All UI is available in Nynorsk (default), Bokmål and English. H5P strings fall back from nn to nb to en. See H5P-008.

  • Acceptance: A test fails if any key is missing in a locale file.
  • Verify: Unit test for key parity.

PROD-013 Should S5 Safe editing of a published activity

When an author edits an activity that already has learner state, the editor warns that structural changes (adding, removing or reordering questions) reset saved progress. It offers Save as new version.

  • Acceptance: Existing learner state is invalidated only when the author confirms. Insight separates results by version.
  • Verify: Integration test.

PROD-014 Could S6 Spaced-retrieval suggestion

After publishing an Etterarbeid activity, the author is shown suggested repetition dates (for example +7 and +21 days) and a one-click copy to place in a later Canvas module.

  • Verify: Component test.

6. Non-functional requirements

NFR-001 Must S6 Performance

An activity page (player plus content) becomes interactive in ≤ 3 s at p95 on a simulated "Fast 4G" profile with 200 concurrent learners on one application node. API p95 is ≤ 300 ms excluding file downloads.

  • Verify: k6 or Artillery load test script in tools/load/; Lighthouse CI on the player route.

NFR-002 Must S6 Availability and recoverability

99.5 % monthly availability during the semester. Database backups run daily with 30-day retention. A documented restore is tested once per semester.

  • Verify: Operations runbook in docs/ops/; restore drill log.

NFR-003 Must S4 Mobile and assistive technology

Works on the last two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on iOS Safari and on Android Chrome, and with NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver. See 03.

NFR-004 Must S1 Maintainability

Source files are ≤ 200 lines and each has a single responsibility. Every file follows DOCUMENTATION-STANDARD. CI runs typecheck, lint, tests and the traceability check.

  • Verify: npm run check:filesize, npm run spec:trace in CI.

NFR-005 Must S1 Open source licence

The repository is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. This is required because @lumieducation/h5p-server is GPL-3.0-or-later. Dependencies must be GPL-3.0-compatible (for example MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC).

  • Verify: A licence check in CI against a GPL-3.0-compatible allow-list (npm run check:licences, D-029).

NFR-006 Must S6 Observability without personal data

Logs are structured JSON with request ID, route, status and latency. They must never contain names, e-mail addresses, Feide IDs, LTI sub values, ltik tokens, or answer contents. See DATA-009.

  • Verify: A unit test runs the log redaction function against a fixture of sensitive fields.

NFR-007 Must S6 Deployable on HVL or Sikt infrastructure

Docker images and docker-compose.yml for local and staging environments. Only EEA-hosted PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible storage. No runtime calls to third-party CDNs (see DATA-011).

  • Verify: docker compose up smoke test in CI.

7. Scope boundaries

In scope (v1): the ten H5P content types; Feide portal; Canvas LTI 1.3 (launch, Deep Linking, AGS, optionally NRPS); universal design theme and validator; læringsdesign studio; pedagogisk mappe export; teacher insight; GDPR controls; Docker deployment.

Out of scope (v1), with the reason:

Not in v1Why
Summative exams or proctoringH5P scores in the browser and can be manipulated; HVL uses Wiseflow for exams.
Generative-AI authoringNeeds its own DPIA, quality and academic-integrity review. Revisit after the pilot.
Individual learner dashboards for teachersCanvas already shows individual grades. Aggregates are enough for teaching decisions and are better for privacy.
Content types beyond the tenKept small on purpose (P10). Adding one is a decision log entry plus accessibility review.
Native mobile appsThe responsive web player is sufficient.
LMSs other than CanvasCanvas is mandatory at HVL. LTI 1.3 keeps other LMSs possible later.

8. Success measures for the pilot (Session 5 onwards, with Pedagogisk akademi and ALU)

MeasureTargetHow measured

Activities whose wrong options all have feedback≥ 75 %PED-H05 results
Teacher-rated usability (SUS)≥ 75Survey of pilot teachers
Pilot teachers who opened Før samlinga before at least half of their seminars≥ 50 %Audit log

1. Verified facts this spec relies on

These facts were checked on 2026-10-16 against the npm registry, the published package source and public advisories. The plan document (HVL_Interaktiv_Development_Plan.pdf) differs on some points. Where it does, this spec wins and the reason is recorded in DECISIONS.md.

FactValue (2026-10-16)Consequence

Risk R-01 (open). h5p-server 10.0.4 was released before Core 1.28. Three incompatibilities are already known (F1–F3 above), each with a workaround; whether others exist is unverified. Session 1 starts with a time-boxed spike (§7). If the spike fails, fall back to Core 1.27 with the Daylight theme turned off, and record a decision. Do not patch node_modules. Use patch-package with a documented patch only.

3. The ten content types

The minimum versions come from the development plan. Session 1 must confirm them against the seed packages and update this table with the exact installed versions.

Deliberately excluded: H5P.DragQuestion (free 2-D drag and drop). It is a significant barrier for keyboard, switch and screen-reader users (D-006). Sub-libraries such as H5P.TrueFalse, H5P.SingleChoiceSet, H5P.DialogCards, H5P.Accordion, H5P.AdvancedText, H5P.Image and H5P.Video stay installed as dependencies and may be used inside containers. They are not offered as top-level choices. DragQuestion is not offered as a sub-content choice either: this is enforced with alterLibrarySemantics on container libraries (see H5P-002).

Nynorsk display names are drafts and must be checked against H5P's own nn language files and by HVL's language advisers.

4. Requirements — H5P engine

H5P-001 Must S1 Target Core API 1.28 and the new Hub

H5pConfigFactory sets coreApiVersion = { major: 1, minor: 28 }, hubContentTypesEndpoint = 'https://hub-api.h5p.org/v1/content-types/' and hubRegistrationEndpoint = 'https://hub-api.h5p.org/v1/sites', plus the F1/F2 workarounds above (getLocalIdOverride, pre-set uuid). Core client files come from the release tag 1.28.0. The editor has no 1.28 release, so its files come from one reviewed, pinned commit with recorded hashes (D-022). The project never tracks a moving branch such as master.

  • Acceptance: On startup the server logs the core version and Hub host. It refuses to start if the core client files on disk report a different version than the config. No code contains the string api.h5p.org/v1/content-types except the test that asserts its absence.
  • Verify: Unit test of the factory; boot test (h5pServerInit).

H5P-002 Must S2 Ten-type authoring whitelist

HvlTop10ContentTypeFilter makes only the ten machine names in §3 appear as creatable in the editor Hub list. Their dependencies remain installable. H5P.DragQuestion is removed from the options of every container's sub-content selector (via alterLibrarySemantics).

  • Acceptance: (a) The content-type-cache AJAX response contains exactly the ten machine names as creatable. (b) Saving content whose main library is not in the list returns HTTP 403 with a translated error. (c) No container semantics offer H5P.DragQuestion. (d) The whitelist is one constant, HVL_TOP10_CONTENT_TYPES, with a comment linking here.
  • Verify: Unit tests for (a)–(c); test names start with [H5P-002].

H5P-003 Must S2 Deterministic offline seeding

npm run seed:libraries installs the ten types and their dependencies from verified .h5p packages in docs/reference/h5p-core-1.28-seed-packages/ (see reference README). It needs no network access. A SHA256SUMS file lists the hash of each package. The script refuses to install a package whose hash does not match.

  • Acceptance: Running the script twice is idempotent. CI seeds from scratch in under 2 minutes.
  • Verify: Integration test against an empty storage.

H5P-004 Must S1 Production storage adapters

InterfaceImplementationBacking store
IContentStoragePrismaContentStoragePostgreSQL (metadata, parameters) + S3 (files)
ILibraryStorageFile-system-backed on a shared volume, wrapped in Lumi's CachedLibraryStorage (D-026)Shared volume; S3 only if S6 needs it
ITemporaryFileStorageS3TemporaryFileStorageS3 with a lifecycle rule as a backstop
IKeyValueStorageRedisKeyValueStorageRedis (shared across nodes)
ILockProvider@lumieducation/h5p-redis-lockRedis
IContentUserDataStoragePrismaContentUserDataStoragePostgreSQL

TemporaryFileCleanupJob calls h5pEditor.temporaryFileManager.cleanUp() every 5 minutes. A Redis lock ensures only one node runs it.

  • Acceptance: Two server instances share the content-type cache and locks. The temporary file cleanup runs once per interval cluster-wide.
  • Verify: Integration tests against PostgreSQL, Redis and an S3-compatible store (D-023). The user-data adapter is built and tested with H5P-005 in S2 (D-028).

H5P-005 Must S2 Learner state persistence (resume)

PrismaContentUserDataStorage stores H5P user data keyed by (contentId, subContentId, dataType, learnerKey, contextId). learnerKey is the pseudonym defined in DATA-002, never a raw ID. contentUserStateSaveInterval stays at the default 5 s. "Invalidate on content change" follows H5P semantics, with the author confirmation in PROD-013.

  • Acceptance: After a simulated reload, the player receives the saved state. A learner in a different Canvas course (context) gets separate state.
  • Verify: Integration test.

H5P-006 Must S2 Permission system

HvlPermissionSystem implements IPermissionSystem with this matrix. Anything not listed is denied.

Permissionlearnerauthoradmin

GeneralPermission.UpdateAndInstallLibraries✗✗✓
