Leaving permissionSystem undefined (Lumi's LaissezFairePermissionSystem) is forbidden. A boot check enforces this.

  • Verify: A table-driven unit test covers every cell above.

H5P-007 Must S3 Authenticated H5P AJAX in iframes

HvlUrlGenerator extends Lumi's UrlGenerator. Every AJAX, user-data and set-finished URL carries the ltik (Canvas mode) or a CSRF token (portal mode), URL-encoded, as specified in LTI-003. Amended in S3 (D-058): the token is added by our class rather than Lumi's queryParamGenerator, which does not encode it consistently; content files use signed URLs (/h5p/files/<grant>/…) instead of a token.

  • Acceptance: A request to an H5P AJAX endpoint without a valid token returns 401.
  • Verify: Integration test for each mode.

H5P-008 Must S2 Nynorsk-first translation

HvlTranslationCallback uses i18next with fallbackLng: ['nb', 'en'] and default lng: 'nn'. When a content-type library has no language/nn.json, the library's nb and then en strings are used.

  • Acceptance: A library without nn renders in nb. The UI language can be switched per user.
  • Verify: Unit test with a fixture library.
  • Amended (D-111, 2026-10-30): an extension, as D-046 was: an HVL language overlay, a library-storage wrapper after D-046's, sets learner-facing defaults in the nn and nb language files of the ten types and their usual sub-content, with the texts in content/ for ALU (drafts until reviewed). Lumi's alterLibraryLanguageFile is not used: in 10.0.4 it drops the editor libraries' libraryStrings. Built in S6's step 7.
  • Built (S6 step 7, 2026-11-05; D-111's amendments): LanguageOverlayLibraryStorage over D-046's wrapper in the editor and the player, with the texts in content/h5p-tekstar/ (drafts until HVL's language advisers and ALU review them, Q2, Q17). Its scope was widened to field labels and the editor libraries' libraryStrings (such as H5P.DragNBar's «Lim inn»); an entry whose English text has changed in the library is skipped, and content:check names it. Activities keep the texts they were saved with. Tests: [H5P-008] in test/h5p/languageOverlay/, including a real nn player and nb editor, and in test/learningDesign/content/h5pTexts*.test.ts.

H5P-009 Must S4 Inject theme and client scripts into player and editor

Use customization.global.styles and customization.global.scripts, or alterLibraryFiles, to add packages/hvl-h5p-theme/dist/hvl-h5p-theme.css (UD-011) and the xAPI bridge script (LTI-010) inside the H5P iframe.

  • Acceptance: The iframe document contains both assets with integrity hashes and nonces that match the CSP.
  • Verify: Playwright test inspects the iframe DOM.
  • Amended (D-070, 2026-10-23): tags that H5P Core writes into its own iframes cannot carry a nonce or an integrity hash; they are allowed by the page's script-src 'self' and the hash of Core's one constant inline script instead. Our own page tags keep integrity hashes. (This sentence was withdrawn on 2026-10-24: no code did this. See the next note.)
  • Amended (D-070, 2026-10-24): our own tags on the H5P player and editor pages (first scripts, boot scripts, stylesheets, Lumi's core and library lists with the theme files) carry no integrity hash or nonce either; they are same-origin files allowed by 'self', like H5P's own tags. This replaces the withdrawn last sentence of the 2026-10-23 note; D-070's amendment gives the reasons. The Next.js pages carry a nonce on every script. What remains of the acceptance in S4 is the theme in each document that holds H5P content, under that policy (apps/server/test/h5p/hvlTheme.browser.int.test.ts); the xAPI bridge arrives with LTI-010 (S6).
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION for the bridge: it is not injected inside the H5P iframe. It is plain JavaScript, packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.js, and runs once in the top player document that h5p/render/playerPage.ts renders (/h5p/play/:contentId, /lti/play), only for a learner principal; H5P Core relays the statements of its own iframes to that document's H5P.externalDispatcher. It never runs in Core's iframes, in the Next.js page around them or in the editor. The theme part of this requirement is unchanged. For the bridge, the acceptance therefore looks at the player document: the bridge loads there for a learner, under the page's script policy, and not for anyone else (D-102; LTI-010 checks that statements arrive).

H5P-010 Should S6 Panopto-first video guidance

Use alterLibrarySemantics on H5P.InteractiveVideo and H5P.Video to replace the upload field's description with nn/nb/en guidance. It recommends HVL's Panopto streaming URL with a .vtt caption track, and allows direct .mp4 uploads only up to 50 MB (enforced in SEC-005).

  • Verify: Unit test on the altered semantics.
  • Amended (D-111, 2026-10-30): the language/nn.json and nb.json of H5P.InteractiveVideo and H5P.Video override a description set in the semantics, so alterLibrarySemantics (composed with the DragQuestion filter) sets the English guidance, and the HVL language overlay (H5P-008's amendment) sets the nn and nb guidance. The texts live in content/, where npm run content:check checks them (D-082); HVL's Panopto host name and the wording are for HVL and ALU to confirm.
  • Built (S6 step 7, 2026-11-05; D-111's amendments): apps/server/src/h5p/semantics/videoGuidance.ts (English, on H5P.InteractiveVideo 1.28 interactiveVideo.video.files and H5P.Video 1.6 sources) and the overlay's content/h5p-tekstar/video-guidance.yaml (nn, nb), a draft until HVL and ALU review it (Q2, Q17). content:check refuses guidance on a field that is not a video field. Tests: [H5P-010] in test/h5p/semantics/videoGuidance.test.ts, test/h5p/languageOverlay/languageOverlay.int.test.ts and test/learningDesign/content/h5pTexts*.test.ts.

H5P-011 Must S2 Controlled library updates

Libraries are installed or updated only by admins, through the seed script or the admin UI. Each change writes an audit event: actor, library, old version, new version and source hash. In production, install from Hub on demand is disabled. Updates first go to staging.

  • Verify: Integration test; audit log assertion.

5. Requirements — upload and content security

SEC-001 Must S2 Sanitise SVG files (CVE-2025-7062 mitigation)

Register SvgSanitizer in fileSanitizers for both editor uploads and .h5p package imports. It wraps @lumieducation/h5p-svg-sanitizer (DOMPurify) and additionally rejects or strips: <!DOCTYPE> and <!ENTITY> declarations (XXE and "billion laughs"), <script>, on* attributes, <foreignObject>, javascript: and data:text/html URLs, and external href/xlink:href references.

  • Acceptance: A corpus of malicious SVGs in apps/server/test/fixtures/svg/ comes out inert. It includes standalone="no" with an external entity, an inline script, an event handler and a foreignObject with HTML. Benign SVGs keep their appearance (snapshot of the rendered PNG).
  • Verify: Unit tests [SEC-001] …; one integration test per upload path.

SEC-002 Must S2 Narrow allowlist and content sniffing

The content file allowlist (contentWhitelist) is narrowed to what the ten types need: json png jpg jpeg gif webp svg webm mp4 mp3 m4a ogg wav vtt webvtt pdf txt csv docx xlsx pptx odt ods odp. xml, swf, md, textile, diff and patch are removed. FileTypeSniffer rejects a file whose magic bytes contradict its extension, for example HTML in a .png.

  • Verify: Unit tests with polyglot fixtures.

SEC-003 Must S2 Uploaded packages never install code for non-admins

When an author imports a .h5p file, the server installs only the content. A library in the package that is not already installed, or that has a different patch version, is rejected with a clear message. Admins can install it after review.

  • Verify: Integration test with a package that contains a modified H5P.MultiChoice.

SEC-004 Must S2 Serve user content defensively

Content files are served with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. SVG and document files are served with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'. Non-media types are served with Content-Disposition: attachment. In production, content files are served from a separate origin (e.g. files.interaktiv.hvl.no), so a script in a file cannot reach the app's origin, cookies or ltik.

  • Verify: Integration test of headers; deployment checklist item.
  • Amended (D-110, 2026-11-05): built in S6: the player's files come from files.<host> of PUBLIC_BASE_URL (or FILES_BASE_URL, https in production), with CORS for the app origin and H5P's crossorigin, and the main origin answers their path with 404. The editor's saved files, fresh uploads and H5P's cookie routes stay on the main origin with the headers above (SPEC-DEVIATION: D-110: H5P's image editor draws into a canvas without crossorigin). Verified by the files-origin integration and e2e tests and the image's smoke test.

SEC-005 Must S1 Size limits and archive safety

maxFileSize is 50 MB and maxTotalSize is 200 MB per package. The server rejects zip entries with path traversal or absolute paths. Package imports are processed in a temporary directory with a quota.

  • Verify: Unit tests with a zip-slip fixture and an oversize fixture.

SEC-006 Should S6 Malware scanning

When CLAMAV_HOST is configured, register @lumieducation/h5p-clamav-scanner in malwareScanners.

  • Verify: Integration test with the EICAR test string (skipped when ClamAV is absent).
  • Amended (D-110, 2026-11-05): the scanner fails closed (only "clean" stores a file, on both upload paths) and gets its settings only from our checked configuration; production requires CLAMAV_HOST unless CLAMAV_ALLOW_UNSCANNED_UPLOADS is set, and TLS off the loopback. Verified by fake-clamd tests in every run, the real EICAR tests when CLAMAV_TEST_HOST names a clamd (CI runs one as a service), and the image's smoke test against its stack's clamd.

SEC-007 Must S1 Dependency hygiene

All runtime dependencies are pinned exactly (no ^) and listed in package-lock.json. CI runs npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high and fails on unreviewed findings. A reviewed exception must be recorded in DECISIONS.md with an expiry date. Renovate (or Dependabot) opens update PRs weekly.

A test saves content with <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> in a plain-text field. It asserts that the stored and rendered value is escaped.

7. Session 1 spike checklist (time-box: 90 minutes)

Record each result in PROGRESS.md, and record a decision in DECISIONS.md whenever a result changes this spec.

2. Two ways in, one identity model

                    ┌────────────────────── interaktiv.hvl.no (one public origin) ──────────────────────┐
 Browser (top-level)│  /            → apps/web  (Next.js App Router)                                    │
  Feide portal      │  /api, /h5p   → apps/server (Express)          principal = Feide session (cookie)  │
                    │  /auth/feide/* → OIDC RP (openid-client)                                           │
                    │                                                                                    │
 Canvas iframe      │  /lti/login, /lti/launch, /lti/keys → ltijs Provider                               │
  (3rd-party ctx)   │  → redirect to /app/…?ltik=…  → web stores ltik in memory → Authorization: Bearer   │
                    └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 files.interaktiv.hvl.no  → user-uploaded H5P content files only (SEC-004), no cookies, no ltik

In S3 (D-048, D-058): apps/web does not exist yet, so apps/server itself renders the start page /, the player /lti/play and the Deep Linking picker /lti/deeplink; ltijs redirects to those pages with ?ltik=… instead of /app/…. apps/web takes over / and /app/* in S4. From S6 the player loads content files from the files origin (files.<host>/h5p/files/<grant>/…, or FILES_BASE_URL), authorised by a signed grant rather than a cookie or an ltik; the main origin answers that path with 404, and the editor's files stay there under grants of their own (D-045, D-110's amendment of 2026-11-05, SPEC-DEVIATION: D-110).

From S4 (D-067, D-068, D-069): when the web app runs (WEB_APP is not off), ltijs sends resource-link launches to /app/play, which Next.js renders after Express has resolved the ltik and removed it from what Next.js sees. The page keeps the ltik in memory and frames the H5P pages /lti/play?ltik=… (player) and /lti/edit?ltik=… (the Rediger tab), which stay server-rendered. The Deep Linking picker stays the server-rendered page /lti/deeplink, restyled with the token CSS and given the formative notice (PROD-011); there is no /app/deeplink (D-067 amendment). Without the web app, launches land on /lti/play as in S3.

Both entry points resolve to a single server-side Principal:

/** What every API handler receives after authentication. Defined in apps/server/src/auth/Principal.ts */
interface Principal {
  userId: string;              // internal UUID; learners have pseudonymous User rows too (D-034, D-053)
  learnerKey: string;          // HMAC pseudonym (DATA-002), always present
  roles: Array<'learner' | 'author' | 'admin'>;   // the H5P role is the highest of them
  mode: 'portal' | 'lti';
  locale: 'nn' | 'nb' | 'en';
  hvlMember: boolean;          // portal: Feide organisation in ALLOWED_FEIDE_ORGS; LTI: false
  feideAuthenticated: boolean; // portal only
  studentAuthor: boolean;      // a student allowed to author through AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS (D-059)
  lti?: { platformId: string; deploymentId: string; contextId: string; resourceLinkId?: string;
          contentId?: string; lineItemUrl?: string; messageType: string };
}

Amended in S3 (D-053): userId is always set, and the principal carries the facts the permission system reads (D-036). auth/principalToH5pActor.ts maps it to the H5P actor.

Putting web and API on one origin behind a reverse proxy avoids CORS and keeps the portal session cookie first-party.

3. Requirements — Feide portal (standalone access)

AUTH-001 Must S3 Feide OpenID Connect login (Authorization Code + PKCE)

The server is a confidential OIDC relying party, registered in the Feide Customer Portal (kunde.feide.no) under HVL (realm hvl.no (verify realm)). It uses openid-client 6 with discovery from issuer https://auth.dataporten.no (document /.well-known/openid-configuration), plus PKCE (S256), state and nonce. ID tokens are RS256-signed. Scopes: openid profile email userid-feide groups-org groups-edu. All six are valid Feide scope (attribute-group) names. Always send the scope list explicitly: a request with openid alone releases every attribute group configured for the client. In the Customer Portal, authorise only the attribute groups userinfo-name, email, userid-feide, groups-org and groups-edu; never userinfo-photo or userid-nin.

  • Acceptance: The full flow works against a mock OIDC provider in tests. ID tokens with a wrong iss, aud, nonce or an expired exp are rejected. The client secret is read from an environment variable or secret store and is never logged.
  • Verify: Integration tests with oauth2-mock-server (or equivalent); test names [AUTH-001] ….

AUTH-002 Must S3 Map Feide affiliation to roles

After login, call GET https://groups-api.dataporten.no/groups/me/groups with the user's Feide access token (Authorization: Bearer). Find the organisation group (type: "fc:org", id: "fc:org:<realm>", for HVL fc:org:hvl.no (verify realm)) and read its membership.affiliation array. Feide's values are faculty, student, staff, alum, member, affiliate, employee and library-walk-in. Course groups for AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS come from groups-edu as FS groups, e.g. fc:fs:fs:emne:<realm>:<course-code>:<version>; they require HVL's FS integration in Feide (verify).

Feide affiliation (any of)Role in HVL Interaktiv
employee, faculty, staffauthor
student and member of an allow-listed course group (config AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS, e.g. PPU, Brettspel som didaktisk ressurs)author (scoped: may author; content visibility limited to the course)
student, member, affiliate, alum, library-walk-inlearner
Feide ID (claim https://n.feide.no/claims/eduPersonPrincipalName, e.g. name@hvl.no; needs userid-feide) in config ADMIN_FEIDE_IDSadds admin
Organisation not in ALLOWED_FEIDE_ORGS (default hvl.no)learner on content shared with "anyone with Feide"; otherwise denied
  • Acceptance: A table-driven test covers every row, including users with both student and employee (→ author).
  • Verify: Unit tests of FeideRoleMapper.

AUTH-003 Must S3 Portal session

The server keeps the session in Redis and gives the browser an opaque ID in a cookie (__Host-hvli_sid; HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/). The session expires after 2 h idle or 12 h absolute. State-changing requests require a CSRF token (synchronizer pattern). Logout clears the session and redirects the browser to Feide's end_session_endpoint (https://auth.dataporten.no/openid/endsession) with post_logout_redirect_uri (registered in the Customer Portal) and id_token_hint. Feide requires both, so the raw ID token is kept in the server-side session only, encrypted at rest and deleted at logout or expiry (D-021).

  • Verify: Integration tests (expiry, CSRF rejection, logout).

AUTH-004 Must S3 Data minimisation at login

Request only the scopes listed in AUTH-001. Never request userid-nin or read the claim https://n.feide.no/claims/nin (national identity number), or other extended attributes. Feide releases name and email for every user once those attribute groups are authorised, so the claims mapper drops them for learners before anything is stored. Store a display name and e-mail only for authors and admins, who need them for co-author search and attribution. Feide never verifies e-mail addresses (email_verified is always false), so e-mail is never used as an identifier; use sub or the Feide ID.

  • Verify: Unit test asserts the scope string. Integration test asserts that no learner row has a name or e-mail.
  • Amended (D-090, 2026-10-29, S5 review): SPEC-DEVIATION: the e-mail is no longer stored for anyone. Co-author search matches the display name or the Feide ID's hash, and the bank and copies show the name only, so a stored address had no use; each staff login now clears User.email.

AUTH-005 Should S3 Link an author's Canvas identity to their Feide identity

The aim is one personal library whether a teacher arrives through Canvas or the portal. To link them, read the custom claim feide_login = $Canvas.user.loginId, configured only on the Deep Linking placements (never tool-wide), so learners' resource-link launches never carry it. The server reads it only when LTI-004 yields author, ignores unresolved values that start with $, and never stores it for learners. In LTI 1.3 Canvas releases custom-field substitutions whatever the privacy_level, so a test launch must confirm the value and that it equals the Feide ID (verify with TeCopp). If it does not, use a one-time "Link with Feide" pop-up instead. Learner identities are never linked across modes.

  • Verify: Integration test of the linking flow.

4. Requirements — Canvas LTI 1.3 core and Deep Linking

LTI-001 Must S3 LTI 1.3 tool with ltijs 7

apps/server/src/lti/LtiProviderFactory.ts builds the ltijs Provider with the routes /lti/login, /lti/launch, /lti/keys, our PrismaLtiDatabaseManager and RedisCacheManager. The Canvas platform registration values for Instructure-hosted Canvas are: issuer https://canvas.instructure.com, auth https://sso.canvaslms.com/api/lti/authorize_redirect, token https://sso.canvaslms.com/login/oauth2/token, keyset https://sso.canvaslms.com/api/lti/security/jwks (Instructure's documentation and source; the documented token fallback is https://<institution-domain>/login/oauth2/token). Leave ltijs's authorizationServer unset, so the client-assertion aud equals the token URL. Beta and test instances use canvas.{beta,test}.instructure.com and sso.{beta,test}.canvaslms.com; which one TeCopp's test Canvas is (verify with TeCopp). The clientId and deployment ID come from the Developer Key after the JSON in docs/reference/canvas-lti13-developer-key.json is pasted. The Developer Key's Redirect URIs field (set in the Canvas UI, not in the JSON) must contain exactly https://interaktiv.hvl.no/lti/launch.

  • Acceptance: A full launch against a mock platform (signed with a test key) succeeds. The launch is rejected if the signature, aud, nonce or deployment ID is wrong, or if the nonce is replayed.
  • Verify: Integration tests [LTI-001] ….

LTI-002 Must S3 PostgreSQL storage for ltijs

PrismaLtiDatabaseManager implements all 14 methods of ltijs's DatabaseManager. consumeNonce is atomic: a single DELETE … RETURNING, so a nonce can be used once even under concurrency. ID-token records expire after 24 h and nonces after 10 min, enforced by a cleanup job. Platform private keys are encrypted at rest with a key from the secret store.

  • Verify: Run ltijs's contract behaviour (save/get/consume) as a shared test suite. Concurrency test for consumeNonce.

LTI-003 Must S3 Cookie-less ltik transport

  1. onResourceLink and onDeepLinking call context.redirect(res, '/app/…'), which appends ?ltik=….
  2. The Next.js page reads ltik once and keeps it only in memory (React context, never localStorage or sessionStorage). It removes it from the address bar with history.replaceState.
  3. All API calls send Authorization: Bearer <ltik>. H5P iframe URLs carry it through HvlUrlGenerator (H5P-007).
  4. Server middleware resolves provider.getLaunchContext(ltik) into a Principal. Invalid or expired → 401 with a "please reopen from Canvas" page.
  5. Pages that receive an ltik send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. The logger redacts ltik in query strings and headers.
  6. Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors lists only the configured Canvas origins (config CANVAS_ORIGINS, e.g. https://hvl.instructure.com, plus TeCopp's test instance and any vanity domain). sso.canvaslms.com is not an ancestor and is not listed. X-Frame-Options is not sent.
  • Acceptance: A Playwright test with third-party cookies blocked completes launch → play → resume inside a cross-origin iframe.
  • Verify: Integration and e2e tests; header assertions.

LTI-004 Must S3 Map LTI roles safely

LTI role claim containsRole
membership#Instructor, membership/Instructor#TeachingAssistant, membership#ContentDeveloperauthor (in this context)
membership#Learner (only)learner
institution/person#Administrator or any other roleauthor at most

An LTI launch never grants admin. H5P library administration requires a Feide login and the admin allow-list (AUTH-002).

  • Verify: Table-driven unit test, including a forged Administrator claim.

LTI-005 Must S3 Deep Linking 2.0 picker

onDeepLinking redirects to /app/deeplink. There the author can (a) choose existing activities (own, co-authored or from the content bank), or (b) create a new one from a pattern (PROD-001) and return when it is published. The server builds content items of type ltiResourceLink with custom: { contentId }, title, an iframe size hint, and, for the graded placement assignment_selection only, a lineItem with { scoreMaximum: 100, label, resourceId: contentId, tag: 'hvl-interaktiv' }. Canvas ignores lineItem from link_selection and editor_button, so those links never sync grades. It returns the items with context.deepLinking.createDeepLinkingForm(items). Multiple selection is offered only when the platform sends accept_multiple: true (Canvas sends false for assignment_selection). Returned resource links always point to https://interaktiv.hvl.no.

  • Acceptance: The auto-submitted form posts a signed JWT to deep_link_return_url. Draft activities cannot be returned.
  • Verify: Integration test decodes and validates the returned JWT. E2e in J1.
  • Amended (D-101, 2026-11-05, S6 step 8): SPEC-DEVIATION: (a) lists own and co-authored activities only, and (b) is not built; the content bank and Create new pass to HVL's bachelor students (docs/handoff/canvas-studio.md). "E2e in J1" is J1 split in two: its Canvas half is e2e/journeyPlaceInCanvas.e2e.test.ts, which places an activity made in the portal.

LTI-006 Must S3 Resource-link launch

onResourceLink reads contentId from the custom claim. It records or updates an LtiPlacement (platformId, contextId, resourceLinkId, contentId, lineItemUrl). Learners get the player. Authors get the player plus Rediger (edit, if owner or co-author) and Innsikt (insight) tabs.

  • Acceptance: An unknown or draft contentId gives a friendly error page, not a stack trace or a redirect loop.
  • Verify: Integration tests.

LTI-007 Should S3 Works after Canvas course copy

When a Canvas course is copied, its resource links keep custom.contentId. Instructors of the new course can launch, play and view insight for their own context. They can duplicate the activity into their own library, but cannot edit the original unless they are co-authors.

  • Verify: Integration test with two contexts and a shared contentId.

5. Requirements — Names and Roles, Dynamic Registration

LTI-008 Should S6 Participation denominators via NRPS

If the launch includes the Names and Roles claim, fetch the number of active learners in the context. Cache it for 1 hour, and use it as the denominator in insight (INS-001). Only counts are stored, never member names or e-mail addresses. This needs the developer-key scope https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-nrps/scope/contextmembership.readonly; with privacy_level anonymous, NRPS members carry no name, e-mail or picture in any case.

  • Verify: Integration test with a mock NRPS endpoint.
  • Amended (D-103, D-104, 2026-10-30): the count is fetched with ltijs's context.namesAndRoles during a launch, while the launch context lives, and cached under the platform-scoped context <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103), so courses with the same ID in two of HVL's Canvas instances never share a count. NRPS paging and role filtering on HVL's Canvas are on the students' Canvas acceptance checklist (verify) (D-101).

LTI-009 Could S6 LTI Dynamic Registration

Support Canvas's LTI Dynamic Registration through ltijs 7, so TeCopp can install the tool from one URL. The JSON developer key in docs/reference/canvas-lti13-developer-key.json remains the fallback.

  • Amended (D-101, 2026-10-30): S6 writes the design only. Trying it needs a Canvas administrator, and a dynamic registration must not be undone by the start-up sync of LTI_PLATFORMS (D-051). The build passes to HVL's bachelor students through the hand-off index (docs/handoff/README.md).

6. Requirements — xAPI-to-AGS grade bridge

LTI-010 Must S6 Capture xAPI in the player

The injected client script (packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.ts, H5P-009) subscribes with H5P.externalDispatcher.on('xAPI', …). It POSTs each statement to /api/h5p/xapi, batched every 2 s and flushed on pagehide, with the ltik or CSRF token. Failed posts are retried from an in-memory queue. They never block or slow down the activity.

  • Verify: Unit test of the batching queue; Playwright test that statements arrive.
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION: the bridge is plain JavaScript, packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.js, like the theme's other client scripts (there is no browser build for TypeScript). It runs once in the top player document (h5p/render/playerPage.ts: /h5p/play/:contentId in the portal, /lti/play in Canvas), not inside H5P's iframes (H5P-009 as amended), and queues each statement once, also one that H5P Core relays from its own iframe. The player page loads it only for a learner principal, so previews and teachers' plays are never sent. It makes a random attemptId for the root activity when the page loads and a new one after the root's scored completed or answered statement (probe P1 checks the real attempt boundaries). Credentials: in Canvas the ltik as Authorization: Bearer from the page's memory, in the portal the session cookie with the X-CSRF-Token header; never an ltik in the query. On pagehide it flushes with fetch and keepalive: true (not sendBeacon, which cannot carry those headers); nothing goes to browser storage. It adds no ✓/✗ text (UD-003 as amended).
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from "It POSTs each statement": the bridge sends only what the server stores (LTI-011 as amended): the page load's first root attempted, every answered and a root completed; never interacted, progressed, or a sub-content attempted or completed. Each statement is cut down to the fields the server reads, with no actor, question text, choices or feedback, and answers capped as DATA-012 (as amended) stores them. Each carries a statementId (crypto.randomUUID(), one per dispatched event) and an attemptId <viewId>:<n>: viewId is made once per page load, and n starts at 1 and goes up by one right after a root result with score.max above 0, so a retry, which H5P does not announce, is a new attempt at its next result. A batch names its content and the version the page was rendered with, and holds at most 50 items and 60 000 bytes of JSON, one request in flight; after a network error, a 5xx or a 429 it goes back to the head of the queue, after any other 4xx it is dropped. On pagehide everything not yet acknowledged, the request in flight included, goes in one keepalive request within the same limits, oldest first. The bridge is the last script in the player's global assets, never the editor's. It registers only in a document that is not one of Core's iframes, and at event time does nothing in a document that H5P marks as one (H5P.isFramed with H5P.externalEmbed === false), so each statement is queued once, by the parent document's bridge, also if H5P's iframe embedding is used.

LTI-011 Must S6 Validate and store statements

/api/h5p/xapi validates statements with a zod schema. It accepts only verbs it uses (answered, completed, attempted, interacted, progressed). It checks that the object belongs to content the principal may view, and that 0 ≤ score.raw ≤ score.max and 0 ≤ scaled ≤ 1. It rate-limits each learner and activity to 120 statements per minute. Then it stores the minimal fields defined in DATA-012 and drops the rest of the statement (including actor.name and actor.mbox).

  • Verify: Unit tests for the schema; integration test for rate limiting.
  • Amended (D-102, D-103, 2026-10-30): statements are stored only from a learner principal; anyone else's request stores nothing. In Canvas the content must also be the launched activity. The stored contextId is the platform-scoped <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103, null for a portal play), and the stored timestamp is when the server received the batch, not what the browser claims.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from "Then it stores the minimal fields": all five verbs are still accepted, but not every accepted statement is stored. Stored: a root attempted; a root answered that is a root result (LTI-012 as amended), and a sub-content answered with a subContentId; a root completed that is a root result and not a replay. Accepted and not stored: interacted, progressed, a sub-content attempted or completed, a sub-content statement without a subContentId, a root answered or completed whose category does not name the activity's main library (DATA-012 stores no category, and insight and the grade queue read every stored root answered and completed as a root result), and a replay: a root completed after no stored answered since its page load's previous root result (or since the load), whose raw score and maximum equal the learner's latest stored root result for the same content, context and version (CoursePresentation re-sends its result on resume; BranchingScenario is exempt). A statement is root when object.id is the content ID with no ?subContentId=, it has no h5p-subContentId extension and no contextActivities.parent (LTI-012 as amended). Each item is checked on its own: an invalid one, including one about another activity or whose scaled differs from raw / max by more than 0.0001, is discarded and counted in the log without its content, so it never blocks its batch. Besides a request without a valid session and CSRF token or ltik (401) and the rate limit (429), a whole batch is refused only when it is about an activity the principal may not view (403; in Canvas, any but the launched one), is over 64 KiB (413), or is no batch envelope, holds no item or over 50, or names a version above the activity's current one (400; a page keeps the version it was rendered with). The schema ignores actor (the learner comes only from the principal), and accepts a bare UUID as object.id, a missing context, a numeric response (stored as text) and a score without scaled when its maximum is 0. The item's statementId becomes the row's ID and is inserted once, so a batch sent twice (the pagehide flush, a request retried after a lost answer) stores nothing twice; the stored timestamp is the receive time plus the item's place in the batch in milliseconds, which keeps the batch's order. A 429 carries Retry-After, and nothing from that batch is stored. The answer is 202, with no detail per item. Not deviated: the five verbs, the score checks, the View check and the rate limit.
  • Amended (D-103, 2026-11-04, step 3 integration): a learner's batch from a Canvas launch whose context claim cannot form <platformId>:<contextId> (empty, over 255 characters, or with a line break) is answered 202 and stores nothing; the log counts it as noCourse. Such a play is neither a portal play (null) nor stored under a made-up course.

LTI-012 Must S6 Publish scores to the Canvas gradebook (AGS)

When a statement concerns the root content (no subContentId), has the verb completed or answered, and carries result.score, the server applies the activity's attempt policy:

Policy (author setting)Score sent to Canvas
best (default)highest scaled score so far, ×100
latestlatest scaled score, ×100
mastery100 once the scaled score ≥ threshold (default 0.8), otherwise latest ×100

The result goes to a durable GradeSyncJob queue. A worker calls context.grading.submitScore(lineItemUrl, { userId: sub, scoreGiven, scoreMaximum: 100, activityProgress: 'Completed', gradingProgress: 'FullyGraded', timestamp }) with exponential backoff (up to 8 attempts in 24 h). Jobs are idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId). If the line item no longer exists, the job is marked orphaned and is not retried. The developer key needs the scopes …/lti-ags/scope/score and …/lti-ags/scope/lineitem.readonly (the latter detects orphaned line items). ltijs's grading service works from a LaunchContext, which lives as long as the ltik (24 h); a job still failing after that window stores what it needs to request a new client-credentials token itself, or is marked failed for the author to retry from a fresh launch.

  • Acceptance: Learning never waits for grade sync. Authors see a per-activity sync status (counts of sent / pending / failed) and can retry failed jobs.
  • Verify: Integration tests with a mock AGS endpoint (success, 5xx retry, 404 orphaned, idempotency).
  • Amended (D-104, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION from the sentence "A worker calls context.grading.submitScore(…)" only: that method works only from a live ltik, which a background worker does not hold and must not store. AgsScoreClient (apps/server/src/grades/) requests the client-credentials token itself, from the first attempt, with a JWT assertion signed by the tool key ltijs stores for the platform, and posts the same score body to the line item's /scores URL. A job is written only for a learner in a Canvas launch, a root statement with completed or answered and a score, and a placement with a lineItemUrl; jobs stay idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId), so a later scored statement of the same attempt updates its job. The worker (one node at a time, about every 15 s) coalesces due jobs per (placement, learnerKey), applies the placement's attempt policy to that learner's attempt scores, sends one current score and settles the coalesced jobs together. Outcomes: 2xx succeeds; a 404 confirmed with a lineitem.readonly read marks the job orphaned, not retried; a 429, 5xx or network error is retried with exponential backoff and jitter, at most 8 attempts, the last within 24 h of the first, then failed; a 401 fetches a new token once; any other 4xx fails at once. The encrypted sub is removed 30 days after the job stops, whatever its outcome. Authors see sent, pending, failed and orphaned counts per placement on the activity page and in /app/play and retry failed jobs there. Not deviated: the score body, the policies, the retry limit, idempotency, orphaned and the developer key's scopes.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): SPEC-DEVIATION from the root as "no subContentId": no single test finds the root (that one takes DragText's context-less interacted inside a QuestionSet, and every child of content saved without subContentIds; H5P's own, no contextActivities.parent, takes InteractiveBook's chapter completed). A statement is root when object.id is the content ID with no ?subContentId=, it has no h5p-subContentId extension and no contextActivities.parent. A grade job is written only for a gradable root result: a root answered or completed whose category[0].id names the activity's main library (http://h5p.org/libraries/<machineName>-<major>.<minor>), with score.max above 0, and not a replay (LTI-011 as amended). scoreGiven is scaled × 100, never success. An attempt holds at most one result (LTI-010 as amended), so each job is one attempt; latest, and mastery below its threshold, send the score of the job whose result was stored last, by GradeSyncJob.resultAt (that result's stored timestamp), then by the attempt number n of <viewId>:<n>, then by the attempt ID as text (D-115's step-3 amendment). Which result each type sends is D-115's table: MultiChoice, Blanks and DragText an answered at every «Sjekk»; QuestionSet, Column, CoursePresentation and BranchingScenario a root completed; InteractiveBook at «Send inn rapport», which the player page offers a learner by setting H5P's reportingIsEnabled (Q18), and only a learner, never an author's preview; InteractiveVideo only with a submit screen its author added; BranchingScenario nothing gradable when its scoring is no-score; ImageHotspots no statement at all. An activity that sends no score never gets a job, and the Deep Linking picker says so for assignment_selection. Not deviated: the two verbs, result.score, the policies and their table.
  • Amended (D-104, two amendments of 2026-11-04, the step-3 security review): jobs are one per (placement, learnerKey) (idempotencyKey <placementId>:<learnerKey>), so one learner can never flood the queue; idempotency per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId) holds a fortiori. Each new gradable result updates the job, and a stopped job is reopened with a new window of 8 attempts in 24 h. The score is computed when it is sent, by the placement's policy over the learner's stored gradable results of that activity in that course, in D-115's result order. Claiming is fair (one place per learner a run); a job that takes in a result while its score is in flight is due again at the next run; each run first reopens a stopped job whose learner stored a newer result 15 to 1 minutes earlier (the reconcile pass). The line item URL must parse, use https in production, hold no credentials and have an origin in CANVAS_ORIGINS or among the platform's own (issuer, authorisation and token endpoints); it is checked when a launch records the placement (refused: stored as none, the link is ungraded) and again by the worker before any request (refused: the job fails as line-item-url). Not deviated: the score body, the policies, the retry limit, orphaned and the scopes.

LTI-013 Must S6 Score integrity is honest

H5P computes scores in the browser, so a determined student can forge them. The system therefore (a) labels AGS scores as formative in the line-item label suffix "(formativ)", (b) shows the formative notice (PROD-011), and (c) never presents these scores as exam evidence. Server checks in LTI-011 reduce accidental and casual manipulation. They are not claimed to prevent deliberate manipulation. On assignment_selection, Canvas uses the line-item label as the assignment name and overwrites the teacher's own name. Whether "(formativ)" belongs in the assignment name, or in the content item's description instead (with Canvas's preserveExistingAssignmentName extension), is a decision for HVL and ALU (verify).

  • Verify: Review item in the evaluator guide; unit test for the label suffix.
  • Amended (D-105, 2026-10-30): AGS_LABEL_MODE chooses: suffix (the default, as written above: the label is «Tittel (formativ)», the title cut when needed so the suffix is never lost) or preserve (the label is the title, the content item carries Canvas's preserveExistingAssignmentName, and its description says the score is formative). The suffix is «(formativ)» in every language. Q8 stays open; HVL and ALU's answer changes the setting, not the code, and a change affects new placements only. The insight views, the INS-009 CSV and the grade-sync status also say that the scores are formative, computed in the browser and not exam evidence. The unit test checks the label in both modes.

Spec 03 — HVL Visual Identity, Universal Design (WCAG 2.2 AA) and the Pre-Publish Validator

StatusApproved for build (v1.1, 2026-10-21: brand tokens and typefaces aligned with HVL's design manual)
Load in sessionsS4 (all); S6 (§6 conformance report, and UD-003; widened by D-101)
Owns requirement IDsUD-*
Code locationpackages/design-tokens/, packages/hvl-h5p-theme/, apps/web/src/app/, apps/web/src/components/, apps/web/src/features/, apps/web/src/styles/, apps/server/src/http/pages/ (server-rendered pages), apps/server/src/validation/, apps/server/a11y/ (the axe suite, UD-030), docs/accessibility/ (manual protocol and results, UD-031)

1. Legal and institutional baseline

  • Statutory floor: the Norwegian forskrift om universell utforming av IKT-løysingar requires the WCAG 2.1 success criteria it lists (based on EN 301 549). UUtilsynet supervises compliance. Public bodies must publish an accessibility statement (tilgjengelegheitserklæring) on uustatus.no.
  • Project target: WCAG 2.2 Level AA in full. This adds 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum).
  • HVL house rules (ALU's universal design guidance): line height ≥ 1.5; left-aligned, ragged-right text; no justified text; underline reserved for links; bold, not italics or capitals, for emphasis; no ALL-CAPS styling; links say where they go (external site, file type).

2. Design tokens (single source of truth)

Tokens live in packages/design-tokens/tokens.json. A build step generates CSS custom properties (used by the web app and by hvl-h5p-theme.css) and a Tailwind preset. No colour value may appear anywhere else in the codebase. A lint rule rejects hex literals outside the tokens package.

Brand basis. Brand colours come from HVL's design manual (Visuell identitet / Profilmanual, v2.0, February 2017, page 16), as documented in docs/reference/hvl-visual-identity.md ↗ (opens external site). HVL's own logo colours are Mørk blå 2 (PMS 3035 U, #004357) and Sjøgrønn (PMS 7710 U, #00AFBA). The manual was read through search extracts and independent transcriptions, not opened directly, so HVL (profil@hvl.no ↗ (opens external site)) must still confirm the values (verify). Colour names in brackets follow a transcription of the manual and are medium confidence; the manual itself calls the logo colours "sjøgrønn PMS 7710" and "mørkblå PMS 3035". Neutral tokens that are not HVL colours are labelled neutral below. (D-017)

Contrast ratios below were computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula. A unit test recomputes them on every build (UD-001). If HVL confirms different values, the test decides whether they may be used.

Corrections to the development plan. The plan's colours (#003D4C "deep fjord teal", #005F6B/#007681 "coastal teal", orange #FF9E1B) do not appear in any HVL source and were replaced by the manual's palette (D-017). The plan's single orange focus outline measured 2.07 : 1 on white, failing WCAG 1.4.11; it is replaced by the two-tone ring (D-007). The plan also overstated two feedback ratios (8.3 : 1 and 7.6 : 1; measured 7.21 : 1 and 7.08 : 1).

Logo. The official logo files (Norwegian, English, negative, square) are configured assets, not token-derived. They are never recoloured, cropped, animated or rewritten by the SVG sanitiser, and the institution name and logo are configuration, because HVL has applied for university status under the proposed name Universitetet på Vestlandet. The Norwegian (Nynorsk-name) logo serves both nn and nb.

3. Requirements — design system and theme

UD-001 Must S4 Tokens are the only source of colour, and contrast is tested

  • Acceptance: packages/design-tokens/test/contrast.test.ts declares every foreground and background pairing actually used and asserts ≥ 4.5 : 1 for text, ≥ 3 : 1 for large text and non-text UI. A Stylelint rule fails on hex, rgb() or hsl() literals outside packages/design-tokens/.
  • Verify: Unit test; lint in CI.

UD-002 Must S4 Typography and reading comfort

Typefaces follow the HVL design manual's office fonts (D-018): headings, UI controls and captions use Arial, "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, sans-serif (stand-in for NB Akademie Std); long-form body text uses Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif (stand-in for Lyon Text). If HVL confirms web-font licences for NB Akademie Std and Lyon Text, they may be self-hosted ahead of these stacks (DATA-011). Text uses font-size ≥ 1rem, line-height: 1.5 (1.55 inside H5P), text-align: left, and max-width: 70ch for paragraphs. text-transform: uppercase and text-align: justify are forbidden by a Stylelint rule. Underline is used only for links. All sizes are in rem or em. Layout survives 200 % text resize (1.4.4) and the text-spacing overrides of 1.4.12.

  • Verify: Stylelint rules; a Playwright test applies the 1.4.12 bookmarklet styles and checks for clipped text.

UD-003 Must S4 Feedback never relies on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1)

Every correct or incorrect state shows an icon and a text prefix as well as colour: ✓ Riktig: / ✗ Feil: (nn, nb), ✓ Correct: / ✗ Incorrect: (en). Prefixes are i18n keys (feedback.correctPrefix, feedback.incorrectPrefix). In H5P iframes, the theme adds them with CSS ::before content and the xAPI bridge script adds a visually hidden text node, so screen readers announce them consistently. Icons are aria-hidden="true".

  • Acceptance: Shown for MultiChoice, QuestionSet, Blanks, DragText and the answer states inside containers. Checked in greyscale screenshots.
  • Verify: Playwright tests per content type, asserting the text prefix in the accessibility tree.
  • Amended (D-072, 2026-10-24): the greyscale check is a manual step (docs/accessibility/manual-test-protocol.md §7); no automated test renders greyscale screenshots. The browser tests assert the drawn and the announced prefix.
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-10-30): the visually hidden text node comes from the theme's feedbackPrefixes.js (D-072 amendment (a)), never from the xAPI bridge. The bridge runs only in the top player document, for learners, and adds no text and no status to the page (LTI-010 as amended); a second prefix from it would be announced twice.

UD-004 Must S4 Visible, unobscured focus (2.4.7, 2.4.11, 1.4.11)

:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--hvl-focus-outer); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--hvl-focus-inner); }. This is applied in the web app and inside H5P iframes. Sticky headers set scroll-padding-top so a focused element is never hidden behind them.

  • Verify: Playwright test tabs through each route and asserts that the focused element is in the viewport and not covered (by elementFromPoint).

UD-005 Must S4 Target size ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (2.5.8) and no drag-only actions (2.5.7)

Every pointer target in the web app meets 2.5.8. Every drag interaction has a single-pointer alternative. In H5P, DragText's keyboard and click mode counts as that alternative. DragQuestion is excluded for this reason (H5P-002).

  • Verify: Playwright measurement script over interactive elements.

UD-006 Must S4 Fully keyboard operable

There is a skip link to <main>. Focus order is logical. There are no keyboard traps, including modal dialogs, which return focus on close. All custom widgets follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns.

  • Verify: Keyboard-only Playwright scripts for J1–J4; manual check (UD-031).

UD-007 Must S4 Honest links

External links get a visible icon plus visually hidden text "(opnar ekstern nettstad)" or the nb/en equivalent. File links show type and size ("PDF, 1.2 MB"). Link text never reads "klikk her" or "click here".

  • Verify: Component tests of <ExternalLink> and <FileLink>; validator rule V-LINK-TEXT.

UD-008 Must S4 Reflow, zoom and orientation

No horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px width (1.4.10), except for content that needs two dimensions, such as images with hotspots, which may pan. Works in both orientations.

  • Verify: Playwright at 320 × 640 for every route and content type.

UD-009 Must S4 Motion and media

Respect prefers-reduced-motion. No autoplay with sound. Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.

  • Verify: CSS review; Playwright with reduced motion emulated.

UD-010 Must S4 Language of page and parts

<html lang> follows the UI locale (nn, nb, en). Each H5P content item carries its own metadata.defaultLanguage, and the player sets lang on the content container.

  • Verify: Playwright assertions.

UD-011 Must S4 HVL theme inside H5P iframes

packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/hvl-h5p-theme.css is layered on top of H5P Core 1.28's Daylight theme. It overrides Daylight's custom properties where possible and selectors only where necessary. Every !important has a /* WHY: … */ comment naming the H5P selector it beats. The theme covers: tokens, typography (UD-002), feedback states (UD-003), focus (UD-004) and target size (UD-005).

  • Verify: Playwright and axe inside the iframe for one seed activity of each of the ten types (UD-030).

UD-012 Should S4 Windows high-contrast and forced colours

Under @media (forced-colors: active), focus rings and feedback borders use system colours (Highlight, CanvasText), and no information is lost.

  • Verify: Playwright with forced colours emulated.

UD-013 Must S4 Consistent help and accessible errors (3.2.6, 3.3.1, 3.3.3, 3.3.7)

A Hjelp link appears in the same place on every page. Form errors are listed in a summary at the top and linked to their fields with aria-describedby. Data the user has already entered is not asked for again (3.3.7). Login uses Feide or Canvas only, with no cognitive tests (3.3.8).

  • Verify: Component tests; axe.

4. Requirements — pre-publish validator

UD-020 Must S4 Validator engine

apps/server/src/validation/validateContent.ts exports a pure function:

/**
 * Inspects authored H5P parameters for universal design and pedagogical problems.
 * Pure and deterministic: no I/O, so it can run on save, on publish, and in tests.
 */
function validateContent(input: {
  mainLibrary: string;            // e.g. "H5P.InteractiveVideo 1.28"
  params: unknown;                // content.json
  metadata: H5PMetadata;          // h5p.json-style metadata
  locale: 'nn' | 'nb' | 'en';
}): Finding[];

interface Finding {
  ruleId: string;                 // e.g. "V-IMG-ALT"
  severity: 'error' | 'warning' | 'hint';
  requirement: string;            // spec ID, e.g. "UD-021"
  path: string;                   // JSON path into params, for "Go to field"
  message: string;                // localised, plain language, says what to do
}

The walker visits nested sub-content recursively (any object with library: "H5P.X a.b" and params). Each rule is a separate file under validation/rules/, ≤ 100 lines, with its own test. Pedagogical hint rules (PED-H*) are specified in 04 §5 and plug into the same engine.

UD-021 Must S4 Rule set (universal design)

V-IMG-ALTH5P.Image (and images inside ImageHotspots, CoursePresentation, InteractiveBook) have non-empty alt. The alt text must not look like a filename (/\.(jpe?g|png|gif|webp|svg)$/i, image1, bilde, IMG_1234), unless the image is marked decorative.error
V-IMG-ALT-LENGTHAlt text is longer than 250 characters. Suggest a long description in the text instead.warning
V-VID-CAPTIONSH5P.InteractiveVideo and H5P.Video have at least one text track (.vtt), or the source is a Panopto URL listed as captioned.error
V-VID-TRANSCRIPTThere is no transcript or text alternative linked.warning

  • Acceptance: Each rule has positive and negative fixtures under apps/server/test/fixtures/content/.
  • Verify: Unit tests [UD-021][V-IMG-ALT] … etc.

UD-022 Must S4 Acknowledgements are recorded

When an author publishes despite an error (PROD-003), a ValidationAcknowledgement (contentId, ruleId, path, reason, userId, at) is stored. Acknowledgements are listed in insight and in the portfolio export.

  • Verify: Integration test.

5. Requirements — verification

UD-030 Must S4 Automated accessibility tests

@axe-core/playwright runs with the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa, wcag22aa on every web route and inside the iframe of one seed activity per content type, in both light theme and forced-colours mode. CI fails on any violation with impact serious or critical. Lower-impact findings are listed in the report.

  • Verify: npm run test:a11y.

UD-031 Must S4 Manual assistive-technology protocol

Automated tools find only part of the barriers. docs/accessibility/manual-test-protocol.md (written in Session 4) defines scripted tasks for J1–J4. They are run with NVDA + Firefox, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari on iOS, keyboard only, and 400 % zoom. Results are recorded per release in docs/accessibility/results/.

  • Verify: Evaluator checks that a dated result file exists for the release.

6. Conformance documentation (Session 6)

UD-040 Must S6 WCAG conformance report

docs/accessibility/WCAG-CONFORMANCE-REPORT.md maps every WCAG 2.2 A/AA criterion to: Supports / Partially supports / Does not support / Not applicable, the evidence (test file, manual protocol result), and known H5P upstream limitations with links to the issues. It is the input HVL needs for its uustatus.no statement.

  • Verify: Evaluator review; the script npm run a11y:report regenerates the automated parts.

Spec 04 — Læringsdesign Studio, Patterns, Pedagogical Hints and the Pedagogisk Mappe Export

StatusApproved for build (v1.0, 2026-10-16)
Load in sessionsS5 (all). S4 loads §5 only, because the hint rules plug into the validator engine. S6 loads MAPPE-003 and MAPPE-004 (the mappe's real results and the PDF in the image; D-101).
Owns requirement IDsPED-*, MAPPE-*
Code locationapps/web/src/app/(portal)/laeringsdesign/, apps/web/src/app/(portal)/mappe/, apps/web/src/features/ (studio views), apps/server/src/learningDesign/ (content loader, patterns, metadata, planner, collaboration, mappe), apps/server/src/validation/rules/*Hint.ts, content/laeringsdesign/, content/mappe/ (amended in S5, D-084, D-089)

This is the part of HVL Interaktiv that teachers will judge it by. It turns research on asynchronous learning into concrete starting points. It nudges authors towards designs that work, and it gives them something useful back for their own career (the pedagogisk mappe).

1. Terminology is configuration, not code

HVL's model. HVL has developed a model for learning design, «HVL læringsdesign», and teaches it to course leaders in the Emnedesign module (UPED854). Its public description (Møgelvang & Isaksen 2025, MNT-konferansen; HVL Årsrapport 2024 p. 23) presents an alignment model built on three interdependent parts, kontekst, kunnskap and samskaping. It applies across levels, from the single læringsøkt (mikronivå) through the emne and studieprogram to the institution, and uses baklengs planlegging (backward planning) and meningsskapande samsvar (constructive alignment). See docs/reference/hvl-laeringsdesign-model.md ↗ (opens external site).

Where HVL Interaktiv sits. The activities live at the model's mikronivå: the work students do before, between and after a samling. HVL's course pages call this work forarbeid, mellomarbeid and etterarbeid (før- og etterarbeid; English "pre-, intermediate and post-work"). These are course-organisation terms, not named phases of the model (D-019).

Every label lives in content/laeringsdesign/phases.yaml, with nn/nb/en strings, and code refers only to stable keys. The proposed file is docs/reference/proposals/phases.yaml ↗ (opens external site); ALU must confirm the labels against the model document (hvl-modellen-for-laeringsdesign.pdf, not yet provided).

KeyLabel (nn / en)Meaning
forarbeidForarbeid / Pre-workAsynchronous pre-work before a seminar, lab or lecture
underveisMellomarbeid / Intermediate workAsynchronous active processing between sessions and during praksis. The key keeps its old name; the label is HVL's term. Not to be confused with undervegsvurdering (formative assessment)
etterarbeidEtterarbeid / Post-workConsolidation, retrieval practice and self-assessment (eigenvurdering)

The synchronous session in the middle (samling; online: nettsamling) is not authored in HVL Interaktiv. It appears on the studio page to show where the activities fit.

PED-001 Must S5 Phases and labels load from content files

  • Acceptance: Renaming a label in phases.yaml changes it everywhere with no code change. The build fails if a key is missing a locale.
  • Verify: Unit test of the loader; key-parity test (PROD-012).

PED-002 Must S5 Guide page content

The guide page contains, in this order:

  1. A 3-sentence introduction to why asynchronous work often fails (passive material, high cognitive load) and what helps.
  2. A short introduction to «HVL læringsdesign» (kontekst, kunnskap, samskaping; backward planning from the learning outcomes) and where the activities sit in it (mikronivå), citing Møgelvang & Isaksen (2025).
  3. Three mechanisms, each with a plain-language explanation, a "what this means for your activity" box and its references (§3): segment and retrieve; explain, don't just mark; practise judgement safely.
  4. The phase matrix (§3), with a filter by phase that also filters the pattern catalogue.
  5. The pattern catalogue (§4) as cards: name, phase, content type, one-line purpose, time to build.
  6. Links to ALU support (hvl.no/alu) and the Emnedesign module (UPED854).
  • Acceptance: Every factual claim has a reference. Page text lives in content/laeringsdesign/guide.{nn,nb,en}.mdx, so ALU can edit it without changing code.
  • Amended (D-083, 2026-10-28): SPEC-DEVIATION: the guide is CommonMark Markdown, guide.{nn,nb,en}.md, rendered from a closed node tree without HTML; the phase matrix and the catalogue are placed by marker lines.
  • Verify: Component test; ALU content review is recorded in PROGRESS.md.

PED-003 Must S5 Pattern filter

Authors filter patterns by phase, content type and estimated build time. The filter state is in the URL, so a filtered view can be shared.

  • Verify: Component test.

4. Pattern catalogue

A pattern is a YAML file in content/laeringsdesign/patterns/ (editable by ALU, PED-011) plus an H5P parameter skeleton in apps/server/src/patterns/skeletons/ (amended, D-084: the skeleton sits beside the YAML in content/laeringsdesign/patterns/<id>/, with text tokens and a pinned library version; guidance is marked ⟦…⟧ and flagged by V-PLACEHOLDER, D-086). Skeleton text is guidance written as placeholders, e.g. "Skriv eit spørsmål som får studenten til å bruke omgrepet, ikkje berre kjenne det att" ("Write a question that makes the student use the concept, not just recognise it").
