PED-010 Must S5 All nine patterns exist and instantiate

  • Acceptance: PROD-001 acceptance holds for every pattern. Each pattern YAML has: id, phase, contentType, purpose, whenToUse, whyItWorks (with reference keys), buildMinutes, skeleton, and nn/nb/en text.
  • Verify: Schema validation test for all YAML files; an integration test instantiates each skeleton.

PED-011 Must S5 Patterns are editable without code

Adding or editing a pattern needs only YAML, MDX and a JSON skeleton, with no TypeScript changes. content/laeringsdesign/README.md explains how, for non-developers.

  • Amended (D-083, D-084, 2026-10-28): YAML, Markdown and a JSON skeleton, all in content/laeringsdesign/patterns/<id>/.
  • Verify: A test adds a fixture pattern directory and asserts it appears.

5. Pedagogical hint rules

These plug into the validator engine (UD-020). Their severity is warning or hint only, so pedagogy is never blocked. Thresholds live in content/laeringsdesign/hint-thresholds.yaml.

Rule IDApplies toTriggers whenSeverityMessage intent
PED-H01InteractiveVideoThe video is longer than 15 min (when known from metadata)warningSplit into segments of 6–9 min (Guo et al. 2014).
PED-H02InteractiveVideoMore than 4 min of video without an interactionhintAdd a check every 2–3 min (Szpunar et al. 2013).
PED-H03InteractiveVideoThere is no summary or reflection task at the endhintEnd with a summary to consolidate.
PED-H04QuestionSetMore than 15 questionswarningPrefer several focused sets of about 10.
PED-H05MultiChoice, QuestionSet, SingleChoiceSetA wrong option has empty chosenFeedback (or equivalent)warningExplain why this option is wrong.
PED-H06BranchingScenarioFewer than 2 or more than 4 decision points on the main path; a choice has no feedback; or no retry pathwarningKeep cases to 3–4 decisions with explanations and a way back.
PED-H07AllenableRetry or enableSolutionsButton is turned offhintFormative activities work best with retry and solutions on.
PED-H08ColumnMore than 3 sub-activitieswarningSplit across pages to manage cognitive load.
PED-H09CoursePresentationA slide has more than 150 words of texthintOne concept per slide.
PED-H10InteractiveBookA chapter has more than 1 500 words and no interactionhintAdd a check per chapter.
PED-H11All with feedbackOverall feedback is only "Correct"/"Wrong" (or Riktig/Feil) without explanationhintSay why.

PED-020 Must S4 Implement the hint rules

  • Acceptance: Each rule is one file with positive and negative fixtures. Messages exist in nn, nb and en, and each names its reference.
  • Verify: Unit tests [PED-020][PED-H05] ….

6. Learning-design metadata and the alignment planner

PED-030 Must S5 Tag each activity

Authors can attach LearningDesignMetadata to an activity. It is optional while in draft and prompted (but not required) on publish.

FieldTypeNotes
phaseforarbeid | underveis | etterarbeid (labels Forarbeid, Mellomarbeid, Etterarbeid)From the pattern by default
courseCodestring, e.g. SYK110Free text. Prefilled from the LTI context label when available
learningOutcomeslist of { text, category }category follows the Norwegian qualifications framework (NKR): kunnskap, ferdigheiter, generell kompetanse
rationaletext ≤ 1 000 characters"Why this design for this outcome?" Used in the portfolio
estimatedStudentMinutesintegerShown to students before they start
learnerPurposetext ≤ 200 charactersAmended (D-087, 2026-10-28): the one-line "why this matters" of PED-032, shown to learners with the activity's language
patternIdpattern keyAmended (D-087): the pattern the activity was created from; kept on copies, never edited by hand
  • Verify: Component and API tests.

PED-031 Should S5 Constructive alignment planner

For one course, the planner shows a grid of learning outcomes × phases filled with the author's tagged activities. It highlights gaps, such as an outcome with no etterarbeid activity or a phase with no activities. It offers Create from pattern inside any empty cell.

  • Acceptance: The grid is an accessible HTML table with row and column headers, not only a visual canvas.
  • Verify: Component test; axe.

PED-032 Should S5 Students see time estimate and purpose

Before an activity starts, learners see the estimated time and a one-line "why this matters" text taken from the metadata. This helps them plan their study and self-regulate.

  • Verify: Component test.

7. Pedagogisk mappe export

HVL asks staff who apply for appointment, promotion (opprykk) or merittert undervisar status to document their teaching practice and their reasoning in a pedagogisk mappe. ALU states that the portfolio also covers work with educational technology, and the 2025 merit criteria name varierte læremidler (sub-criterion 2.3). This feature produces a ready-to-edit draft from work the teacher has already done. The evidence behind this section is in docs/reference/hvl-pedagogisk-mappe-criteria.md ↗ (opens external site) (D-020).

MAPPE-001 Should S5 Select and export

On /mappe, an author selects activities, filtered by course, phase or date. The author exports Markdown (for editing) and PDF (for submission).

  • Verify: Integration test produces both files from fixtures.

MAPPE-002 Should S5 Dossier structure

Headings come from content/mappe/template.{nn,nb,en}.md and criterion texts from content/mappe/criteria.{nn,nb,en}.yaml, keyed by criteria set (default hvl-merittering-2025). HVL revises the merit criteria for every call (next call 2027), so a new set is a content change only. The proposed Nynorsk template is docs/reference/proposals/mappe-template.nn.md ↗ (opens external site). The default structure follows HVL's three-part merit portfolio:

  1. Reader's guide: a table mapping each 2025 criterion (1.1–1.4, 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.3) to the chapter and attachment that address it, as in published HVL portfolios.
  2. Del 1 – Samanhengande framstilling: chapters ordered by the criteria, each with a pre-filled writing prompt. The teacher's learning-design approach opens the text. For each selected activity (under 2.3, varierte læremidler): title, content type, phase, course, learning outcomes, didactic rationale, universal design status (validator result plus any acknowledgements with reasons), a link, and anonymised aggregates (participants, completion rate, median attempts, change between first and last attempts). A live word count shows Del 1 against the limit (default 7 500 words, references excluded).
  3. Del 2 – Pedagogisk CV: entries HVL Interaktiv can document (digital learning resources developed, with dates), to paste into HVL's own CV template.
  4. Del 3 – Suggested attachments (default limit 11, including the manager's letter, which the tool never produces): documentation of developed learning resources, and an anonymised summary of student feedback.
  5. References, pre-filled from the patterns' research keys (§3).

The word limit, attachment limit and criteria set are content values marked (verify) until ALU confirms them. A promotion mode (opprykk, rules in force from 13 June 2025) uses the same three parts; its Del 1 headings wait for ALU.

  • Acceptance: Switching the criteria set changes every criterion text and the reader's guide with no code change. The word count excludes the references and the reader's guide.
  • Verify: Integration test with two fixture criteria sets.

MAPPE-003 Must S5 Privacy in the export

Aggregates apply the same minimum group size as insight (INS-006, default k = 5). No learner identifiers, free-text answers or individual scores ever appear. The export is generated on demand and not stored on the server.

  • Verify: A test with a 4-learner fixture asserts suppression.
  • Amended (D-095, 2026-11-04, S6 step 4): the results come from the stored learning data, read on demand and written nowhere. Because the mappe adds up what insight shows one course, version and period at a time, only groups of at least k learners per course (or the portal), content version and semester count, and a completion rate or median is hidden when it would let a count insight hides be worked out.

MAPPE-004 Should S5 Accessible PDF

The PDF is rendered from the same semantic HTML template with headless Chromium and tagged-PDF output enabled. It has document language, a title, a heading outline and real text, never images of text.

  • Verify: The test checks the PDF has a structure tree and outline (e.g. with pdfjs-dist); a manual check with PAC or a screen reader is recorded in the accessibility results.

Spec 05 — Teacher Insight (Learning Analytics) and Data Protection

StatusApproved for build (v1.0, 2026-10-16)
Load in sessionsS1: §2 (DATA-001, DATA-002, DATA-009), §4, §5 · S4: DATA-006, DATA-011 · S6: all
Owns requirement IDsINS-*, DATA-*
Code locationapps/server/src/insight/, apps/server/src/privacy/, apps/server/src/web/, apps/server/src/http/h5pPageCsp.ts, apps/web/src/features/ (the Innsikt tab on the activity page /aktivitet/[id] and in the Canvas view /app/play; there is no /innsikt page) (amended in S6, D-101, D-106)

Insight exists for one purpose: to help a teacher decide what to do in the next synchronous session (Just-in-Time Teaching). It is not for surveilling or ranking individual students. Every design choice below follows from that purpose.

1. Teacher insight ("Innsikt")

The default view is Før samlinga ("before the session"): results since a chosen date (default 7 days ago), for one activity, in one Canvas context (or all portal users for that activity).

  • Amended (D-101, D-103, D-106, 2026-10-30): insight is an Innsikt tab, on the activity page and in the Canvas view /app/play, never a page of its own, and it shows one activity, one content version (the current one by default, PROD-013) and one context at a time: a Canvas context the activity is placed in, or the portal's plays. There is no view across contexts. A Canvas context is stored and compared as <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103), so courses from two of HVL's Canvas instances never merge. SPEC-DEVIATION D-106: the period is chosen from fixed values, the last 7 (the default), 14 or 30 days or since the semester started, each starting at midnight Oslo time, not from any date, so that two overlapping views cannot isolate one learner. The semester starts on 1 January or 1 August until HVL gives its semester dates.
  • Amended (D-106, 2026-11-04, the step-4 privacy review): SPEC-DEVIATION D-106: every period ends at the latest midnight in Oslo, so a view holds the data up to and including yesterday («Tal til og med i går») and two views of the same period on the same day are the same whatever is stored in between; the semester view on 1 January or 1 August is the semester that has just ended. No period crosses 1 August, when the pseudonym secret changes (DATA-002): a 7-, 14- or 30-day view whose days would reach back before 1 August starts on 1 August instead, and the tab says so; each view reads only rows of its own academic year's key (academicYear, D-107). Canvas's Student View test student is in no view (D-102's amendment of 2026-11-04, DATA-012). What remains (views on consecutive days, nested periods) is in the DPIA input's residuals R3 and R8 (DATA-005).

INS-001 Must S6 Participation overview

Shows: learners who started, learners who completed, completion rate (denominator from NRPS when available, LTI-008, otherwise "of those who started"), median time on task, and median number of attempts.

  • Acceptance: Numbers match a hand-calculated fixture of 30 synthetic learners.
  • Verify: Unit tests of the aggregation queries.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): what each number reads, since H5P marks no attempts. A learner has started with any stored statement for the activity (InteractiveBook without a cover counts at load, Column from its first answer; no statement is made up). Completed is a stored root result (LTI-012 as amended), and attempts are the stored root results. Time on task comes from the stored timestamps of each page load, from its first to its last stored statement, never from durationMs. Where a type cannot send a root result, completed, the completion rate and attempts are shown as not available, never as 0; ImageHotspots sends no statement at all, and its tab says that it sends no learning data. Residuals, named in the DPIA input and the students' checklist: attempts count each Column re-check and each CoursePresentation summary slide reached after new answers; a learner who opens a Column and never checks is not counted as started; and reading before the first stored statement and time after the last are not counted.

INS-002 Must S6 Item difficulty

For each question (sub-content) the view shows: % correct on the first attempt, % correct on the latest attempt, and the number of learners. Items are sorted from hardest first. The question text is shown next to each item so the teacher does not need to open the editor.

  • Verify: Unit tests.

INS-003 Must S6 Misconceptions

For choice questions, it shows how answers are distributed across options, with the teacher's own feedback text for each wrong option next to it. For Blanks and DragText, it shows the most frequent wrong answers per gap, normalised (trimmed, case-folded) and limited to the top 5. A free-text answer is displayed only if at least k distinct learners gave it (INS-006), so a rare and identifiable answer is never shown. A "Ta opp i samlinga" ("bring to seminar") button adds the item to a shortlist that can be printed or projected.

  • Verify: Unit tests, including the k rule for free text.
  • Amended (D-106, 2026-11-04): SPEC-DEVIATION for older content versions only: the distributions are shown for the current version, whose options and gaps the stored parameters describe; for an older version the tab says so. A single-answer question's right options and wrong options (with «no answer») are suppressed as two groups, since INS-002's share gives the right options' total.

INS-004 Should S6 Branching paths

For BranchingScenario, the view shows the distribution of choices at each decision node and how many learners used a retry path.

  • Verify: Unit tests.
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): not built in S6. BranchingScenario's choices are in no statement H5P dispatches (its choice interacted carries no response), only in its getXAPIData() and saved state, and the last choice before an end screen sends nothing at all. Building it needs statements that the bridge makes itself, a SPEC-DEVIATION from LTI-010 and LTI-011 that needs its own decision, after a probe shows that retried choices are kept. It passes to HVL's bachelor students through the hand-off index (D-101).

INS-005 Could S6 Video engagement

For InteractiveVideo, it shows the share of learners who answered each embedded interaction. This serves as a proxy for how far they watched. The spike in Session 6 decides whether H5P's progressed statements are reliable enough for a drop-off curve.

  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): the spike's answer: InteractiveVideo sends no progressed statement at all, so there is no drop-off curve, and the bridge sends no progressed from any type (LTI-010 as amended). The measure is the share of learners who answered each interaction, read from the stored answered statements by subContentId, with INS-006's suppression.

INS-006 Must S6 Minimum group size and no individual view

Any cell, bar or list item that represents fewer than k = 5 distinct learners is shown as "< 5" and its value is suppressed. k is configurable, with a minimum of 3. If suppression of one cell would let a hidden value be worked out from the totals, the next-smallest cell is suppressed too. The insight API has no endpoint that returns per-learner rows.

  • Amended (D-106, 2026-10-30): applied as written: a value about fewer than k learners is shown as «< k» and the API answer carries no value for it. The mappe's two-sided rule (D-095, a rate of 0 % or 100 % hidden) is not added for insight. The grade-sync status counts are exempt (§3), and the property tests cover the insight endpoints and the CSV.
  • Amended (D-106, 2026-11-04): SPEC-DEVIATION: a count of 0 is shown, since it is about no learner; it is hidden only as a complement or in a hidden group. "The next-smallest cell" becomes the rule that leaves no hidden value to work out: in a group with a shown total, when one cell is hidden (or several, all 1 or all k − 1), every shown 0 is hidden, or, without a 0, the smallest shown count and each next one less than k above it. When the learners who started are hidden, every question cell is. An exhaustive test checks every group of two to five cells for k = 3–6.
  • Acceptance: Property-based test: for random datasets, no API response contains a group smaller than k.
  • Verify: fast-check property test [INS-006] ….

INS-007 Must S6 Who can see insight

Owners and co-authors of an activity can see its insight. In LTI mode, authors of the launch context see results for that context only. Admins can see it only through an audited support action. Each view writes an audit event (DATA-007).

  • Verify: Permission tests.
  • Amended (D-106, 2026-10-30): for a context: the activity's owner and co-authors, and an LTI author whose launch comes from that context, whether or not they own the activity (after a course copy, LTI-007). In /app/play the context is the launch's and cannot be changed. The audited support action for admins is not built in S6, so admins see no insight. A view writes insight.view and a CSV download insight.export, with details limited to the view, the period, the context and the content version: no learner key, count or answer.

INS-008 Must S6 Accessible charts

Each chart has a visible data table alternative and a text summary (e.g. "Question 2: 38 % correct on first attempt; most common wrong answer: B"). Charts use patterns or labels as well as colour (UD-003) and meet non-text contrast requirements.

  • Verify: axe; component tests.

INS-009 Should S6 Export aggregated CSV

Insight can be exported as CSV, with the same suppression (INS-006) applied.

  • Verify: Unit test.

INS-010 Should S6 Validator status in insight

Insight shows the activity's current validator findings and acknowledgements (UD-022), so accessibility debt stays visible.

2. Data protection requirements

HVL is the data controller. Processing of learner data for teaching rests on GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) (task in the public interest: higher education). HVL's data protection officer must confirm this during the DPIA (DATA-005).

DATA-001 Must S1 Data inventory

docs/privacy/DATA-INVENTORY.md lists every stored field: purpose, category, legal basis, retention period and location. It must match the Prisma schema (apps/server/prisma/schema/). A CI script fails if a Prisma model or field is missing from the inventory.

  • Verify: npm run privacy:inventory-check.

DATA-002 Must S1 Pseudonymous learners

learnerKey = HMAC-SHA256(PSEUDONYM_SECRET[academicYear], source), where source is feide|<feide-id> or lti|<iss>|<sub>. The secret is held in the secret store, rotated per academic year, and destroyed when that year's data is purged. Learner rows store no names, e-mail addresses, Feide IDs, national ID numbers or raw LTI sub values. The one exception is the encrypted ltiSub in GradeSyncJob, which AGS needs; it is deleted 30 days after a successful sync.

  • Verify: Unit tests for key derivation; schema test asserting no PII columns on learner tables.
  • Amended (D-104, 2026-10-30): the encrypted ltiSub is deleted 30 days after the job stops, whether it succeeded, failed or was orphaned, so a job that never succeeds keeps it no longer.

DATA-003 Must S6 Annual retention purge

A scheduled job runs on a configured date (default 15 August), for the academic year that has ended. It deletes XapiStatement, H5PUserData, GradeSyncJob and learner Identity rows older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days, then learner User rows that have no Identity left (D-034), and destroys that year's pseudonym secret. Only aggregate snapshots that already satisfy k-suppression are kept, for the pedagogisk mappe.

  • Acceptance: A dry-run mode reports counts without deleting. Each run writes an audit event with the counts.
  • Verify: Integration test with time travel.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION in three points. (1) The default date: the job runs by default on 31 August, Oslo time, for the academic year that ended on 31 July, because the boundary plus 30 days ends on 30 August; the date is configurable, but not to a day before 31 August, so the 30 days always pass first. (2) Which rows go: XapiStatement, H5PUserData and GradeSyncJob store an academicYear, set, when a row is written, to the year of the secret that made its learnerKey (DATA-012 as amended, §4), and the purge deletes the ended year's rows by that stored year, in batched transactions, then the learner Identity rows created before that year ended, then learner User rows left without an Identity (D-034); not every row "older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days", which, read on the run date, would also take the new year's first 30 days. The 30 days after the boundary are kept as the time before the purge may run. (3) Who destroys the secret: not the job. The secrets are an environment value (PSEUDONYM_SECRETS) that the server cannot destroy, so HVL operations remove the year's secret in a runbook step after the real run, and DATA-002's rule holds through that step; at start-up the server names, by year only, any secret still configured for a purged year, so a forgotten step shows. Before anything is deleted, the year's InsightSnapshot rows are written per activity, context (D-103) and content version, already suppressed with the configured k (D-106); only they outlive the purge, and the values the mappe reads from them follow D-095's rules. The dry run (counts per table, nothing deleted) and the audit event of every run are as written. A leased job runs the purge on one node, and a CLI runs the same code by hand.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-11-04, the purge built): PURGE_RUN_DATE names a day from 31 August to 31 December (a day in spring would keep a year's rows for most of another year); the job checks hourly and runs once the date is reached and no completed run for the ended year is audited. A run deletes every stored year before the current academic year, so a year a missed run left behind goes too. A snapshot holds the mappe's figures for the year (MAPPE-002) under the mappe's group rules. The runbook is docs/ops/yearly-purge.md.

DATA-004 Must S6 EEA residency and encryption

PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible storage are hosted in Norway or the EEA. All traffic uses TLS 1.2 or later. Storage is encrypted at rest. Backups are encrypted and retained for 30 days.

  • Verify: Deployment checklist (docs/ops/).
  • Amended (D-109, 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05): in production the server refuses to start with a DATABASE_URL whose sslmode is not require, verify-ca or verify-full, a redis:// REDIS_URL, an http: S3_ENDPOINT, either of the AWS SDK's own endpoint variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL), or file storage outside the EEA allow-list in apps/server/src/config/storageResidency.ts. These checks catch a wrong setting, not where a server stands: the EEA location, encryption at rest and backups stay the deployment checklist's evidence (Q5), and the start-up log names the database and Redis hosts and the storage region for it (docs/ops/database-roles.md).

DATA-005 Must S6 DPIA input

docs/privacy/DPIA-INPUT.md describes processing operations, data flows (with a diagram), risks and mitigations. It cross-references this spec, so HVL's data protection officer can complete the formal DPIA. It records the Canvas developer key's privacy_level (anonymous) and its custom fields: in LTI 1.3, custom-field substitutions such as $Canvas.user.loginId release data whatever the privacy level, so adding one requires a DPIA update.

  • Verify: Evaluator review.

DATA-006 Must S4 Transparency for students

The player footer links to a short privacy notice in nn, nb and en. It says what is stored, why, for how long, and who can see what. In particular, teachers see only groups of at least k learners.

  • Verify: Component test; content review.

DATA-007 Must S6 Audit log

AuditEvent(at, actorUserId, action, targetType, targetId, details jsonb) records: insight views, exports, library installs and updates, permission changes, data-subject actions and purge runs. The audit log itself has no free-text personal data. It is kept for 2 years.

  • Verify: Integration tests assert events for each action.
  • Amended (D-107, D-108, D-109, 2026-11-04): a purge run writes purge.run with the academic year as its target; a data-subject request writes dataSubject.export or dataSubject.erase with a random request ID as its target, never an identifier, key or hash; both hold counts, years and fixed words only. The app's database role may add and read audit rows but never change or delete them (D-109), so the deletion after 2 years, which is not built yet, needs its own amendment and grant (DPIA input R27).

DATA-008 Must S6 Data-subject requests

An admin-only tool takes a Feide ID or an (iss, sub) pair. It derives the learner keys for the retained academic years, then exports (JSON) or deletes that learner's data. Every use is audited.

  • Verify: Integration test of export and erasure.
  • Amended (D-108, 2026-10-30, and its amendments of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05): the tool is a CLI on the server host, with no web page or HTTP route, that HVL operations run on the instruction of HVL's data protection officer, naming an HVL admin as the operator. The identifiers come on standard input, never in the arguments; the CLI derives the learnerKey for every year in PSEUDONYM_SECRETS and the identity hash under every identity key; erase is a dry run unless it is given --confirm; learner H5P state is deleted through our own storage, because Lumi 10.0.4's deleteAllContentUserDataByUser deletes the acting user's state. The audit target is a random request ID. The export also lists the person's portal login events (AuthAuditEvent), which the erasure keeps for their 2 years; a staff member's own data and Canvas's own data are outside the tool (Q6). Runbook: docs/ops/data-subject-requests.md.

DATA-009 Must S1 Logs contain no personal data

The logger (pino) redacts authorization, cookie, ltik, id_token, email, name, sub, feide*, and any key named response (answer content). Application logs are kept for 30 days.

  • Verify: Unit test of redaction paths (NFR-006).

DATA-010 Must S6 Least-privilege access to infrastructure

Separate database roles are used for the app, for migrations and for read-only analytics. Production data is never copied to development; test data is synthetic.

  • Verify: Ops checklist; migration role used only in CI/CD.
  • Amended (D-109, 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05): the roles are hvli_migrator (owns the schema; used only in the deployment's migrate step, which runs views-down, prisma migrate deploy and grants), hvli_app (rows only; on the audit tables add and read only) and hvli_analytics, narrowed from "read-only analytics": it reads no table, only views in schema analytics of aggregates already suppressed below k (today analytics.insight_snapshot), and its sessions start read-only. Scripts in apps/server/prisma/roles/, runbook docs/ops/database-roles.md, and HVL's checklist in the DPIA input §11 (DATA-005).

DATA-011 Must S4 No third-party tracking or CDNs

Student-facing pages load no third-party scripts, fonts, analytics or embeds other than ones the author has explicitly added (e.g. a Panopto video). Fonts are self-hosted. A Content-Security-Policy enforces this.

  • Verify: Playwright test records all network requests on a seed activity and asserts first-party only.

DATA-012 Must S6 Minimal xAPI storage

For each statement, store only: contentId, subContentId?, contentVersion, contextId?, learnerKey, verb, scoreRaw?, scoreMax?, scaled?, success?, completion?, response? (choice indices or short gap text), durationMs?, attemptId, timestamp. Everything else is dropped, including actor names, mailboxes and extensions.

  • Verify: Unit test of the mapper.
  • Amended (D-102, D-103, 2026-10-30): contextId holds the platform-scoped <platformId>:<contextId> (null for a portal play; one module builds and parses it), attemptId is made by the xAPI bridge, since H5P sends none, and timestamp is when the server received the batch. Only learner principals' statements are stored.
  • Amended (D-107, 2026-10-30): SPEC-DEVIATION: XapiStatement also stores academicYear, a field outside the list above, set when the row is written. It holds no statement data, only the academic year of the secret behind the row's learnerKey, which the key cannot reveal and a timestamp can misstate (a portal session made before 1 August can keep its learnerKey for up to 12 hours after it, D-057); the annual purge (DATA-003 as amended) deletes by it. H5PUserData and GradeSyncJob store it too (§4).
  • Amended (D-115, 2026-10-30, probe P1): the field list is unchanged; what fills it is made exact. Which statements become rows is LTI-011 as amended: a root attempted, a root answered or completed only as a root result (LTI-012 as amended; a root completed only when it is not a replay), and a sub-content answered with a subContentId. Every stored root answered and completed is therefore a root result, which INS-001 counts without a category field. A row's ID is the bridge's statementId, inserted once, so a batch sent twice stores nothing twice; a content hash is never an identity, because identical statements are normal. timestamp is the receive time plus the item's place in its batch in milliseconds, so the batch's order survives; the browser's clock is never read. attemptId is <viewId>:<n> (LTI-010 as amended). subContentId comes from the h5p-subContentId extension, else from object.id. response is kept only for the interaction types choice and fill-in: each gap (between [,]) is cut to 100 characters, enough to group the answers k learners share, and a response still over 1 000 characters is not stored, since a shortened list would shift its gaps; a numeric response is stored as text. durationMs is parsed from result.duration (null when absent, unreadable or over 24 hours), and no insight reads it, because H5P's durations mean different things by type.
  • Amended (D-102, 2026-11-04, the step-4 privacy review): SPEC-DEVIATION: XapiStatement also stores testUser, true for a statement of Canvas's Student View test student (the LTI TestUser role), set from the launch, never from the statement; database default false. Like academicYear it holds no statement data. Insight, the mappe and the yearly purge's snapshots never read a flagged row, so k − 1 test students cannot make a group of k around one real learner; the grade worker does read them, so a teacher can test the score passback.

3. What teachers can and cannot see (summary for privacy notices and evaluators)

Teachers can seeTeachers cannot see
How many learners started or completed (groups ≥ k)Which named student did what (individual grades are only in Canvas, through AGS)
% correct per question, distribution of answers (groups ≥ k)Rare free-text answers given by fewer than k learners
Their own feedback texts next to the resultsData from other courses' contexts
Grade-sync status countsRaw xAPI statements
  • Amended (D-104, D-106, 2026-11-04): the grade-sync status counts are per course and not k-suppressed, with one count per learner and placement since D-104's amendment, so a count can be about one learner. "Data from other courses' contexts" means that no view mixes courses: in Canvas a teacher sees the launch's course only, while an activity's owner and co-authors see insight and these counts for each course the activity is placed in, one course at a time, also a colleague's course. Both are residuals for HVL's data protection officer (DPIA input R1, R2; Q22). Canvas's Student View test student is in none of insight's learner numbers (DATA-012 as amended, D-102); its score is sent, so its grade job is in the grade-sync counts.

4. Consolidated logical data model

Session 1 turns this into the Prisma schema in apps/server/prisma/schema/*.prisma. PII marks fields that are personal data; P marks pseudonymous fields.

EntityOwner specNotable fields
User, Identity02displayName for staff only (PII; email is kept null since S5, D-090; from S5 the name is shown to HVL colleagues in co-author search, bank listings and copy attribution, D-090–D-092); coAuthorSearchableAt (staff, D-090); subjectHash (P)
H5PContent, H5PContentFile, ContentCollaborator, LibraryAuditEvent01ownerUserId; sourceAuthorUserId on copies (S5, D-092)
H5PUserData01learnerKey (P), data (P); academicYear, as on XapiStatement (D-107)
LtiPlatform, LtiIdToken, LtiNonce, LtiAccessToken, LtiPlacement02ID tokens (PII, 24 h)
GradeSyncJob02ltiSub (PII, encrypted, 30 days after success; amended, D-104: 30 days after the job stops, whatever its outcome); academicYear, as on XapiStatement (D-107)
LearningDesignMetadata, LearningOutcome04none
ValidationAcknowledgement03userId (author)
XapiStatement05learnerKey (P), response (P); contextId as <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103); academicYear, the year of the secret behind learnerKey, by which the yearly purge deletes (SPEC-DEVIATION from DATA-012, D-107); testUser, true for Canvas's Student View test student, whose rows no aggregate reads (SPEC-DEVIATION from DATA-012, D-102, amended 2026-11-04)
InsightSnapshot05aggregates only, already k-suppressed; contextId as <platformId>:<contextId> (D-103); contentVersion (D-107: the purge writes one snapshot per activity, context and content version)
AuditEvent05actorUserId; for a data-subject request targetId is a random request ID, never an identifier (D-108, amended 2026-11-04)

5. Pseudonymisation sequence (for evaluators)

Feide login / LTI launch
   │  raw id (feide id or iss+sub) — exists only in memory during the request
   ▼
learnerKey = HMAC_SHA256(secret[yyyy], "lti|" + iss + "|" + sub)
   │
   ├─► H5PUserData.learnerKey     (resume state)
   ├─► XapiStatement.learnerKey   (insight aggregates, k ≥ 5)
   └─► GradeSyncJob.ltiSub (encrypted) only while a Canvas grade is pending
At the yearly purge: rows deleted; after the real run, operations destroy secret[yyyy] (runbook, D-107)
   → any remaining aggregate can no longer be linked to anyone.

Documentation Standard

StatusMandatory from Session 1 (v1.0, 2026-10-16)
Owns requirement IDsDOC-*
Applies toEvery file in apps/, packages/, tools/ and content/

Why this standard exists

HVL Interaktiv will be reviewed by people who did not write it: ALU learning designers, TeCopp administrators, security and privacy reviewers, and external evaluators. Most will not know H5P, LTI or Norwegian higher-education terms. They should be able to open any file and answer these five questions within a minute:

  1. What does this file do?
  2. Why does it exist? Which requirement in docs/specs/ does it fulfil?
  3. What must never go wrong here? (invariants, security or privacy assumptions)
  4. How do I know it works? Which tests prove it?
  5. What does it connect to? (callers and collaborators)

The rules below make those answers appear in predictable places. Wherever possible a tool checks them, so the documentation cannot quietly rot.

The documentation layers

LayerWhereAnswersRule
1. Repository orientationREADME.md, docs/GLOSSARY.md, docs/DECISIONS.md, PROGRESS.md, docs/EVALUATOR-GUIDE.mdWhat is this project, what state is it in, what was decided and why?—
2. Specificationsdocs/specs/*.mdWhat must the system do, and how will we know?Requirement IDs
3. Package READMEsapps/*/README.md, packages/*/README.mdHow is this package structured, and how do its main flows work?DOC-005
4. Module headersTop of every source fileWhat / why / spec / invariants / tests / collaboratorsDOC-001
5. API docs (TSDoc)Every exported symbolHow to call it correctlyDOC-002
6. Rationale commentsInline, taggedWhy this non-obvious line is the way it isDOC-003
7. Tests*.test.ts, e2e/*.spec.tsExecutable proof, named by requirementDOC-006
8. Traceabilitydocs/TRACEABILITY.md (generated)Requirement → code → test, at a glanceDOC-004

Rules

DOC-001 Must S1 Every source file starts with a module header

Use exactly these labels. Omit a label only when it truly does not apply, never "TODO".

/**
 * SvgSanitizer — removes executable content from SVG files that authors upload.
 *
 * Why: @lumieducation/h5p-server up to and including 10.0.4 is affected by
 *      CVE-2025-7062 (stored XSS through uploaded files) and no fixed release
 *      exists, so HVL Interaktiv sanitises every SVG itself (decision D-003).
 * Spec: SEC-001
 * Invariants:
 *   - Output never contains <script>, on* attributes, <foreignObject>,
 *     <!DOCTYPE> or <!ENTITY>.
 *   - Never throws on malformed input; returns NotSanitized and the file is rejected.
 * Collaborators: registered in H5pEditorFactory via `fileSanitizers`.
 * Tests: apps/server/test/security/SvgSanitizer.test.ts
 */

Checked by: tools/doc-lint (added in Session 1). It fails if a file under apps/, packages/ or tools/ lacks a header, or if a Spec: ID does not exist in docs/specs/. React components and CSS files use the same header in their language's comment syntax.

DOC-002 Must S1 Every exported symbol has TSDoc

Each exported function, class, method, type and constant has a one-sentence summary. Add @param and @returns where they add meaning beyond the type. Use @throws for every error a caller must handle. Add an @example for anything with more than two parameters or a non-obvious call order. Add @spec <ID> when the symbol directly implements a requirement.

/**
 * Derives the learner pseudonym for the academic year that contains `at`.
 * @param source - Feide or LTI identity of the learner.
 * @param secrets - Per-year secrets from PSEUDONYM_SECRETS.
 * @param at - The moment of the event; defaults to now.
 * @returns The 43-character base64url `learnerKey`.
 * @throws MissingPseudonymSecretError when the year has no secret.
 */
export function deriveLearnerKey(source: LearnerSource, secrets: PseudonymSecrets, at: Date = new Date()): string { … }

(From apps/server/src/privacy/deriveLearnerKey.ts.)

Checked by: eslint-plugin-jsdoc (require-jsdoc for exported functions, classes, interfaces, types and enums; require-param for exported functions; check-tag-names with spec as a defined tag) and doc-lint's export-docs check (TSDoc on every exported declaration, known @spec IDs). Class methods that implement a documented interface, such as Lumi's storage interfaces, may rely on that interface's documentation. Browsable API docs (TypeDoc) are added with the HTTP API in S2 (D-031).

DOC-003 Must S1 Explain non-obvious code with tagged rationale comments

Comments explain why, never restate what. Use one of these tags so reviewers can grep for them:

TagUse whenMust contain
WHY:The obvious alternative is wrong for a reasonThe reason
SECURITY:The line defends against a threatThe threat and how this line mitigates it
PRIVACY:The line limits personal dataWhich data, and which DATA-* requirement
A11Y:The line exists for accessibilityThe WCAG criterion or user need
PEDAGOGY:A threshold or default comes from learning researchThe reference key from spec 04 §3
UPSTREAM:A workaround for a bug in H5P, Lumi, ltijs or CanvasLink to the upstream issue, and when it can be removed
SPEC-DEVIATION:The code knowingly differs from a specThe decision ID in DECISIONS.md
// SECURITY: the ltik grants access to a learner's launch for 24 h. Strip it from the URL
// immediately so it cannot leak through Referer headers, history or screenshots (LTI-003).
window.history.replaceState(null, '', withoutLtik(window.location.href));

Checked by: review (see the PR template). grep -rn "SECURITY:" apps/ must give an evaluator a complete tour of the security-relevant lines.

DOC-004 Must S1 Requirement IDs connect spec, code and tests

  • Code: Spec: in the module header and/or @spec in TSDoc.
  • Tests: the title of an it() or test() call that runs starts with the ID in brackets: it('[SEC-001] strips inline <script> elements', …). Mentions in comments, strings, describe titles and skipped tests do not count (D-033). A test that pins a bug in an upstream library passes while the upstream code is unsafe, so it proves nothing: its title starts with upstream pin: instead, and its describe title and module header name the requirement the workaround protects.
  • node tools/spec-trace/specTrace.mjs (wired as npm run spec:trace in Session 1) regenerates docs/TRACEABILITY.md. With --check it fails CI on: duplicate IDs, references to unknown IDs, and MUST requirements of completed sessions that have no test reference.

DOC-005 Must S1 Each app and package has a README

Sections, in order:

  1. Purpose (2–3 sentences).
  2. How to run it locally.
  3. Folder structure, one line per folder.
  4. Key flows as Mermaid sequence diagrams. Required: Feide login, LTI launch, Deep Linking, xAPI → AGS, pseudonymisation, library install.
  5. Configuration (link to .env.example).
  6. Which specs it implements.

DOC-006 Must S1 Tests are written to be read

  • Name tests as behaviour, not implementation: [H5P-006] denies library installation to authors, not test checkForGeneralAction 2.
  • Use Arrange / Act / Assert comments in tests longer than 10 lines (// Arrange, // Act, // Assert, or // Act and assert where the steps interleave). npm run doc:lint fails on an it()/test() body of more than 10 lines whose comments do not name its Act and Assert steps.
  • Every fixture directory has a README.md that says what each fixture represents and why it exists (e.g. svg/xxe-external-entity.svg — standalone="no" with an external entity; must be neutralised).
  • Table-driven tests (it.each) are preferred for permission and role matrices, so the table in the test matches the table in the spec.

DOC-007 Must S1 Small, explicitly named files

Source files have ≤ 200 lines and one responsibility. Names say what the file is (HvlTop10ContentTypeFilter.ts, not utils.ts). PascalCase is used for files exporting a class or component, and camelCase for files exporting functions. Checked by: npm run check:filesize.

DOC-008 Must S1 Configuration is documented where it is defined

Every environment variable appears in .env.example with: a purpose comment, whether it is secret, its default, and an example value. Startup validation (zod) fails with a message naming the variable and pointing to .env.example.

DOC-009 Must S1 Language conventions

  • Code, comments and developer docs are in English, so international reviewers and the open-source community can read them.
  • Norwegian domain terms keep their Norwegian form in identifiers and enums (forarbeid, laeringsutbytte, mappe) and are explained in GLOSSARY.md. Do not invent English translations that a teacher at HVL would not recognise.
  • No user-facing string is hard-coded. UI text lives in nn/nb/en locale files. Checked by: eslint-plugin-i18next (no-literal-string in JSX) and the key-parity test (PROD-012).

DOC-010 Must S1 Decisions and deviations are logged

Record a decision in DECISIONS.md whenever you: choose between real alternatives, deviate from a spec, pin or accept a vulnerable dependency, or add or remove a content type. The entry gives context, the decision, its consequences, and the date. Code affected by a deviation carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-xxx.

DOC-011 Must S1 Commit messages are traceable

Use Conventional Commits (feat(h5p): …, fix(lti): …, docs(spec): …). Add a Refs: footer listing requirement IDs, for example Refs: SEC-001, H5P-006.

DOC-012 Should S3 HTTP APIs are self-describing

Request and response bodies are zod schemas. An OpenAPI document is generated from them and served at /api/docs in development. Every route file states its authentication mode (portal, LTI, either, or admin) and its error responses in the module header.

DOC-013 Must S1 No silent leftovers

  • No commented-out code.
  • No TODO without an owner and a reference: TODO(S4, UD-012): … or an issue URL.
  • No comment that contradicts the code. If you change behaviour, update the header, the TSDoc and the spec in the same commit.

DOC-014 Must S1 Content that non-developers edit has its own guide

content/**/README.md explains, for ALU staff, how to edit patterns, guide text, phase labels and portfolio templates. It includes an example and states which tests will catch mistakes.

Reviewer checklist (also in .github/pull_request_template.md)

  • ○ To do: Every new or changed file has a correct module header (DOC-001).
  • ○ To do: New exports have TSDoc; @spec IDs exist (DOC-002, DOC-004).
  • ○ To do: Security, privacy, accessibility and pedagogy decisions are tagged and explained (DOC-003).
  • ○ To do: Tests are named with requirement IDs and readable on their own (DOC-006).
  • ○ To do: docs/TRACEABILITY.md is regenerated and --check passes.
  • ○ To do: Any deviation is in DECISIONS.md and marked in code (DOC-010).
  • ○ To do: UI strings exist in nn, nb and en (DOC-009).

Evaluator Guide

This guide is for people who review HVL Interaktiv without having built it: ALU learning designers, TeCopp administrators, security and privacy reviewers, examiners and external code reviewers. It explains how to check, efficiently and independently, that the code does what the specifications promise.

Current state (2026-11-05): Sessions 1–3 passed their gates on 2026-10-23, Session 4 (universal design) on 2026-10-24 and Session 5 (the læringsdesign studio) on 2026-10-30. Session 6 (the grade bridge, insight, the privacy operations and deployment) started on 2026-10-30 (D-101) and is built, integrated and documented; its review and its gate (§5) have not run yet. What it does not reach, and what only HVL can verify (limitation 23), passes to HVL's bachelor students through the hand-off index ↗ (opens external site). Session 1 built the monorepo, apps/server foundations and the tools spec-trace, spec-site, doc-lint, dependency-check, privacy and h5p-core. Session 2 added the H5P engine with the ten types, the permission system, learner state, upload security, seeding and our own H5P routes. Session 3 made the server a running service (npm start): Feide login for the portal, Canvas LTI 1.3 launches through ltijs 7, Deep Linking, Canvas–Feide account linking and the sharing API behind one Principal, tested against the mock Feide and mock Canvas in tools/mock-platform (limitation 5). Session 4 brought the ten real content types from GitHub at pinned commits (D-078, R-01 settled in D-047), strict script policies on every page type (D-070), the web app apps/web (Next.js inside Express, D-067, D-068) with the activity pages, the publish flow and the Canvas chrome page /app/play, the design tokens and the HVL H5P theme, the pre-publish validator (22 rules), and the accessibility suite npm run test:a11y (D-079, D-080). Session 5 added the læringsdesign studio of spec 04, in the portal only (its Canvas side passed to the students in S6, limitation 20): the public guide and pattern catalogue on /laeringsdesign with ALU's texts loaded from content/ and checked by npm run content:check (D-082, D-083); nine patterns that create a draft activity with marked guidance (⟦…⟧, rule V-PLACEHOLDER; D-084–D-086); the Læringsdesign tab with outcomes, rationale, time and purpose, and the alignment planner (D-087, D-088); co-authors, the content bank and copies on the Deling tab (D-090–D-092); a save choice in the editor so that a structural change does not silently reset students' progress (D-093); and the pedagogisk mappe export as Markdown and as a tagged PDF printed by Chromium on the server (D-094–D-096). Its texts are drafts for ALU (Q17, limitation 16). Session 6 added the xAPI bridge in the learner's player page and the grade passback to Canvas through our own AGS client in a durable worker (D-102–D-105, D-115), teacher insight as an Innsikt tab with k-suppression and fixed periods (D-106), the yearly purge, data-subject requests, database roles and the production checks (D-107–D-109), the Docker image with a separate files origin and ClamAV, backups and the load harness (D-110, D-114), the conformance report (UD-040), HVL's Nynorsk and Bokmål texts for H5P's own buttons (D-111), problem reporting for the pilot and the drafts owed upstream (D-112), and end-to-end tests of the five user journeys. Build progress is tracked in PROGRESS.md. Commands marked (from S) below arrive with that session.

1. Orientation in 20 minutes

Prefer a browser? docs/site/index.html holds the same documents as one searchable page, with a requirement explorer. Regenerate it with node tools/spec-site/buildSpecSite.mjs.

MinutesReadYou will know
3README ↗ (opens external site)What the service is and how the repository is organised
6Spec 00 §1–§4Who it is for, the five user journeys, and the pedagogical principles
2GLOSSARYThe Norwegian terms used in code and UI (forarbeid, læringsutbytte, …)
4DECISIONSWhat was decided, including where the build deliberately departs from the original plan, and why
3apps/server README ↗ (opens external site)How to run the server against the mock platform, what each folder does, and the start-up, Feide login, LTI launch and Deep Linking flows
2content/README.md ↗ (opens external site) (from S5)What ALU edits without code (phases, guide, patterns, mappe template and criteria) and how npm run content:check catches mistakes; the review packet for ALU is reference/alu-review-s5.md ↗ (opens external site)
2TRACEABILITY ↗ (opens external site)Which requirements are planned, in code or tested

To see it run (from S3; the web app and the real content types from S4): set up the services, the H5P files and apps/server/.env as for npm start (§3; .env.example already holds the mock's values and WEB_APP=dev), start npm run mock:platform in one terminal and run npm start in another. The mock Canvas home page (http://127.0.0.1:4100/) offers demo launches into the tool, and the start page (http://localhost:3000/) offers Feide login against the mock Feide. The Hub's seed packages are not in the repository (Q7, Q10), so install the real content types first: npm run h5p:fetch-libraries, then npm run seed:libraries -- var/h5p-real/packages (D-078). Then sign in (the mock Feide signs in its author), create an activity at /aktivitet/ny, save it and publish it from Sjekk og publiser; the mock Canvas can then launch it by the ID in its address (/aktivitet/<id>) or place it through Deep Linking. With WEB_APP=prod, run npm run build first. The e2e tests (npm run test:e2e) create their own activities and show the whole flows in a browser. Details: tools/mock-platform/README.md ↗ (opens external site).

The studio (from S5): with the server running as above, /laeringsdesign shows the guide, the phase matrix and the pattern catalogue to anyone, signed in or not, and each pattern has a page /laeringsdesign/monster/<id> (for example fa-video). Signed in as the mock author (HVL staff), «Lag frå dette mønsteret» creates a draft and opens its Rediger tab; the activity page also has the Læringsdesign and Deling tabs. Give a few activities a course code, a phase and outcomes, then open /laeringsdesign/planlegg (the planner), list a published activity shared with HVL in the bank from its Deling tab and open /laeringsdesign/innhaldsbank, and choose activities on /mappe to download the portfolio as Markdown and as PDF. The PDF needs a Chromium the server can start: npx playwright-core install chromium (or PDF_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE), and, in a container that runs as root, the development-only PDF_ALLOW_NO_SANDBOX=true in apps/server/.env (D-096); without it the PDF button answers that the PDF is unavailable and points to the Markdown file, which always works. A banner on the studio pages says their texts are drafts until ALU confirms them (Q17).

2. Checking one requirement end-to-end

Every requirement has an ID such as SEC-001. The same ID appears in the spec heading, in the code (Spec: header or @spec tag) and in test titles ([SEC-001] …). To verify one:

# 1. Read what is promised (statement, acceptance criteria, verification method)
grep -n "SEC-001" docs/specs/*.md

# 2. Find the implementation and read its module header: what, why, invariants, tests
grep -rln "SEC-001" apps packages tools --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx

# 3. Run exactly the tests that claim to prove it                         (from S1)
npx vitest run -t "SEC-001"

# 4. Confirm the matrix agrees and nothing references an unknown ID
node tools/spec-trace/specTrace.mjs --check

Things to judge as you go: Do the acceptance criteria in the spec match what the test actually asserts? Does the module header's Invariants section match the code? Is every SECURITY:, PRIVACY:, A11Y: and PEDAGOGY: comment justified?

"Tested" is not "verified" for the two manual requirements. TRACEABILITY ↗ (opens external site) calls a requirement tested as soon as one test title carries its ID. For UD-031 and NFR-003 that test is apps/server/a11y/accessibilityDocs.a11y.test.ts, a check of documents. It proves that the manual protocol scripts J1–J4 for the five set-ups UD-031 names, that the NFR-003 matrix names every browser and screen reader of the requirement and only suites that exist, and that every file in docs/accessibility/results/ has a dated name. It does not prove that anyone has run the protocol, that a browser other than Chromium works, or that a screen reader announces anything: it passes while the results folder holds no result. Both requirements are documented protocols whose results HVL records (D-079); UD-031's own check, a dated result file for the release, stays an open item in PROGRESS.md until HVL's first run.

npm run h5p:fetch-libraries (from S4)Clones the ten content types and their dependencies at pinned commits, builds those without committed files and verifies every tree against tools/h5p-libraries/libraries.manifest.json (D-078); a cached checkout is reused only while its HEAD is still the pinned commit, which CI's cache of the checkouts relies on

With the pinned content types installed (npm run h5p:fetch-libraries; CI always has them) it also checks each skeleton's library versions, keys and field lengths. CI runs it, and so does the pre-commit hook when a file under content/ is staged. Needs no services

Also -t "PROD-001|PROD-009" (creating from a pattern; formative defaults), -t "PROD-007|PROD-013" (co-authors, the bank and copies; the save choice and its reset) and -t "MAPPE-" (the portfolio; its PDF tests need Chromium). The integration tests among them need the services and the real packages

4. Evaluation rubric

For each area: what good looks like, where to look, and the red flags that should fail a review.

4.1 Pedagogical fitness: does it help teachers help students learn asynchronously?

  • Good: Teachers start from patterns (PED-010), not a blank list. Defaults are formative: retries on, no timers (PROD-009). Hints nudge towards short segments and explanatory feedback (PED-020). Insight answers "what should I address in the next session?" (INS-002, INS-003).
  • Look at: content/laeringsdesign/ (the guide, the phases and the nine patterns with their skeletons), apps/server/src/learningDesign/patterns/, apps/server/src/validation/rules/*Hint.ts and placeholderRule.ts, and the Innsikt tab on the activity page and in /app/play (from S6; one activity, one context and one fixed period at a time, no separate page, D-101, D-106; the code is in apps/server/src/insight/ and apps/web/src/features/insight/). In the studio (from S5): the guide on /laeringsdesign, whose research claims cite references.yaml (PED-002); each pattern's page, with when to use it, why it works and the times it asks of authors and students (PED-010); a new activity from a pattern, whose guidance «⟦…⟧» the check reports until the author replaces it (D-086); the Læringsdesign tab, which asks for outcomes and a rationale before publishing without blocking it (PED-030); the planner's gaps (PED-031); and the pedagogisk mappe, which turns that rationale into the author's own teaching portfolio (MAPPE-002). What ALU and the pilot teachers are asked to judge is listed in reference/alu-review-s5.md ↗ (opens external site).
  • Red flags: Thresholds without a PEDAGOGY: reference. Hints that block publishing. Insight that ranks individual students. Pattern text that is not editable without code (PED-011). A phase label written in code rather than read from phases.yaml (PED-001). A research claim in the guide or a pattern without a citation. A pattern whose skeleton turns retries or «Vis svar» off or sets a timer (PROD-009). Students' scores presented in the mappe as evidence of learning rather than as formative aggregates (MAPPE-003).
  • Best evidence: Pilot results against the success measures in spec 00 §8, and ALU's review of the studio's drafts (Q17).

4.2 Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA and HVL house rules)

  • Good: All colour comes from tokens, with a contrast test (UD-001). Feedback shows text and an icon (UD-003). Two-tone focus ring (UD-004). The validator blocks missing alt text and captions unless acknowledged (UD-021, UD-022). axe runs inside H5P iframes (UD-030). Manual screen-reader results are recorded (UD-031). The portfolio PDF is tagged, with an outline, a language and a title (MAPPE-004), and what Chromium cannot tag is checked by hand with PAC and NVDA (D-096, protocol J4).
  • Look at: packages/design-tokens/, packages/hvl-h5p-theme/, docs/accessibility/.
  • Red flags: Hex colours outside the tokens package. outline: none without a replacement. !important without a WHY: comment. H5P.DragQuestion creatable anywhere.

4.3 Security

  • Good: Every SVG is sanitised on both upload paths (SEC-001). User files are served from a separate origin with CSP: sandbox (SEC-004). Non-admins can never install library code (H5P-006, SEC-003). An LTI launch never grants admin (LTI-004). The ltik is stripped from URLs and logs (LTI-003). Nonces are consumed atomically (LTI-002).
  • Look at: grep -rn "SECURITY:" apps packages, apps/server/src/security/, HvlPermissionSystem.ts, apps/server/src/lti/.
  • Red flags: LaissezFairePermissionSystem anywhere. localStorage holding an ltik. A ^-ranged runtime dependency. An npm audit exception without an expiry date.

4.4 Privacy (GDPR)

  • Good: Learners exist only as HMAC pseudonyms (DATA-002). No insight cell under k = 5 (INS-006, backed by a property test). Yearly purge with secret destruction (DATA-003). The data inventory matches the schema (DATA-001). Logs are redacted (DATA-009). No third-party requests (DATA-011). Staff names reach colleagues only through co-author search and the content bank, which /personvern says (D-090, D-091), and the portfolio export shows learners only as aggregates of at least k and stores nothing (MAPPE-003, D-095). (From S6) Insight views end at the latest Oslo midnight and never cross 1 August, and Canvas's test student never counts (D-106's and D-102's amendments). Data-subject requests are a CLI that HVL operations run, audited with counts only (DATA-008, D-108). The app's database role can only append to the audit tables, and the analytics role reads k-suppressed views only (DATA-010, D-109). Production refuses clear-text connections and storage outside the EEA list (DATA-004). The request log names route patterns and a request ID only (NFR-006).
  • Look at: docs/privacy/ (the inventory, the DPIA input with its residuals R1–R40, the research-export design), docs/ops/ (the runbooks), apps/server/src/privacy/ (with purge/ and dsr/), apps/server/prisma/roles/, apps/server/src/config/connectionEncryption.ts and storageResidency.ts, apps/server/src/http/requestLog.ts, apps/server/src/insight/, apps/server/prisma/schema/.
  • Red flags: Learner names or e-mails in any table. An endpoint returning per-learner rows to teachers. actor.name or mbox persisted from xAPI. A learner key, identity hash, Feide ID or sub in an audit event, a CLI's output or a log line. A purge that selects rows by timestamp instead of their stored year (D-107).

4.5 Interoperability (Canvas and Feide)

  • Good: A Playwright test passes with third-party cookies blocked (LTI-003). Deep Linking returns a valid signed JWT (LTI-005). AGS sync is durable, idempotent and visible to teachers (LTI-012). Feide roles follow the table in AUTH-002.
  • Look at: apps/server/src/lti/, apps/server/src/grades/, apps/server/src/auth/, the mock platform in tools/mock-platform/.
  • Red flags: Values marked (verify) in spec 02 still unverified at Session 3's gate. Grade sync happening inside the request path.

4.6 Code quality and documentation

  • Good: Every file has a module header that answers the five questions in the Documentation Standard. Tests read as specifications. Files are under 200 lines. Every decision is logged.
  • Red flags: Files called utils.ts or helpers.ts. Comments that restate code. TODO without a session or requirement reference. Hard-coded UI strings.

6. Known limitations (stated honestly)

  1. Scores are computed in the browser. H5P scoring cannot be made tamper-proof. HVL Interaktiv is for formative use only (LTI-013, PROD-011).
  2. Upstream accessibility. Some barriers are inside H5P content types and can only be fixed upstream. The conformance report (UD-040) lists them with links to the upstream code. No issue is filed yet: the reports are drafted in upstream/README.md ↗ (opens external site) for the owner to file (D-112), and each link goes into the register once filed.
  3. The H5P Hub is still unreachable; real content types come from GitHub (D-078, D-047). The ten content types and their dependencies are cloned at pinned commits and verified file by file; all ten install through the seed path, play, open in the editor and save under Core 1.28 and Lumi 10.0.4 (R-01 settled). Hub registration and the Hub's own packages stay untested while hub-api.h5p.org is unreachable from the build environment (Q7); the S3 end-to-end flows still use a synthetic content type, the S4 flows and the accessibility suite the real ones.
  4. Institutional reference material is not yet in the repository (see reference/README.md). Labels, brand colours and portfolio headings are therefore kept in configuration, so they can be corrected without code changes.
  5. Feide and Canvas are tested against mocks only; HVL's own values are open. Feide login and the Canvas tool run end to end, but only against tools/mock-platform (D-049): HVL's Feide client and redirect URIs (Q3) and TeCopp's developer key, client ID and deployment ID (Q4) are not available yet, and auth.dataporten.no and *.instructure.com are unreachable from the build environment (Q7). The (verify) values in spec 02 therefore stay unverified at the S3 gate (§4.5), and so do whether Canvas sends feide_login under privacy level anonymous (Q4) and the hvl_placement field in the developer key (Q13). Canvas–Feide account linking stays off for a platform until "feideLinking": true is set in LTI_PLATFORMS after that test launch (D-063). Every HVL value is an environment variable, so the real services need configuration rather than code, unless they behave differently from the documented values the mocks follow. From S6 the facts the mocks assume are checks that can run against ALU's test Canvas and real Feide (npm run test:live), with a checklist for what a test cannot do; both pass to HVL's bachelor students (handoff/live-contract-seam.md ↗ (opens external site), handoff/canvas-acceptance.md ↗ (opens external site)).
  6. Strict package versions. An author's .h5p import is refused when any library differs from the installed one in its patch version (SEC-003, Q9), which will refuse many packages exported elsewhere.
  7. Some pages stay server-rendered (D-067). The web app (apps/web) serves the start page, the activity pages, /hjelp, /personvern and the Canvas chrome /app/play; the Deep Linking picker (/lti/deeplink) and the friendly error pages stay server-rendered by Express (they need its 401/403/404/503 statuses) but use the token CSS, the formative notice and the Hjelp link. Sharing had only an API until S5; the activity page's Deling tab now sets the visibility through it (PATCH /api/content/:contentId/sharing). Since S6 the activity page and /app/play also have the Innsikt and Poeng til Canvas tabs, one context at a time (D-101, D-106).
  8. The H5P pages allow inline styles, and Panopto's script once a Panopto site is configured (D-070). Since S4 the player (/h5p/play/:contentId, /lti/play) and editor pages (/h5p/edit/:id, /h5p/new, /lti/edit) send script-src 'self' plus the hash of H5P Core's one constant inline script, so a script inside an activity cannot run and read the page's URL token (the ltik or the CSRF token). When EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS lists a Panopto site, script-src also allows one third-party file, https://developers.panopto.com/scripts/v1.2.0/embedapi.min.js, which H5P.Video needs to play Panopto videos and loads without SRI, on pages that hold the ltik in memory (SPEC-DEVIATION from H5P-009 and DATA-011); with no Panopto site configured, no outside script can run. Our own tags on these pages carry no SRI or nonce either: they are same-origin files allowed by 'self' (D-070). style-src still allows 'unsafe-inline', because H5P sets style attributes throughout; injected CSS can change how an activity looks but not run code. The S2 upload checks (SEC-001, SEC-002) and admin-only library installation (SEC-003) limit what an activity can carry.
  9. Tokens travel in some URLs, so proxies must not log query strings (D-057, D-058). A launch reaches /app/play, /lti/play, /lti/edit and /lti/deeplink with the ltik in the query (a first-party script then removes it from the address bar), and the H5P AJAX and learner-state URLs carry the ltik or the CSRF token as a query value, because H5P builds those URLs itself. Our logs redact these values (DATA-009), but a reverse proxy, load balancer or CDN in front of the server must not log query strings and must not cache responses that set cookies. The deployment checklist carries this rule (ops/runbook.md ↗ (opens external site) §9); whether HVL's proxy keeps it is checked only when HVL deploys.
  10. Only the player's files are on the separate origin (D-045, D-110's amendment of 2026-11-05). The player's content files load from files.<host> (or FILES_BASE_URL) through signed, expiring URLs (D-058), with nosniff, a sandbox CSP, no cookie and no ltik. The editor's saved files (/h5p/editor-files/…), fresh uploads and H5P's cookie fallback routes stay on the app origin, behind the same headers (SPEC-DEVIATION: D-110: H5P's image editor draws into a canvas without crossorigin). files.<host> is the same site as the app; a separate registrable domain is HVL's choice (Q5). A grant opens every file of one activity for 12–13 hours.
  11. No launch where frame storage is blocked and the platform offers no Platform Storage (D-050). ltijs keeps a short-lived recovery token for its login state in the frame's localStorage or, where the browser blocks that, in LTI Platform Storage. With storage blocked and no lti_storage_target in the login request, ltijs cannot recover its state and the launch ends on our error page (pinned by apps/server/e2e/ltiIframe.e2e.test.ts). Canvas sends lti_storage_target, so this affects only other platforms. Where storage is blocked, the Canvas player gives H5P Core a page-memory stand-in for localStorage (apps/server/src/lti/pages/client/h5pStorageGuard.js), so what H5P keeps there (the xAPI actor ID, the copy-and-paste clipboard, the xAPI queue) lasts only as long as the page; learner state is saved on the server and is not affected.
  12. ltijs loads database drivers it never uses (D-050). ltijs 7.0.7 imports mongoose (with mongodb) and ioredis when it loads. They are installed and loaded but never connected: our PrismaLtiDatabaseManager and node-redis LtiCacheManager replace them, and ESLint forbids importing ltijs's MongoLegacyDatabaseManager and RedisCacheManager. They still count in the audit and licence checks; an upstream issue asks ltijs to load them lazily.
  13. No build step for the server. npm run build builds the web app, but the server runs its TypeScript sources through tsx, so every start compiles them in memory. Since S6, tsx is a runtime dependency of apps/server (D-110), so npm ci --omit=dev and the Docker image start it (node --import tsx src/server/main.ts); a compiled server would need its import.meta.url anchors reworked.
  14. Two interim rules wait for the owner (Q12). Student authors (through AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS) may share an activity only as private until a course visibility exists (D-059), and from S5 they neither add co-authors nor see or list in the content bank, which shows colleagues' names (D-090, D-091); Feide users without a Feide ID, such as guests, cannot log in (D-054).
  15. Accessibility is verified automatically in Chromium only; H5P's own barriers are listed, not hidden (D-079, D-080). Firefox, Safari, Edge, mobile browsers and the three screen readers are covered by the manual protocol in docs/accessibility/, which HVL runs and records (UD-031, NFR-003); no run is recorded yet, and the "tested" status of both in docs/TRACEABILITY.md comes from a check of the documents (§2). Barriers in H5P's own markup that a run-time repair cannot remove safely are listed in apps/server/a11y/support/upstreamRegister.ts with links to the upstream code; they are reported in every run but do not fail CI (SPEC-DEVIATION from UD-030).
  16. The studio's texts are drafts until ALU confirms them (Q17, D-100). The phase labels and texts (phases.yaml says status: proposed, so the studio pages show a draft banner), the guide in three languages, the sixteen references (every one verify: true), the nine patterns, the mappe template, the criteria and their limits (7 500 words and 11 attachments, (verify)), the content bank's consent text (also for HVL's lawyers) and the privacy sentences about colleagues seeing staff names were written by the build from public sources and have not been reviewed by ALU or tried by pilot teachers. Some guide claims rest on search excerpts of Møgelvang & Isaksen (2025), and some criteria are translations or paraphrases. The review packet reference/alu-review-s5.md ↗ (opens external site) lists each; the review is required before the pilot. The English guide keeps Norwegian terms such as kontekst and samskaping in running text, which its Markdown cannot mark with their own language (WCAG 3.1.2 allows such terms).
  17. The portfolio PDF needs Chromium on the server (D-096). playwright-core 1.56.1 prints it with the server's own Chromium, in a fresh context per export with JavaScript off, offline and every request aborted; at most PDF_MAX_CONCURRENCY exports at once (2) and one per person, 30 seconds each. Where no browser starts, the PDF export answers 503 and the page points to the Markdown export, which always works. The S6 image carries Playwright's full Chromium 141 and fonts with æ, ø and å (the PDF uses Liberation Serif, because Georgia, the body font token, is not installed) and runs the server as uid 10001; Chromium keeps its sandbox only with Playwright's seccomp profile and CAP_SYS_CHROOT, which OpenShift's restricted-v2 does not allow (Q5; the development-only PDF_ALLOW_NO_SANDBOX=true is refused in production). The server logs at start whether the export works (PDF export availability). HVL keeps Chromium patched by rebuilding the image.
  18. What the PDF does not tag yet is checked by hand (D-096, MAPPE-004). The automated test reads the structure tree, the outline, /Lang, the title and the text with pdfjs-dist; a person checks the rest with PAC and NVDA (protocol J4 in docs/accessibility/manual-test-protocol.md). Known residuals to record there: list numbers are untagged, list items have no Lbl or LBody, and lists carry no numbering attribute; a table's caption and header row become NonStruct; there is no XMP metadata and so no PDF/UA identifier; links have no /Contents; the header says PDF 1.4; activity titles and references carry no language of their own (D-094 amendment); and an activity's address is plain text, not a link. No manual check is recorded yet.
  19. Students' results in the mappe last until the yearly purge, not one academic year (D-095 and its amendments, D-107). Since S6 the mappe reads the stored learning data on demand: groups of at least k (MIN_GROUP_SIZE, 5 by default, never below 3) per course, version and semester, with two-sided suppression, from rows stored before the latest midnight in Oslo, as insight reads them; Canvas's test student never counts. No period limits it: every stored row counts until the purge deletes it on PURGE_RUN_DATE (31 August by default, at the latest 31 December), so an export made after 1 August and before that day still holds the ended year's groups. It does not read the purge's k-suppressed snapshots yet, so after the purge an ended year's results leave the mappe (open in PROGRESS.md, S6 step 5).
  20. The Canvas side of the studio passes to the students (D-098, D-101). S6 did not reach the content bank and "new from a pattern" in the Deep Linking picker or the LTI-007 duplicate in /app/play; they pass to HVL's bachelor students with a design note (handoff/canvas-studio.md ↗ (opens external site)), and the hand-off index ↗ (opens external site) lists everything else that does. In Canvas the editor's save choice offers only resetting the students' progress or cancelling, with a pointer to the portal for saving a new version.
  21. Known limits of collaboration and copies, accepted for now (D-091, D-092, D-093). The content bank shows the 200 newest listings without paging, and a listing only while its owner is findable HVL staff (an eligible Feide login in the last 13 months). People search allows 30 searches a minute per person, a fixed number. A copy whose source and source author are both deleted shows no «Kopi av …» sign and looks like an original. On the Deling tab a student-author owner still sees the people search, because the web app knows roles but not that fact, and gets the server's explanation (hvl:sharing-not-allowed) when searching (D-092). When HVL installs a newer minor version of a content type, the first save of each older activity counts as structural, because H5P's editor upgrades it, so authors whose students have saved progress are asked to reset or copy.
  22. Some of H5P's own texts are still English in Nynorsk and Bokmål (D-111). HVL's language overlay translates the learner-facing buttons and messages of the ten types and their common sub-content, the editor labels of MultiChoice, QuestionSet, InteractiveBook and BranchingScenario, and DragNBar's toolbar; its texts are drafts until HVL's language advisers and ALU review them (Q2, Q17), and an activity keeps the texts it was saved with. Most other editor labels, the H5PEditor.* libraries' strings and less common sub-content stay English. Three texts no language file reaches are listed in the upstream register (UPSTREAM_ENGLISH_TEXTS): H5P.Video's "Video source is missing.", ImageHotspots' "Missing required background image" and InteractiveVideo's end-screen summary of a scored question, which screen readers read in English.
  23. What cannot be verified here waits for HVL (D-101, D-113). The build environment has no access to HVL's Canvas, Feide, servers or people, so the items below stay verified by document review or against the mocks, not by HVL until HVL acts. Each is listed with S6's gate output and among the open questions in PROGRESS.md, and the hand-off index ↗ (opens external site) says who takes it on.
    • Real Canvas and real Feide (limitation 5). Every LTI, AGS, NRPS and Feide test runs against the mocks in tools/mock-platform. The facts the mocks assume are checks that npm run test:live runs against ALU's test Canvas and real Feide, which only HVL or the students can do, and the Canvas acceptance checklist (handoff/canvas-acceptance.md ↗ (opens external site)) covers what a test cannot see, such as how Canvas shows the formative label (Q3, Q4, Q7, Q8, Q13).
    • The 200-learner load test (NFR-001). Only npm run load:smoke runs here: 20 learners for 30 seconds on one node. npm run load:full, on a node like production, is HVL's (ops/runbook.md ↗ (opens external site) §8).
    • Backups and the restore drill on HVL's hardware (NFR-002). The backup round trip runs here on the local services; the daily backup with its encrypted copy off the server, and the restore drill each semester with its log, are HVL's (runbook §6).
    • Hosting (DATA-004, NFR-007, SEC-004, SEC-006). Storage in the EEA, a container runtime that allows Playwright's seccomp profile and CAP_SYS_CHROOT, the files host's DNS name and certificate, and a clamd with daily signatures (Q5) are ticked on the deployment checklist (runbook §9) when HVL deploys. The image and its smoke test run here; .github/workflows/docker.yml has not yet run on GitHub (Chromium from Playwright's CDN and its SHA-256, AppArmor, the /proc check on the runner).
    • The manual assistive-technology run (UD-031, NFR-003; limitation 15), the manual PDF check (limitation 18) and the conformance report's 56 verdicts, each Not yet determined until HVL's dated evaluation (UD-040).
    • The data protection officer's review of the DPIA input and its residuals (DATA-005, Q6), and the DPO's questions Q15, Q22, Q25 and Q27–Q30. Running the database roles' script on the real database (DATA-010) and destroying an ended year's pseudonym secret (DATA-003) are steps for HVL operations.
    • Reviews and choices for ALU, HVL or the owner: the studio's and the H5P texts (Q2, Q17), which types send a score (Q18–Q20), the build rule for containers (Q21), how a graded link counts plays (Q23), insight's freshness (Q24), deleting audit rows after two years (Q26), and the earlier questions Q9, Q10, Q12 and Q14.
  24. Insight and grade passback have known gaps (D-104, D-106, D-115). Every insight view ends at the latest midnight in Oslo, so what learners do today shows tomorrow, and no view crosses 1 August (Q24, handoff/insight-freshness.md ↗ (opens external site)). Branching paths (INS-004) are not built, because BranchingScenario's choices are in no statement H5P sends (handoff/branching-paths.md ↗ (opens external site)); nor is the spaced-retrieval suggestion (PROD-014, a COULD), and LTI Dynamic Registration (LTI-009) is a design note only. Some activities send Canvas no score as they are set up today: ImageHotspots never, InteractiveVideo only with a submit screen, and BranchingScenario not when it is set to «No scoring»; the Deep Linking picker says so beside each of them (D-115, Q18), and every ending of the uv-case pattern scores 10 of 10 (Q19). The grade-sync counts on Poeng til Canvas are live, not k-suppressed, and include Canvas's test student, and an activity's owner and co-authors see them for every course it is placed in (Q22; DPIA input R1, R13). A learner's score in a graded link counts their plays of the same activity in the same course through any other link too (Q23).

Lightweight architecture decision records. Add an entry for each real choice between alternatives, each deviation from a spec, each accepted vulnerability, and each change to the content-type set (DOC-010). Code affected by a deviation carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-xxx.

D-001 · Node.js 24 LTS instead of 22
