  • Context: The plan specifies Node 22 LTS. ltijs@7.0.7, the current maintained release, declares "engines": { "node": ">=24" }. Node 24 is an LTS line supported until April 2028.
  • Decision: Target Node.js 24 LTS (.nvmrc, Docker node:24-* images, engines field).
  • Consequences: Development containers that ship Node 22 must install Node 24. Revisit once Node 26 becomes LTS.
  • Re-check: npm view ltijs@7 engines.

D-002 · Pin @lumieducation/h5p-server@10.0.4 and h5p-express@10.0.5

  • Context: The plan says "lock to version 10.1.0 or newer". No such version exists. The latest h5p-server is 10.0.4 (2025-03-08) and the latest h5p-express is 10.0.5.
  • Decision: Pin the exact versions (SEC-007). Watch the upstream repository for a release that fixes CVE-2025-7062 (see D-003).
  • Re-check: npm view @lumieducation/h5p-server versions.

D-003 · Own SVG sanitising and defensive file serving

  • Context: CVE-2025-7062 (stored XSS through uploaded files) affects h5p-server versions up to and including 10.0.4. 10.0.4 removed svg from the default allowlist, but it still identifies files by extension only. No fixed version is published. (CVE-2025-47828, which the plan also cites, is a different bug, fixed in 9.3.3.)
  • Decision: Defence in depth: @lumieducation/h5p-svg-sanitizer plus our own extra rules (SEC-001), magic-byte sniffing (SEC-002), a separate file origin with CSP: sandbox (SEC-004), and a narrowed allowlist.
  • Consequences: Slightly slower uploads. SVG stays usable for diagrams.
  • Re-check: OSV and NVD entries for CVE-2025-7062; the h5p-server CHANGELOG.

D-004 · Library installation is a GeneralPermission

  • Context: The plan restricts ContentPermission.InstallRecommended. In h5p-server 10.0.4 the enum is GeneralPermission (CreateRestricted, InstallRecommended, UpdateAndInstallLibraries).
  • Decision: Use GeneralPermission.*, admin-only (H5P-006).
  • Re-check: build/src/types.d.ts in the installed package.

D-005 · ltijs 7 with a PostgreSQL DatabaseManager

  • Context: The plan describes the ltijs 5 API (lti.setup(…, { ltiaas: true })) with ltijs-postgresql. ltijs 7 is a TypeScript rewrite: Provider, LaunchContext, a cookie-less ltik (24 h), and a pluggable 14-method DatabaseManager that ships with MongoDB only. ltijs-postgresql and ltijs-sequelize were last published in 2022 and target v5.
  • Alternatives: (a) ltijs 5 with sequelize: legacy and unmaintained. (b) Add MongoDB just for LTI: a second database to run and back up. (c) Implement DatabaseManager on Prisma/PostgreSQL: about 14 small methods.
  • Decision: (c), as PrismaLtiDatabaseManager (LTI-002). Keep ltijs behind our own LtiProviderFactory so a future library change stays local.
  • Re-check: npm view ltijs@7 dependencies; services/database-manager/database-manager.types.d.ts.

D-006 · Branching Scenario replaces Drag and Drop in the ten types

  • Context: H5P.DragQuestion is popular, but free 2-D dragging is a well-known barrier for keyboard, switch and screen-reader users (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7). Case-based judgement is central to HVL's professional programmes.
  • Decision: Exclude DragQuestion from authoring, including as sub-content; include H5P.BranchingScenario (H5P-002).

D-007 · Two-tone focus ring instead of an orange outline

  • Context: The plan pairs coastal teal with a #FF9E1B focus outline. Measured contrast against white is 2.07 : 1, which fails WCAG 1.4.11 (needs 3 : 1). The plan also overstated two feedback contrast ratios (7.21 : 1 and 7.08 : 1 measured; both still pass).
  • Decision: outline: 3px solid HVL Mørk blå 2 (#004357, 10.82 : 1 on white; originally #003D4C, changed by D-017) with a 2 px white inner ring, which works on light and dark surfaces (UD-004). Contrast is tested in CI from the tokens (UD-001). #FF9E1B is not an HVL colour; HVL's orange is Oransje #EB6851. It clears 3 : 1 on white only narrowly (3.17 : 1), so it stays decorative.

D-008 · Formative use only

H5P scores in the browser, so scores can be forged. AGS scores are labelled formative and the UI says so (LTI-013, PROD-011). Exams stay in Wiseflow.

D-009 · Nynorsk first, with Bokmål and English fallback

HVL's main administrative language is Nynorsk. i18next uses nn → nb → en for both UI and H5P strings (H5P-008, PROD-012).

D-010 · Teachers see aggregates only, with k = 5

  • Context: Insight helps teaching decisions. Individual grades already exist in Canvas through AGS.
  • Decision: No per-learner insight endpoint. Suppress groups smaller than k = 5, with complementary suppression (INS-006).
  • Consequences: Very small classes see little insight. This is an accepted privacy trade-off, and k can be lowered to 3 by configuration.

D-011 · Learners are HMAC pseudonyms with yearly key rotation

learnerKey = HMAC(secret[academicYear], source). Destroying the secret at the yearly purge makes the remaining aggregates unlinkable (DATA-002, DATA-003). Resume state does not carry across the 1 August boundary. This is acceptable because the summer break falls there.

D-012 · One public origin, plus a separate origin for uploaded files

A reverse proxy serves Next.js and Express on one origin, which removes CORS and keeps the portal cookie first-party. User-uploaded files come from a cookie-less second origin, which limits the damage any file-borne script can do (SEC-004).

D-013 · Validator errors can be acknowledged rather than hard-blocking

Teachers sometimes publish while captions are still being produced (for example in Panopto). A hard block would push them to tools with no checks at all. An acknowledgement with a reason is stored, re-raised after 14 days, and visible in insight and the portfolio export (PROD-003, UD-022).

D-014 · English in code, Norwegian domain terms preserved

English makes the code reviewable by international evaluators and the open-source community. Domain terms such as forarbeid or laeringsutbytte keep their Norwegian form so teachers and ALU recognise them. They are explained in GLOSSARY.md (DOC-009).

D-015 · Licence GPL-3.0-or-later

  • Context: @lumieducation/h5p-server is GPL-3.0-or-later, so a server that combines with it must be GPL-compatible. The other main dependencies are compatible: ltijs (Apache-2.0), marked (MIT), H5P content types (MIT).
  • Decision: The whole repository is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. The repository owner asked Claude to confirm the choice on 2026-10-16. LICENSE holds the unmodified GPL v3 text. Its SHA-256, 3972dc9744f6499f0f9b2dbf76696f2ae7ad8af9b23dde66d6af86c9dfb36986, is the hash of the FSF's gpl-3.0.txt, and it was cross-checked against the copy shipped in @lumieducation/h5p-server.
  • Consequences: Anyone who distributes a modified version must release its source under the same licence. Network use alone does not trigger that. The HVL name and logo are trademarks of Høgskulen på Vestlandet and are not licensed by the GPL. Logo files must not be committed without HVL's permission. Third-party files keep their own licences, for example tools/spec-site/vendor/marked.LICENSE.md.
  • Re-check: sha256sum LICENSE.

D-016 · Specs beyond the plan's four, plus requirement IDs and traceability

The plan defines four module specs. This repository adds spec 00 (product, users, pedagogy), spec 05 (insight and privacy), the Documentation Standard and Evaluator Guide. Requirement IDs connect spec, code and tests, and tools/spec-trace/specTrace.mjs enforces them. The plan's session structure and its progressive loading of one spec per session are kept.

D-017 · Brand tokens follow HVL's design manual

  • Context: The plan's colours (#003D4C, #005F6B, #007681, #FF9E1B, "deep fjord teal", "coastal teal") appear in no HVL source. HVL's Visuell identitet / Profilmanual (v2.0, February 2017, p. 16) defines the logo colours Mørk blå 2 #004357 (PMS 3035 U) and Sjøgrønn #00AFBA (PMS 7710 U), plus signal, support and additional colours. The values were read through search extracts of the manual and agree with independent transcriptions and with two public copies of the logo (docs/reference/hvl-visual-identity.md ↗ (opens external site)).
  • Decision: Spec 03 §2 uses Mørk blå 2 for headings, links, primary buttons and the focus ring (10.82 : 1 on white), Mørk blå 1 #008AAF for non-text UI only (4.00 : 1), Sjøgrønn and Oransje for decoration only, Blågrå lys #C9D5DA for bands, Mørk rød #6D2439 for incorrect-answer text. Body text stays a neutral near-black #111111, because the HVL palette has no text black and its greys fail 4.5 : 1. Neutral tokens are labelled as such.
  • Consequences: CLAUDE.md, UD-004 and D-007 now name #004357. HVL (profil@hvl.no ↗ (opens external site)) must confirm the values, the four hex/RGB mismatches noted in the reference file, and whether derived shades are allowed.
  • Re-check: python3 -I docs/reference/tools/contrast.py.

D-018 · Typefaces: Arial and Georgia

  • Context: The plan specified Inter, Arial and Calibri. HVL's manual names NB Akademie Std (titles, captions) and Lyon Text (body) as profile fonts, with Arial and Georgia as the office substitutes. Both profile fonts are commercial; no source shows that HVL holds web-font licences.
  • Decision: Headings, UI controls and captions use Arial; long-form body text uses Georgia (UD-002). The licensed profile fonts may be self-hosted in front of these stacks once HVL confirms web licences. Inter and Calibri are dropped.
  • Consequences: No third-party font requests are needed (DATA-011).

D-019 · Phases are course-organisation vocabulary at the model's mikronivå

  • Context: Spec 04 assumed that Modellen for læringsdesign ved HVL defines phases. HVL's annual report 2024 (p. 23) confirms the model exists. Its only public description (Møgelvang & Isaksen 2025, MNT-konferansen) presents an alignment model built on kontekst, kunnskap and samskaping, applied across levels from the læringsøkt (mikronivå) to the institution, using baklengs planlegging. HVL's course pages use forarbeid, mellomarbeid and etterarbeid (and før- og etterarbeid) for work around a samling. No HVL page uses underveis as a phase name, and it is easily confused with undervegsvurdering (formative assessment). (docs/reference/hvl-laeringsdesign-model.md ↗ (opens external site))
  • Decision: Keep the stable keys forarbeid, underveis, etterarbeid. Label them Forarbeid, Mellomarbeid and Etterarbeid (en: Pre-work, Intermediate work, Post-work). Present them as the structure of a læringsøkt around a samling, not as the phases of HVL's model. The studio introduces the model itself (kontekst, kunnskap, samskaping; backward planning) and links to its public description.
  • Consequences: Spec 04 §1, the glossary and the proposed phases.yaml change. ALU must confirm the labels against the model document.

D-020 · Portfolio export follows HVL's merit portfolio, as content

  • Context: The plan cited criteria "1.1–3.2". HVL's 2025 merit call has three main criteria and eleven sub-criteria (1.1–1.4, 2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.3), revised for each call. The merit portfolio has three parts: Del 1 samanhengande framstilling (up to 7 500 words, references excluded), Del 2 pedagogisk CV, and Del 3 up to 11 attachments including the manager's letter. (docs/reference/hvl-pedagogisk-mappe-criteria.md ↗ (opens external site))
  • Decision: MAPPE-002 follows the three-part structure with a criterion table as a reader's guide. Criteria texts, the word limit and the attachment limit live in content files keyed by criteria set (hvl-merittering-2025), so the 2027 call needs only a content change. A promotion (opprykk) mode waits for ALU to confirm its headings.

D-021 · The Feide ID token is kept in the server-side session for logout only

  • Context: Feide's RP-initiated logout requires both post_logout_redirect_uri and id_token_hint. The ID token contains the user's name and e-mail when those attribute groups are released.
  • Decision: Keep the raw ID token only in the Redis session (encrypted at rest, deleted at logout or expiry). Never write it to PostgreSQL or logs. Learner name and e-mail are dropped before anything is persisted (AUTH-003, AUTH-004).

D-022 · H5P editor 1.28 client files come from a pinned, reviewed commit

  • Context: H5P-001 asked for core and editor files from a released, versioned 1.28 package. Core has the release tag 1.28.0. The editor (h5p-editor-php-library) has no 1.28 release tag: its newest semver tag is 1.25, and 1.28-era code exists only on platform branches and untagged commits. Lumi's own master pins editor commit ab2daa18bd61b19e7f8729e22eec88f3b637a868 (seed-package status ↗ (opens external site) §5).
  • Decision: Pin core to tag 1.28.0. Pin the editor to one reviewed commit (start from Lumi's pin), record its per-file SHA-256 in docs/reference/, and review the diff before any change. Never track a moving branch.
  • Consequences: H5P-001 and the CLAUDE.md invariant ("never unreleased H5P git branches") now mean "never a moving branch; a pinned commit only where no release exists, with this entry". Revisit when H5P tags an editor 1.28 release.

D-023 · Integration tests use docker compose or CI service containers, not Testcontainers

  • Context: H5P-004 names Testcontainers for its integration tests. Testcontainers starts containers from inside the test process and needs a Docker socket there. CI runners and many development containers (including the one Session 1 was built in, where Docker Hub also rate-limited pulls) do not offer that reliably, while GitHub Actions service containers and docker compose do.
  • Decision: Integration tests read DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL and S3_* from the environment. Locally, docker compose up -d provides PostgreSQL 16, Redis 7 and an S3-compatible store; CI uses service containers with the same images. Tests that need a service are named *.int.test.ts and skip with a clear message when the service is not configured, so npm test still runs the unit tests anywhere.
  • S3 emulator: the moto server (motoserver/moto, pinned tag) emulates the S3 API in one container that needs no start command. GitHub Actions service containers cannot pass a command, which MinIO needs (server /data), so moto is used both locally and in CI. Production uses any S3-compatible store in the EEA.
  • Consequences: H5P-004 and the evaluator guide say "integration tests against PostgreSQL, Redis and S3" instead of naming Testcontainers; CLAUDE.md names the emulator instead of MinIO. CI must never skip them: test/support/services.ts throws when CI=true and a service variable is missing.

D-024 · TypeScript pinned to 6.0.3

  • Context: TypeScript 7.0 (the native compiler) is the newest release, but typescript-eslint 8.72, the newest release of the linter we need for typed rules, supports TypeScript <6.1 only.
  • Decision: Pin typescript 6.0.3. Revisit when typescript-eslint supports 7.x.
  • Re-check: npm view typescript-eslint@latest peerDependencies.

D-025 · Own S3 adapters on AWS SDK v3 instead of h5p-mongos3

  • Context: Lumi's @lumieducation/h5p-mongos3 stores content metadata in MongoDB and uses AWS SDK v2, which reached end of support in September 2025. Our metadata lives in PostgreSQL (H5P-004).
  • Decision: PrismaContentStorage keeps metadata and parameters in PostgreSQL and delegates file I/O to S3ContentFileStore; S3TemporaryFileStorage handles temporary files. Both use @aws-sdk/client-s3 v3 and work with any S3-compatible store (MinIO, Ceph, Sikt's object storage).
  • Consequences: We own these adapters and their tests. Lumi's h5p-mongos3 source is a reference for edge cases (key sanitising, range reads), not a dependency.

D-026 · Library storage on a shared volume until deployment needs S3

  • Context: H5P-004 allows S3- or file-system-backed library storage. Libraries change only when an admin installs or updates a content type and are read on every page view. Lumi's CachedLibraryStorage caches their metadata in each node's memory; its own default lifetime is 24 hours.
  • Decision: S1 uses Lumi's FileLibraryStorage on a volume shared by all server instances, wrapped in CachedLibraryStorage with a per-node in-memory cache of 300 s (LIBRARY_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS). An S3 ILibraryStorage is added in S6 only if the target platform has no shared volume.
  • Consequences: Deployment (S6, NFR-007) must mount one volume for H5P_LIBRARY_DIR on every node. After a library install or update (including a security update, H5P-011), other nodes can serve the old library metadata for up to 5 minutes. If S6 needs instant propagation, use a Redis-backed cache store or a cross-node invalidation message.

D-027 · H5P core and editor files are fetched and verified, not committed

  • Context: The server needs H5P's client files (core tag 1.28.0, editor commit per D-022). Committing these 281 third-party files (67 core, 214 editor) would bury our own code in reviews and diffs.
  • Decision: tools/h5p-core/fetchCoreClients.sh fetches them into apps/server/h5p/ (git-ignored). The script checks that each tag or commit resolves to the expected commit hash, then checks every file against a committed per-file SHA-256 list (h5p-php-library-1.28.0.files.sha256, h5p-editor-php-library-ab2daa18.files.sha256); a changed, missing or extra file stops it. CI runs the script before the tests. The server refuses to start when the core API version in the fetched files is not 1.28 (H5P-001).
  • Consequences: A fresh clone needs one npm run h5p:fetch-core. doc-lint and spec-trace skip apps/server/h5p/.

D-028 · The H5P user-data adapter moves to S2 with H5P-005

  • Context: H5P-004 (S1) lists IContentUserDataStorage, but the adapter's key and behaviour are defined by H5P-005 (S2), which needs the LTI context and the learner pseudonym in a request.
  • Decision: Build and test PrismaContentUserDataStorage in S2 together with H5P-005. S1 creates its database table, so the schema is complete.
  • Consequences: The S1 integration test of H5P-004 covers the other five adapters.

D-029 · Own licence and audit checks instead of license-checker and plain npm audit

  • Context: NFR-005 suggests license-checker; it is unmaintained and pulls in its own dependency tree. SEC-007 allows reviewed, expiring exceptions to npm audit, which plain npm audit cannot express.
  • Decision: tools/dependency-check/checkLicences.mjs reads production packages with npm query ':not(.dev)' (since S4 npm query '*' filtered on the dev flag, D-071) and checks their SPDX expressions against a GPL-3.0-compatible allow-list. checkAudit.mjs runs npm audit --omit=dev --json and fails on any high or critical advisory that has no unexpired entry in audit-exceptions.json pointing to a decision here.
  • Consequences: No extra dependencies. Packages with legacy licence metadata are listed by name and version after a person has read their licence file.

D-030 · Accepted advisory: image-size parser loops (until 2027-01-31)

  • Context: @lumieducation/h5p-server 10.0.4 depends on image-size@^1.0.2. Advisories GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq (JXL and HEIF) and GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr (ICNS) affect every version up to 2.0.2; no 1.x release is fixed. Version 2 changes the API that H5PEditor.saveContentFile calls (it passes a file path), so an override would break image uploads. A third advisory (underscore ≤ 1.13.7, via jsonpath) is fixed by an npm overrides entry pinning underscore 1.13.8, a patch release.
  • Decision: Accept both image-size advisories until 2027-01-31. The loop is reachable only through an authenticated author's file upload. In S2, SEC-002 content sniffing rejects any file whose magic bytes are not on the allowlist (JXL, HEIF and ICNS are not) before H5P calls image-size.
  • Consequences: audit-exceptions.json lists both advisories with this decision and the expiry date. Review again at expiry, or earlier if h5p-server releases a version with image-size ≥ 2.0.3.

D-031 · Session 1 items that finish in Session 2

  • Context: Some Session 1 work depends on things that only exist in Session 2, or on a network this build environment does not have. The Session 1 review (2026-10-22) found these were not recorded as a decision.
  • Decision: These move to S2 and are listed in its PROGRESS.md checklist:
    1. Spike steps 3–6 (spec 01 §7): site registration and seeding against hub-api.h5p.org, rendering H5P.MultiChoice, the Daylight theme with the F3 CSS, and the R-01 choice between 1.28 and the 1.27 fallback. This environment's proxy blocks hub-api.h5p.org (Q7).
    2. Wiring workaround F1: getLocalIdOverride: () => localIdFor(<site UUID>) is an H5PEditor option, so it is set in H5pEditorFactory. S1 provides and tests localIdFor.
    3. Injecting the F3 theme CSS through the player and editor customisation hooks (needs the S2 routes).
    4. SEC-005's "temporary directory with a quota": the S2 package import route runs inspectZip before Lumi's PackageImporter. The quota is maxTotalSize, checked from the central directory; yauzl checks the real sizes while extracting into a fresh os.tmpdir() folder that is removed afterwards. S1 provides the guard, the limits and the size-limited S3 uploads.
    5. TypeDoc API pages for DOC-002, added with the HTTP API.
  • Consequences: SEC-005 and H5P-001 have tests in S1 for what exists; their S2 parts get their own [ID] tests in S2.

D-032 · h5p-express installed in S1; its Express 4 is overridden to 4.22.3

  • Context: Spike step 1 installs @lumieducation/h5p-express@10.0.5. It depends on express 4.21.2 exactly, whose dependencies have advisories: path-to-regexp < 0.1.13 (GHSA-37ch-88jc-xwx2, high), plus moderate ones in qs and body-parser. Express 4.22.3 (2026-09-14) uses the fixed versions.
  • Decision: A scoped npm override ("@lumieducation/h5p-express": { "express": "4.22.3" } in the root package.json) replaces Express only inside h5p-express. Our own server (S2) uses Express 5 as its own dependency, which the override does not touch. check:pins checks nested override values too.
  • Consequences: S2 must test the h5p-express routers on Express 4.22.3. Remove the override when Lumi releases an h5p-express with a fixed Express.
  • Superseded by D-035 (2026-10-22): S2 does not use h5p-express, so the override and Express 4 are removed.

D-033 · Only running it()/test() titles prove a requirement

  • Context: DOC-004 said "the describe or it title starts with the ID". The Session 1 review found that spec-trace counted an [ID] anywhere in a test file, including comments, strings, describe titles of groups whose tests name other IDs, and skipped tests. Such a mention proves nothing.
  • Decision: A requirement counts as tested only when its ID opens the title of an it() or test() call that runs. Calls in comments, strings and regex literals are ignored; skip, todo, skipIf, fails and the x prefix, on the test or on an enclosing describe, mean it does not run. describe titles may still carry IDs for readers. tools/spec-trace/testTitles.mjs holds the rule; spec-trace and doc-lint's DOC-006 check both use it. DOC-004 in the Documentation Standard says so.
  • Consequences: Conditional groups such as describeWithServices count, because CI always runs them (it fails when services are missing). A title built at run time (not a string literal) is not counted.

D-034 · The yearly purge also deletes learner User rows

  • Context: DATA-003 lists XapiStatement, H5PUserData, GradeSyncJob and learner Identity rows. In the schema the cascade runs from User to Identity, not back, so a purge that follows the list leaves each learner's User row (id, kind, createdAt) behind. The data inventory already gave those rows the yearly purge as retention.
  • Decision: DATA-003 also deletes learner User rows that have no Identity left after the purge. The inventory labels a learner's userId references (Identity.userId, AuthAuditEvent.actorUserId) "Pseudonymous (stable key)", because Identity.subjectHash links that ID to the person until the purge.
  • Consequences: The S6 purge test checks that no learner User row without an Identity survives. Staff User rows are unaffected.

D-035 · Own Express 5 routes over H5PAjaxEndpoint; h5p-express removed

  • Context: S2 needs the H5P HTTP endpoints. @lumieducation/h5p-express 10.0.5 builds Express 4 routers. Mounted in our Express 5 app they route correctly, but: the Express 4 layer ignores returned promises, so an error after a stream has started is an unhandled rejection that ends a Node 24 process; its error handler returns internal error messages; 206 responses get the file name as Content-Type; content files get no nosniff, CSP or Content-Disposition; the library-administration and content-type-cache routers have no authorisation; ?asUserId= and contextId come straight from the query string; and the download route never reaches our permission system (Lumi builds its PackageExporter without one).
  • Decision: apps/server/src/http/ implements the routes in Express 5 on top of h5p-server's exported H5PAjaxEndpoint and H5PEditor/H5PPlayer. @lumieducation/h5p-express and the root override for its Express 4 are removed (D-032 superseded). ESLint forbids importing it. D-002's pin of h5p-express no longer applies; the h5p-server pin stays.
  • Consequences: We own about ten small route handlers and their tests. The D-032 checklist item "test the h5p-express routers on Express 4.22.3" is closed by removal. CLAUDE.md §1/§2 say so.

D-036 · The H5P actor has an account view and a state view

  • Context: Lumi passes one IUser everywhere and uses user.id both as the content owner and as the key of learner state. DATA-002 requires learner state to be keyed by the pseudonym (learnerKey), never by an internal or raw ID, while ownership needs the account ID.
  • Decision: HvlH5pActor (src/h5p/HvlH5pUser.ts) carries the account ID, role, learnerKey, context and visibility facts. Two IUser views wrap it: the account view (id = User.id) for content and temporary files, and the state view (id = learnerKey) for user data and the player. The permission system reads the actor's explicit fields, never user.id, so the wrong view fails closed. contextId comes from the authenticated request; ?asUserId is refused with 400. An undefined or unknown user is always denied; files an author removes are deleted by our code as that author. The H5P-006 boot check: createH5pRuntime runs assertPermissionSystem on the editor and player the factories build (every Lumi component must hold HvlPermissionSystem), plus an ESLint ban on LaissezFairePermissionSystem.
  • Consequences: S3 maps its Principal to HvlH5pActor. Own state also requires View on the content.

D-037 · H5P "finished" data is off; the state save interval is fixed at 5 s

  • Context: Lumi stores a separate "finished" record (score, times) per learner. Spec 05 has no such entity; scores reach the LMS through xAPI → AGS in S6. H5P-005 asks for the default 5 s save interval, and S1 allowed both settings to be loaded from storage.
  • Decision: setFinishedEnabled is false and contentUserStateSaveInterval is 5000, set in code after loading. There is no /finishedData route; the storage's finished-data methods store nothing.
  • Consequences: Less learner data (data minimisation). S6 reads scores from xAPI statements.

D-038 · How learner state is stored, deleted and invalidated

  • Context: H5P sends state as a JSON string and deletes it by posting data=0. Lumi deletes invalidated state before checking the Edit permission on save (H5PEditor.js:527-528), so any signed-in user could wipe learners' state, and Lumi sorts state by Number(subContentId), which is NaN for UUIDs.
  • Decision: The state string is stored as a JSON string value in H5PUserData.data (no migration); data=0 deletes the row; invalidated rows are deleted only after a save that passed the permission check; the storage returns the main state (subContentId '0') first.
  • Consequences: PROD-013 (S5) adds the author's confirmation before invalidating.

D-039 · Our own sub-content policy on save (list items, DragQuestion, titles)

  • Context: Lumi's ContentScanner passes a list's array, not its parent object, to the SemanticsEnforcer for list items (ContentScanner.js:119). Text fields that are list items (for example H5P.Blanks questions) are therefore never sanitised (a CVE-2025-47828 regression), and a disallowed library that is a list item (for example a DragQuestion in a QuestionSet) is neither removed nor checked. Metadata titles are not sanitised either.
  • Decision: On save, our SubContentPolicy walks the params with the (altered) semantics, refuses with 403 any sub-library that the field does not offer and H5P.DragQuestion anywhere, sanitises list-item text with Lumi's own text rules, and sanitises the titles in main and sub-content metadata. A test pins the upstream behaviour so we notice when Lumi fixes it. Two gaps found in the S2 review are closed the same way: Lumi adds every library: "H5P.Name 1.2" value it finds, under any key, to the content's dependencies, so the policy refuses any such value the semantics walk did not reach (semantics/libraryReferences.ts); and H5P's "Rights of use" dialog shows metadata without escaping, so every metadata string is reduced to plain text, source is kept only as an http(s) URL, and a field that becomes empty is dropped. The verification pass after that review showed the dialog reads more than the semantics reach: h5p.js findCopyrights walks the whole tree, renders every metadata and file copyright object, and writes an image's path and the sub-content's alt into <img src="…" alt="…">. So semantics/rightsOfUse.ts cleans these anywhere in the parameters: metadata and copyright objects become plain text (sanitize-html with no tags, pinned as a direct dependency at the version Lumi uses; Lumi's own default for a field without tags still allows links and tables); a path with quotes, angle brackets, control characters or a scheme other than http(s) is refused with 400; and a straight double quote in alt becomes ”, because Lumi's sanitiser runs after ours and turns &quot; back into ". A second verification pass found three more ways out, now closed: WHATWG keeps a quote in a URL's host raw, so a source whose serialised form still holds ", ', <, > or a backtick is removed; the walk now continues inside metadata and copyright objects, as h5p.js does; and h5p.js joins arrays into the HTML, so an array path is refused, an array alt is emptied, and metadata nested deeper than the limit is dropped instead of kept as it was. A third, focused check (a sink audit of h5p.js and Chromium fuzzing with more than 60 variants) found no further way to run script, but five inputs that Lumi or PostgreSQL turned into a 500. They are now refused as the request's fault (400): text with U+0000 or a lone surrogate (storage/storableText.ts, also for learner state), nesting deeper than 256 levels before Lumi's recursive walks see it (semantics/nestingDepth.ts, also for an imported content.json), and values whose JSON type Lumi's scanners cannot read (paramsWalker.ts: text, list, group, library, file, image, video and audio fields); a sub-content library object without a usable toString is refused with 403 like any other.
  • Consequences: The walker (semantics/paramsWalker.ts) is reused by the S4 validator. Cleaning data for a renderer that does not escape is a list of known sinks, not a guarantee: the real ten types render their own copyright data (getCopyrights), so their sinks must be reviewed when the Hub packages arrive (Q7), and the player page gets a script CSP without 'unsafe-inline' in S4 (DATA-011), which stops injected handlers whatever their source.

D-040 · Our own page templates with script-safe JSON

  • Context: Lumi's default templates write JSON.stringify(integration) into a <script> element (renderers/player.js:16). JSON.stringify does not escape </script>, so a title or an unknown parameter key containing it would run script for every learner. H5PIntegration.user also carries the user's ID.
  • Decision: We render the player page ourselves and escape <, >, &, U+2028 and U+2029 in the embedded JSON. H5PIntegration.user is blank (no pseudonym or account ID in the page). The editor returns only its model until S4 adds its page with the same escaping; Lumi's templates are never used.
  • Consequences: S4 adds the editor page and extends both with the theme; S6 adds the xAPI bridge.

D-041 · Library change control: one audited install path, no Hub installs

  • Context: H5P-011 requires an audit event for every library change and no Hub installs on demand in production. Lumi has no install hook, and an empty content-type cache makes it call the Hub on every request.
  • Decision: Libraries change only through (a) the seed command and (b) an admin's package import; both write a LibraryAuditEvent per new or patched library. Installing from the Hub is refused for everyone, in every environment. LibraryAuditEvent.actorUserId becomes nullable (the seed command has no user) and gains source (seed or upload). An empty content-type cache is stored as [], so the server never calls the Hub while serving requests; npm run hub:check contacts it explicitly (spike step 3). The audit rows are written before Lumi installs anything (libraries/auditBeforeInstall.ts, which predicts Lumi's new/patch decision from the package), so a failed audit write installs nothing; changes beyond the prediction are recorded right after. The editor's Hub download and Content Hub calls are replaced at construction (disconnectFromHub).
  • Consequences: New content types arrive through new seed packages, reviewed like code.

D-042 · The seeder lives in apps/server; where the seed packages are kept

  • Context: Spec 01 §2 places seedLibraries.ts in tools/seed/, but seeding needs the server's H5P configuration, library storage and Prisma (for the audit).
  • Decision: The seeder is in apps/server/src/h5p/libraries/ (npm run seed:libraries), and tools/seed/ keeps the fetch script. Spec 01 §2 was amended to match, so no code carries a deviation tag. The ten packages are committed under docs/reference/h5p-core-1.28-seed-packages/ when every file is under 50 MB and all together under 150 MB; otherwise they are published as a GitHub Release asset and only SHA256SUMS is committed (as D-027).
  • Consequences: CI will seed from the committed (or release) packages and never fetches from the Hub. Until the packages can be fetched (Q7), CI has no seed step; the integration tests seed synthetic packages.

D-043 · Multipart uploads keep their extension and are limited while streaming

  • Context: Lumi requires a temporary file path when file sanitisers are registered, and its SVG sanitiser ignores any path that does not end in .svg; common upload middlewares write temporary files without an extension. Lumi also has no size limit on direct editor uploads, and it trusts the client's MIME type.
  • Decision: @fastify/busboy parses uploads into a fresh mkdtemp folder; each file keeps its lower-cased extension, its MIME type comes from the extension, and the 50 MB limit is enforced while streaming (413).
  • Consequences: The folder is removed after every request, successful or not.

D-044 · SVG sanitising rules and order

  • Context: SEC-001 asks to reject or strip DOCTYPE/ENTITY, scripts, event handlers, foreignObject, javascript:/data:text/html URLs and external references. Inkscape and Illustrator exports carry a public DOCTYPE, which is harmless without an internal subset.
  • Decision: An internal DTD subset or any <!ENTITY is rejected. A plain DOCTYPE and xml-stylesheet instructions are stripped. href/xlink:href may only point to a #fragment or a raster data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp). script, foreignObject, use, set, on* attributes and animations of href are removed (<use> can load an external document); @import and external url() are removed from styles. Order: our pre-check, Lumi's sanitiser, our stricter DOMPurify pass, and a final check that nothing forbidden is left. Benign SVGs must render identically in Chromium before and after (screenshot comparison).
  • Consequences: SVG files larger than 5 MB are refused. DOMPurify parses with the HTML parser (its XML mode returns nothing for a file with an <?xml?> prolog); that parser keeps xmlns but its SVG profile removes <use>, so a drawing that relies on <use> loses those parts (pinned in SvgSanitizer.test.ts). Lumi's profile is SVG only (no filter elements), so filter primitives such as feGaussianBlur are lost too, and DOMPurify removes ids that name document properties (title, blur, …), which breaks url(#…) references to them; a test pins all three losses. Our pass writes its result with XMLSerializer, and the final check parses it again as XML, as a browser does, and fails closed. Lumi alone let 15 of the 41 attack payloads in SvgSanitizer.bypass.test.ts through (13 once our pre-check had run); the added layers stop all of them.

D-045 · Headers for user files; the separate files origin moves to S3/S6

  • Context: SEC-004 asks for nosniff, a sandbox CSP for SVG and documents, and attachment for non-media types, and for a separate files origin in production. Files on another origin need their own authorisation (signed URLs, part of S3's HvlUrlGenerator) and deployment (S6).
  • Decision: Every content and temporary file is served with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; everything except raster images, audio, video and VTT captions is served as attachment. The separate origin is an S6 checklist item.
  • Consequences: A stricter superset of SEC-004 in S2; the origin isolation follows in S3/S6. Text types, SVG included, carry charset=utf-8. An SVG is an attachment too: a browser still draws it in <img>, but opening it directly downloads it instead of showing it as a page.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05): the separate origin is built in S6 as D-110's amendment of the same day describes: the player's files come from FILES_BASE_URL (by default files.<host>), every answer there carries these headers, and the editor's files stay on the app origin for now (SPEC-DEVIATION: D-110).

D-046 · Library language files fall back nn → nb → en

  • Context: H5P-008 asks that a content type without language/nn.json uses its nb strings, then en. Lumi falls back from nn straight to en (LibraryManager.js:109-168), and its alterLibraryLanguageFile hook cannot supply a missing file.
  • Decision: A library-storage wrapper serves language/nb.json when language/nn.json is missing. The translation callback for Lumi's own strings uses i18next (lng: 'nn', fallbackLng: ['nb', 'en']); our own server messages stay in src/i18n/translate.ts.
  • Consequences: Lumi's own nn client strings are partly Bokmål; HVL's language advisers review them (Q2).

D-048 · The Session 3 LTI views are server-rendered pages until apps/web (S4)

  • Context: LTI-003 and LTI-005 describe the Canvas views as Next.js pages, but apps/web and its design tokens arrive in S4. Building the views in Next.js now would add React and Next.js to S3 and style the pages twice. The owner chose server-rendered pages for S3 (2026-10-23).
  • Decision: SPEC-DEVIATION: in S3 the server renders /lti/play (the player Canvas embeds), /lti/deeplink (the picker) and the friendly error pages. LTI-003 still holds in full: the ltik lives only in page memory (a script closure or the H5PIntegration URLs), never in localStorage, sessionStorage or cookies; a first-party script removes it from the address bar with history.replaceState; our APIs take Authorization: Bearer; every page that receives an ltik sends Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cache-Control: no-store and CSP frame-ancestors from CANVAS_ORIGINS, and never X-Frame-Options. Page scripts are static files (script-src 'self'). The pages are unstyled until S4.
  • Consequences: S4 moves the views to apps/web /app/* and keeps the same server APIs.

D-049 · A mock Feide and a mock Canvas in tools/mock-platform; HVL values from env

  • Context: HVL's Feide client values and the TeCopp Canvas instance are not available yet (Q3, Q4), and auth.dataporten.no and *.instructure.com are not reachable from the build environment (Q7).
  • Decision: tools/mock-platform holds a mock Feide (oauth2-mock-server plus a Groups API route) and a mock Canvas (our own node:http + jose server: an OIDC auth endpoint with form_post, JWKS, the LTI Platform Storage frame, a course page that embeds the tool cross-site, and deep-link return verification). Tests start it in-process; npm run mock:platform runs it by hand. It is not a docker compose service: the server on the host and the browser must reach the mock Feide at the same URL. Every HVL value is an environment variable.
  • Consequences: The (verify) items in spec 02 stay open until HVL IT and TeCopp deliver (Q3, Q4).

D-050 · How we use ltijs 7: our router, our cache, our pages, our ltik checks

  • Context: ltijs 7.0.7 registers its routes through a pluggable HttpHandler; its own ExpressHttpHandler creates an Express app with cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }) and helmet, and Provider.listen() installs a SIGINT handler that calls process.exit(). Its RedisCacheManager uses ioredis. mongoose and ioredis load at import. getLaunchContext(ltik) does not check whether the platform is still active.
  • Decision: ltijs runs on our ExpressRouterHttpHandler (an Express Router); we never call Provider.listen(). SPEC-DEVIATION: our node-redis LtiCacheManager replaces ltijs's RedisCacheManager (LTI-001 wording); it caches only public JWKS and keysets. ltijs's own HTML gets a CSP with hashes of its inline scripts. Its default handlers are replaced by friendly pages. Our ltik resolver also checks platform.active. ltijs's OIDC recovery token (at most 10 minutes, grants nothing on its own) may sit in the frame's partitioned localStorage (stock Chrome) or, where storage is blocked and localStorage throws, in LTI Platform Storage; the ltik never does.
  • Consequences: mongoose, mongodb and ioredis are installed and loaded but never connected; an upstream issue asks ltijs to load them lazily. ESLint forbids importing RedisCacheManager, ExpressHttpHandler and MongoLegacyDatabaseManager. The S3 probes (test/lti/upstream/ltijsProvider.test.ts) also showed: ltijs copies the claims for the handler only after saveIdToken returns, so our storage filters a copy, never its argument; a resumed context (getLaunchContext) has only the stored claims, so the claim allowlist (D-052) must keep everything a later request reads (e.g. Deep Linking settings); and our handler must pass Express's lower-case req.headers through, or ltijs skips its Sec-Fetch-Site check without an error. ltijs 7.0.7's launch page calls localStorage.removeItem outside its try, so where frame storage is blocked (the getter throws) the launch form is never submitted. A static guard script (src/lti/pages/client/ltijsStorageGuard.js) runs before ltijs's scripts and, only when the getter throws, puts a stand-in in its place that stores nothing and whose setItem still fails, so ltijs falls back to Platform Storage as designed. The cookie-less e2e launch (apps/server/e2e/ltiIframe.e2e.test.ts) found the same problem in H5P Core 1.28: it reads localStorage without a try (xAPI actor UUID, clipboard, xAPI queue), so H5P.init stopped and learner state was never saved. The LTI player therefore loads src/lti/pages/client/h5pStorageGuard.js before H5P Core: only when the getter throws, it puts a page-memory stand-in in its place (nothing reaches disk; the ltik is never written to it). With storage blocked and no lti_storage_target, ltijs cannot recover its state and the launch ends on our "launch failed" page; Canvas sends lti_storage_target, so this affects only other platforms.

D-051 · LTI platforms and deployments from LTI_PLATFORMS; deployment IDs checked by us

  • Context: LTI-001 requires rejecting a launch with a wrong deployment ID. ltijs 7 checks only that the claim is a string, and its platform model has no deployment field.
  • Decision: A new table LtiDeployment(platformId, deploymentId). LTI_PLATFORMS (JSON in env) is synced at start-up: new platforms are registered (ltijs generates the tool key pair), endpoints updated, removed platforms deactivated, and each platform's deployments replaced. The deployment ID is checked in saveIdToken, so no ltik is ever minted for a foreign deployment, and again on every use of an ltik.
  • Consequences: Adding a Canvas deployment is a configuration change and a restart. Dynamic Registration (LTI-009) stays in S6.

D-052 · ltijs records: 10-minute nonces, 24-hour ID tokens with a claim allowlist

  • Context: LTI-002 says nonces expire after 10 minutes; the data inventory said 1 hour. ltijs stores the whole ID token, which can carry names, e-mail, lis identifiers and custom fields.
  • Decision: Nonces live 10 minutes (the inventory is corrected), matching ltijs's 600-second state. consumeNonce is one conditional DELETE, which is atomic. ID tokens live 24 hours and expired rows are never returned. The stored claims are an allowlist of what the launch needs; names, e-mail, lis, feide_login and unknown custom fields are dropped before storage. A cleanup job runs every 10 minutes under a Redis lease.
  • Consequences: The launch handler still sees the full claims in memory; only storage is minimised.

D-053 · The Principal: always a user ID, roles as a list, one mapping to the H5P actor

  • Context: Spec 02 §2 types Principal.userId as a string but comments "null for learners", while D-034 gives learners pseudonymous User rows and HvlH5pActor.accountId is required (D-036).
  • Decision: userId is always set. roles is a list; the H5P role is the highest of them. LTI principals have hvlMember = false and feideAuthenticated = false, so in Canvas they see the launched activity and their own content. auth/principalToH5pActor.ts is the one mapping to HvlH5pActor (D-036). Spec 02 §2 is amended.
  • Consequences: No code path has to handle a missing user ID.

D-054 · The Feide subject is the Feide ID; Groups API failures fail closed

  • Context: DATA-002 derives the learnerKey from feide|<feide-id>, AUTH-005 compares Canvas's login ID with the Feide ID, and ADMIN_FEIDE_IDS lists Feide IDs. AUTH-004 allows sub or the Feide ID.
  • Decision: The Feide subject is the Feide ID (eduPersonPrincipalName, trimmed and lower-cased). It feeds Identity.subjectHash, the learnerKey, ADMIN_FEIDE_IDS and account linking; sub is never stored. A login without a Feide ID is refused with a friendly page. The organisation comes from the Groups API (fc:org:<realm>); if that call fails, the login fails closed (503 page). enableNonRepudiationChecks adds an ID-token signature check against Feide's JWKS on top of openid-client's claim checks.
  • Consequences: Feide users without a Feide ID (guests, eduGAIN) cannot log in (owner to confirm, Q12).

D-055 · A stable identity key ring with HKDF purposes and a rotation rule

  • Context: Identity.subjectHash and AuthAuditEvent.ipHash need a keyed hash whose key does not rotate every year (the learnerKey's key does, D-011), and the rotation must be defined (PROGRESS S3).
  • Decision: IDENTITY_HASH_KEYS is a key ring id=base64,… whose first entry is current; HKDF derives the purpose keys identity-subject and auth-audit-ip. New columns Identity.subjectKeyId and AuthAuditEvent.ipKeyId record which key made a hash. Rotation: put the new key first; lookups try every key and re-hash a match in place at that login. Remove an old key after at least 13 months (learner rows are purged by then; a dormant staff member gets a new account). On compromise, rotate the same way at once.
  • Consequences: Rotation needs no downtime and no bulk re-hash.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, S3 verification): rotation has three steps, as in D-056: (1) add the new key second and restart every server, so every server finds rows under either key; (2) when every server runs that ring, move it first and restart every server (logins re-hash to it, new audit rows use it); (3) remove the old key at least 13 months after the last step-2 restart. Putting the new key first in one step lets a server still on the old ring miss a row hashed with the new key and give that person a second account, and the lookup cannot repair that later (src/auth/identity/identityLookup.ts prefers the current-key row, else the oldest). A leaked key is rotated with the same steps, started at once, and stays in the ring while rows re-hash. Residual risk, accepted: whoever holds the leaked key and a copy of the database can test guessed Feide IDs and IP addresses against every hash made with that key for as long as such rows exist: AuthAuditEvent.ipHash rows with that ipKeyId (up to 2 years) and Identity rows of people who never log in or launch again (retention: account). Removing the key from the ring does not end this; without a guess the hashes reveal nothing.

D-056 · Secrets at rest are encrypted with AES-256-GCM from a key ring

  • Context: LTI-002 requires platform private keys encrypted at rest; D-021 requires the Feide ID token in the session encrypted; S6 stores GradeSyncJob.ltiSubEncrypted.
  • Decision: DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS key ring; AES-256-GCM with a per-purpose HKDF key and the purpose as AAD. Format 0x01 | keyIdLength | keyId | iv(12) | tag(16) | ciphertext. Used for LtiPlatform.privateKeyEncrypted, LtiAccessToken.tokenEncrypted, the session's Feide ID token, and in S6 for ltiSubEncrypted. Values are re-encrypted with the current key when they are next written.
  • Consequences: A database dump alone reveals no private key or token. A platform's key pair is written only at registration, so the server re-encrypts stale platform private keys at every start-up (src/lti/platforms/reencryptPlatformKeys.ts); access tokens and session ID tokens expire within 12 hours. Because the first restarted server rewrites the platform keys for everyone, a rotation has three steps (S3 verification): (1) add the new key second and restart every server, so every server can read both; (2) move it first and restart every server; (3) remove the old key 12 hours after the last step-2 restart. Putting the new key first in one step would break LTI on servers not yet restarted, and a key that has been first must stay in every ring until nothing uses it.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 6 integration): step (3) waits at least 31 days after the last step-2 restart, not 12 hours. Since S6, GradeSyncJob.ltiSubEncrypted stays under the key of the job's last write until the job's subject is cleared, 30 days after the job stopped (D-104, DATA-002, apps/server/src/grades/GradeSubjectCleanupJob.ts), and a job whose key is gone fails as subject-unreadable (apps/server/src/grades/gradeJobSend.ts). Found by the skeptic review of the backup and runbook work (D-110's backup amendment); apps/server/.env.example and docs/ops/runbook.md §4 say the same.

D-057 · Own Redis portal sessions, login transactions and a synchronizer CSRF token

  • Context: AUTH-003 asks for a Redis session behind an opaque __Host-hvli_sid cookie (idle 2 h, absolute 12 h) and CSRF protection; H5P-007 requires 401 for an H5P request without a valid token. Generic middleware (express-session, csurf) does not give these exact semantics, and csurf is deprecated.
  • Decision: Small own modules. Sessions in Redis under a hash of the session ID; the cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/. A single-use login-transaction cookie (10 minutes) binds state, nonce and PKCE verifier to the browser, which prevents login CSRF. One synchronizer token per session, read from the X-CSRF-Token header, a csrf query value (H5P URLs) or a csrf form field; it is required on every unsafe method and on /h5p/ajax and /h5p/contentUserData for any method. A missing or wrong token is 401 hvl:csrf-invalid. Roles are computed at login only.
  • Consequences: A role change in Feide takes effect at the next login. Details settled in the implementation: the session cookie has no Max-Age (a browser-session cookie; the server enforces both limits); a cookie name sent twice is ignored entirely (defence against cookie tossing); logout is a POST, so the CSRF token protects it; the session's ID-token blob is sealed once at login, so a retired DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS key is kept at least 12 hours. Reverse proxies must not cache responses that carry Set-Cookie and must not log query strings (csrf, ltik).

D-058 · H5P URL tokens and signed content-file URLs

  • Context: H5P-007 asks that H5P's AJAX and user-data URLs carry the ltik (Canvas) or a CSRF token (portal). Lumi's UrlGenerator puts the token unencoded, and contentFilesUrl receives no user, while H5P builds file URLs as contentUrl + "/" + path, so a query token cannot work there. D-045 puts signed file URLs in S3.
  • Decision: HvlUrlGenerator appends ltik or csrf, URL-encoded, from a new actor field urlToken. Content files are served from a public route /h5p/files/:grant/:contentId/*file, where the grant is an HMAC over contentId|expiry with URL_SIGNING_KEYS, valid for 12 hours and issued only by a render that passed the View check. An ltik in a query string is accepted only on /h5p/ajax, /h5p/contentUserData/*, /lti/play and /lti/deeplink; everywhere else it must be a Bearer header.
  • Consequences: Script inside content could read the token from its page; the S2 sanitising and the S4 CSP limit that. The separate files origin stays in S6 (D-045). Details settled in the implementation: Lumi's csrfProtection.queryParamGenerator is not used, because it does not encode the token the same way on the three URLs (SPEC-DEVIATION from H5P-007's wording); a grant's expiry is rounded up to the hour, so it lives 12 to 13 hours and a file URL stays the same (cacheable) for an hour, verification allows 5 minutes of clock skew, and an old URL_SIGNING_KEYS key is removed at least 13 h 5 min after rotation; responses are Cache-Control: private, max-age=<seconds left>; the signed route reads only an activity's registered files (no temporary-file fallback); the player factory refuses Lumi's render options that skip the View check (ignoreUserPermissions, parameter overrides), so no grant is ever signed without it. The authenticated /h5p/content/:id/*file route stays for the H5P editor, whose integration has no contentUrl; an editor in a cookie-less Canvas iframe (S4) needs grant-bearing URLs issued after an Edit check.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, S3 verification): URL_SIGNING_KEYS rotates in the three steps of D-056: (1) add the new key second and restart every server; (2) move it first and restart every server; (3) remove the old key at least 13 h 5 min after the last step-2 restart. Putting it first in one step would make servers not yet restarted refuse the file URLs that restarted servers sign.

D-059 · How the Feide and LTI role tables are read

  • Context: AUTH-002 and LTI-004 leave some cases open: unknown LTI roles, how a course group matches, and what "visibility limited to the course" means for student authors when no course visibility exists yet.
  • Decision: LTI institution/person#Administrator gives author, never admin; unknown roles and TestUser give learner. An AUTHOR_COURSE_GROUPS entry matches a group ID exactly or as a prefix followed by :. Student authors may share only private until a course visibility exists. Users from other organisations are learner and see only feide-visible activities. ADMIN_FEIDE_IDS grants admin only to an HVL member (a realm in ALLOWED_FEIDE_ORGS); a listed Feide ID from another organisation gets no admin role.
  • Consequences: The owner confirms the student-author rule (Q12).

D-060 · Authors may view a published activity they launched from Canvas (course copy)

  • Context: LTI-007 lets instructors of a copied course launch and play an activity they do not own. The S2 rules granted launched activities to learners only.
  • Decision: Amendment to H5P-006: an author may View a published activity opened by their own LTI launch. Edit stays with the owner and co-authors. The spec 01 matrix and its test are updated.
  • Consequences: Copying a course never gives edit rights.

D-061 · Deep Linking in Session 3

  • Context: LTI-005 names a picker with the author's activities, the content bank and "new from a pattern"; the last two arrive in S5. Canvas sends lineItem only for assignment_selection.
  • Decision: The picker lists the author's own and co-authored activities; drafts are shown but cannot be selected. The graded placement is recognised from Canvas's placement claim or, failing that, from our custom field hvl_placement set per placement in the developer key. A lineItem is sent only for assignment_selection. We use createDeepLinkingMessage with our own form (no inline script); the return URL must be http(s); several items only when accept_multiple is true.
  • Consequences: TeCopp adds hvl_placement to the developer key (Q13).

D-062 · The LTI-006 tabs and the LTI-007 duplicate come with their pages

  • Context: LTI-006 gives authors Rediger and Innsikt tabs; the editor page is S4 (D-040) and insight is S6. LTI-007's "duplicate" belongs to the content bank (PROD-007, S5).
  • Decision: SPEC-DEVIATION: in S3 both roles get the player; the tabs arrive with the editor page (S4) and insight (S6), and duplicating with PROD-007 (S5).
  • Consequences: LTI-006 and LTI-007 are tested for what S3 delivers.

D-063 · Linking an author's Canvas and Feide identities

  • Context: AUTH-005 links an author's Canvas identity to their Feide identity through the custom claim feide_login.
  • Decision: feide_login is read only when LTI-004 gives author; values starting with $ are ignored; it is never stored. If only the Feide account exists, the LTI identity joins it; if both exist and differ, the LTI identity moves only when its account owns no content and no co-authorship, otherwise link.conflict is audited and nothing changes. Learner identities are never linked.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, S3 review): the value is whatever the platform says, and AUTH-005 itself asks for it to be confirmed first (verify with TeCopp). So linking runs only for a platform with "feideLinking": true in LTI_PLATFORMS (default false; set after the Q4 test launch), only for a Feide ID whose realm is in ALLOWED_FEIDE_ORGS, and only onto a Feide account that a Feide login created and that is not a learner's. A Feide identity is never created or attached from the Canvas side: the earlier cases "neither exists → one account gets both" and "only the LTI account exists → the Feide identity joins it" are dropped, because they let a Canvas user pre-claim someone else's Feide ID and linked student TAs whose Feide role was unknown. A Feide account that already holds another identity from the same platform is refused (link.conflict, platform-identity-exists); that check and the write run in one transaction with the Feide account's row locked; the same person's launch arriving twice at once (a double click) is no rival and no conflict. A refusal is audited on the claimant's own account (the one the launch uses), never on the Feide account it named; a link is audited on the account the launch then uses, which is the Feide account. If the launch fails after linking, the outcome (link or refusal) is audited without an actor.
  • Consequences: No content ever changes owner through linking. A teacher who starts in Canvas is linked at the first Deep Linking launch after their first Feide login; if their Canvas account owns content by then, the two libraries stay apart (link.conflict) until a "Link with Feide" step that proves both identities exists (the AUTH-005 fallback, not built in S3). A Canvas administrator who can set login IDs on a linked platform can still join a Canvas account to an existing HVL staff account; that trust in the platform is why the flag exists.

D-064 · What the authentication audit records

  • Context: spec 02 §7 defines AuthAuditEvent(at, actorUserId?, event, ipHash).
  • Decision: Recorded events: login.feide, login.feide.failed, logout, launch.lti.author, launch.lti.failed, link.feide-lti, link.conflict; ipHash uses the D-055 key. Learner LTI launches are not recorded (volume and data minimisation). ipHash is recorded for logins, failed logins, logouts and failed launches; author launches and link outcomes carry the actor instead (a link outcome has none when its launch then fails, D-063).
  • Consequences: The owner confirms the learner rule (Q15).

D-065 · End-to-end tests in Session 3

  • Context: The EVALUATOR-GUIDE says npm run test:e2e runs journeys J1–J5 from S3, but spec 00 places J1–J5 in S6 (they need S4–S6 features). The S3 gate needs the cookie-less iframe e2e (LTI-003).
  • Decision: In S3 npm run test:e2e runs three Chromium flows: launch → play → resume in a cross-site iframe with third-party cookies blocked, the Deep Linking round trip, and portal sharing with logout. J1–J5 stay in S6; the EVALUATOR-GUIDE is corrected.
  • Consequences: The e2e tests use the mock platform and run in CI. The S3 probe (test/browser/thirdPartyCookies.browser.test.ts) fixed the mechanism: full Chromium (channel: 'chromium', not the headless shell, which ignores it) with --test-third-party-cookie-phaseout, checked by a canary. CDP Network.setCookieControls is not used: in full Chromium it misses a site-isolated frame after its first load. With Playwright's defaults the blocked frame's localStorage throws, which exercises ltijs's Platform Storage fallback; partitionedStorage: true restores stock Chrome's partitioned storage. CI must keep installing full Chromium (never --only-shell).

D-066 · Friendly "not available" pages and visibility-only sharing until S4

  • Context: PROD-004 asks for a friendly page with 404 for drafts; PROD-006 asks that visibility changes take effect immediately. Publishing (PROD-003) belongs to S4's validator flow.
  • Decision: An unknown, draft or invisible activity always gets the same "not available" page with 404, so its existence is not revealed. A portal page without a session sends the browser to Feide login with a checked returnTo. The S3 sharing API changes visibility only; every change writes an audit event.
  • Consequences: Activities are published through S4's flow (owner to confirm, Q14).

D-047 · R-01 settled: Core 1.28 and Lumi 10.0.4 run the ten real content types

  • Context: R-01 asked whether Lumi h5p-server 10.0.4 works with Core 1.28 libraries (spike steps 3–5, S2); the fallback was Core 1.27 without the Daylight theme. The Hub stayed unreachable (Q7), so the spike was carried into S4.
  • Decision: Keep Core 1.28 with Lumi 10.0.4 and the F1–F3 workarounds. Evidence (2026-10-23): the ten types at their newest Core-1.28-era releases (MultiChoice 1.16.14, Blanks 1.14.13, DragText 1.10.52, QuestionSet 1.21.13, Column 1.18.8, CoursePresentation 1.28.25, InteractiveVideo 1.28.37, InteractiveBook 1.15.1 with Column 1.22.0, ImageHotspots 1.11.6, BranchingScenario 1.10.1; 120 libraries in all, built from GitHub, D-078) install through the seed path with the S2 package checks, import with their files, save through the editor with the sub-content policy, and play on our player page in Chromium without console errors, page errors or failed requests (apps/server/test/h5p/realTypes.browser.int.test.ts). Spike step 3 (Hub registration) still waits for Q7.
  • Consequences: No downgrade to 1.27. Findings for later work: QuestionSet 1.21 announces its end feedback to screen readers but no longer shows it (relevant to PED-H11 and UD-030); several libraries' Nynorsk files leave UI strings in English or are out of step with their semantics (BranchingScenario l10n), so authors may need to correct labels; InteractiveBook 1.15 offers only Column 1.22, which has no release tag (pinned commit, D-022 rule).

D-067 · H5P runtime pages stay in Express; the Next.js app frames them

  • Context: S4 brings apps/web (Next.js), the H5P editor page (D-040) and the move of the S3 LTI views (D-048). H5P needs its own global jQuery, CSS and iframes, and UD-011/DATA-011 need a strict script policy. Next.js App Router pages always contain inline scripts, and H5P Core writes <script src> tags into its iframes, which a nonce policy with 'strict-dynamic' would block.
  • Decision: The H5P player (/h5p/play/:id, /lti/play) and editor (/h5p/edit/:id, /h5p/new, /lti/edit) stay server-rendered by Express with a hash-based policy (D-070). Next.js pages are the application chrome and frame them on the same origin: /, /aktivitet/[id], /aktivitet/ny, /app/play, /app/deeplink, /personvern, /hjelp. Amends D-048: the picker and the LTI chrome move to /app/*; the friendly error pages stay server-rendered (they need Express's 401/403/404/503 statuses) but use the token CSS. Amends D-062: the Rediger tab arrives on /app/play for authors. H5P pages refuse a top-level navigation and send the browser to their chrome page, so the privacy link (DATA-006) is always on screen.
  • Consequences: The S2/S3 player tests keep their page; e2e tests reach H5P one frame deeper. Same-origin framing does not isolate the ltik from H5P content; the script policy is the defence (D-058).
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, workstream planning): the Deep Linking picker stays the server-rendered page at /lti/deeplink from S3, restyled with the token CSS and given the formative notice (PROD-011); there is no /app/deeplink. Its form post to Canvas works today, and a Next.js picker would need a new API for the signed Deep Linking answer without adding anything for the teacher. ltijs sends resource-link launches to /app/play only when the web app runs (WEB_APP is not off); otherwise to /lti/play as in S3, so the integration tests without the web app keep their flow.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, integration): the refusal of top-level navigations is src/web/chromeRedirect.ts, mounted only when the web app runs. A browser's own navigation (Sec-Fetch-Dest: document, Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) to /h5p/play/:id or /h5p/edit/:id gets 303 to /aktivitet/:id, /h5p/new to /aktivitet/ny, and /lti/play or /lti/edit to /app/play with only the ltik carried over (no-store, no-referrer). Frames, fetches and clients without fetch metadata get the page as before, so the integration tests and older browsers are unaffected.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review): the pages Express still renders (the friendly error pages and the Deep Linking picker) show the web app's header themselves when the web app runs and they are opened on their own, in the browser or as the page of Canvas's iframe (UD-013): a skip link, the site name and Hjelp to /hjelp, which opens a new tab inside Canvas (UD-007). Inside our own chrome (the error pages of /lti/play and /lti/edit in /app/play, the not-available pages of /h5p/play and /h5p/edit in /aktivitet) the chrome's header already shows Hjelp, so a frame our own origin asked for (Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe with Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin) gets no second header; Canvas's iframe is cross-site, also after the launch's redirects. A browser without fetch metadata shows both headers, which repeats Hjelp but hides nothing. With WEB_APP=off there is no /hjelp, so there is no header. The picker lists its problems in an error summary below the heading that takes focus and links to the choices (UD-013). The editor's outer page uses the server pages' stylesheet for its save button and status (UD-002).

D-068 · Express is the front door and runs Next.js in the same process

  • Context: D-012 puts a reverse proxy in front of Express and Next.js in production. Development and tests need one origin too, and the session cookie (__Host-, D-057), ltijs's same-origin checks and PUBLIC_BASE_URL must not change.
  • Decision: Express mounts Next.js's request handler (next({ dev, dir })) after all its own routes, for GET and HEAD only. Before handing over, Express removes cookie, authorization and the ltik query from the request, overwrites any client-sent content-security-policy and x-hvli-* request headers, and sets the per-request nonce policy and x-hvli-locale. apps/web has no route handlers, server actions or middleware (a test enforces it): every data request goes from the browser to the Express API. WEB_APP=off|dev|prod selects the mode; integration tests run with off. If the in-process mount fails, the fallback is next start behind a small Express proxy with the same header code.
  • Consequences: Amends D-012 for development and tests; production may still put a proxy in front (S6). npm run build builds apps/web before npm start in production mode and before the e2e and a11y suites.
  • Probe result (2026-10-23): the in-process mount works in both modes (Turbopack for dev and build); Next.js reads the nonce from the request's content-security-policy header and puts it on every script and the stylesheet preload; pages are dynamic because the layout reads x-hvli-locale. Findings: next 16.0.0–16.4.0 carry GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw, GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r and GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr, so the pin is 16.4.2 (with React 19.3.1, one copy shared by server and app), and the image optimiser stays off (images.unoptimized); Next.js reports telemetry unless NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED is set, which the build script and the server set; the server imports Next.js through a computed specifier with its own type for the factory, because Next.js's global types make process.env.NODE_ENV read-only and would break the server's compilation; next-env.d.ts differs between dev and build in Next.js 16, so it is generated (next typegen in typecheck) and ignored, not committed.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review): the development server's WebSocket upgrades (/_next/, hot reload) get the same removal of cookie, authorization, x-hvli-* and the ltik query before Next.js sees them; any other upgrade is closed. Production refuses WEB_APP=dev, so the development server and its relaxed policy (D-070) never run there.

D-069 · Query-ltik paths and file grants for the S4 views and the editor

  • Context: D-058 accepts an ltik in a query string on four paths. S4 adds the LTI chrome pages and the editor in a cookie-less Canvas iframe, whose file URLs cannot carry a cookie.
  • Decision: The query ltik is accepted on /app/play, /app/deeplink, /lti/play, /lti/edit, /h5p/ajax and /h5p/contentUserData/*; /lti/deeplink goes away with the server-rendered picker. Express resolves the ltik on /app/* before Next.js runs and passes only the page; the page script keeps the ltik in memory and removes it from the address bar. The editor's content files get signed grants issued after an Edit check (D-058's grant, bound to the content), and uploaded temporary files get a grant over temp|userId|expiry from the same key ring.
  • Consequences: Amends D-058. The redaction and query-ltik tests cover the new paths.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23): Express resolves the ltik of /app/play inside the LTI router (an invalid one gets the friendly 401 page there), checks View, and hands the web app the request header x-hvli-launch = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ contentId, title, mayEdit, locale })) (header values must be Latin-1; titles are not). The header is removed from client requests like every x-hvli-* header, and carries no token or user ID. /app/deeplink is not built (D-067 amendment).
  • Probe result (2026-10-23): the editor page (/h5p/edit/:id, /h5p/new, /lti/edit) opens all ten real types and saves through the content API, also in the cookie-less Canvas iframe with frame storage partitioned or blocked. Upload grants use their own HKDF purpose (temporary-file-url) over the uploading account, served at /h5p/uploads/<grant>/<account>/<file>; content grants go into H5PIntegration.contents, which H5P's editor reads for saved files. Findings fixed on the way: Lumi's editor render checks no permission, so the route checks Edit before rendering or issuing a grant; Lumi lists every editor script for the outer page too, where H5P's h5peditor.js reads window.parent and fails when Canvas is that parent, so the outer page loads only H5P Core, the iframe creator and its language file, as H5P's own integrations do; H5P's getAjaxUrl lives in h5peditor-init.js, which Lumi does not load, so our boot script defines it; the editor iframe needs the page's storage stand-in where frame storage is blocked (hvliGuardFrameStorage); the editor keeps its UI state as user data of activity 0, which is now answered empty and never stored; and H5P's hub client always asks for Content Hub metadata, which D-041 refused with 403 and now answers with empty lists (still without a network request).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-4): two parts of the Decision above did not happen as written. /lti/deeplink did not go away: the picker stayed server-rendered there (D-067 amendment), so its first page load still takes the query ltik as in S3, and /app/deeplink does not exist. The query ltik is therefore accepted on the pages /app/play, /lti/play, /lti/edit and /lti/deeplink, whose routes in the LTI router resolve it themselves, and on /h5p/ajax and /h5p/contentUserData/* (LTIK_QUERY_PATHS in apps/server/src/auth/requestPrincipal.ts, which also lists the three /lti pages). Upload grants are HMAC-SHA256 with the HKDF purpose key temporary-file-url over <accountId>|<expiry>, as the probe result above says, not over temp|userId|expiry (apps/server/src/h5p/contentFileGrants.ts).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review WEBA11Y-5): activity 0 (the editor's own UI state) is still never written, but its GET answer now depends on the flag. H5P's editors read such a flag from the browser's localStorage and then let the server's answer override it (ns.storage in h5peditor.js; BranchingScenario's UserStorage). { success: true, data: false } arrives as "not set". That is right for an "important description" (Blanks, DragText), which stays open until the author closes it. It is wrong for BranchingScenario's three guided tours (h5p-editor-branching-scenario-*tour-v1-seen), which then started on every open and faded the editor (inert, D-080 amendment of review THEME-V3). Those three flags are now answered { success: false, message: 'hvl:editor-ui-state-not-kept' }, and H5P then keeps the browser's own flag. Every other flag keeps the empty answer, because an error answer for all of them would hide the important descriptions on a first open (apps/server/src/http/routes/userDataRoutes.ts). No table holds author UI preferences. Residual: in a browser that never closed the tour, or whose storage is cleared or blocked, the tour shows again. After its "I got it", focus falls to the frame's body because the tour removes its button (upstream), and the tour's repair in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/a11yEditorRepairs.js stays attribute-only. «Gå til feltet» presses the tour's "I got it" itself when a tour shows in the BranchingScenario editor (apps/server/src/h5p/render/client/editorFields.js). Tests: apps/server/test/http/userData.int.test.ts, apps/server/test/h5p/branchingTour.browser.int.test.ts (which reopens the editor after "I got it").
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review WEBA11Y-4, WEBSEC-3): x-hvli-launch may also carry language, the activity's own language tag (activityLanguage, UD-010), read after the View check (apps/server/src/lti/play/appLaunchRoutes.ts), so the Canvas page marks the title with lang when it differs from the page (WCAG 3.1.2, apps/web/src/i18n/partLanguage.ts); present but malformed means no launch (apps/web/src/lti/launchHeader.ts). The portal's content summaries and details carry the same optional language (packages/api-contract/src/content.ts), for the activity page's h1 and the links of the activity list; of the stored metadata only this tag leaves the server (apps/server/src/content/contentSummaries.ts). An activity saved without defaultLanguage reads as en, the language Lumi writes as a default on every editor save, as on the player's content container; activities from our editor and the real packages state defaultLanguage. Next.js 16 reads location into its router's canonicalUrl before the page script removes the ltik, and writes it back on every router update (refresh, hot reload); after removing the ltik the page calls replaceState once more, after Next.js's history hooks are installed, with Next.js's __NA marker left out of the state, so the router adopts the clean address (UPSTREAM, apps/web/src/features/lti/ltikFromAddress.ts). A browser test refreshes the router and checks the address (apps/server/test/web/webChrome.browser.int.test.ts).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, second verification V2-ED-1, V2-ED-2, V2-ED-3: «Gå til feltet»): three corrections. (1) The WEBA11Y-5 amendment's sentence that «Gå til feltet» presses the tour's "I got it" did not hold when the web app posts the path on the editor frame's load event (the first opening of Rediger, apps/web/src/features/activity/ActivityView.tsx) in a browser that never closed the tour: BranchingScenario asks for its tour flag with H5P.getUserData (a jQuery request) and shows the tour only once answered, which was often after the field had been opened, so the tour made it inert and focus fell to the frame's body. The path is now followed only once no request of BranchingScenario's editor is open (H5P.jQuery.active, within the same 20 s), and a tour that still shows after the field was opened is pressed and the path followed again (apps/server/src/h5p/render/client/editorFields.js). (2) A path that ends at a list (QuestionSet's questions, ImageHotspots' hotspots, Column's content) has no field-name- wrapper; the whole form stood in for it, focus went to the form's first control and nothing was said. The list's own wrapper is now found by the ID of its list element (H5P's ListEditor and VerticalTabs give it getId()), and the whole form is never counted as a field's own, so a path that ends there is announced as not reached. The code that opens what hides a field moved to its own file, apps/server/src/h5p/render/client/editorFieldReveal.js, served as a boot script before editorFields.js (apps/server/src/http/routes/staticRoutes.ts, apps/server/src/h5p/render/editorPage.ts). (3) A "not reached" status stayed on screen after a later «Gå til feltet» that reached its field (WCAG 4.1.3); each attempt now empties that text first, so a new one is announced again, while a refused save's reason stays (apps/server/src/h5p/render/client/editorPage.js). Tests: apps/server/test/h5p/editorGoToFieldEarly.browser.int.test.ts (posted on the load event in a fresh browser, four runs; the three list paths; not reached, then reached), apps/server/test/h5p/render/editorFieldChain.test.ts.

D-070 · Content Security Policy for H5P pages and Next.js pages; no YouTube

  • Context: D-039 and DATA-011 require a script policy without 'unsafe-inline' on the player page and no third-party requests. H5P Core writes one constant inline script into its iframes (h5p.js getHeadTags) and sets inline styles. The owner decided on 2026-10-23 that YouTube is not offered (it loads scripts and tracks viewers).
  • Decision: H5P pages move H5PIntegration from an inline script into a <script type="application/json"> block read by a static boot file, and send default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-<getHeadTags>'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: <EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS>; media-src 'self' blob: <EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS>; connect-src 'self'; frame-src 'self' <EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS>; font-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self' <CANVAS_ORIGINS>. A test computes the hash from the installed h5p.js, so a core update cannot drift silently. Next.js pages get a per-request nonce policy with the same first-party sources.
