EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS (for example HVL's Panopto) is the only way to allow outside media; YouTube is never listed. SPEC-DEVIATION: H5P-009 asks for nonces or SRI on every script; tags that H5P writes into its iframes cannot carry either, so they are covered by 'self' instead.
  • Consequences: A content type that needs inline handlers or eval gets a scoped, recorded exception, never 'unsafe-inline' for scripts. Inline styles stay allowed on H5P pages only.
  • Probe result (2026-10-23): all ten real types play and open in the editor under this policy with no script exception. Two changes: base-uri is 'self' instead of 'none' on H5P pages, because jQuery's HTML parser gives its scratch document a <base> with the page's own URL on every editor field (another origin stays refused); and BranchingScenario's editor embeds H5P's online tutorial (documentation.h5p.com), which the policy keeps out as intended (DATA-011); the editor works without it, and the browser test lists it so a new outside frame is noticed.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, integration of the web shell): the web pages' form-action is 'self' plus the origin of FEIDE_ISSUER. The start page's logout form posts to /auth/logout, which answers 303 to Feide's end-session endpoint, and Chromium applies form-action to that redirect as well (the web workstream's probe); with 'self' alone, logout from the web app was refused. No other directive names an outside origin.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, Panopto): the owner decided on 2026-10-23 that videos come from sources HVL allows in configuration, for example Panopto, and never YouTube. H5P.Video 1.6 plays a Panopto viewer link only through Panopto's embed API, which scripts/panopto.js inserts as a script tag for https://developers.panopto.com/scripts/v1.2.0/embedapi.min.js; under script-src 'self' such a video stayed on "loading". script-src on H5P pages therefore also lists that file as a path source (the file, not the whole developers.panopto.com origin), but only when an EXTERNAL_MEDIA_ORIGINS entry is a Panopto site (a subdomain of panopto.com or panopto.eu); a configured media origin itself never gets script rights. SECURITY: this is a third-party script on pages that hold the ltik in memory (D-058), so it is opt-in by configuration and limited to that one file; the player's iframe comes from the configured site, which frame-src already lists. Whether embedapi.min.js loads further scripts could not be checked (the file was not reachable from the build machine); if it does, Chromium reports the refusal and the video stays on "loading", and the source is widened to exactly the further file after checking it on HVL's network. SPEC-DEVIATION: H5P-009 asks for SRI on every script and DATA-011 for no third-party scripts beyond the media the author added; H5P.Video writes the tag without integrity, so SRI is impossible. A Chromium test plays a Panopto-shaped source with the request intercepted: the script loads when a Panopto site is configured and is refused when none is, and another script on developers.panopto.com stays refused.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review): font-src on H5P pages is 'self' data:: H5P.DragNBar 1.3 and 1.5 (CoursePresentation, InteractiveVideo) inline their icon font as a data: WOFF in styles/context-menu.css; a data: font reaches no other origin. The friendly portal pages (not available, error, 404, logged out) send default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; object-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self' instead of frame-ancestors 'self' alone, so DATA-011 is enforced on them too; connect-src 'self' keeps a page script's request to /auth/session working (the PROD-006 e2e flow). The WEB_APP=off start page sends the same without form-action, because its logout redirect goes on to Feide (see above). The error pages of /lti/play and /lti/edit (matched as Express routes them: with a trailing slash and in any case) may be framed by 'self' and CANVAS_ORIGINS like those pages, because /app/play frames them on our origin; launch, login and Deep Linking pages stay framed by Canvas only (LTI-003).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-1): the SPEC-DEVIATION from H5P-009 also covers our own tags on the H5P pages. The player and editor pages (apps/server/src/h5p/render/playerPage.ts, editorPage.ts) write plain <script src> and <link rel="stylesheet"> tags, with neither integrity nor a nonce, for the first scripts (/static/lti/…), the boot scripts (/h5p/boot/…), the server pages' stylesheet and Lumi's core and library lists, which on the player page include HVL's theme files (/h5p/theme/…). Like the tags H5P writes, they are allowed by 'self' (in script-src, next to Core's hash, and in style-src). Spec 01's note of 2026-10-23 that our own page tags keep integrity hashes was wrong: no code wrote one. SRI was not added, for three reasons. Every one of these files is same-origin, served by the server that sends the page and its policy, so whoever can change a file can change the hash in the page as well; SRI guards against content changing on another origin, and the only other origin is Panopto's file (amendment above). The same theme files reach the iframes H5P Core writes (for content types it embeds in an iframe, and the editor's) only through H5PIntegration.core and editor.assets, as tags without integrity, so SRI on our tags would cover some documents with H5P content and not others. A nonce would add nothing while 'self' must stay for H5P's own tags, because a script runs when any source of script-src allows it. The Next.js pages are not affected: Next.js puts the nonce on each of its scripts (D-068).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-15): with WEB_APP=dev only, the Next.js pages' policy adds 'unsafe-eval' to script-src, which React's development tools need, and allows inline styles (style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' instead of the nonce), because the development server injects style elements without one (apps/server/src/web/webPageCsp.ts). This is the "relaxed policy" of D-068's 2026-10-24 amendment. Production refuses WEB_APP=dev (apps/server/src/config/productionChecks.ts), WEB_APP=prod sends the nonce policy above unchanged, and the H5P pages' policy has no development variant.

D-071 · CC-BY-4.0 is an allowed licence (caniuse-lite)

  • Context: next depends on caniuse-lite, a browser-support data set under CC-BY-4.0, which the licence check (tools/dependency-check/checkLicences.mjs) does not list. Adding it showed that the check never saw it: D-029's npm query ':not(.dev)' drops every package that any dev tool also reaches, which left about 230 of 470 production packages unchecked since S1.
  • Decision: CC-BY-4.0 joins the allowlist. The FSF lists it as compatible with GPLv3, and the package is data, not code. A per-version exception was rejected because caniuse-lite releases weekly. Amends D-029: the check now reads npm query '*' and counts every package whose npm dev flag is false, i.e. what a production install contains. The packages that surfaced: MIT-0 (@csstools/color-helpers via jsdom) joins the allowlist; @visx/vendor (declared "MIT and ISC") is listed as reviewed; elkjs (EPL-2.0, not GPL-compatible) ships only in Prisma Studio, the GUI of the prisma CLI that production runs as its own process for migrations, and is listed by name and version as a separate program (aggregation, not a combined work).
  • Consequences: Attribution is kept by shipping the package's licence file. A new version of a listed separate program fails the check until a person reviews it again.

D-072 · Design tokens: generated CSS, a Tailwind v4 theme file and colour lint

  • Context: UD-001 makes packages/design-tokens/tokens.json the only source of colour and asks for "a Tailwind preset". Tailwind v4 configures themes in CSS (@theme); a JS preset loads only through the legacy @config.
  • Decision: A generator writes dist/tokens.css (custom properties, forced-colours overrides) and dist/tailwind-theme.css (@theme aliases to var(--hvl-*), with Tailwind's own palette removed). Both are committed and checked by npm run tokens:check, so the server needs no build step. SPEC-DEVIATION: the Tailwind "preset" is this theme file. Stylelint (color-no-hex, no colour functions or names, no uppercase or justify) and an ESLint rule against colour literals in apps/*/src and packages/*/src apply everywhere except packages/design-tokens; vendored H5P files, the mock platform and test fixtures are exempt, each with a WHY.
  • Consequences: HVL's confirmed values (Q2) change one file; the contrast test decides whether they may be used.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, W1): (a) the visually hidden feedback prefix comes from the theme's static feedbackPrefixes.js in S4, not from the xAPI bridge that UD-003 names (S6); (b) where a library already draws its own ✓/✗ for a state (MultiChoice, Blanks, DragText), that icon is the UD-003 icon and the visible prefix is the label only, so no icon is doubled; (c) the prefix language follows :lang() of the element: the UI locale on our player page, metadata.defaultLanguage in iframes Core writes, and a container lang wins; (d) Stylelint also bans color-mix() (derived shades need HVL's approval, D-017) and ignores all of tools/spec-site (the generated spec website, not product UI); (e) the generated dist/ folders are committed through package-level .gitignore files that re-include dist/; (f) H5P's own hard-coded colours remain where a library ignores Daylight (BranchingScenario 1.10 start screen); the accessibility suite decides whether they need overrides.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review A11Y-1/A11Y-2 and THEME-V1/V2/V9): the answer prefixes also cover the question types the containers offer: TrueFalse 1.8, MarkTheWords 1.11 with its missed words, SingleChoiceSet 1.11, Summary 1.10, MultiMediaChoice 0.3, and ImageHotspotQuestion 1.8 (offered by Column 1.18 and 1.22; none of the ten example packages installs it, a Hub package of Column does). They also cover MultiChoice's solution, whose filled or empty radio is no ✓/✗ and so gets the full prefix. Where a library uses the answer's pseudo-elements itself (TrueFalse, Summary, MultiMediaChoice), feedbackPrefixes.js shows its label as text (prefixOn: "label", .hvl-feedback-text), which is then both the visible and the announced prefix beside the library's own icon. SPEC-DEVIATION: UD-003 names a ::before prefix plus a visually hidden text node. ImageHotspotQuestion marks a click with a fixed 32 px circle that its image clips, so its visible label is the image's ::after (prefixPseudo: "after"), placed beside the circle with CSS anchor positioning (in the image's corner where that is not supported). Where a library styles the answer's first paragraph as :first-child (SingleChoiceSet), the label goes into that paragraph. An answer inside a radio, checkbox, option or button named by aria-label (Summary's wrong claim, MultiMediaChoice's option) does not read its content, so the script puts the label in front of that name unless the name already states the state as H5P writes it (the label's word and a full stop, Summary's "Feil. …"), and restores the name when the state ends. tokens.json pairings may name a color-mix(in srgb, …) of two tokens where an H5P library draws one (CoursePresentation's progress bar), and the contrast test fails when a pair drawn over Daylight is not declared there. The cues for where an answer goes and which tasks are answered (DragText's empty drop zone, CoursePresentation's answered-task dot, the dot also under forced colours) are in hvl-h5p-indicators.css.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review F11): SPEC-DEVIATION: UD-003's acceptance "Checked in greyscale screenshots" is not an automated check; no test renders or stores a greyscale screenshot. A grey screenshot proves nothing until a person judges it, and a stored reference image would need that judgement again after every library update (D-078). The browser tests check instead what lets a state be told apart without colour: the text prefix drawn as ::before content or as .hvl-feedback-text (with its own ✓ or ✗ where the library draws none, W1 (b) above) and announced in the accessibility tree, for the ten types and the question types they offer (apps/server/test/h5p/hvlFeedback.browser.int.test.ts, hvlFeedbackContainers.browser.int.test.ts, hvlFeedbackHotspot.browser.int.test.ts); packages/design-tokens/test/contrast.test.ts checks the colour pairs they are drawn in. The look in greyscale is a step of the manual protocol (docs/accessibility/manual-test-protocol.md §7, "Greyscale"), which HVL runs with the operating system's greyscale filter and records with the other manual results (D-079).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review NEW-1): a correction of the F11 amendment above, which says more than the tests prove. The browser tests answer in MultiChoice, Blanks and DragText, and in the question types inside QuestionSet (TrueFalse, MarkTheWords, MultiMediaChoice), Column (SingleChoiceSet, ImageHotspotQuestion) and InteractiveVideo (Summary). No browser test answers a question inside CoursePresentation, InteractiveBook or BranchingScenario; the questions there are the same libraries, and packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/feedbackPrefixesCss.test.ts checks that the target list covers each of these question types in both states. The prefix is drawn as ::before content, as the image's ::after (ImageHotspotQuestion, prefixPseudo: "after", amendment of review A11Y-1 above) or as .hvl-feedback-text. So "for the ten types and the question types they offer" should read "for the question types the ten types offer".

D-073 · The validator is pure: shape-based walk, configuration passed in

  • Context: UD-020 asks for a pure, deterministic validateContent. The S2 parameter walker needs an asynchronous semantics lookup, and spec 04 §5 keeps hint thresholds in content/laeringsdesign/hint-thresholds.yaml.
  • Decision: validateContent(input, context): context carries the thresholds and the captioned media origins, loaded and checked with zod once at start-up (a bad file stops the server). Sub-content is found by shape (an object with library: "H5P.Name x.y" and params), recursively. Rich text is parsed with htmlparser2 (synchronous, the parser sanitize-html already uses); htmlparser2 and yaml become direct, pinned dependencies. Lint forbids I/O modules under src/validation/. Rule messages live in src/validation/locales/.
  • Consequences: The second parameter is an addition to the spec's signature, not a change to its behaviour.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, W2): interpretations the rules make where spec 04 §5 and UD-021 leave room, each also in its rule's module header, for ALU to confirm: PED-H06's main path is the path from the first node that meets the most decision points without repeating a node (the search stops after 20 000 steps), and "a way back" is backwards navigation or a loop to an earlier node; PED-H08 counts learner tasks only, also in InteractiveBook chapters (which are Columns); PED-H05 also flags verdict-only wrong-answer feedback («Feil.») and reads TrueFalse's behaviour.feedbackOnWrong; SingleChoiceSet has no per-answer feedback to check; V-VID-CAPTIONS counts a track only when its kind is subtitles, captions or unset (stricter than "any text track"); PED-H01 uses a lower bound of the video length from the latest interaction time, because content.json has no duration; V-VID-TRANSCRIPT accepts any authored text or link that mentions a transcript, since H5P has no transcript field; V-HOTSPOT-ORDER accepts numbered icons or a list order that follows reading order. Findings are unique per (ruleId, path), as the acknowledgements of D-074 need.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review fixes, validator): corrections after checking the rules against the code of the installed libraries (D-078); each one is also in its rule's module header. V-HOTSPOT-ORDER checks the order in which learners meet the hotspots, and only the hotspots the player shows: from 1.10, ImageHotspots drops a hotspot whose content has no item with a library, and 1.5 drops one without content. Unless the icons are numbers, ImageHotspots (1.5, 1.10, 1.11) sorts the hotspots strictly by y, then x, before it builds the DOM (a hotspot whose x or y is 0 goes last), so the list order never reaches the learner. The rule warns when hotspots on one visual row (within 10 percentage points of height) are read right to left, or when a hotspot moved last breaks the reading order. Its remedy is to place each hotspot of a row a little lower than the one to its left, because hand-placed hotspots rarely get exactly the same height. Numbers as icons are offered only from ImageHotspots 1.11 (V-HOTSPOT-ORDER.unorderedWithoutNumbers for older versions). With numbers (1.11) the list order is kept and only hotspots with the default icon get a number, so a list with unnumbered hotspots must follow the image (V-HOTSPOT-ORDER.partlyNumbered). V-VID-CAPTIONS counts a track only when its kind is subtitles or captions: H5P.Video 1.6 does not add a track without a kind, and InteractiveVideo hands its tracks to it (V-VID-CAPTIONS.kindNotSet). V-IMG-ALT and V-IMG-ALT-LENGTH also check Dialogcards (dialogs[n].imageAltText), MemoryGame from 1.2 (cards[n].imageAlt, cards[n].matchAlt; 1.1 has no alt-text fields, and 1.2 gained them in patch 1.2.6), Collage (collage.clips[n].alt) and a shown QuestionSet cover from 1.21 (introPage.backgroundImageAltText). These have no decorative flag, so an empty alt text is an error to fix or acknowledge. V-HEADING-ORDER reads the reading texts of an H5P.Column (every InteractiveBook chapter) as one outline. V-COLOUR-WORDS leaves only a BranchingQuestion's choice texts to V-BRANCH-COLOUR. PED-H07 does not report a task's switch that its QuestionSet, CoursePresentation or InteractiveVideo forces on with override.* = "on". PED-H06 merges alternatives that lead to the same node and computes the best path on from each node on no cycle only once. A case without loops is therefore counted exactly as long as it is at most 500 nodes deep and fits the 20 000-expansion budget, which in practice limits only the search inside loops; past either bound PED-H06 reports no count rather than a guess. Message numbers are written per locale (11,5 and 1 500 in nn and nb), and PED-H01/PED-H02 round minutes up to a tenth, so a message never contradicts its threshold. Findings stay keyed on the same (ruleId, path) for unchanged content.

D-074 · Publishing: server re-validation, acknowledgements and concurrency

  • Context: PROD-003 and UD-022 let an author publish despite an error with a recorded reason, raised again after 14 days. D-066 waited for this flow.
  • Decision: GET /api/content/:id/findings returns the findings and which errors are acknowledged. POST /api/content/:id/publish takes the updatedAt it checked and acknowledgements {ruleId, path, reason}; the server validates the stored content again and never trusts the client's findings. An error is covered by an acknowledgement for the same rule and path younger than 14 days, or by one in the request; acknowledging something that is not a current error is a 400; remaining errors are 409 hvl:publish-blocked. The status change, the new acknowledgements and an audit event (rule IDs only, no reason text, DATA-007) are one transaction conditional on updatedAt (409 hvl:content-changed). POST …/unpublish returns an activity to draft. Saving an activity that is already published runs the same gate. Only those who may edit (H5P-006) may publish.
  • Consequences: Acknowledgements keyed on a path ask again when list items move; that fails safe.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, W3): every save of an existing activity increases H5PContent.version (the inventory used to say "on structural change"; since D-093's 2026-10-29 amendment only a structural save does); a refused save of a published activity is 409 hvl:published-save-blocked with the findings, and nothing is saved; findings, publish and unpublish answer 404 when the person may not view the activity and 403 hvl:edit-not-allowed when they may view but not edit; unpublish clears publishedAt, and publishing an activity that is already published validates again and moves publishedAt to now.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review fixes F-01, F-02): the save gate validates what the editor will store, not the request: HVL's sub-content policy and Lumi's semantics enforcer run on copies of the request first (apps/server/src/content/savedForm.ts), so markup the sanitiser removes (e.g. an alt text that is only <style>…</style>) is judged as removed. A save of an existing activity (gate, Lumi's write, version count) and a publish (from its read to its commit) each hold the activity's Redis lock hvli:content:write-lock:<contentId> with the ID in lower case (apps/server/src/content/ContentWriteLock.ts, writeLockKey; lease 60 s, wait 30 s, then 409 hvl:content-changed), because the save passes the ID as its URL spells it and the publish passes the stored ID; so a publish can no longer commit between the gate's status read and Lumi's write. A PostgreSQL lock was rejected because it would hold a pooled connection through the whole Lumi save, which needs connections from the same pool. Residual risk: if the gate's read and Lumi's write of the parameters were more than the 60-second lease apart, a publish could commit in between; only database reads and semantics walks lie between them, no file transfer. While Redis is unreachable, the client's offline queue holds the lock command, so a save or publish waits for Redis, as the Redis-backed session on the same request already does; it is refused only on an error answer from Redis. The saved form repeats the editor's cleaning steps; apps/server/test/content/publishedSaveRealTypes.int.test.ts compares it with what the editor stores, so a new step in HvlH5PEditor's save must be added to savedForm.ts as well.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review F1, F3, F4, F5, NEW-6): a published activity with an error that has no acknowledgement that holds (it ran out, or the error is new to a later rule; the findings show both as acknowledgement: null, so the note names neither) offers Grunngje på nytt on Sjekk og publiser, next to Gjer om til utkast: the publish dialog, labelled for new reasons, which sends the same POST …/publish (W3: it validates again and moves publishedAt). With nothing to explain it offers only Gjer om til utkast. Publish and unpublish share one button element, so keyboard focus stays on it when the status changes, and after a publish or new reasons focus is put on it again, since Grunngje på nytt goes away once every error has a reason; unpublishing runs one request at a time (aria-disabled while it runs; apps/web/src/features/activity/CheckPanel.tsx). The refusal of such a save no longer blames the change: error.publishedSaveBlocked and the editor page's page.editor.blockedSave say that some errors have no reason that holds, that a reason holds for 14 days, and how to fix, explain or unpublish; the editor page lists the errors in its error summary, each with «Gå til feltet» (apps/server/test/h5p/editorBlockedSave.browser.int.test.ts). The Canvas page has no Sjekk og publiser tab (LTI-006), so in Canvas the editor says page.editor.blockedSaveCanvas: fix the errors and save again, or explain them on the activity's page in HVL Interaktiv, which needs a Feide login.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, second verification V2-ED-4, SEC2-1, V2W-1, V2W-2): the F3 amendment's refusal texts offered «Grunngje på nytt» for every refused save. Sjekk og publiser checks the stored version, and a refused save stores nothing, so an error that the change itself adds is never listed there and «Grunngje på nytt» cannot explain it; the publish request would refuse a reason for it too. error.publishedSaveBlocked, page.editor.blockedSave and page.editor.blockedSaveCanvas (nn, nb, en) now say so by case: fix the errors and save again; an error that is also in the published version can be explained with «Grunngje på nytt» (a reason holds for 14 days); an error new in the change can be explained only by publishing: in the portal, «Gjer om til utkast», save, and publish with a reason; in Canvas, it must be fixed while the activity is published (apps/server/test/h5p/render/blockedSaveTexts.test.ts). On the tab itself, a hvl:content-changed answer to the dialog now reloads the activity as well as the findings, so renew compares the two of one moment again; and when the control that had focus goes away (Grunngje på nytt behind its dialog, Sjekk på nytt after a retry that worked), focus moves to the main action instead of body (apps/web/src/features/activity/CheckPanel.tsx, apps/web/test/features/CheckPanelFocus.test.tsx).

D-075 · Notice dismissals are stored per user

  • Context: PROD-011 remembers the formative-use notice's dismissal per user; User has no preference fields and the Redis session ends at logout.
  • Decision: A table NoticeDismissal(userId, noticeId, noticeVersion, at); a new notice version is shown again. GET /api/me and PUT /api/me/notices/:noticeId. Learners never see these notices, so no learner data is added.
  • Consequences: New rows in docs/privacy/DATA-INVENTORY.md; deleted with the account.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review fix F-03): PUT /api/me/notices/:noticeId refuses a version above NOTICE_VERSIONS[noticeId] with 400 error.badRequest, so a stored version always fits the INTEGER column and can never hide a later version of the notice in advance; an older version is stored as sent (a page left open).

D-076 · The web app's own typed translations

  • Context: UI strings exist in nn, nb and en only (CLAUDE.md). The server's messages are typed from nn.json (D-046). next-intl adds routing and middleware that D-068 does not use.
  • Decision: apps/web/src/i18n/ has the same typed t() and locales/{nn,nb,en}.json (locale-parity checked); the locale comes from Express's x-hvli-locale header (session or launch locale, else nn).
  • Consequences: No next-intl dependency; one key style across server and web.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review WEBSEC-2/F2, NEW-3, WEBA11Y-1/DOC-2): the locale is the launch's, else an allowlisted ?lang= (nn, nb, en; any other value or a repeated parameter is ignored), else the portal session's, else nn (apps/server/src/web/webRoutes.ts). The web app's Hjelp and Personvern links carry the page's locale (apps/web/src/config/paths.ts infoHref), and so does Hjelp on the server-rendered pages (apps/server/src/http/pages/htmlPage.ts), because inside Canvas they open a new tab without the launch, and portal sessions are always Nynorsk; without it the nb and en privacy notices (DATA-006) were unreachable. Every page but the start page now has its own title, " – HVL Interaktiv" (WCAG 2.4.2, apps/web/src/i18n/pageTitle.ts); the start page is titled "HVL Interaktiv", and the activity page is titled "Aktivitet – HVL Interaktiv" until the activity has loaded, then "<activity's title> – HVL Interaktiv". Tests: apps/server/test/web/webChrome.browser.int.test.ts (an English launch's links open English pages; each route's title), apps/web/test/features/ActivityView.test.tsx.

D-077 · API schemas in packages/api-contract and an OpenAPI document

  • Context: DOC-012 (moved from S3) asks for zod request and response schemas and an OpenAPI document at /api/docs in development. The web app becomes the first client of the API.
  • Decision: packages/api-contract holds the zod schemas the server validates with and the web app types against. The OpenAPI 3.1 document is built from them with zod 4's own z.toJSONSchema, served at /api/docs when NODE_ENV is not production, and a test checks that every /api route is listed.
  • Consequences: No OpenAPI library is added.

D-078 · Real H5P libraries from GitHub at pinned commits

  • Context: hub-api.h5p.org and github.com's web pages are unreachable from the build environment (Q7), but git reaches public GitHub repositories. Without real content types, UD-003, UD-011 and UD-030 would be tested on stand-ins only, and R-01 (D-047) stays open.
  • Decision: tools/h5p-libraries (npm run h5p:fetch-libraries) clones each library's repository at a commit pinned in a committed manifest (repository, tag, commit SHA), resolves library.json dependencies recursively, builds libraries whose built files are not committed (npm ci --ignore-scripts and their build script), and packs one .h5p per content type with our own example content into the gitignored apps/server/var/h5p-real/. The packages are installed through the admin package import, so the S2 package checks run on them. Library files are not committed (Q10 stays open); synthetic libraries remain for unit tests.
  • Consequences: Versions can differ from what the Hub serves; the Hub packages (D-042) replace them when Q7 is resolved. A type that cannot be assembled stays synthetic and is listed in PROGRESS. SPEC-DEVIATION: H5P-003 seeds from packages downloaded from the Hub; these are built from H5P's own repositories at pinned commits and serve development, tests and CI until the Hub is reachable.
  • Amendment (2026-10-23, probe 1): the H5P registry (github.com/h5p/h5p-registry, pinned) maps machine names to repositories. The resolver follows required dependencies and, as optional, the sub-content types each library's semantics offers (without them InteractiveBook could not save its own pages): 120 libraries, 23 of them built with webpack; 39 offered old versions are skipped and listed in the manifest (their dependencies are not in the registry, or they need a build without a lockfile). Three libraries have no matching release tag and are pinned to a reviewed commit (D-022 rule). Network errors are retried and never cause a skip. Builds run outside the repository, because a library's build otherwise picks up this repository's TypeScript configuration. Installing the first real package showed that S2's narrowed contentWhitelist (SEC-002) also applied to library folders through Lumi's libraryWhitelist, so every real package, from GitHub or the Hub, was refused for its icon fonts: libraryWhitelist now adds eot ttf woff woff2 otf (library folders only; content files keep the SEC-002 list).

D-079 · What S4 verifies automatically and what HVL records by hand

  • Context: NFR-003 names the last two versions of four browsers and three screen readers; UD-031 asks for dated manual results. The build environment has Chromium only and no assistive technology.
  • Decision: CI runs the axe suite and the browser checks in Chromium. docs/accessibility/manual-test-protocol.md scripts the manual tasks and the browser/assistive-technology matrix; HVL/ALU record dated results in docs/accessibility/results/. The S4 gate lists what remains manual.
  • Consequences: Firefox, Safari, Edge and the screen-reader results stay open until HVL runs the protocol.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-7): docs/TRACEABILITY.md lists UD-031 and NFR-003 as "tested" because apps/server/a11y/accessibilityDocs.a11y.test.ts carries their IDs. That test checks that the protocol, the matrix and the results README agree with each other, and it passes while no result is recorded. We accept this mechanical status and do not give spec-trace a special case for the two. The traceability legend defines "tested" as "at least one test title carries the ID". spec:trace --check --done-through=S4 must still count both as covered, because this decision leaves their manual results to HVL and outside the S4 gate. A status kept by hand inside the generator would be a second record of what PROGRESS already tracks, and nothing would clear it once HVL records results. The open work is the unchecked S4 item "First manual run of the protocol and the matrix" in PROGRESS.md. The matrix (§1, §3), the Evaluator Guide (§2, limitation 15) and tools/spec-trace/README.md say what "tested" means for these two.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 6: the conformance report, UD-040): the split of this decision continues inside docs/accessibility/WCAG-CONFORMANCE-REPORT.md, which npm run a11y:report (tools/a11y-report/) writes with one section for each WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion: 56, counting 4.1.1 Parsing, which WCAG 2.2 marks obsolete but WCAG 2.1 and EN 301 549, on which the Norwegian regulation rests, still list.
    • Generated parts: per criterion, how it is tested (the axe rules that carry the criterion's tag in the axe-core that @axe-core/playwright runs, under the suite's own tags, without the rules axe excludes by default; our own checks by requirement ID and suite file), which views, the result of the last full run of npm run test:a11y, links to the tests, the manual protocol's steps and §7 checks for it, and the upstream entries of apps/server/a11y/support/upstreamRegister.ts it concerns, with their issue links (none filed yet, D-112). Also a summary table, the dated manual results in docs/accessibility/results/, the register in full, and an appendix of the last run. The mapping from criterion to our checks is data in the tool, reviewed like code; a protocol step it names must exist in the protocol, or the generator stops.
    • Manual parts: text between <!-- manual:start <id> --> and <!-- manual:end <id> -->: per criterion the verdict (Supports, Partially supports, Does not support, Not applicable or Not yet determined) and the manual evidence; and the scope, the assistive-technology runs, the cognitive review, the barriers axe cannot see and the notes for the uustatus.no statement. The generator copies each block as it is; it stops on a broken, duplicate or unknown marker, a missing verdict line or an unknown verdict instead of dropping or guessing text, and seeds a missing block with Not yet determined and Not yet tested by HVL. No verdict is derived from the automated results: axe and our checks find only part of the barriers (the protocol's §1), so a Supports from them would overstate; the summary table copies the verdict people wrote.
    • Determinism: a run enters through a distilled, committed summary, docs/accessibility/automated-run.json (--from-run=<dir> reads Vitest's JSON report and the axe JSON lines of A11Y_REPORT_DIR; --run runs the suite first and needs npm run build). The report carries no time except the run's date and commit from that summary, so regenerating an unchanged tree gives the same file, and --check fails when the committed report differs from what its sources give: the gate's «regenerates the automated parts unchanged» (D-113). A new test file whose title opens with a mapped ID, a new suite or a new register entry therefore needs a regeneration in the same commit, as docs/TRACEABILITY.md does.
    • Alternatives considered: (a) reading the raw run outputs on every regeneration: a fresh checkout could not regenerate the report, and two runs never give the same file; (b) one table for all criteria: the manual blocks need a place per criterion; (c) a status kept in spec-trace: rejected above for UD-031, for the same reason.
    • Consequences: UD-040's tests (tools/a11y-report/test/, [UD-040]) are its document check under D-113: the manual blocks survive a regeneration byte for byte, two regenerations give the same file, every criterion is listed and the committed report's blocks parse. HVL's evaluation of each criterion stays open until HVL acts.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 6 review of the UD-040 generator): the review found four ways in which the report could say more than is true. They are closed as follows.
    • A failed file is a failure. Vitest 5 reports a file whose hook (beforeAll, e.g. the browser or the services not starting) or import failed as failed, with its tests skipped or none at all; the summary then said "0 failed". The summary (format 2) now records such files in failedFiles, the report names them in the run's header, in the criterion lines of their checks and in appendix A, and --from-run exits 1 for a failed run, as --run does. A run is "clean" only when git status --porcelain shows nothing, untracked files included, since an untracked test or source file changes what ran.
    • Only the whole suite is "the last full run". --from-run and --run refuse, writing nothing, a run that lacks a suite file with running tests (a run of one file or a filtered folder), and a run with two suite files of the same path. Files are keyed by their path under apps/server/a11y/.
    • No HVL verdict without a dated HVL evaluation. A criterion block whose verdict is not Not yet determined needs the line **Evaluated by HVL:** beginning with a date (YYYY-MM-DD), and a block holds one verdict line only; otherwise the generator stops. So the summary's «Verdict (HVL)» column never shows a verdict that no dated evaluation stands behind, nor one of two contradicting lines.
    • No text is lost to a marker the parser does not see. Markers are found whatever their letter case (a <!-- Manual:start … --> stops the generator instead of its block being rewritten as generated text), and the composed report is read back before it is returned: it must give exactly the blocks that went in, byte for byte.

D-080 · H5P markup barriers: repaired in the page where we can, registered where we cannot

  • Context: UD-030 lets CI fail on any serious or critical axe violation on every route and inside each type's iframe. The suite found such violations in H5P's own markup (player, editor and the content-type list): empty links, role="tab" items inside <li>, inputs without labels, drop zones with aria-label but no role. They come from the pinned upstream libraries (D-078), which we do not fork; UD-040 already expects known upstream limitations to be listed with links.
  • Decision: Barriers that a local, attribute-only change can remove without changing behaviour are repaired at run time inside H5P documents by packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/a11yRepairs.js, loaded like feedbackPrefixes.js into player and editor iframes: it adds names, roles and labels, and re-applies them when H5P rebuilds the markup (MutationObserver). It never removes H5P's own handlers, focus order or content. Every barrier the suite still finds is an entry in apps/server/a11y/support/upstreamRegister.ts, matched by rule and markup, with the reason and a link to the upstream source at the pinned commit; an entry that stops occurring fails the suite, so the register cannot hide a fixed problem or a new one. SPEC-DEVIATION: UD-030 says CI fails on any serious or critical violation; registered upstream violations are reported in every run but do not fail CI. Our own pages (the web app and the server-rendered pages) have no registered entries.
  • Consequences: The register is the list for the UD-040 conformance report (S6) and for issues to file upstream. A library update (D-078) re-runs the suite: a repair that no longer matches shows up as a new failure.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, repairs): a11yRepairs.js repairs eight barriers, each read against the pinned upstream code. (1) CoursePresentation's progress bar becomes a list of links (role="list"/"listitem", the current slide's link aria-current="step", a link without text named by its part's aria-label, the slide title). The parts keep that aria-label, which H5P.Tooltip shows, so they cannot become presentational for a valid tab structure. aria-selected is dropped from the list items, and so is the summary slide's aria-controls, which points at no element (cp.js creates that slide without an index, id="slide-undefined"). The slides, which H5P writes as the role="tabpanel" of those tabs, become groups still named by their part. The links keep H5P's roving tabindex: one of them is in the Tab order and the arrow, Home and End keys move between them, which the list no longer announces (manual protocol §8). (2) DragText's drop zones get role="group", not button, because a dropped word (a button) sits inside them. (3) The score-range "to" field is labelled by the column heading, the row's "from" value and the dash, for example "Poengområde* 51 % –" in MultiChoice; the "" is H5P's required marker, which the name of every required field in H5P's editor carries ("Tittel"). (4) The editor's vertical tabs become a list of buttons, the open item aria-current, because a tab list may not hold the items' remove and order buttons; their forms (<fieldset role="tabpanel">) lose the role and are native groups. (5) The editor-mode switch becomes a group named by its title, the active mode aria-pressed. (6) The hotspot picker's copy of the background image gets alt="". (7) DragNBar's paste button gets its tooltip text as its name: "Paste", which DragNBar 1.5 leaves untranslated in nn and nb (a translation gap to report upstream and to list for UD-040). (8) The hub's content-type list becomes a group named by its heading. What attributes cannot remove stays recorded. The hub's nested-interactive entry (tabs and content types) stays in the register: the tabs' focus and Enter belong to the inner link, the hub's CSS lays them out by [role=tab], and each content type is a button that holds its own Details button. Two keyboard barriers that axe cannot see (WCAG 2.1.1, UD-006): QuestionSet's editor-mode switch cannot be used by keyboard (Enter and Space do nothing; tabindex="1"), and the vertical-tab buttons open with Space only, not Enter. apps/server/test/h5p/a11yRepairs.browser.int.test.ts holds an upstream pin: test for each (DOC-004), so a library update that fixes one fails there and this record is updated; both belong on the UD-040 upstream list. The theme sizes CoursePresentation's progress-bar parts to 24 px itself, since they are no longer [role=tab] (UD-005). The theme also removed two register entries: under forced colours it sets the text fill of BranchingScenario's controls, so the forced-colours "measurement artefact" entry is gone, and while BranchingScenario's guided tour is open the parts it fades are inert (amendment of review THEME-V3 below), so the tour entry, whose pattern matched any element, is gone too. No entry may match a bare element (apps/server/a11y/upstreamRegister.a11y.test.ts). The editor's disabled «Paste» item stays registered in both colour modes, after the tour only, because its opacity: .5 also fades it in a contrast theme (3.94:1). Of the register's 15 entries before the repairs, 2 remain. Tests: packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/a11yRepairs.test.ts, apps/server/test/h5p/a11yRepairs.browser.int.test.ts, apps/server/a11y/upstreamRegister.a11y.test.ts.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, review THEME-V3): one repair changes focus order. While BranchingScenario's editor tour shows a step, H5P fades the rest of the editor (.tour-fade: opacity 0.15, pointer-events: none) but leaves it reachable by keyboard and screen readers, where its text and focus ring are all but invisible. a11yRepairs.js makes each faded part inert for as long as it has the class (marked data-hvl-inert, so only those parts are given back), as H5P's own pointer-events: none intends; the tour's dialog is never inside a faded part. The theme no longer keeps the faded parts at full opacity: that hid the spotlight while clicks there still did nothing. axe skips inert content, so the tour adds no register entry; the reuse panel with the Paste item is faded too, so the Paste entry applies after the tour only (tour: false).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-9): a third keyboard barrier that axe cannot see (WCAG 2.1.1, UD-006): ImageHotspots' hotspot position picker (H5PEditor.ImageCoordinateSelector 1.2.7, scripts/image-coordinate-selector.js) is a <div> with a click handler only, with no tabindex, no key handler and no x or y field, and a new hotspot starts at 50 % / 50 %. A keyboard-only author can add a hotspot but cannot move it. Attributes cannot add the missing input, so the barrier stays as H5P wrote it (repair 6 only gives the picker's copy of the image alt=""); the manual protocol (§8) names it, and it belongs on the UD-040 upstream list with the other two. It has no upstream pin: test of its own yet: the repairs' browser test file has 199 of its 200 lines (DOC-007), so the pin needs a file of its own; until it has one, the manual protocol is where the barrier is checked.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-13): no upstream issue has been filed for any repair or register entry. Filing them belongs to the UD-040 work (S6), from this record and the register. SPEC-DEVIATION: DOC-003 asks an UPSTREAM tag for a link to the upstream issue; until an issue exists, each tag links the library source at the pinned commit (D-078 manifest), and the issue link replaces it once the issue is filed. A repair can be removed once a pinned version of its library (version pinned now in brackets) writes itself what the repair adds: (a) CoursePresentation (1.28.25) a progress bar that is a list of named links, not a tab list of <div>s, and (b) slides that are no role="tabpanel"; (c) H5P.Components (1.0.99, DragText's drop zones) a role on the drop zone; (d) H5PEditor.RangeList (1.0.13) a label on the "to" field; (e) H5PEditor.VerticalTabs (1.3.16) no role="tablist" around items that hold other buttons and no role="tabpanel" on their forms; (f) the H5P editor (D-022 commit) a mode switch that is a named group whose active mode is pressed; (g) H5PEditor.ImageCoordinateSelector (1.2.7) an alt on its copy of the image; (h) H5P.DragNBar (1.5.23) a name on the paste button; (i) the hub client (in the H5P editor) a content-type list that is a list of items or a named group; (j) H5PEditor.BranchingScenario (1.5.13) a tour that makes the parts it fades inert. A repair is removed together with its expectations in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/a11yRepairs.test.ts and apps/server/test/h5p/a11yRepairs.browser.int.test.ts, and npm run test:a11y must then still pass. A register entry needs no such condition: an entry that stops occurring fails the suite (Decision above).
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-13, tests of (j)): repair (j), the tour, is not tested in the two files the amendment above names. Its expectations are in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/a11yRepairsTour.test.ts and apps/server/test/h5p/branchingTour.browser.int.test.ts, and the axe scan of the BranchingScenario editor with the tour open is in apps/server/a11y/axeEditor.a11y.test.ts. Removing (j) removes or adjusts those.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, pin): the position picker now has its upstream pin: test, apps/server/test/h5p/upstreamPins.browser.int.test.ts, so the DOC-9 amendment's "no upstream pin: test of its own yet" no longer holds. The pin presses arrow keys, Enter and Space on the picker in the real editor and expects the hotspot not to move, then clicks as a positive control; a library update that gives the picker keyboard input fails it.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review DOC-13 and NEW-1: repair (k) and the editor's own file): the repairs are now two files, one per surface, loaded in this order into every H5P document after feedbackPrefixes.js (apps/server/src/h5p/h5pAssets.ts). packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/a11yRepairs.js repairs the content types' markup: (a) to (c) of the DOC-13 amendment and (k) below. packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/a11yEditorRepairs.js repairs H5P's editor, its widgets, DragNBar, the hub's list and BranchingScenario's tour: (d) to (j), so it is also the file that makes the tour's faded parts inert (amendment of review THEME-V3), which the Decision and the earlier amendments credit to a11yRepairs.js. The jsdom tests follow the split: (a) to (c) and (k) are in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/a11yRepairs.test.ts, (d) to (i) in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/test/a11yEditorRepairs.test.ts (not in a11yRepairs.test.ts, as the DOC-13 amendment says), and a11yRepairsTour.test.ts loads a11yEditorRepairs.js. A ninth barrier is repaired, (k): H5P.Question (1.5.47, scripts/explainer.js) writes the title of the explanation shown after a check (DragText's "Forklaring") as role="heading" without the aria-level that ARIA 1.2 requires (axe aria-required-attr, critical). a11yRepairs.js gives it level 2, because the player document has no heading of its own and the page around it gives the activity's title as its h1. It can be removed once a pinned H5P.Question writes a heading level itself; it is removed together with its case in a11yRepairs.test.ts, and the axe scan of DragText answered (apps/server/a11y/axeContentTypes.a11y.test.ts) must still pass. No upstream issue is filed for (k) either.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, final review NEW-4: CoursePresentation's bar): the 24 px progress-bar parts of the repairs amendment above lay over CoursePresentation's footer. The bar (.h5p-cp-navigation) is 3 % of the player's height, 5 px at 320 CSS px wide, and the parts' links (z-index: 3) covered «Vis sidemeny», «Neste side» and «Fullskjerm» at 320 and 640 px wide, so a pointer could not press them (WCAG 1.4.10, 2.5.8). A taller bar alone was clipped by the player's overflow: hidden. Outside full screen the theme now gives the bar room and the player grows by what that adds: .h5p-wrapper is content-box with padding-bottom: max(0px, 24px - 1.6875%) (CoursePresentation 1.28 keeps its height at 9/16 of its width, so 3 % of the height is 1.6875 % of the width), the bar and its parts are at least 24 × 24 px, and the summary slide's part keeps its 2.2em but at least 24 px (packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/hvl-h5p-theme.css, with a removal condition). apps/server/a11y/reflowAndMotion.a11y.test.ts checks with a pointer that nothing covers a footer control at 320 × 640 and 640 × 320, and apps/server/a11y/targetSize.a11y.test.ts measures the parts with every other target of the player. Residual: in full screen, which H5P fits to the screen, the bar stays H5P's own. Its parts then cover nothing, but on a phone they are 5 to 10 px high, below 2.5.8's size and spacing; UD-005 is met there only through 2.5.8's equivalent-control exception, because the side menu and the previous and next buttons, which the theme's 24 px rule for buttons covers, reach every slide. No automated test opens full screen; the manual protocol (§8) checks it.
  • Amendment (2026-10-24, second verification V2T-1, V2T-2, V2T-3: CoursePresentation's footer): the NEW-4 amendment above is corrected. Its fix gave the bar room, but the footer stayed 7 % of the player's height (11 to 15 px on a phone) with 24 to 29 px controls, so their top lay under the bar's links and the player's overflow: hidden cut off their bottom: a pointer reached «Neste side» in 15 × 11 px at 320 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8, UD-005). The footer's middle column (20 %) was also narrower than the slide buttons, and the navigation around them (H5P.Components 1.0, a size container with overflow: hidden) cut 7 to 9 px off each. The sentence "checks with a pointer that nothing covers a footer control" was true of one point per control only, and "its parts then cover nothing" in full screen was false: there the bar's 5 to 7 px links lay over the top of the footer's controls, so no control met 2.5.8 itself and the equivalent-control exception did not apply. QuestionSet's dot spacing moved to the same file. apps/server/a11y/support/pointerReach.ts now tries every pixel of a control and requires the points that reach it to span 24 rows and 24 columns; apps/server/a11y/reflowAndMotion.a11y.test.ts runs it at 320 × 640, 640 × 320 and 390 × 844, in the page and in full screen, on the slide where both slide buttons work, and apps/server/a11y/targetSize.a11y.test.ts measures CoursePresentation's targets at 320 × 640 and 390 × 844. The accessibility suite now moves to CoursePresentation's question slide with a real pointer click on «Neste side» (apps/server/a11y/support/views.ts). The manual protocol (§8) still confirms the slides can be reached in full screen on a phone. Remove the rules when a pinned CoursePresentation gives its bar and footer 24 px.
