D-081 · One Node.js system with Lumi's H5P server half; an official PHP server half was considered and not chosen

  • Context: H5P has a browser half (Core and the editor client) and a server half (storing content, installing libraries, the editor's AJAX, the Hub). We run H5P's official browser half unchanged (Core 1.28.0, editor commit ab2daa18, D-022) and Lumi's Node.js server half, @lumieducation/h5p-server@10.0.4 (D-002), which was built for Core 1.27. That costs us adapters: the config factory's Core 1.28 and hub-api.h5p.org settings, the 15-character local_id and the non-200 /v1/sites answer (spec 01 §1), Daylight's CSS that Lumi leaves out of the asset lists, our own Edit check before Lumi renders the editor (D-069), our own file security for CVE-2025-7062, which is Lumi's, not H5P's (D-003), and S6's data-subject tool deleting learner state through the storage (Lumi's deleteAllContentUserDataByUser deletes the acting user's data). The owner asked (2026-10-24) whether the H5P part could run on H5P's official server half in PHP instead, beside our Node.js system. That half is h5p-php-library with h5p-editor-php-library: a library, not a server; a host implements dozens of framework functions (about 60 in H5PFrameworkInterface, plus the editor's storage and AJAX interfaces) for its database, files, users and permissions, as the Moodle, WordPress and Drupal plugins do.
  • Decision: Keep one Node.js/TypeScript system with Lumi's server half. Reasons: (1) Sign-in and permissions stay in one process. The ltik travels as a Bearer header in a cookie-less Canvas frame and lives in memory only (LTI-003, D-069); Feide sessions, CSRF and the View/Edit decisions (D-066) are made in one place. A PHP half would need every H5P request's identity and rights handed across a second service, a new security seam inside exactly the frames S3 and S4 hardened. (2) Privacy is enforced in one place: learners as HMAC pseudonyms (DATA-002), the yearly purge (DATA-003), the data inventory checked against one schema (DATA-001), k-suppression (INS-006). A PHP half would store learner state in its own tables and on local disk by default (H5PDefaultStorage), so each rule would be built and checked twice. (3) One language, runtime, deployment and set of checks for HVL IT to run, and one test suite. (4) The validator (D-073), the publish flow (D-074), the læringsdesign studio (S5) and the grade bridge (S6) read and write H5P content directly, inside the same transactions and locks (D-074's write lock). (5) The browser half, where H5P's behaviour and markup live, is already H5P's own. The accessibility barriers are in the content types and Core (D-080) and stay with either server half, and so does Core writing unescaped markup (D-039, D-070). (6) Lumi's server half works with Core 1.28 and the ten real types under these adapters (D-047), and a browser test replays them after every library change (D-078). A PHP half would mean redoing most of S2–S4's H5P work (D-035…D-080: permissions, upload security, the ten types, the editor in Canvas, the strict page policy, file grants).
  • Lumi's state (checked 2026-10-24): npm's latest is still 10.0.4 (2025-03-08), but the repository's master is active: about 620 commits since that release, the newest on 2026-10-13. Unreleased changes that concern us: "buffer sanitizer and malware scanners and many other improvements in file security checks" (#4600, 2026-09-06), "accept SVG uploads with an XML prolog" (2026-10-04) and "reject packages with unsatisfied library dependencies" (#4625, 2026-10-06). Recheck: npm view @lumieducation/h5p-server time and the repository's commit log.
  • Consequences: We keep carrying the adapters and the security work above, each marked UPSTREAM: or SPEC-DEVIATION: in code. S6 adds a checklist item: ask Lumi's maintainers for a release, or review and pin a Lumi commit built from source as D-022 pins the editor (a change to the CLAUDE.md invariant "h5p-server@10.0.4 ↗ (opens external site)", so it needs its own decision and the full gate), then remove the adapters it makes unnecessary; report our fixes and the D-080 barriers upstream to Lumi and H5P.
  • Revisit when: Lumi's repository has no commit for 12 months; a serious security flaw in Lumi can be neither fixed nor contained in our code; a Core version Lumi cannot support becomes necessary; or HVL decides to run regular H5P (h5p.com or a Moodle or WordPress installation) and give up the HVL-specific parts.

D-082 · The studio's content pipeline: files in content/, loaded and checked at start-up

  • Context: Spec 04 puts the phase labels, the guide, the patterns and the portfolio template in files that ALU edits without code (PED-001, PED-011, MAPPE-002). The web app reads no files (D-068), and the server already loads the hint thresholds from content/ at start-up and refuses a bad value by name (D-073, config/validationContext.ts). ALU has not yet confirmed the proposals in docs/reference/proposals/.

  • Decision: The studio's content lives in:

    • content/laeringsdesign/phases.yaml: the proposal (status: proposed), plus each phase's pedagogical purpose and Canvas placement for the phase matrix (spec 04 §3). The recommended patterns per phase come from the patterns' own phase field, so the matrix and the catalogue cannot disagree.
    • content/laeringsdesign/references.yaml: reference key → the full reference, with a verify flag until ALU has checked it.
    • content/laeringsdesign/guide.{nn,nb,en}.md (D-083).
    • content/laeringsdesign/patterns/<id>/pattern.yaml and skeleton.json, or skeleton.<type>.json for a pattern with two content types (D-084).
    • content/mappe/template.{nn,nb,en}.md and content/mappe/criteria.{nn,nb,en}.yaml (D-094).

    The server loads all of it once at start-up, checks it with strict zod schemas and freezes it; any error stops the start with a message that names the file and the key, as D-073 does. The checks:

    • every text exists in nn, nb and en; unknown and repeated keys are refused;
    • the three guides have the same headings (by level and order), markers and citation keys in the same order;
    • the three templates have the same template variables, and the three criteria files the same criteria IDs;
    • every reference key cited by a guide or a pattern exists;
    • every skeleton names its main library with a version (H5P.X a.b) that the pinned library list of D-078 contains.

    npm run content:check runs the same loader without starting the server; CI runs it, and lint-staged runs it when a file under content/ is staged. The web app gets the content as read-only JSON from /api routes. While phases.yaml says status: proposed, the studio pages show a banner saying the texts are a draft awaiting ALU.

  • Consequences: Renaming a label is a content change (PED-001). A library that is pinned but not installed makes its patterns unavailable at runtime (D-085), not a boot failure. The shared YAML error reporting moves out of validationContext.ts into the new loader's folder, apps/server/src/learningDesign/content/.

  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W2a): skeleton versions are checked by content:check against the installed libraries' own semantics (the main library is the newest installed minor; each sub-content is a version its field offers), which CI runs after h5p:fetch-libraries. The server's start-up checks only the H5P.X a.b form, not the pinned list; a skeleton naming a library that is not installed is answered 409 hvl:pattern-unavailable at creation instead.

  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration of the accessibility suite): a reference in references.yaml states the language it is written in (language, a language tag such as nb; English when left out, as most research is), the contract's Reference carries it, and the guide and pattern pages give the reference's text that lang when it differs from the page's (UD-010, WCAG 3.1.2): on a Nynorsk page an English reference was read with Norwegian pronunciation. A malformed tag is refused by content:check. mogelvang2025 is in Bokmål and says nb.

D-083 · SPEC-DEVIATION PED-002: the guide is CommonMark Markdown, not MDX

  • Context: PED-002 puts the guide in guide.{nn,nb,en}.mdx. MDX is compiled to JavaScript, so a content file becomes code: ALU could break the build or run script, and the web app bans dangerouslySetInnerHTML and reads no files (D-068). The guide needs headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, the "what this means for your activity" boxes, citations and the places where the phase matrix and the catalogue go.

  • Decision: The guide is CommonMark, parsed on the server by markdown-it 14.3.3 with html: false, into a closed tree of nodes: heading, paragraph, list, list item, text, strong, emphasis, link, box, citation and marker. React renders the tree; links go through the existing ExternalLink component; there is no innerHTML. Conventions:

    • a line that is only {{phase-matrix}} or {{pattern-catalogue}} places that component;
    • a blockquote becomes the box, a <section> with its own heading «Kva dette betyr for aktiviteten din» (from the locale files);
    • a citation is [@key], resolved against references.yaml, and the page ends with the references it cites;
    • headings start at ##, because the page's h1 comes from the locale files.

    Raw HTML, images, tables, code and links other than https:, mailto: and same-site paths are refused by the loader, naming the file and line.

  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION in spec 04 (PED-002, PED-011) and CLAUDE.md §2 ("ALU-editable YAML/Markdown"). content/laeringsdesign/README.md documents the conventions for ALU.

  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probe P5): html: false cannot refuse raw HTML by line: markdown-it then emits no HTML tokens, and <script> reaches the tree as visible text. The guide builder therefore parses with a fresh MarkdownIt({ html: true, linkify: false, typographer: false }), only reads the tokens (it never calls render), and refuses every token type outside its closed allowlist, so html: true opens no HTML path:

    • Allowed: heading_open at level 2 or 3 written with # (a setext heading made with === or --- is refused, because ALU may mean a rule), paragraph, bullet and ordered list (the start number is ignored), list item, blockquote (the box), and inline text, strong, emphasis, link and soft break (rendered as a space).
    • Refused, naming the file and line: html_block, html_inline, image, table, fenced and indented code, inline code, rule, strikethrough, hard break, a level-1 or level-4+ heading, {{ outside a marker line, and reference definitions (found in env.references; they would silently turn citations into links).
    • Links: md.validateLink lets every link through and the builder checks the href itself: https: and mailto: ignoring case, or a same-site path that starts with / but not //. A title attribute is dropped. markdown-it would otherwise drop javascript: links silently and let http: and data:image through.
    • Lines: a block uses map[0] + 1; an inline token uses its paragraph's start line plus the line breaks before it, which is exact unless a link destination spans lines, so such a link is refused.
    • Prose: an ALU author who writes < before a letter gets an error and writes &lt; instead.

  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W1a):

    • No guide yet: the three guide files are optional until written: all three absent is "no guide yet" (the guide route answers no nodes and no references, so the contract's Guide.nodes may be empty, and the page shows the phase matrix and the catalogue alone); one or two present is an error naming each missing file.
    • Markers: each marker stands exactly once in each language, since the page shows each component once and the catalogue's section id must be unique; a missing marker would hide the catalogue (PED-003). The matrix has its own caption and the catalogue its own heading.
    • Links: a same-site path is also refused when it decodes to // or /\ (for example /%2F%2Fhost), and a link whose text is empty or only spaces is refused, since nobody could see or name it.
    • Patterns: each pattern's whyItWorks is built with the same tree builder in prose mode (paragraphs and lists only) and checked when the pattern folder loads, so the pattern route never meets a text it cannot build.
    • Routes: GET /api/studio (phases, anchor, status and the catalogue with each pattern's available, asked per request), GET /api/studio/guide/:locale and GET /api/studio/patterns/:patternId, public (auth: 'none'); an unknown pattern or language is 404 error.notFound.
    • Phase matrix: the phases are columns with the samling as a column between the first and the second, and each phase has a link that filters the catalogue by it (spec 04 PED-002 §4: "a filter by phase that also filters the pattern catalogue"); the filters live only in the address. Following that link moves focus to the catalogue's heading, because a Next.js link scrolls to #monsterkatalog but leaves focus on the link.

  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration of stage 3): the public GET /api/studio and GET /api/studio/patterns/:patternId keep each pattern's availability for 60 seconds (learningDesign/http/patternAvailabilityMemo.ts), because working it out builds every skeleton and these routes need no sign-in ("asked per request" above now means within that minute). Requests that arrive during a build share it, and a failure is never kept. A library installed or removed shows in the catalogue within a minute; creating an activity always checks the libraries itself. Each guide box is a region named by its own heading and the guide heading it follows, so the three mechanisms' boxes have distinct names.

D-084 · SPEC-DEVIATION spec 04 §4: pattern skeletons live in content/, with text tokens and pinned versions

  • Context: Spec 04 §4 puts the skeletons in apps/server/src/patterns/skeletons/, but PED-011 asks that a new pattern needs no code change, and ALU edits content/. A skeleton holds H5P parameters, and its texts must exist in three languages. Creating content on the server lacks the editor's localised semantics defaults and subContentIds.
  • Decision: Each pattern is a folder content/laeringsdesign/patterns/<id>/ with pattern.yaml (the fields of PED-010 and the texts in nn, nb and en) and its skeleton JSON. The skeleton names its main library as H5P.X a.b, pinned to the versions of D-078. A text in the skeleton is a token {{key}} resolved from pattern.yaml in the language the author chooses; the value is plain text and is HTML-escaped on insertion, as H5P stores text fields. At creation the server:
    • fills in the fields the skeleton leaves out with the library's localised semantics defaults (a port of tools/h5p-libraries/semanticDefaults.mjs);
    • gives every sub-content node a fresh subContentId (UUID), ignoring any in the skeleton.
  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION in spec 04 §4. content/laeringsdesign/README.md explains how to make a skeleton from an exported .h5p file. A library update that changes a skeleton's fields shows up in content:check and in the integration test that creates every pattern (PED-010).
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probes P1 and P6): what creating from a skeleton needs on the real libraries:
    • Versions: the main library is the newest installed minor, the one the editor offers (Column 1.22, CoursePresentation 1.28, ImageHotspots 1.11 and so on). A sub-content node names exactly a version its parent field's semantics options list (BranchingScenario 1.10 offers CoursePresentation 1.27); anything else is refused by SubContentPolicy. content:check checks both against the semantics of the pinned libraries that npm run h5p:fetch-libraries installs; without them it says so and, in CI, fails.
    • Metadata: the save gets title, license: 'U', and both defaultLanguage and language set to the chosen language. Without them Lumi writes language: 'en', and V-LANG treats a Nynorsk activity as English.
    • Sub-content: every node has metadata: { title, license: 'U' } (otherwise the editor writes "Untitled …"); every list item is written out (the defaults never lengthen a list); BranchingScenario question nodes leave out nextContentId (its editor removes it) and end screens use contentId: -1.
    • Language: many nn and nb library defaults are English (MultiChoice, QuestionSet, InteractiveBook, BranchingScenario buttons and messages). A pattern sets these fields from its own nn, nb and en texts. Sub-content titles that learners see (InteractiveBook chapters and their table of contents) are pattern texts or guidance markers too.
    • Escaping: a token value is plain text, HTML-escaped on insertion; ⟦ and ⟧ stay raw characters. Lumi clips a text to its field's maxLength after escaping (& counts as five characters) and refuses a title over 255 characters, so content:check checks every resolved value, escaped, in all three languages, against its field's limit. Guidance inside a Blanks blank or a DragText draggable may not contain : or /, which those types read as a tip or an alternative.
    • Defaults: semanticDefaults.ts also gives isSubContent groups (H5P.Summary statements) a subContentId, as the editor does, and the creation step passes a copy of the parameters, because the save changes them in place.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W2b): content:check also refuses a skeleton key that the library's semantics do not define, so a misspelt behaviour switch cannot silently leave a PROD-009 setting at its default. A sub-content node may hold only library, params, metadata and subContentId; a key a library's own editor writes beside its semantics (BranchingScenario's contentId on each content item) is accepted, so a skeleton made from an exported .h5p passes as exported. A test runs the check on every real seed package.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): typo tolerance in fill-in tasks. H5P.Blanks' «Godta mindre skrivefeil» (acceptSpellingErrors) counts an answer as correct when it is one edit away from a solution longer than three characters (two edits beyond nine), and numbers get no exception: «125» and «1,25» both pass for «12,5». Spec 04 §4 asks for typo tolerance only in ea-terms, whose answers are terms; the real-pattern tests had widened it to every Blanks task without a record. Now:
    • ea-terms' Blanks accepts small typos (spec 04 §4).
    • uv-column, whose example is a dosage calculation, matches exactly (acceptSpellingErrors: false), so a number with one wrong or swapped digit is never marked correct. Its guidance tells the author to give each accepted form of a number as an alternative (12,5/12.5) and to switch typo tolerance on only when every answer is a word.
    • The other patterns' Blanks keep typo tolerance as ALU's draft choice; the tests no longer require it, so ALU can make a pattern strict with no code change (PED-011). Every Blanks task stays case-insensitive.
    • apps/server/test/learningDesign/patterns/realPatternSkeletons.test.ts pins the setting of ea-terms and uv-column; content/laeringsdesign/README.md («What catches mistakes in a pattern») and the ALU packet §6.2 say so.

D-085 · Creating an activity from a pattern is one server request

  • Context: PROD-001 opens the editor "pre-filled with a pedagogically sound skeleton". The editor client could prefill, but then the metadata and the skeleton would travel through the browser, and no test could create every pattern without one. Two patterns have a choice: ea-terms has two content types and ea-diagnose two phases.

  • Decision: POST /api/patterns/:patternId/activities with { language, phase?, courseCode?, contentType? }:

    • who: a signed-in portal author (Feide), with the CSRF token;
    • what: the server builds the skeleton (D-084) and saves it through HvlH5PEditor's save path, so the whitelist, the sub-content policy and the installed-library check run as for any save. In the same request it writes the learning-design metadata (the phase, the patternId, the course code and the pattern's suggested student minutes) and answers { contentId }. If writing the metadata fails, the new activity is deleted;
    • language: the activity's language is the one chosen (nn, nb or en), defaulting to the page's language;
    • choices: a pattern with two types needs contentType, and one with two phases takes phase from its own list; anything else is a 400;
    • unavailable patterns: a pattern whose library is not installed is shown as unavailable, and creating from it answers 409 hvl:pattern-unavailable.

    The web app then opens /aktivitet/:id on the Rediger tab. A blank activity stays available from /aktivitet/ny and from the catalogue.

  • Consequences: The created activity is a private draft like any other. The Canvas side of "new from a pattern" waits for S6 (D-098).

  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probe P1): "unavailable" covers every library the completed skeleton names, not only the main one: the defaults add libraries (InteractiveVideo's summary brings H5P.Summary), and some are installed only as dependencies. Without that check Lumi's own error would answer 500 instead of 409 hvl:pattern-unavailable.

  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): an installed library whose skeleton cannot be built for another reason (a semantics.json that does not parse, which Lumi's package validator lets through, or a damaged library folder) makes only the patterns that use it unavailable in the overview and the pattern pages, as a missing library does; before, one such pattern made GET /api/studio answer 500, and with it the guide, the planner and /mappe. The failure is logged once per pattern and content type (a warning with the pattern ID, the content type and the error's name) until a build succeeds again. Creating from such a pattern still fails (500): the overview has already called it unavailable.

D-086 · Guidance placeholders are marked ⟦…⟧, and V-PLACEHOLDER is an error that can be acknowledged

  • Context: PROD-001 allows a created activity to fail validation only on "placeholders that are deliberately flagged as needing input". Guidance text published to students by mistake is a real defect. D-074 lets an author publish past an error by acknowledging it with a reason.
  • Decision: Skeleton guidance is wrapped in ⟦ and ⟧ (U+27E6, U+27E7), which do not occur in ordinary text and are visible to the author. A new validator rule, V-PLACEHOLDER, has severity error. It reports every marked text in the parameters and in the metadata title, after decoding entities and removing tags, with the field's path for «Gå til feltet». It can be acknowledged with a reason as D-074 sets out; D-074 is unchanged. Probe P6 shows that the marker survives CKEditor and Lumi's sanitiser.
  • Consequences: The integration test that creates every pattern expects V-PLACEHOLDER errors and no others (PED-010, PROD-001). The rule's messages exist in nn, nb and en.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probes P1 and P6):
    • Where V-PLACEHOLDER looks: every string of the parameters, including the UI, l10n, texts, a11y, confirmCheck and confirmRetry groups the shared walker skips, plus the activity's and every sub-content's metadata.title (InteractiveBook shows chapter titles as headings). It skips extraTitle, which the editor copies from the title, so a marker is reported once.
    • How it reads them: through parseRichText (validation/richText.ts), which removes tags and then decodes every character reference exactly once, zero-padded and semicolon-less ones included. Decoding twice would turn the literal text &#10214; into a marker. A lone ⟦ or ⟧ counts, because authors' partial edits leave them. The editor sends plain-text fields back as loaded and only the save makes them raw, and package imports store references as they are, so the rule never assumes raw text.
    • Missing media: the rule also reports a required media slot that is empty: an InteractiveVideo without a video source and an ImageHotspots without a background image. Learners would see only an English error message instead of the activity, and nothing else flags it. The finding can be acknowledged like the others.

D-087 · Learning-design metadata: learner purpose, pattern, course code and access

  • Context: PED-030 lists the metadata fields. PED-032 shows students a one-line "why this matters" that the model lacks. The planner and the portfolio need a course code that matches across activities, and outcomes that can be recognised again.
  • Decision:
    • New fields: learnerPurpose (plain text, at most 200 characters, shown to learners in the activity's language) and patternId (the pattern the activity came from).
    • Course code: normalised (Unicode NFC, trimmed, upper case, inner spaces removed) and checked against ^[A-ZÆØÅ0-9][A-ZÆØÅ0-9-]{1,19}$. The field suggests the course labels of the author's own Canvas placements, stored from the launch's context.label in the new LtiPlacement.contextLabel (a course label, not personal data).
    • Outcomes: two outcomes are the same when their category matches and their text matches after normalising (NFC, trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed, case ignored). The form offers the outcomes the author already uses for the same course code as checkboxes.
    • API: GET and PUT /api/content/:id/learning-design. PUT replaces everything and must send the updatedAt it read (409 hvl:learning-design-conflict when stale). Only people who may Edit the activity read or write it.
    • Limits: at most 20 outcomes of 1–300 characters, a rationale of at most 1 000 characters and 1–600 student minutes.
    • What learners get: the minutes and the purpose only, and only after the View check: in /app/play through the x-hvli-launch header, and in the portal's Spel tab through the activity summary. They never get the rationale.
    • Publishing: the publish dialog shows a prompt to fill in the metadata that never blocks publishing.
  • Consequences: Migration s5_learning_design and new rows in the data inventory.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts):
    • Course labels and privacy: Canvas sandbox courses often carry a teacher's name in their label. The server therefore stores LtiPlacement.contextLabel only when the label, after D-087's normalisation, is a course code that contains at least one digit (HVL course codes do; names rarely do), and stores null otherwise. It strips control characters and cuts the label to 255 characters by code point. Each launch overwrites the value.
    • Whose labels: "the author's own placements" means placements of activities the author owns or co-authors; a placement has no user.
    • The pattern: a full replace keeps the stored patternId; only creation and duplication write it.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W3):
    • The purpose: besides a line break, any control character (a pasted tab) is refused (400). The web app's strict x-hvli-launch parser refuses the whole header on one, so a single stored tab would have shown «no launch» to every learner of the activity in Canvas. The server also leaves out such a stored purpose, and a language tag longer than the parser's 35 characters, rather than send them.
    • The stored label: LtiPlacement.contextLabel holds the cleaned label (control characters removed, at most 255 code points), not the normalised code; suggestions normalise it when read. Residual risk, accepted: a sandbox label that normalises to a code with a digit, such as «Kari 2025», is stored as if it were a course code. It is never shown to anyone but the authors of activities placed in that course.
    • The prompt: the metadata prompt shows in the first-publish dialog only, not when an already published activity is published again with new reasons.

D-088 · The alignment planner: one course, outcomes × phases, two gap rules

  • Context: PED-031 asks for a grid of learning outcomes × phases for one course, with gaps highlighted and Create from pattern in empty cells, as an accessible table.
  • Decision:
    • Scope: one course code at a time, chosen from the author's own. The grid holds the author's own and co-authored activities with that code; drafts are included and marked as drafts.
    • Rows and columns: rows are the distinct outcomes (D-087), ordered by category (kunnskap, ferdigheiter, generell kompetanse) and then by text; columns are the three phases in content order.
    • Untagged activities: activities with the course code but no outcomes or no phase are listed below the table, not hidden.
    • Gaps: an outcome with no Etterarbeid activity, and a phase with no activity at all. Each gap is shown with an icon and a text, never by colour alone.
    • Empty cells: a link «Lag frå mønster» whose accessible name names the phase and the outcome. It opens the catalogue filtered by that phase, carrying the course code, which creation then pre-fills.
    • Markup: a <table> with a <caption>, th scope="col" for the phases and th scope="row" for the outcomes, inside a focusable, labelled region that scrolls sideways on narrow screens.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W3): the course chooser lists the codes the author's own and co-authored activities use; Canvas labels are only suggestions in the Læringsdesign tab. The outcomes of an activity that has the course code but no phase still become rows (with empty cells and the no-Etterarbeid gap), and the activity is also listed as untagged, so an outcome is never hidden. The empty-phase gap counts only activities that have a phase.

D-089 · Studio access, routes and tabs

  • Context: Spec 04 §2 says the guide is "public within HVL". The owner decided on 2026-10-28 that the guide and the catalogue are public: they hold research summaries and patterns, nothing about people.
  • Decision:
    • Public (no sign-in): /laeringsdesign (guide, phase matrix and the catalogue, with its filters in the URL) and /laeringsdesign/monster/[patternId]. «Lag frå dette mønsteret» asks a signed-out visitor to sign in.
    • Authors only: /laeringsdesign/planlegg, /laeringsdesign/innhaldsbank (the content bank, D-091) and /mappe, with the same sign-in redirect and refusal pages as the other portal pages.
    • New tabs on /aktivitet/[id]: Læringsdesign (people who may Edit) and Deling (visibility, which until now had only an API, plus co-authors, the bank listing and «Lag ein kopi»).
    • Navigation: the header has the studio links in the same place on every portal page.
    • Code location: the pages are apps/web/src/app/(portal)/laeringsdesign/… and apps/web/src/app/(portal)/mappe/.
  • Consequences: Spec 04 §2 and its code location are amended. ActivityView is split into a tab registry so that no file passes 200 lines.

D-090 · Finding co-authors: HVL staff only, rate-limited, audited

  • Context: PROD-007 finds co-authors "by name or Feide ID" among HVL staff. Staff names come from Feide at login and are stored only for staff (D-021, DATA-001). Student authors may not share beyond their own work (D-059).
  • Decision:
    • Who can be found: a person can be found only while User.coAuthorSearchableAt is set and less than 13 months old. It is set at each Feide login of an HVL member with an employee, faculty or staff affiliation, and cleared at a Feide login without one. Student authors, LTI accounts and learners are never listed.
    • Search: GET /api/people?q= by name needs at least 3 characters and returns at most 10 matches as { userId, displayName }, with no e-mail and no Feide ID. A query in the form of a Feide ID is an exact lookup through the identity's login hash. Searches are limited per user in Redis (429 when exceeded), and the query is never logged.
    • Co-authors: the owner adds and removes them; a co-author may remove themselves; an activity has at most 20. Only a person who can be found may be added, so student authors are refused (hvl:coauthor-not-eligible).
    • Audit: every change is audited with user IDs only.
  • Consequences: /personvern says that colleagues can see staff names through co-author search and bank attribution.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts):
    • Who can be found: someone eligible for the co-author directory is an HVL member with the author role who is not a student author (hvlMember, author, not studentAuthor in the Feide login's roles), not anyone of kind staff: student authors and admin-only members are kind staff too. Only the Feide login path writes coAuthorSearchableAt, never an LTI launch.
    • One predicate: the name search, the exact Feide-ID lookup and the check when a co-author is added all use the same rule: eligible, and coAuthorSearchableAt less than 13 months old.
    • Search: LIKE wildcards in the query are escaped; the query is never logged or echoed in an error; a 429 carries Retry-After.
    • Portal only: every studio route except the public guide and catalogue starts with requirePortalAuthor (learningDesign/http/studioPrincipal.ts), which refuses an LTI ltik (401) and a portal learner (403), so a Canvas launch can never search HVL staff names.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W4):
    • Who may search and add: only an HVL staff author (the same rule): a student author is refused with 403 hvl:sharing-not-allowed (D-059: they share nothing beyond their own work), an admin-only member with 403 error.forbidden. A student-author owner therefore adds no co-authors either; removing is always allowed.
    • The limit: 30 searches per person in a fixed 60-second window in Redis (hvli:people-search:<userId>, a count only); every valid search counts; the 429's Retry-After is the rest of the window, at least 1 second.
    • The routes: listing the authors needs Edit; adding and removing answer the list as it is afterwards; adding an existing co-author and removing someone who is not one change nothing and write no audit event. Adding locks the activity's row, so two concurrent adds never pass 20. The permission facts are read on every request, so a removed co-author loses Edit at the next one.
    • The predicate: learningDesign/collaboration/staffEligibility.ts; the Feide login writes coAuthorSearchableAt through AccountResolver, which ignores the field for an LTI launch.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): staff e-mail is no longer stored. SPEC-DEVIATION AUTH-004 ("store a display name and e-mail only for authors and admins"). AUTH-004 kept the e-mail for co-author search and attribution, but search matches the display name or the Feide-ID hash and answers { userId, displayName }, the bank and a copy show the name only, and nothing in the code base reads User.email. Keeping it had no purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) and (c)), and /personvern and the data inventory named a use that does not exist. The Feide login therefore keeps only the display name (authorProfile), and AccountResolver writes email: null at each staff login, so an address stored before is cleared at the next one; there is no migration, as nothing is deployed yet. The column stays until a schema change drops it. FEIDE_SCOPE keeps email (AUTH-001 fixes the scope string): the claim is only in the encrypted ID token kept for Feide logout, as /personvern already says.

D-091 · The content bank: opt-in, published, shared with HVL, for HVL authors

  • Context: PROD-007 lets authors "publish an activity to the HVL content bank so that colleagues can duplicate and adapt it".
  • Decision:
    • Listing: the owner lists an activity in the bank (H5PContent.bankListedAt). Listing needs a published activity whose visibility is HVL (organisation) or wider, and an owner who is not a student author.
    • Unlisting: making the activity private, or unpublishing it, removes the listing in the same transaction.
    • Who sees it: the bank page lists the activities for HVL authors only, with title, type, phase, purpose, minutes, outcomes and the owner's name.
    • Consent text: listing shows a consent text: colleagues see the activity, your name and its learning-design information and can make their own copies, and withdrawing the listing leaves existing copies with their authors. The text is a draft for ALU's and HVL's legal review.
    • Audit: listing and unlisting are audited.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts): the bank is for HVL staff authors, the same people D-090 lets be found: student authors neither see the bank nor list in it, because it shows colleagues' names, and /personvern says colleagues see them. The header link shows to every author, since the web app knows only roles; the bank page shows the server's refusal to a student author. Unpublishing an activity or making it private clears bankListedAt in the same transaction (ContentPublisher and the sharing routes).
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W4):
    • Who sees and changes the listing: people who may edit the activity read its listing ({ listedAt, eligible }), so a co-author sees it on the Deling tab; only the owner lists and unlists. A student author's GET /api/bank and listing are 403 hvl:sharing-not-allowed, which the bank page explains.
    • "Eligible": published, organisation or feide, and an owner who is HVL staff: the owner's own login facts when the owner asks, else the owner's coAuthorSearchableAt (an owner who has not signed in as staff for 13 months is not eligible).
    • Not a change of the activity: listing and unlisting do not move H5PContent.updatedAt, so the publish flow's precondition and the "newest change first" lists stay as they were. Listing is one conditional update, so an activity unpublished or made private meanwhile is never listed. Each real change is audited (content.bank.list with { consentVersion }, content.bank.unlist with { cause: owner | unpublish | private }).
    • The bank list: the 200 newest listings the reader may view, each passing the same View rule as opening it.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration of stage 4): the bank shows a listing only while its owner is findable staff (D-090: an eligible Feide login in the last 13 months), checked each time the bank is read. The name of someone who has left HVL, or who now signs in as a student author, then stops showing to colleagues without anyone unlisting, and the listing returns at the owner's next eligible login. The bank shows the 200 newest listings, without paging, until use shows a need.

D-092 · Duplicating an activity

  • Context: PROD-007: a duplicate keeps a link to its source and the original author's attribution, and never copies learner data. Lumi copies a duplicate's files only when their paths are rewritten to the paste-source form ../<sourceId>/<file>, and it checks View on the source.
  • Decision:
    • Permission: a pure rule table (duplicateRules): a person may duplicate an activity they may Edit, or a published, bank-listed activity they may View.
    • Copied: the parameters, the H5P metadata and the files, through the paste-source rewrite. Of the learning-design data, the phase, patternId, outcomes, minutes and purpose are copied. A copy made through the bank leaves out the rationale and the course code, which belong to the source's author.
    • Never copied: learner state, statements, insight snapshots, placements, acknowledgements, co-authors, the bank listing and the published status.
    • The copy: a private draft owned by the person who copied it, with sourceContentId and the new sourceAuthorUserId. The source author's name is read when the copy is shown, so a later change of name shows.
    • API: POST /api/content/:id/duplicate answers { contentId }; it is audited. The copy is saved through HvlH5PEditor's save path.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probe P2): Lumi does not refuse a paste source the saver may not View: it saves the copy with every such file path emptied, and stores no file. Therefore:
    • Our check first: ContentDuplicator decides duplicateRules before it calls the editor and refuses with our own error.
    • What is rewritten: only references to files the source stores, to ../<sourceId>/<file>. URLs and names the source does not store stay as they are. A #tmp reference is kept, because «Lagre som ny versjon» (D-093) saves new uploads with the copy.
    • Unsafe names: a stored name outside Lumi's pattern (^[\w\-./_]+$; spaces or æøå from an imported package) is copied by the duplicator itself, through the content storage under a safe name, and its path fixed.
    • Checked afterwards: a saved copy with an emptied path or a ../ path left is deleted and the duplicate fails, so nothing half-done remains. Lumi gives copied files new names (cut at the first hyphen or with stacked suffixes), so nothing may rely on the source's file names.
    • Speed: Lumi streams every file through the server; a large video makes a duplicate slow, so the route's time limit allows for it.
    • Editor saves: the editor's own save routes accept ../<id>/<file> paths too (H5P's copy and paste). HvlH5PEditor now allows such a path only from an activity duplicateRules allows, and refuses a path the storage would refuse (.., a leading /, a backslash, control characters) before Lumi writes anything; before, Lumi wrote the activity and then failed with a 400, leaving a half-saved draft.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts):
    • The rule, exactly: decideDuplicate answers unavailable (404, D-066) for an unknown activity or one the person may not View, and refused (403) unless the person may create activities (an author or an admin in the account view). Then Edit allows it, and otherwise a published, bank-listed activity allows it for a person the bank is for (D-091 as amended: not a student author).
    • Errors: a refusal the editor raises before any row exists (the sub-content policy, the paste guard, Lumi's metadata schema) reaches the author unchanged as a 4xx; any failure after a row exists removes the copy and answers 500 hvl:duplicate-failed, logged with its cause by the route. The audit details are { sourceContentId, via, kind }; the source author is on the copy's sourceAuthorUserId.
    • Who sees the source: the copy's detail shows its source's title and author only to people who may Edit the copy; learners and other viewers get none of it.
    • Editor saves: PasteSourceGuard checks every ../<id>/<file> path on every editor save against the same rule, and every #tmp and paste path against the storage's safe-name rule, before Lumi writes anything; a web address whose scheme has capitals (Https://) passes, as H5P plays it. An existing activity that still holds a path the guard refuses must have that element removed before it can be saved.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W4):
    • The bank branch in the actor: HvlH5pActor carries the login's studentAuthor, so duplicateRules allows a bank copy only to an author signed in with Feide who is an HVL member and not a student author (isBankReaderActor); the editor's paste guard decides with the same rule. A Canvas launch never copies through the bank (D-098).
    • The route: POST /api/content/:contentId/duplicate (portal authors, CSRF) answers 201 { contentId } and lets its socket stay idle for up to 15 minutes while Lumi streams a large video's files; a proxy in front must allow as long.
    • Who sees the source: the copy's detail names its source (ID and title) only while the person may View the source, and its author by the account's current display name; an unknown part is left out, and the page says so in words.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration of stage 4): known limit, accepted: both links of a copy are SetNull, so a copy whose source and source author are both deleted (or whose source is deleted and whose author has no name) shows no «Kopi av …» sign and looks like an original. Telling it apart would need a column that survives the deletion; that waits until someone needs it. On the Deling tab a student-author owner still sees people search (the web app knows roles, not the student-author fact) and gets the server's explanation (hvl:sharing-not-allowed) when searching.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): a bank copy needs the listing to be in the bank now. The bank shows a listing only while its owner is findable staff (D-091 amendment, S5 integration of stage 4), but the bank branch of duplicateRules checked only bankListedAt, so a colleague who knew the ID could still copy a hidden listing (by the duplicate route, «Lagre som ny versjon» or an editor paste), and the copy named the departed owner. The facts' bankListed (ContentAccessRepository.factsFor) now means "listed, and its owner is findable staff" (isFindableStaff, the in-memory form of the bank list's findableStaffWhere), so the duplicator, the copy route and the editor's paste guard refuse such a source with 403 hvl:duplicate-not-allowed until the owner's next eligible login. Copying through Edit is unchanged.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): copies are limited per person. A duplicate and «Lagre som ny versjon» each stream every file of the source through the server, and nothing bounded how many one person could start. Both now count against one per-person fixed window in Redis, the people search's pattern (D-090): at most 20 copies in 10 minutes (hvli:copies:<userId>, a count only), counted once the duplicate rule has allowed the copy, so an unknown or refused source answers as before. Past the limit the answer is 429 hvl:rate-limited, and POST /api/content/:contentId/duplicate sends Retry-After with the rest of the window (at least 1 second). The limiter is built with the H5P runtime and reaches the duplicator through the editor it saves with (HvlH5PEditor.copyLimit), because the studio services take only the editor from the runtime. Not covered: the bytes of one copy (a source that repeats one stored file many times) and the editor's own saves of pasted paths; both stay open for a per-save copy budget.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): the source's title carries its language. The «Kopi av …» sign put the source's title in the page's language, so an English source on a Nynorsk page was read with a Norwegian voice (UD-010, WCAG 3.1.2). The attribution now also has sourceLanguage, the source's own language tag (activityLanguage of its metadata), given only together with sourceTitle and under the same View check; the sign marks the title with lang when it differs from the page's language.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review leftovers): both copy routes send Retry-After. «Lagre som ny versjon» (POST /h5p/content/:contentId/copy) answered the copy limit's 429 hvl:rate-limited without Retry-After, so only the duplicate route told the person when to try again. Now both send it, with the same seconds, and the /api contract documents the 429 of duplicateContent as it does people search's.

D-093 · Safe editing: a structure signature, a confirmation, and saving as a copy

  • Context: PROD-013: editing an activity that has learner state warns that structural changes reset saved progress, offers Save as new version, and invalidates state only when the author confirms. Today every save deletes the state H5P marks as invalidated (D-038, HvlH5PEditor.ts), including after a typo fix and including the author's own preview state.
  • Decision:
    • Structure signature: for each sub-content node, its library, subContentId and position, plus the answer shape of leaf questions (for example the number of options or blanks). Probe P3 on the ten types settles the details, erring on the strict side. Any difference counts as structural.
    • Whose state counts: other people's. The saver's own state never prompts.
    • Non-structural save: keeps all learner state. This amends D-038.
    • Structural save, other people's state present: answers 409 hvl:learner-state-reset-needed and saves nothing. The answer has no counts, so it reveals nothing about how many learners there are.
    • Confirmed reset: a retry with confirmLearnerStateReset: true saves, deletes the activity's learner state and raises H5PContent.version, so S6 insight can separate results by version.
    • Save as a copy: POST /h5p/content/:id/copy saves the edited parameters as a copy (D-092, owner's copy) and leaves the original and its learner state untouched. This is the owner's choice for «Lagre som ny versjon» (2026-10-28).
    • The dialog: a new boot script, editorSaveChoice.js, shows a native <dialog> in the editor page: focus starts on «Avbryt», and Esc cancels. In Canvas it offers only reset or cancel, with a pointer to the portal.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probes P3 and P7):
    • The signature, in detail: a pre-order walk of every object with library and subContentId, recording its JSON path, its library as Name major.minor and its subContentId, plus the main library. Containers add: every CoursePresentation slide element's position; BranchingScenario's node count and every nextContentId; QuestionSet's poolSize; InteractiveVideo's video paths and its interactions sorted by start time, with the end summary after them. Leaves add their answer shape: MultiChoice's option count, its single or multiple mode and its option texts; Blanks' list of blank solutions; DragText's drop-zone and distractor words; a branching question's alternatives. A leaf list is structural if its length changes or its texts move; a text changed in place is not. Appends count: an appended InteractiveBook chapter crashes the player for learners with state.
    • Two kinds of leaf: a library without getCurrentState (AdvancedText, Text, Image, Table and others) is stateless, so only its position counts and editing its text is never structural. A stateful leaf without a rule counts any change of its parameters as structural.
    • Old pages: a learner page opened before a structural save keeps sending old state every few seconds. The player therefore sends the content version with each state write, and a write for an older version is dropped.
    • The saver's own state: a structural save always deletes it, even with no prompt, because stale state can crash the author's own preview. "Own" means the saver's current learner key; their Canvas or last year's preview counts as someone else's, which errs on the safe side.
    • Reset: a confirmed reset deletes the rows, and learners start again. H5P's RESET marker is not used: its dialog title is hard-coded English and Lumi's Nynorsk strings are Bokmål.
    • Order: the check runs before Lumi saves and before dropped files are deleted, so a refused save changes neither the parameters nor the files.
    • The dialog: the editor is always in a frame (the portal's Rediger tab and Canvas), where a native modal dialog lets Tab leave the frame. editorSaveChoice.js therefore keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the dialog, and takes focus back only when the H5P editor's own frame takes it. After the dialog closes it re-enables «Lagre», focuses it and only then announces the outcome. In the portal the editor page asks the activity page to make its own controls inert while the dialog is open; Canvas's page is out of our reach. The dialog's look comes from a stylesheet file under the page's policy, with the :focus-visible ring the rest of the service uses.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 server side):
    • The version: only a structural save that goes through raises H5PContent.version, not every save as D-074's 2026-10-23 amendment said: a text-only save keeps the learners' state, so the pages they have open must go on saving under the same version. This amends D-074 and the data inventory.
    • What a reset deletes: every structural save that goes through deletes all the activity's state rows and raises the version in one transaction, also when the check found only the saver's: a row written between the check and the write belongs to the old structure.
    • The confirmation: confirmLearnerStateReset (a boolean, else 400) in the body of PUT /h5p/content/:id reaches HvlH5PEditor.saveOrUpdateContent as an explicit last argument (SaveChoice), not through the request's async context: every save of an existing activity comes through that route, so a save without it can never reset by accident. POST /h5p/content creates an activity, which has no state.
    • Old pages: the player's state URL (the portal and /lti/play) carries contentVersion=<version>, read before Lumi renders. The state route makes such a write only while the activity has that version, checked in the write's own transaction under a FOR SHARE lock on the activity row, which the reset's version update waits for. A stale write is answered 200 { success: false, message: 'hvl:learner-state-stale' }: h5p.js hands it to an error callback the players' autosave does not set, so nothing is retried or shown. A write without the parameter is not checked; a malformed one is 400.
    • Save as a copy: POST /h5p/content/:id/copy takes { params, metadata } as the editor gives them, is for portal authors only (an ltik is 401 hvl:unauthenticated, a portal learner 403, the CSRF token as on every unsafe method), answers 201 { contentId }, and passes the duplicator's errors on unchanged.
    • Shuffling: MultiChoice's randomAnswers and QuestionSet's randomQuestions are not structural (a resumed attempt keeps its saved order, questionset.js:391); poolSize is.
    • The real editor's round trip: an unchanged save through the editor page must stay text-only for every type (editorRoundTrip.browser.int.test.ts). H5P's editor drops a branching-question node's own nextContentId: -1, which the player reads as -1 when it is missing, so a missing one counts as -1. The editor also upgrades an activity to the newest installed minor version of its library when it saves it; as the signature compares Name major.minor, the first save after HVL installs a newer minor version is structural and asks, which errs on the strict side.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W5b):
    • Canvas wording: from Canvas, the 409 keeps its status and code but its message (safeEditing.resetNeededCanvas) does not offer a new version, which Canvas does not have (D-098).
    • «Gå til feltet» on titles: metadata.title and a sub-content's title reach the title field (Column, QuestionSet, InteractiveBook and InteractiveVideo interactions) or the metadata popup (AdvancedText, ImageHotspots content). BranchingScenario node titles and CoursePresentation element titles are not reached by those custom editors; the page says so («feltet kan ikkje opnast») rather than failing silently, as for their other fields.
    • The activity page: while the dialog is open, the portal's activity page and /app/play make their own controls inert; after «Lagre som ny versjon» the portal opens the copy's editor tab.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W4):
    • The copy's library version: H5P's editor upgrades an activity to the newest installed minor version of its library and shapes the parameters for it, so «Lagre som ny versjon» saving them under the source's older version stored parameters its semantics did not describe. The editor page now sends its content.library with the copy (POST /h5p/content/:id/copy takes { params, metadata, library? }; a library that is not a string is 400), and the copy is saved with it when it has the source's machine name and major version and is installed (learningDesign/collaboration/copyLibraryChoice.ts); anything else keeps the source's version without an error. «Lag ein kopi» names no library and always keeps the source's version.
    • Who sees where it came from: the copy's page shows «Kopi av av » to the people who may edit it (D-092), so the copy «Lagre som ny versjon» opened says lastingly what it is, also when the announcement before the navigation was cut off.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration of the accessibility suite): besides making everything around the editor frame inert, the page takes the tabindex of the elements that hold the frame (the tab panel's 0, main's -1 as the skip link's target) while the dialog is open and gives it back afterwards: a click beside the frame focused the tab panel and left the dialog. a11y/axeSaveChoice.a11y.test.ts checks that nothing outside the frame takes focus or is exposed in the accessibility tree while the dialog is open.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration): while «Nullstill …» or «Lagre som ny versjon» runs, the editor page's status region says so («Nullstiller framgangen og lagrar endringa …», safeEditing.busy.*) before the result, so a screen-reader user knows the request has started. (The tabindex of the frame's holders while the dialog is open is recorded once, in the amendment above; S5 review, 2026-10-29.)
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): the reset is part of the parameter write. A structural save's reset (state rows deleted, version raised) used to be its own transaction after Lumi's save. Lumi's first parameter write commits before it copies files and writes a second time, so a failed reset, a failed file copy or a restart in between left the new structure with the old state and the old version, and the next save, comparing against the new structure, never reset it. Now the editor's learner-state step marks the save in its async context (h5p/storage/learnerStateResetWrite.ts), and PrismaContentStorage's first update of that activity writes the parameters, raises the version (that update comes first, for the FOR SHARE order) and deletes every state row in one transaction. A save that fails before that write changes nothing; one that fails after it leaves the new structure with its reset. A storage without the hook (the unit tests' file storage) gets the separate reset after the write, as before.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): focus while a chosen request runs. The dialog's close removed the focused choice while «Lagre» was still natively disabled, so focus fell to the page's <body> for the whole reset or copy (a copy may take minutes), and Tab went into H5P's form. Now, once the author has chosen «Nullstill …» or «Lagre som ny versjon», the editor page focuses «Lagre» before the busy text is announced, keeping it unavailable with aria-disabled="true" (a click is ignored) instead of disabled, which cannot hold focus. When the request ends, «Lagre» is available again and the outcome is announced, as before. The ordinary save keeps its native disabled.

D-094 · Rendering the pedagogisk mappe

  • Context: MAPPE-002 takes headings from the template and criteria from the criteria files, keyed by criteria set; switching the set changes every criterion text and the reader's guide. The word count excludes the references and the reader's guide. Activity titles and texts come from authors and must not turn into Markdown structure.
  • Decision:
    • Template: content/mappe/template.{nn,nb,en}.md uses Mustache 4.2.0. The loader removes comments and front matter and checks every tag against an allowlist of variables; triple braces and {{& }} are refused.
    • Escaping: Mustache's escape function is replaced by a Markdown escaper, so a title such as # x or [a](b) stays text.
    • Reader's guide: built from the criteria data (criterion → chapter and attachment), not written in the template.
    • Limits: criteria.{nn,nb,en}.yaml holds, per set, the criteria and the limits: Del 1 words (default 7 500) and attachments (default 11). Both are marked (verify).
    • Word count: counts Del 1 only, between markers the loader requires, without the reader's guide and the references.
    • Activities: the author's own and co-authored activities, filtered by course, phase and date. Each gives its title, type, phase, course, outcomes, rationale, the validator's result with any acknowledgements and their reasons, a link, and the aggregates of D-095.
    • API: POST /api/mappe/preview answers the word count, which the page announces politely. POST /api/mappe/export?format=md|pdf answers the file, which is not stored.
    • Opprykk: the promotion mode waits for ALU.
  • Consequences: Amends D-020: the reader's guide is generated, and the limits live per criteria set.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probe P5): how Mustache is used safely:
    • Rendering: Mustache.render(template, view, undefined, { escape, tags: ['{{', '}}'] }). Never assign Mustache.escape or Mustache.tags, which are global to the process, and never pass {} as partials.
    • Loading: the loader reads Mustache.parse's tokens without changing them (they are cached and reused by render) and strips comments in the source text. It allows only name, #, ^ and ! tags with allowlisted names, and refuses & (which also covers triple braces), >, =, images, a value inside backticks, a value straight after ]( or a backslash, and a value at the start of a line that follows a table header.
    • The view: every key is present on every list item (null when unknown), so a missing field never falls back to the parent's field of the same name. Dates and numbers are formatted as strings first.
    • Empty values: an optional value sits in a {{#x}} section or gets a localised placeholder, because an empty value can turn the template's own **…** into a rule, ## … into an empty heading and […](…) into an empty link.
    • The escaper (mappe/markdownEscape.ts) is safe in inline positions only: line starts, after a heading, list or quote marker, mid-line, table cells and link text.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W6a): how the template, the counts and the routes are built:
    • No portfolio yet: the six files (template.{nn,nb,en}.md, criteria.{nn,nb,en}.yaml) are optional until written, all six or none, as the guide is (D-083 amendment). Without them the mappe routes answer 409 hvl:mappe-not-ready (new in the contract), which the page explains; the activity list still answers.
    • Markers: the reader's guide and the references are blocks the server builds, so they are placed by markers instead of {{{…}}}: a line that is only {{lesarrettleiing}} or {{referansar}}. Two pairs mark the counted parts: {{del1_start}} … {{del1_slutt}} (the word count) and {{vedlegg_start}} … {{vedlegg_slutt}} (the suggested attachments, counted as the outermost list items between them, which the preview's attachments reports against the set's limit). Each marker stands once, outside every section; the loader cuts the template at the marker lines and Mustache parses each part, so a section cannot span a marker.
    • Names: the allowlist is a tree of Nynorsk names (apps/server/src/learningDesign/mappe/mappeVariables.ts): top values, the lists aktivitetar (with uu_merknader inside) and emneoversikt; a list opens only where it is defined. Every value is text and never empty: the view gives a localised placeholder for anything unknown, so no {{#x}} guard is needed around a single value.
    • Value places: besides the probe's refusals, a value may not stand straight after < (a title such as script> would open raw HTML in a renderer with HTML on) or straight after ] (a value starting with ( would turn the brackets into a link to the value). So {{lenke}} is written as plain text; the PDF does not make it a link.
    • Word count: what markdown-it reads as text in Del 1, without the blocks; a word is a run between spaces that holds a letter or a digit, and a no-break space joins, so a grouped number (7 500) is one word. The template is rendered twice, the second time with the count; the count cannot change between them.
    • References: the full references the chosen activities' patterns cite, each once, sorted by text.
    • Validator result: the UD-021 findings of the stored activity (the findings route's validator and input), each error with the newest reason given for it at any age: the 14 days decide whether publishing asks again, not whether a reason was given. Who gave it is not read.
    • Routes: GET /api/mappe/activities, GET /api/mappe/criteria-sets (the sets with their limits and the default set; new schemas MappeCriteriaSet and MappeCriteriaSetList), POST /api/mappe/preview and POST /api/mappe/export?format=md|pdf, all requirePortalAuthor. More than 50 IDs is 400 hvl:mappe-too-many before the body's schema; an ID that is not the author's own or co-authored is 404 hvl:activity-unavailable, like an unknown one. The file name is ASCII, pedagogisk-mappe-YYYY-MM-DD.md|pdf.
    • The page filters the author's list in the browser (course, phase from GET /api/studio, change dates in Oslo time), and the portfolio's language is chosen apart from the page's.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration): SPEC-DEVIATION UD-007: the /mappe download buttons name the file type but not its size, because the server makes the file only when asked and stores nothing (MAPPE-003); the size is unknown until then. The reference list of the export carries no language per reference yet, so an English reference in a Nynorsk PDF is not tagged with /Lang (a residual for the manual PAC check, D-096).
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): link destinations over two lines, and activity IDs in either case.
    • Value places: CommonMark lets a link destination start on the line after ]( or ]:, so the loader looks for an open destination in the whole paragraph before the value, not only on its line. It refuses a value in a destination that starts on the next line (also when the template writes the start of the address), and any value in a paragraph that holds a link reference definition. A value after a closed link, or in link text over two lines, is allowed. The verification of the review added: a ]( stays open until the ) that balances it (a destination may hold balanced parentheses or an escaped \)), and a reference definition counts also in a block quote or a list item (> [a]:, - [a]:, 1. [a]:); all three passed the loader before. A second verification added two more that had passed: a definition whose label holds an escaped bracket ([a\]b]:), and one whose label runs over a line that holds only a no-break space, because only a line of spaces and tabs ends a paragraph in CommonMark, and the scan had taken any white space for a blank line.
    • IDs: the mappe routes match an activity ID without regard to case, as the other S5 lookups do: an upper-case ID finds the author's activity, and the same ID twice in two cases is 400 error.badRequest ("named twice").

D-095 · Minimum group size in exports

  • Context: MAPPE-003 applies INS-006's minimum group size (k = 5, configurable, at least 3, with complementary suppression) to the portfolio's aggregates. No results are stored before S6: setFinished is off and no xAPI is recorded.
  • Decision: privacy/minimumGroupSize.ts reads k from MIN_GROUP_SIZE (an integer of at least 3, default 5). It suppresses a count below k, and suppresses the completion rate when either the completers or the non-completers number fewer than k, so a hidden value cannot be worked out from the other. In S5, ActivityResultsSource answers "no results yet", and the export says so. S6 adds the real source and the insight views on the same module.
  • Consequences: The 4-learner test of MAPPE-003 runs against a fixture source.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W6a): ActivityResultsSource.learnerSummaries hands over one summary per learner (attempts, completed, the first and last scaled score) and no identifier or answer text; only aggregates leave activityResults.ts. Below k learners nothing at all is shown, not even the count; the median attempts need k learners, and the change from the first to the last attempt (the mean, in percentage points) needs k learners with both scores. A rate of 0 % or 100 % is always hidden by the two-sided rule.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, S6 step 4, MAPPE-003: the real results source): StoredActivityResults (learningDesign/mappe/storedActivityResults.ts) replaces S5's "no results yet". It reads the stored XapiStatement rows of the export's activities (the author's own and co-authored ones only, D-066), with no period: every row until the yearly purge (D-107). A learner's figures mean what insight's do (D-115): started with any stored statement, completed with a stored root result, attempts are the stored root results, and the scores are those of root results with a maximum above 0. Decided: the mappe adds up what insight shows one group at a time (D-106), so an activity's learners are grouped by context (a Canvas course as <platformId>:<contextId>, D-103, or the portal), content version (PROD-013) and semester (from midnight Oslo time on 1 January or 1 August, as insight's semester period), and only groups of at least k distinct learners count; a learner in two groups gives one summary in each. Otherwise the mappe's totals less insight's views would give a group that insight hides (the "all contexts minus one" D-106 refused), or tell how many learners played in two groups. When a counted group's completers number 1 to k − 1 (insight hides them), the completion rate and the median attempts are shown only if those groups' completers and non-completers each number at least k together. First and last scores are given only to a learner with two or more scored results in the group, so a single attempt never shows as a change. Consequences: an activity played only in small groups shows no figures in the mappe, even when its learners together number k or more, so the mappe's participants can be fewer than all who played; the hand-worked figures are tested on stored rows (storedActivityResults.int.test.ts, learnerSummaries.test.ts).

D-096 · The portfolio PDF is rendered by Chromium on the server

  • Context: MAPPE-004 asks for a tagged PDF with language, title, outline and real text from the same semantic HTML. The owner decided on 2026-10-28 that the server renders it with Chromium. playwright-core 1.56.1 is already pinned as a development dependency, and its page.pdf has tagged and outline.
  • Decision:
    • Dependency: playwright-core 1.56.1 becomes a production dependency.
    • Rendering: Markdown → semantic HTML with lang and <title> (markdown-it, html: false) → page.pdf({ tagged: true, outline: true }).
    • Isolation: one shared browser per process, started lazily, and a fresh context per export with JavaScript off, offline, and every request aborted. The browser starts with a scrubbed environment (no secrets) and keeps Chromium's sandbox.
    • Limits: at most PDF_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) exports per process and one per user, with a time limit.
    • No browser: answers 503 hvl:pdf-unavailable, and the page points to the Markdown export, which always works. PDF_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE names the browser.
  • Consequences: S6's production image needs Chromium and fonts with æ, ø and å. Probe P4 checks the structure tree, outline, /Lang and title with pdfjs-dist. Anything Chromium cannot set, such as DisplayDocTitle, is recorded as a residual for the manual PAC check.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 probe P4):
    • Launch: chromium.launch({ chromiumSandbox: true, env: { PATH, HOME }, executablePath }), all explicit: playwright-core's defaults pass the server's whole environment (secrets included) to Chromium and turn the sandbox off. Each export uses a fresh context with JavaScript off and offline: true (which blocks prefetches the route never sees), every request aborted, and the context closed afterwards. The mappe HTML holds no images; even an aborted image paints a placeholder.
    • Root: Chromium refuses its sandbox when the process runs as root, as everything does in the development container. A development-only PDF_ALLOW_NO_SANDBOX=true lets the PDF export work there; the production checks refuse it. Production runs the server as a non-root user whose runtime allows unprivileged user namespaces (S6). CI runs as a non-root user and lifts Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor restriction on those namespaces first.
    • Tables: markdown-it writes no scope, so the mappe renderer gives header cells scope="col" and makes the first cell of each body row a row header with scope="row".
    • Residuals: Chromium sets DisplayDocTitle, so that is not a residual. The manual PAC check records these instead: list numbers are untagged and lists carry no numbering attribute, caption and thead become NonStruct, there is no XMP metadata and so no PDF/UA identifier, links have no /Contents, and the header says PDF 1.4.
    • Fonts: Georgia, the body font token, is not installed here, so the PDF uses Liberation Serif. The S6 image installs fonts-liberation, or the fonts HVL licenses, so that æ, ø and å always embed.
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts): PDF_ALLOW_NO_SANDBOX (default false) lets the root development container render PDFs; the production checks refuse it. Tests set it from whether they run as root, so the same test keeps the sandbox on the non-root CI runner. PDF_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE must be an absolute path; start-up does not require it to exist, since a missing browser only means 503 hvl:pdf-unavailable.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 W6a): the limits in numbers: one export may take 30 seconds and a launch 20; past either, or when the browser will not start, the answer is 503 hvl:pdf-unavailable, and the next export tries again. A full process or a person's second export is 503 hvl:pdf-busy at once (no queue) with Retry-After: 10. Playwright's signal handlers are off, so only the server's shutdown closes the browser. A crashed browser is forgotten on disconnected and started again on the next export.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 stage 5): Chromium's tagged-PDF outline drops the space where a heading wraps over two lines («emneom»), so a screen reader's bookmark list ran words together for long activity titles. The PDF's headings now have white-space: pre-wrap, which keeps the space and renders a one-line Markdown heading the same; the PDF browser test has a title that wraps, and its outline must equal the Markdown headings.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 integration): the full residual list for the manual PAC check, in one place: list items have no Lbl/LBody and lists no numbering attribute; captions, thead and tbody give no Caption, THead or TBody element (NonStruct); no XMP metadata, so no PDF/UA identifier; links have no /Contents; the header says PDF 1.4; activity titles have no language of their own; references have no language of their own (D-094 amendment); the activity address is plain text, not a link. taggedPdf.browser.test.ts pins the first two.
  • Amendment (2026-10-29, S5 review): the time limit covers opening the context, and a stalled browser is replaced. In the review, a Chromium that was frozen (SIGSTOP) but still connected never answered newContext. That call ran before the 30-second limit started, so the export waited for good, and two such exports left every later one 503 hvl:pdf-busy until a restart.
    • The limit now starts before the context opens and covers opening, loading and printing. Past it the answer is 503 hvl:pdf-unavailable, and a context that opens late is closed at once. The launch keeps its own 20 seconds.
    • Discarding: a browser that fails to open a context, or does not open one or finish closing one within the limit, is treated like a crashed one. It is forgotten and closed without waiting, and the next export starts a new one. An export that is only slow to print keeps the browser, so other exports running in it are not cut off. The context's close after an export still waits at most one more limit, so a browser that stalls during a print gets its answer after at most two limits (60 seconds), and its slots are free then.
    • Tests: pdfRendererTimeLimit.test.ts (a newContext that never answers, a late context, a hung close, a slow print). pdfRenderer.test.ts pins the request handler (abort, never continue), and pdfRendererIsolation.browser.test.ts shows with the real renderer and Chromium that no stylesheet, image or frame of the document reaches a local listener; offline alone does not stop a frame, so the abort is needed.

D-097 · New dependencies in S5

  • Context: CLAUDE.md pins every runtime dependency exactly, and D-029's checks allow only listed licences.

  • Decision:

    • mustache 4.2.0 (MIT, no dependencies).
    • @types/markdown-it 14.2.0 and @types/mustache 4.2.6 (MIT, development).
    • pdfjs-dist 6.4.299 (Apache-2.0, development, for the PDF test).
