D-098 · The Canvas side of the studio moves to S6

  • Context: LTI-005's picker includes the content bank and "new from a pattern" (D-061), and LTI-007's duplicate was to come with PROD-007 (D-062). LTI principals are not HVL members (hvlMember is false), Canvas and Feide accounts stay separate while feideLinking is off (D-063), and Canvas has no publish interface, so a draft from a pattern could not be placed.
  • Decision: The owner decided on 2026-10-28 that the bank in the picker, "new from a pattern" in Canvas and the LTI-007 duplicate in /app/play move to S6. In Canvas, S5's safe-editing dialog offers reset or cancel (D-093).
  • Consequences: Amends D-061 and D-062. S6's checklist carries the three items.

D-099 · The API contract gets binary responses and DELETE

  • Context: D-077 describes every route as JSON in packages/api-contract. The portfolio returns Markdown and PDF files, and removing a co-author or a bank listing is a DELETE. apiRoutes.ts and openApi are close to 200 lines.
  • Decision: A route may declare mediaType for a binary or text answer, which the OpenAPI document shows with Content-Disposition: attachment. The web app's apiRequest gets DELETE. The route list and the OpenAPI builder are split by area.
  • Consequences: Amends D-077. docs:api and the route test keep the document and the mounted routes in step (DOC-012).
  • Amendment (2026-10-28, S5 contracts):
    • Query parameters: a route may declare query, documented as in: query parameters (people search, course code, export format).
    • Leaf modules: content.ts imports only the leaf modules learnerInfo.ts and sourceAttribution.ts, so the contract has no import cycle that would leave a schema undefined at load.
    • Deliberate 5xx codes: the studio's own 5xx answers (hvl:duplicate-failed, hvl:pdf-*) keep their code and translated message, like the authentication 503s.
    • Areas: each studio area registers routes only, under /api, in its own module; a path-less router.use would run for every later area and is refused by a test. Middleware sits on the route itself.
    • The web app imports only types from the contract, so zod stays out of the browser bundle.

D-100 · The S5 gate, and the ALU and pilot review left open (Q17)

  • Context: The studio's texts, patterns, references, mappe template and criteria, and the bank's consent text, are drafts until ALU confirms them. Teachers in the pilot have not tried the patterns. The owner decided on 2026-10-28 that S5 may close with this review requested and open.

  • Decision: The S5 gate is the S1–S4 gate plus:

    • npm run content:check;
    • npx vitest run -t "PED-0", -t "PROD-001|PROD-009", -t "PROD-007|PROD-013" and -t "MAPPE-", and each S5 ID on its own;
    • npm run spec:trace -- --check --done-through=S5;
    • WEB_APP=dev npm start showing the studio pages and downloading both exports.

    The review is open question Q17, with a review packet in docs/reference/alu-review-s5.md.

  • Consequences: Q17 must be answered before the pilot. The manual PDF check with PAC or NVDA is recorded in the accessibility results.

D-101 · Session 6: order, specs to load, insight in tabs, and what passes to the bachelor students

  • Context: S5 passed its gate on 2026-10-30 (b8ab740), and PR #8 merged it into main (47e235e), which also answers Q16: GitHub now runs CI. S6 is the last planned session: the xAPI → Canvas grade bridge, teacher insight with k-suppression, the privacy jobs, deployment and operations, and the carry-overs from S4 and S5 (PROGRESS, S6). It is too large for the days before 1 November 2026, when the project proposal for HVL's bachelor students in programming (spring 2027) goes to HVL; their project is to review this AI-written code with their own tools and to finish the Canvas integration against ALU's test instance. Mapping S6 (six agents, 2026-10-30) also found that PROGRESS's spec-load row for S6 ("02 §5–7; 05; 00 §6") is narrower than its checklist, while CLAUDE.md §4 says to read only the listed specs, and that several parts need HVL's own Canvas, Feide or servers, which this environment cannot reach.
  • Decision: The owner decided on 2026-10-30:

    • Order: learning data first. (1) The grade bridge: LTI-010…LTI-013, DATA-012, LTI-008 and the bridge part of H5P-009. (2) Insight: INS-001…INS-010, PROD-010, the Innsikt tab of LTI-006, results by version (PROD-013) and the mappe's real results source (MAPPE-003, D-095). (3) The privacy operations: DATA-003…DATA-005, DATA-007, DATA-008, DATA-010 and NFR-006. Then deployment and operations (NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-007, SEC-004, SEC-006, UD-040, Chromium in the image for MAPPE-004), then the carry-overs (the language overlay with H5P-010, problem reporting, upstream drafts). Before 1 November the realistic target is the start, the probes, the shared infrastructure, the grade bridge and insight, with parts of the privacy operations; the rest continues afterwards or passes to the students.

    • Specs to load in S6: 02 §4–§8; 05 (all); 00 §3 (journeys J1–J5) and §6; 01 H5P-009, H5P-010, SEC-004 and SEC-006; 03 UD-003 and §6 (UD-040); 04 MAPPE-003 and MAPPE-004.

    • Insight lives in tabs only: an Innsikt tab on the activity page /aktivitet/[id] and in the Canvas view /app/play, one context at a time (D-106). There is no /innsikt page, so CLAUDE.md §2 (the apps/web routes), spec 05's code location (apps/web/src/app/innsikt/) and the Evaluator Guide §4.1 are amended.

    • Running the session: the hourly restart task stays on until S6's gate passes, and the gate keeps its full form, run in parts (D-113).

    • What passes to the students when S6 does not reach it, each with a design, a seam or a checklist:

      • the Canvas side of the studio that D-098 moved to S6: the content bank and "new from a pattern" in the Deep Linking picker, and the LTI-007 duplicate in /app/play;
      • LTI-009 Dynamic Registration (COULD), which needs a Canvas administrator to try and must not be undone by the start-up sync of LTI_PLATFORMS (D-051); S6 writes its design only;
      • confirming against the real services what S6 can only mock: HVL's Feide client (Q3); the developer key, the client and deployment IDs and feide_login (Q4); the AGS token audience, content type and error answers (D-104); how Canvas shows the line-item label (D-105, Q8); NRPS paging and role filter (LTI-008); a course copy keeping custom.contentId (LTI-007);
      • the Lumi path (D-112), including the image-size audit exceptions that expire on 2027-01-31 (D-030), early in the students' term, after which check:audit fails unless one of D-112's choices has been made;
      • whatever of the operations and carry-over steps is not reached.

      One index, docs/handoff/README.md (written in S6's step 7), says what is done, what needs HVL, where the live-contract seam is (apps/server/live/: an opt-in suite that runs the mock-platform tests against HVL's test Canvas and real Feide) and what the Canvas acceptance checklist holds. It links the runbook, the deployment checklist and the privacy documents instead of repeating them.

  • Alternatives considered: (a) Operations first, so that a deployable image exists early: the owner chose learning data, which is the product's purpose (spec 05: insight for the next seminar) and the part nobody can build from the specs alone. (b) A separate /innsikt overview across activities and courses: spec 05 §1 defines the view as one activity in one context, and an overview across contexts invites the differencing D-106 guards against. (c) Reaching everything before 1 November by testing less: the owner kept the full gate (D-113).
  • Consequences: PROGRESS's S6 row and checklist change in the same step. A part handed to the students is listed in the hand-off index, in PROGRESS's open items and in the Evaluator Guide's limitations, and its requirement is tested only for what S6 built. Where a MUST cannot pass without such a part (J1's Canvas half, "new from a pattern" in the picker, which LTI-005's "E2e in J1" needs), the J1 test is split and the gap gets its own SPEC-DEVIATION amendment once it is certain, not before. What J5's end-to-end test covers (its staging-to-production promotion is an operations procedure, not a page) is decided at the integration step, also by amendment.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: problem reporting for the pilot): the owner decided on 2026-10-24 that the pilot's testers report problems through GitHub issue forms, with a short tester guide in Nynorsk (PROGRESS, S4 and S6 step 7). This records how.
    • Two forms and nothing else: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feil.yml (a fault) and uu-barriere.yml (an accessibility barrier) ask for the steps, what was expected and what happened, the device, the browser, the assistive technology and the zoom, the page or tab and the activity type (the ten authorable types by the web app's Nynorsk names), a screenshot and the severity. The fault form also asks for the exact error text, the time and, for HVL IT, the server's log lines as a code block; the barrier form asks for the manual protocol's set-up and result file when the barrier was found in a protocol run. config.yml turns blank issues off, so no issue skips the forms, and links the guide (docs/testing/rapportere-problem.md) and the security policy.
    • No personal data in an issue: each form opens with the rule and requires a ticked confirmation: no names of students or colleagues, no e-mail addresses, Feide IDs, national identity or student numbers, no students' answers, and screenshots cropped or covered (Canvas shows the user's name and picture). The server's log lines may be pasted, because they hold no personal data by design (DATA-009); Canvas's and the browser's logs may not. A log line that does show personal data is itself a privacy fault and is reported privately. An issue is a path from the pilot to development, so this is DATA-010's "production data is never copied to development" applied to issues; a fault is reproduced with synthetic test data only.
    • Security goes privately: SECURITY.md names HVL's contact (a placeholder the owner fills) and GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (which the owner turns on). A vulnerability, or a privacy fault that someone could misuse, never goes into an issue or a pull request.
    • Severity and labels: three levels, and the reporter picks the highest that fits: 1 Kritisk (someone cannot use it at all, or it concerns privacy or security), 2 UU-barriere, 3 Kosmetisk; a barrier that stops someone completely is level 1. The labels are listed in .github/labels.yml: two types, the three severities, four statuses and H5P oppstraums. A form adds its type label and treng vurdering; the person who triages sets the severity label that matches the reporter's choice, because a form cannot set a label from a choice. The owner creates the labels with gh label create (docs/testing/labels-and-triage.md); the agent creates nothing on GitHub.
    • How a problem is fixed: it is reproduced in the test set-up, a test that fails is written first, the cause is fixed, the area's tests and the gate pass, and the change goes on a branch with a pull request that HVL reviews and merges. A problem seen only in HVL's Canvas or Feide needs the error text and the server's log lines; one seen only on a device or with a screen reader needs a precise description and a re-test by HVL (treng HVL-test). H5P's own barriers are repaired at run time or registered (D-080) and reported upstream (D-112). Manual results stay dated in docs/accessibility/results/ (D-079), linked from the issue and back.
    • Language: the guide and the forms are in Nynorsk only: GitHub's forms have no language switch, they are not product UI (the three locales of DOC-009 cover the product), and the pilot's testers read Nynorsk. The maintainers' label and triage document is in English, as developer documents are.
    • Alternatives considered: (a) a feedback form in the product: it would store free text that can hold personal data, would need its own privacy review, and would come too late for the pilot; (b) e-mail to a shared inbox: no labels, no link from a problem to the test and the pull request that fix it, and nothing the bachelor students can pick up; (c) a GitHub Actions workflow that sets the severity label from the choice: it needs write access to issues and would run on text from anyone, for a step a person does in seconds.
    • Consequences: tools/issue-forms/ checks the forms, the chooser and the label list on every test run. The hand-off index links the guide. Before the pilot the owner creates the labels, fills in HVL's security contact and turns on private vulnerability reporting. If the repository moves, the absolute links in the forms and in config.yml move with it.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: the students' hand-off index, the live-contract seam and the Canvas acceptance checklist): decided before the documents and the seam were written.
    • The index: docs/handoff/README.md is in English, the language of the developer documents and of the students' project (DOC-009), with a short summary in Nynorsk at the top. Five parts: what is done, by session and requirement, with where to read it (the README module maps, this file, docs/TRACEABILITY.md, the spec site, PROGRESS's gate output); what needs HVL (the open questions, hosting, the DPO, the manual accessibility run, the 200-learner load test, the restore drill and the owner's own tasks); what passes to the students; suggested review targets for their code-review project, the riskiest modules first, each with why; and how to set up (the Codespaces container, a local machine, CI). It links the runbook, the deployment checklist, the privacy documents and PROGRESS instead of repeating them, and names no person.
    • One design note per item that passes on, beside the index: canvas-studio.md (D-098's three items), dynamic-registration.md (LTI-009), branching-paths.md (INS-004, deferred by D-115), insight-freshness.md (Q24), research-export.md (the students' part of docs/privacy/research-export.md, Q25), simplification-check.md (plan step 10's check, for whatever S6 does not reach), lumi-path.md (D-112's three choices before 2027-01-31) and live-contract-seam.md. A note states what is known, the options and a recommended default, the tests it would need and what must be decided first. It decides nothing: each choice gets its own decision or amendment here before code (CLAUDE.md §1).
    • The live-contract seam (apps/server/live/): D-101 above describes it as running "the mock-platform tests against HVL's test Canvas". As written that cannot work: those tests drive the mock's own controls (fault injection, setMembers, deleteLineItem) and launch made-up users, which a real Canvas has no equivalent for. The seam instead states each fact the mocks assume as a check that can run against either platform: the client-credentials token (the assertion's audience, the token answer, a refused audience, a scope the developer key lacks); AGS (the line item a Deep Linking return created, with its label in the configured AGS_LABEL_MODE, a line item read, 404 for a missing line item, 401 without the score scope and with a bad token, the answer for a user outside the course and, only with a named test student, a score sent by our own AgsScoreClient); NRPS (the media type, the full role URI against the short name Learner, paging links, no names or e-mail addresses under privacy_level anonymous, 401 for a token without the NRPS scope); and Feide's discovery document and key set. The checks call the server's own modules where one exists (signClientAssertion, AgsAccessTokens, AgsScoreClient, scoresUrlOf, outcomeOfStatus, LEARNER_ROLE_URI, activeLearnerCount, buildDeepLinkItems), so a difference shows in the code that runs in production, and each failure message names the mock module that assumed otherwise.
    • When it runs: only when asked. The LIVE_CANVAS_* variables select ALU's test Canvas, with LIVE_DATABASE_URL and LIVE_DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEYS of the test server whose /lti/keys the developer key names, from which the tool key is read as the grade worker reads it, read-only. LIVE_FEIDE_ISSUER selects real Feide's public discovery. LIVE_TARGET=mock runs the same checks against the mock Canvas and the mock Feide on the local services, so a check is known to work before it meets Canvas, and refuses to start when a Canvas target is also set. With none of them every check is skipped; a partly set Canvas target fails at once, naming the missing variables, rather than skipping. The tests use describe.runIf, as realClamd.test.ts does, so spec-trace counts their [ID] titles; they lie outside the root Vitest projects, so the gate's per-ID runs do not select them, and they are evidence about Canvas only through a dated run recorded with the checklist.
    • Safety: the Canvas checks read only the platform row (and its key) from the test server's database, post a score only when LIVE_CANVAS_STUDENT_SUB names a test student, and never print a token, an assertion, a key or a member's ID (DATA-009). They are for a test course with test accounts only, never a course with real students.
    • The Canvas acceptance checklist (docs/handoff/canvas-acceptance.md) holds the steps against ALU's test instance that a test cannot automate: the developer key and deployment (Q4), launches in a browser that blocks third-party cookies, the Deep Linking round trip from each placement (Q13), the assignment name and points Canvas shows (Q8), a score in the gradebook, a deleted assignment, a course copy (LTI-007), Student View (D-102's test user), feide_login (Q4) and a real Feide login (Q3), and the seam's run. Each step names the mock assumption it confirms and what changes when Canvas differs: a decision or amendment first, then the mock and its tests, then the code. Results are recorded dated, without personal data.
    • Alternatives considered: (a) a Playwright flow that signs in to Canvas to automate the Deep Linking round trip: it needs a test account's password in the environment and breaks with each change to Canvas's pages; the checklist does it by hand and the seam checks its result through AGS. (b) A developer key for the seam alone: Canvas ties a line item to the tool that created it (verify), so a second key could not read or score the tool's line items. (c) Running the seam against the mock in every CI run: worth doing, but it needs a script and a CI step outside the hand-off's files (below).
    • Consequences: for the integrator: a root script test:live (vitest run --root apps/server --config live/vitest.live.config.ts), apps/server's typecheck script adding live/tsconfig.json, a CI step with LIVE_TARGET=mock if wanted, and links to the index from the root README's documentation map, the Evaluator Guide's limitations and PROGRESS's step 7.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: problem reporting, after review): a review of the reporting files changed three things before the pilot. (1) Health data: why someone uses assistive technology is health information (GDPR art. 9), and an issue ties it to the reporter's GitHub account in public. The forms ask which assistive technology was used and say that the reason is not needed; the guide adds health to what is never written and offers the contact person, who opens the issue without the tester's account; triage removes such text like other personal data. (2) Level 2, UU-barriere, is any barrier that hinders someone or withholds information while they can still go on, also without assistive technology (low vision, no sound, a video without captions); level 1 stays "cannot use it at all". (3) What an edit cannot undo: an uploaded screenshot stays reachable at its URL after it is removed from the text (verify), and notification e-mails cannot be recalled, so the guide asks testers to edit at once and tell their contact person, and triage asks GitHub Support to delete the file; real data about someone still goes to the DPO the same day.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: the live-contract seam and the hand-off index, after review): a review of the seam and the index changed four things before hand-off. (1) What a failing check prints: Vitest prints what an assertion was given, so the NRPS checks printed members' user_ids and, in the very case they exist to catch, a member's name and e-mail address. They now compare counts and booleans only; the seam's safety rule above holds for failures too. (2) Where a token goes: a line item's id and a Link: next URL come from Canvas's answers, and the seam sent the bearer token to them unchecked; a URL that is not on LIVE_CANVAS_API_ORIGIN is now refused before anything is sent (onApiOrigin, tested in canvasRequests.test.ts), as the server checks a launch's service URLs (D-104). (3) LIVE_AGS_LABEL_MODE set alone counts as a Canvas target set in part and fails loudly, like LIVE_CANVAS_STUDENT_SUB. (4) The index and the checklist as built: /app/play shows Innsikt and Poeng til Canvas only to a launch that may edit (D-106's amendment), so a copied course's teacher who may not edit sees Spel only; the checklist expects that, and canvas-studio.md lists LTI-007's insight tab with the duplicate. The index says which parts of LTI-005 and LTI-007 are built, since TRACEABILITY marks a requirement tested once one test names it.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: the integration): decided before the integrator's changes; it applies what the five step-7 workstreams (the language overlay, problem reporting, the upstream drafts, the hand-off index with the live-contract seam, and the hardening after step 6's review) left for integration.
    • The seam runs from the root and in CI against the mocks. A root script test:live runs apps/server/live/vitest.live.config.ts; apps/server's typecheck also checks live/tsconfig.json; and CI runs npm run test:live with LIVE_TARGET=mock after the end-to-end step (about 10 s), so a change to a mock or to the server code the seam calls cannot break the checks unnoticed before the students point them at Canvas. Without the variable, or with a Canvas target, nothing in CI changes: CI never holds a Canvas or Feide secret.
    • One read of content/h5p-tekstar/. main.ts passes the start-up's loaded H5P texts to createH5pRuntime (D-111), so the overlay the engine uses is the one the start checked, and a test's content folder reaches the engine (startupLanguageOverlay.test.ts). createH5pRuntime still loads the folder itself when no overlay is given (the seed command, the test beds).

Checked on 2026-11-05 at the pinned commit and on the default branch (114f513): both pass endCardTableRowSummary, which the semantics do not have.

  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 8: the journey tests and the Canvas half of the studio): it records what the Consequences above left to an amendment. The step-8 tests cited D-101 for both before it existed, and spec 02 §8 still said these parts "come in S6" (found in the docs-trace review). The tests named are in apps/server/.
    • J1 is split (SPEC-DEVIATION from LTI-005's "E2e in J1" and PROD-001's "e2e for J1"). The picker lists the author's own and co-authored activities only: its content bank (LTI-005 (a)) and «Create new» from a pattern (LTI-005 (b), J1 step 2) pass to the students with docs/handoff/canvas-studio.md parts 1 and 2, as the LTI-007 duplicate in /app/play and a copied course's Innsikt tab do with its part 3. That only admin installs or updates libraries, also through an uploaded .h5p, and that nobody installs from the Hub, is proved over HTTP by test/http/packageImport.int.test.ts and test/http/ajax.int.test.ts (H5P-006, SEC-003, H5P-011), not in a browser. Installing a new version in staging, verifying it and promoting it to production is the procedure A new content-type version in docs/ops/runbook.md §2: the re-pinned manifest in a pull request, one image with its bundle, the seed step and checks in staging, then the same image in production. No test runs it; HVL operations does.

D-102 · SPEC-DEVIATION LTI-010: the xAPI bridge is plain JavaScript in the player document, for learners only

  • Context: LTI-010 puts the bridge in packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.ts: it subscribes to H5P.externalDispatcher and posts statements to /api/h5p/xapi every 2 s and on pagehide, with the ltik or the CSRF token, retrying from an in-memory queue and never slowing the activity down. H5P-009 injects it "inside the H5P iframe", CLAUDE.md §2 describes the theme package as "injected into H5P player and editor iframes", and UD-003 says the bridge adds the visually hidden ✓/✗ text. What S4–S6 found:
    • The theme's client scripts are plain JavaScript (an IIFE with JSDoc: feedbackPrefixes.js, a11yRepairs.js, reducedMotion.js), which the package exports from src/ and the server serves unbundled under script-src 'self' (D-070). There is no browser build for TypeScript.
    • H5P Core relays every event raised in an iframe it wrote itself (H5P.isFramed && H5P.externalEmbed === false) to window.parent.H5P.externalDispatcher (h5p.js). The document that holds H5PIntegration therefore sees the statements of div-embedded and iframe-embedded content alike. A bridge only inside the iframes would miss div-embedded content, one in both places would send each iframe statement twice, and every frame would need the credential.
    • The hidden prefix already comes from feedbackPrefixes.js (D-072 amendment (a)); a second one from the bridge would be announced twice.
    • H5P sends no attempt identifier, but DATA-012 stores an attemptId.
    • Authors play activities too: the portal's Spel tab is the author's preview, and teachers open /app/play.
  • Decision:
    • File and place: packages/hvl-h5p-theme/src/xapiBridge.js, plain JavaScript in the style of its siblings. It runs only in the player document that h5p/render/playerPage.ts renders (/h5p/play/:contentId in the portal, /lti/play in Canvas): not in Core's iframes, not in the Next.js page around them, and never in the editor.
    • Once per statement: it subscribes to that document's H5P.externalDispatcher and queues a statement object once, so a statement relayed from a Core iframe is not queued twice. Probe P1 checks this on the ten real types.
    • Learners only: the player page loads the bridge only for a learner principal (whose highest role is learner), and the server stores and grades statements only from one; anyone else's request stores nothing. LTI-011's View check still applies, and in Canvas the content must also be the launched activity. Previews in the portal and teachers' plays in Canvas never reach insight or the gradebook.
    • Attempts: the bridge makes a random attemptId for the root activity when the page loads, and a new one after the root's scored completed or answered statement, so a retry is a new attempt. Probe P1 records the real attempt boundaries of the ten types; a different rule is an amendment made before the mapper is written.
    • Credentials: in Canvas, the ltik as Authorization: Bearer from the page's memory (LTI-003); in the portal, the session cookie with the X-CSRF-Token header (D-057). /api/h5p/xapi takes no ltik in the query (D-058, D-069).
    • Sending: a batch every 2 s. On pagehide, fetch with keepalive: true, which can carry those headers (navigator.sendBeacon cannot). A failed batch stays in the in-memory queue and is retried while the page lives; nothing goes to browser storage, and the activity never waits for the bridge. Browsers limit keepalive requests to 64 KiB in flight per page, so a very large last flush can lose its tail; for formative data that is accepted.
    • Time: the stored timestamp is when the server received the batch, not what the browser claims.
    • No feedback text: the bridge adds no ✓/✗ prefix; feedbackPrefixes.js does (D-072).
  • Alternatives considered: (a) A bridge inside every H5P iframe, as H5P-009 reads: statements missed or sent twice, and the ltik or CSRF token handed to every frame. (b) TypeScript compiled for the browser: a build step for one file that its siblings do not have. (c) Storing everyone's statements and filtering when reading: previews would still be stored as learning data, and the grade worker would need the same filter.
  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION from LTI-010 (the file is JavaScript, xapiBridge.js) and, for the bridge, from H5P-009: it runs in the player document, not "inside the H5P iframe", so the acceptance's check of the iframe document becomes a check of the player document (the theme part is unchanged; D-070 deviated from H5P-009 the same way for nonces). The code carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-102. Amended in the same step: CLAUDE.md §2 (the bridge's file and where it runs), H5P-009, and UD-003 (the hidden prefix comes from feedbackPrefixes.js, never from the bridge, as D-072 amendment (a) already decided). Residuals, for the DPIA input and the students' checklist: Canvas's Student View sends the TestUser role, which D-059 maps to learner, so a teacher's Student View play counts as one learner in insight and is graded for Canvas's test student; reloading the page in the middle of an attempt starts a new attemptId, which inflates INS-001's median attempts; and a learner can forge their own statements and attempt IDs, which LTI-013 already accepts.
  • Amendment (2026-10-30, probe P1): D-115 makes three parts of this decision concrete. Once per statement: the bridge registers only in a document that is not one of Core's iframes (window.frameElement is not an h5p-iframe) and ignores an event that H5P.isFramed && H5P.externalEmbed === false marks as relayed; a set of seen events cannot work, because each window's bridge has its own. Learners only: the bridge is the last script in playerGlobalAssets, and the player page leaves it and its configuration out for anyone but a learner principal; without a configuration it does nothing. The server's own check is unchanged. Attempts: the rule stands, written as attemptId = <viewId>:<n>. The bridge sends only the statements the server stores, each with a statementId that the server inserts once, and the stored timestamp keeps the batch's order (D-115).
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 3 integration): the bridge is three player-only scripts, not one file, to keep within DOC-007's 200 lines: xapiStatements.js (D-115's root tests and the cut), xapiBatching.js (sizes, fitting, back-off) and xapiBridge.js, still the last script in playerGlobalAssets (XAPI_BRIDGE_FILES, never in HVL_THEME_FILES, so never in the editor). Its configuration is a separate inert JSON block #hvl-xapi-bridge (endpoint, content ID and version, and the request's own ltik or CSRF token), not a key of H5PIntegration, so Core's iframes, which copy H5PIntegration, never see the token. The endpoint must be same-origin path segments (/api/h5p/xapi), or the bridge does not start. ESLint's LTI-003 storage ban covers the three scripts. Where CLAUDE.md §2 and spec 01's H5P-009 and spec 02's LTI-010 notes name xapiBridge.js alone, they mean these three (CLAUDE.md is the owner's to amend). The end-to-end test e2e/xapiToCanvas.e2e.test.ts runs the bridge in a real Canvas launch into /app/play and checks that a portal author's preview loads none of it.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-4 privacy review: Canvas's Student View): Found: the residual above is worse than a single extra learner. Canvas's Student View launches a test student with the LTI TestUser role (http://purl.imsglobal.org/vocab/lti/system/person#TestUser, which D-059 maps to learner), and each «Reset Student» makes a new test student, so a new sub and a new learnerKey (verify with TeCopp). A teacher who plays k − 1 test students beside one real learner makes a group of k in which every value is that learner's, so insight, the mappe and every k count would show what one learner did. Decided:
    • Carried, not refused: the launch facts say testUser when the roles claim holds the TestUser role (lti/LtiRoleMapper.ts isLtiTestUser, read in lti/launchFacts.ts), and the principal carries it as Principal.lti.testUser (lti/ltikPrincipal.ts). Nothing else about the principal changes: it is a learner.
    • Stored, flagged: a test student's statements are stored as before, with XapiStatement.testUser = true (a column, default false; migration s6_test_user_statements), so the grade worker still sends its score and a teacher can test the passback to Canvas's gradebook. The flag comes from the principal, never from the body.
    • Left out of every aggregate: insight's statement reader (insight/data/insightStatements.ts) and the mappe's results source (learningDesign/mappe/storedActivityResults.ts) read only rows with testUser = false, so a test student is never in a view, a distribution, a «Starta» count, a mappe group or any other count compared with k. The grade queue (grades/) reads one learner's own rows by learnerKey and is unchanged.
    • Not chosen: storing nothing for a test student (the teacher could not test the passback, and the grade job needs stored results, D-104); keeping test students out of the counts by their role at read time (the role is not stored, and every reader would need it).
    • Consequences: testUser is a field outside DATA-012's list, a SPEC-DEVIATION like academicYear (D-107): it holds no statement data, only that the launch was Canvas's test student; spec 05 gets a note on DATA-012. The data inventory has its row. The purge and the data-subject CLI treat these rows like any other. Canvas's NRPS count (LTI-008) is Canvas's: whether it lists the test student is not known (verify with TeCopp); if it does, the course count is one higher than the real learners, which only lowers a completion rate. Verified by LtiRoleMapper.test.ts, launchFacts.test.ts, xapiTestUser.int.test.ts (mock Canvas launches with the TestUser role through the real ingestion route: the flagged rows, the queued grade job, and the insight route, where four learners and two test students stay «< 5») and storedActivityResults.int.test.ts.

D-103 · Course contexts are stored with their platform: <platformId>:<contextId>

  • Context: DATA-012 stores a contextId? per statement, InsightSnapshot has one, LTI-008 caches a learner count per context, and INS-007 limits a Canvas author to "that context only". A Canvas context ID is unique within one Canvas only. Every hosted Canvas shares the issuer https://canvas.instructure.com, so a platform is known by issuer and client ID (docs/reference/canvas-platform-values.md, D-051), and Canvas's test and beta instances are copies of production with the same course IDs (verify with TeCopp). LtiPlacement keeps platformId and contextId apart, but XapiStatement.contextId and InsightSnapshot.contextId hold the bare ID, so courses from two of HVL's Canvas instances could merge in insight.
  • Decision: Wherever S6 stores or compares a course for insight and grades, it uses the string <LtiPlatform.id>:<context ID>, where the context ID is the launch's context claim (idToken.launch.context.id, read in lti/launchFacts.ts; never ltijs's LaunchContext.contextId, CLAUDE.md §5). That covers XapiStatement.contextId, InsightSnapshot.contextId, the Redis key of the NRPS learner count, the insight scope and its list of contexts (D-106), and the data-subject export (D-108). The platform ID is a UUID, so the first : splits the string whatever the context ID contains. A portal play has no context (null). One module builds and parses the string; nothing else joins or splits it.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) A platformId column beside contextId on the analytics tables: tidier, but a field outside DATA-012's list (a SPEC-DEVIATION), and every index and query would need both. (b) Keeping the bare ID: a teacher in HVL's production Canvas could see aggregates that include plays from a test instance.
  • Consequences: DATA-012's field list is unchanged; the data inventory says what the value holds. The platform ID is stable while the platform stays in LTI_PLATFORMS, and a removed platform is deactivated, not deleted (D-051), so stored contexts still resolve. The NRPS count key and the xAPI rate-limit key are added by hand to the inventory's Redis section, which the inventory check does not read. H5PUserData.contextId (learner state per course, auth/principalToH5pActor.ts) keeps the bare ID: a collision there only shares one learner's own saved state between two copies of the same course, while changing the key would reset every learner's saved progress. The students' checklist names it.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 3 integration): the one module is apps/server/src/xapi/platformContextKey.ts (platformContextKey, parsePlatformContextKey, principalContextKey); the NRPS count imports it. A Canvas launch without a storable course (an empty context claim, over 255 characters, or with a line break; ltijs accepts such a launch): a learner's xAPI batch is answered 202, nothing is stored, and the log counts it as noCourse. Storing it under null would make it a portal play, 403 would misread a launched activity, and a 500 would make the bridge resend for as long as the page is open. Spec 02's LTI-011 note says the same.

D-104 · SPEC-DEVIATION LTI-012: our own minimal AGS client in a durable worker, not ltijs's submitScore

  • Context: LTI-012 has a worker call context.grading.submitScore(lineItemUrl, …); spec 02 §1 lists grading.submitScore on ltijs's LaunchContext among "the APIs used below"; and CLAUDE.md §5 names context.grading.submitScore among the ltijs 7 calls to use (D-005). In ltijs 7.0.7 that method exists only on a LaunchContext, which Provider.getLaunchContext(ltik) rebuilds from a live ltik (24 h). It takes the platform and the learner's sub from that context, and its token from an internal AccessTokenManager (services/grading/grading.service.js). The package exports only Provider and types (its exports map has "." alone), so neither service can be used without a launch. A durable worker runs after the learner's request is gone and holds no ltik; keeping one for it would store a bearer credential for the learner's whole launch, against CLAUDE.md §1 (the ltik is kept in memory only). LTI-012 itself already lets a job that outlives the 24 h "request a new client-credentials token itself".
  • Decision:
    • Token: AgsScoreClient in apps/server/src/grades/ requests the client-credentials token itself, from the first attempt. Its JWT client assertion is signed RS256 with the tool's private key for that platform, read through ltijs's Provider.platformManager (getPlatformById, getPrivateKey; our PrismaLtiDatabaseManager decrypts it, D-056). It carries the claims ltijs's own token manager signs: iss = sub = the client ID; aud = the platform's token endpoint (ltijs's default while authorizationServer stays unset, which Canvas accepts, canvas-platform-values.md §2); a fresh jti; a 60 s lifetime; and kid = the platform ID, which /lti/keys publishes. Scopes: …/lti-ags/scope/score and …/lti-ags/scope/lineitem.readonly. A token is cached per platform and scope until shortly before it expires, and is never logged.
    • Score: a POST to the line item's URL with /scores added to its path (any query string kept, as ltijs does), with the content type application/vnd.ims.lis.v1.score+json and LTI-012's body: the learner's sub as userId, scoreGiven, scoreMaximum: 100, activityProgress: 'Completed', gradingProgress: 'FullyGraded' and timestamp.
    • Queue: a GradeSyncJob is written only for a learner principal in a Canvas launch (D-102), a root statement (no subContentId) with the verb completed or answered and a result.score, and a placement found by (platformId, contextId, resourceLinkId) that has a lineItemUrl. Jobs are idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId): a later scored statement of the same attempt updates its job. The learner's sub comes from the request's launch and is stored only encrypted (ltiSubEncrypted, D-056).
    • Worker: a LeasedIntervalJob (one node at a time) claims due jobs about every 15 s (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the new nextAttemptAt) and coalesces them per (placement, learnerKey). It applies the placement's stored attempt policy (best, latest, or mastery with its threshold; defaults as in LTI-012) to that learner's attempt scores in the placement's jobs (an XapiStatement has no placement, and DATA-012 fixes its fields), sends one score with timestamp = the time of sending, and settles the coalesced jobs together. AGS lets a platform ignore a score older than the result it holds; sending one current score means that a late retry can never put an old result back.
    • Outcomes: a 2xx answer succeeds. A line item that no longer exists (404, confirmed with a lineitem.readonly read) marks the job orphaned, a new status, and it is not retried. A 429, a 5xx or a network error is retried with exponential backoff and jitter, at most 8 attempts, the last within 24 h of the first; then the job is failed. A 401 fetches a new token once. Any other 4xx fails the job at once. The new terminalAt records when a job stopped.
    • The sub: ltiSubEncrypted is set to null 30 days after terminalAt, whether the job succeeded, failed or was orphaned (DATA-002 names success; a job that never succeeds keeps it no longer). A failed job retried after that has no sub; it stays failed, and the learner's next scored play makes a new job.
    • Authors see the counts sent, pending, failed and orphaned per placement on the activity page and in /app/play, and retry failed jobs there (LTI-012's acceptance). Who may see them follows D-106; the counts are not k-suppressed (spec 05 §3).
    • NRPS (LTI-008) still uses ltijs's context.namesAndRoles: it runs during a launch, while the context lives.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) submitScore with a stored ltik: a 24-hour bearer credential stored per learner, and the job still fails once it expires. (b) submitScore inside the learner's own request: learning would wait for Canvas, against LTI-012's acceptance, and nothing would retry once the page is closed. (c) ltijs within the 24 h and our client after, the spec's literal reading: two code paths for one request, and the first still needs an ltik in the worker. (d) Importing ltijs's internal AccessTokenManager by file path: refused by the package's exports, and it would break silently with an ltijs update.
  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION, exactly from: LTI-012's sentence "A worker calls context.grading.submitScore(…)"; spec 02 §1's row naming grading.submitScore among the APIs used; and CLAUDE.md §5's list of ltijs calls, which repeats D-005's API context. D-005's decision (ltijs 7 with our PrismaLtiDatabaseManager) is unchanged, and ltijs still handles launches, Deep Linking, NRPS and the key set (D-061 likewise replaced createDeepLinkingForm with ltijs's message and our own form). Not deviated: the score body, the policies, the retry limit, idempotency, orphaned and the developer key's scopes. The code carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-104; spec 02 §1 and §6 and CLAUDE.md §5 get amendment notes. Migration s6_grade_bridge_insight adds orphaned, nextAttemptAt, attemptId and terminalAt. What Canvas does that S6 can only mock (the token's aud on HVL's instance, the answers for a deleted assignment and for a learner who has left the course) goes into the students' Canvas acceptance checklist (D-101). Residual: the learner key changes on 1 August (D-011), so a learner's policy history starts again, and in a course that runs across 1 August an earlier best score can be replaced by a lower later one; accepted for D-011's reason (the summer break) and named in the checklist.
  • Amendment (2026-10-30, probe P1): "a root statement (no subContentId) with the verb completed or answered and a result.score" is D-115's gradable root result: the root by three structural tests, the activity's main library in its category, score.max above 0, and not a replay. scoreGiven is scaled × 100. Each attempt holds at most one such result, so latest is the job created last. "A later scored statement of the same attempt" is then a duplicate, which the statement's ID already stops, or a forged one (LTI-013), which still updates its job as above (D-115).
  • Amendment (2026-10-30, S6 step 3): latest is not "the job created last" (P1 amendment above): it is the job whose result was stored last, by GradeSyncJob.resultAt, then by attempt number and attempt ID (D-115's step-3 amendment).
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-3 security review, findings 1 and 4: the queue): Found: jobs were per attempt, and D-115 makes every gradable root result an attempt, so one Canvas learner could write a job for each of the 120 statements a minute that LTI-011 lets them post per activity, all made up. The worker claims at most 50 due jobs a run, oldest first, every 15 s (about 200 a minute), so one learner could hold back every other learner's score, and the table grew with every result. Separately (finding 4), a job was lost when its write failed after the batch's statements were stored, since the batch is answered 202 and a resend is skipped. Decided, in place of "Jobs are idempotent per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId)" above and the two amendments before this one:
    • One job per placement and learner. idempotencyKey is <placementId>:<learnerKey>, so the queue holds at most one job per pair, however many results a learner stores. The job is that learner's score in that gradebook column. A newly stored gradable result updates its attemptId, scoreGiven and resultAt (the result the job took in last, which the worker's settlement compares) and the encrypted sub (from the request); a pending job keeps its attempts and nextAttemptAt; a stopped job (succeeded, failed or orphaned) becomes pending at once, with its attempts, terminalAt, succeededAt and lastError reset and createdAt set to that moment, so each reopening gets the 8 attempts within 24 hours again. An author's retry still keeps createdAt (one attempt per retry after the 24 hours). LTI-012's idempotency per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId) holds a fortiori: a result taken in twice changes nothing but the job's state.
    • The score comes from the stored results, read when it is sent. The worker applies the placement's policy to the learner's stored gradable root results (D-115) of the placement's activity in the placement's course (<platformId>:<contextId>, D-103): best the highest, latest the last in D-115's result order (timestamp, then attempt number, then attempt ID), mastery 100 once any reaches the threshold, else the latest. It reads the best result and the results with the latest timestamp, which give the same score as all of them. A job with no stored result (a data-subject erasure, or a link that now opens another activity) fails as no-result, unsent.
    • Fair claiming. A run still claims at most 50 jobs, oldest due first; as a job is one learner's score, one learner takes at most one place a run. A job that takes in a result while its score is in flight is not settled over: it is due again at once (a retry keeps its backoff), so the new result goes at the next run, not after the 30-minute claim.
    • Reconciling (finding 4). Each run also reopens a stopped job, sub still kept, whose learner has a gradable result in the job's activity and course stored after the job's resultAt, from 15 minutes up to 1 minute before the run (the minute lets the ingestion's own job write finish first), and takes that result in as above. This mends a failed job write for a learner who already has the job. One whose first job write failed has no job, and so no sub in our records: their next gradable result in that placement writes the job, whose send includes the lost result; if they never play again it never reaches Canvas. A failure while the worker was down for more than 15 minutes is likewise left to the learner's next result. Both are residuals for the students' checklist; an outbox in the ingestion's transaction would close them, at the price of a grade write in every batch.
    • No cap on stored results per minute: with the queue bounded by pairs, a flood costs at most one score post per learner and run; LTI-011's limit still bounds the statements, whose table grows with it as before.
    • Consequences: the status counts (D-106) are learners' scores in each state, one per learner and placement, not attempts; they are still LTI-012's "counts of sent / pending / failed". That a count can then be about one learner, also in a colleague's course whose counts an owner or co-author sees unsuppressed (D-106's residual), is recorded for the DPO (docs/privacy/DPIA-INPUT.md, R1; Q22). Two links to one activity in one course read the same stored results (a statement names no link, DATA-012), graded or not: each graded link applies its own policy and has a job only for a learner who played that link, and that learner's score there also counts plays through the other link, an ungraded practice link included, whose newer results also reopen the stopped job (the reconciling pass). Keeping them apart needs the link in the statement, a DATA-012 change for the owner to weigh (the skeptic review of 2026-11-04). The S6 migration is unchanged; the meaning of idempotencyKey, attemptId, scoreGiven, resultAt and createdAt changes as above, which the schema's comments and the data inventory must say. Rows written per attempt before this amendment (development databases; S6 is not deployed) are still sent and settled; their learner's next result writes the per-learner job. Spec 02 LTI-012 gets an amendment note.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-3 security review, finding 2: the line item's URL): the worker sends the learner's sub and a bearer token to the lineItemUrl that the launch's AGS claim names, and nothing checked it. Canvas serves AGS on the institution's own domain (canvas-platform-values.md §1, the AGS service URLs row), the domain CANVAS_ORIGINS already lists so that Canvas may frame the tool. Decided: a line item URL is allowed only when it parses as a URL, holds no user name or password, uses https where https is required (production), and its origin is in CANVAS_ORIGINS or is the origin of one of the platform's own configured URLs (its issuer, as a self-hosted Canvas serves AGS on its issuer's host, and its authorisation and token endpoints). The placement recorder checks it at every launch and stores none instead (the link is then not graded; the refusal is logged with its origin only); the worker checks it again before it asks for a token, and fails the job as line-item-url without any request (a URL stored before this rule, or after CANVAS_ORIGINS changed). Redirects were already refused. Wiring: the server passes CANVAS_ORIGINS and NODE_ENV === 'production' to both; without them only the platform's own origins are allowed, and production's checks keep those on https (productionChecks.ts). Not chosen: a per-platform origin list in LTI_PLATFORMS (a configuration change, while HVL's CANVAS_ORIGINS names HVL's own Canvas domains only); a DNS check against private addresses, which the allow-list makes unnecessary.

D-105 · The formative line-item label is configurable, and scores are labelled formative wherever shown

  • Context: LTI-013 labels AGS scores formative with the suffix "(formativ)" on the line-item label. On assignment_selection Canvas uses that label as the assignment name and overwrites the teacher's own; spec 02 leaves to HVL and ALU whether the suffix belongs there, or in the content item's description with Canvas's preserveExistingAssignmentName extension (Q8, open). lti/deepLinking/deepLinkItems.ts sends the plain title today. LTI-013 (c) also says that these scores are never presented as exam evidence, and S6 shows scores in three new places: the insight views, the INS-009 CSV and the grade-sync status.
  • Decision:
    • AGS_LABEL_MODE, read at start-up, chooses between:
      • suffix, the default and the spec as written: the line item's label is «Tittel (formativ)», the title cut when needed so the suffix is never lost;
      • preserve: the label is the title, the content item carries "https://canvas.instructure.com/lti/preserveExistingAssignmentName": true, and its description says that the score is formative.
    • The suffix is «(formativ)», as LTI-013 writes it, in every language.
    • The insight views, the CSV and the grade-sync status say that the scores are formative, computed in the browser and not exam evidence, with PROD-011's notice or a label from the same locale texts.
    • Q8 stays open; HVL and ALU's answer changes the setting, not the code.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) Only the suffix, waiting for Q8: a "no" from HVL would need a new release. (b) Only preserve: it departs from LTI-013 (a) before HVL has decided.
  • Consequences: A unit test checks the label in both modes (LTI-013's Verify). A change of mode affects new placements only; assignments already in Canvas keep their names. How Canvas shows the name in each mode is on the students' Canvas acceptance checklist (verify).

D-106 · SPEC-DEVIATION spec 05 §1: insight per context, fixed periods, suppression as INS-006 writes it

  • Context:
    • INS-007: owners and co-authors see an activity's insight; in LTI mode, authors of the launch context see that context only; admins only through an audited support action; every view is audited (DATA-007).
    • Spec 05 §1: the view covers one activity in one Canvas context (or all portal users), with results "since a chosen date (default 7 days ago)". §3: teachers cannot see data from other courses' contexts, and they can see grade-sync status counts, which, unlike the learner counts and answer distributions there, carry no "(groups ≥ k)".
    • INS-006: a cell, bar or list item about fewer than k learners shows "< 5" and hides its value; the next-smallest cell is hidden too when a hidden value could be worked out from the totals; and there is no per-learner endpoint. privacy/minimumGroupSize.ts (D-095) shows nothing at all below k and also hides a rate of 0 % or 100 % (the two-sided rule).
    • Found while mapping: a free "since" date lets two overlapping views isolate one learner (differencing); PROD-013 wants results separated by version; tokens.json has one non-text colour for chart marks (accent), and derived shades wait for HVL (D-017, D-072, Q2). Spec 00 §8 measures from the audit log whether pilot teachers opened Før samlinga.
  • Decision: The owner decided on 2026-10-30 that insight is shown in tabs, one context at a time (D-101). In detail:
    • One view: one activity, one content version (the current one by default; PROD-013, D-093) and one context: a Canvas context the activity is placed in (D-103), or the portal's plays. There is no view across contexts.
    • Who: for a context, the activity's owner and co-authors, and an LTI author whose launch comes from that context, whether or not they own the activity (after a course copy, LTI-007). On the activity page the owner or co-author picks one of the activity's contexts, labelled with LtiPlacement.contextLabel where one is stored (D-087); in /app/play the context is the launch's and cannot be changed. An admin gets no insight through the role: INS-007's audited support action is not built in S6, so admins see none.
    • Periods: fixed choices only: the last 7, 14 or 30 days, or since the semester started. Each starts at midnight, Oslo time, so a teacher cannot place two start dates to difference two views. The semester starts on 1 January or 1 August until HVL gives its semester dates (open; HVL and ALU decide).
    • Suppression as INS-006 writes it: each value is about a known number of distinct learners. A value about fewer than k is shown as «< k» (for example «< 5»), and the API answer carries no value for it; when a hidden value could be worked out from a shown total and the other cells, the next-smallest cell is hidden too. A free-text answer appears only when k distinct learners gave it (INS-003). D-095's two-sided rate rule is not added: a rate of 0 % or 100 % over at least k learners is shown, because "nobody got question 3 right" is the signal a seminar needs. minimumGroupSize.ts gets the insight rules beside the mappe's, and its "never shown as fewer than" stays true for the mappe.
    • Exempt: the grade-sync status counts (spec 05 §3), which Canvas's gradebook shows per learner anyway. The INS-006 property tests (D-114) cover the insight endpoints and the CSV, not those counts.
    • Charts (INS-008): a single hue, the accent token, with each value written as a label next to its bar, a visible data table and a text summary; no new colours. A suppressed cell shows its «< k» text and no bar.
    • Audit: a view writes insight.view and a CSV download insight.export (DATA-007), with the activity as the target and details limited to the view, the period, the context (D-103's string, or the portal) and the content version: no learner key, count or answer. That is enough for spec 00 §8's measure.
    • The formative label: D-105.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) An all-contexts view for owners: not in spec 05, and "all contexts minus one" differences out a single course. (b) A free "since" date, as spec 05 §1 reads: open to differencing. (c) The mappe's two-sided rule for insight rates too: it would hide the items a teacher most needs to see. (d) New chart colours: they need HVL's approval (Q2).
  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION spec 05 §1: the period is chosen from fixed values, not any date; the code that builds periods carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-106, and spec 05 gets an amendment note. Residuals for the DPIA input (DATA-005) and the DPO (Q6): views of the same period on two days differ by one day's learners; an owner or co-author sees aggregates for every course their activity is placed in, including a colleague's course that placed it from the bank or copied it, which spec 05 §3's "data from other courses' contexts" can be read to forbid, so the DPO and the owner may narrow it by amendment; and a 0 % or 100 % rate tells what every learner in a group of at least k did.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, S6 step 4: suppression and the tab as built): Found in the insight core's review: an exhaustive check of every group of two to five cells for k = 3 to 6 showed that hiding only "the next-smallest cell" lets a reader who knows the rule (it is public, here and in INS-006) work hidden counts out in about one answer in ten (with k = 5, the cells (hidden, 0, hidden, 5) of a total of 6 can only be [0, 0, 1, 5]); and INS-002's share right times its learners tells how many chose the right options, which INS-003 may hide. Decided, in place of "the next-smallest cell is hidden too" and "minimumGroupSize.ts gets the insight rules beside the mappe's" above:
    • A 0 is shown. A count of 0 is about no learner, so it singles no one out, and it is the "nobody chose this" a seminar needs, as a rate of 0 % is. A 0 is hidden only as a complement or inside a hidden group (below). SPEC-DEVIATION INS-006, whose "fewer than k" read literally takes in 0 (insight/suppression/insightCells.ts).
    • Complementary suppression. In a group whose cells add up to a shown total (a choice question's options and «no answer»; a gap's right answers, listed wrong answers, other wrong answers and empty gaps), a complement is needed when exactly one cell is hidden, or when two or more are and all hold 1 or all hold k − 1. Then every shown 0 is hidden; in a group without a 0, the smallest shown count is hidden, then each next shown count less than k above the last one hidden. A hidden total hides every cell of its group. This hides more than one "next-smallest cell" where that is needed, and never less. The tab's privacy note says that a hidden cell may hold more than k − 1 learners; nothing says which cells are complements.
    • Parts another view gives away. A single-answer choice question is protected as two parts, its right options and its wrong options with «no answer», each with its own total, since INS-002's share gives the right options' total; a task with one gap likewise (right, and the rest). A multi-answer question stays one group, since INS-002 counts only fully right answers there.
    • A hidden starter group hides every question cell. When the learners who started number 1 to k − 1, every INS-002 and INS-003 cell is hidden, zeros included, as participation and video engagement already are.
    • INS-003 for the current content version only. A version is raised only by a structural save (D-093), which may reorder options or change gaps, and older parameters are not stored, so an older version's option numbers and gap answers cannot be matched to texts. For an older version the tab says that answer distributions are shown for the current version only; participation, INS-002 and INS-005 read by sub-content and are shown for every version. SPEC-DEVIATION INS-003 for older versions (insight/buildInsightReport.ts, the web's MisconceptionSection.tsx).
    • Where the rules are: apps/server/src/insight/suppression/ (insightCells.ts, additiveGroupCells.ts), with k from minimumGroupSize() (MIN_GROUP_SIZE); privacy/minimumGroupSize.ts keeps the mappe's rules.
    • The Canvas tab: /app/play shows Innsikt to a launch that may edit the activity, as it shows Poeng til Canvas, since the launch tells the page only mayEdit. The API admits every LTI author of the launch's course where the activity is placed (as above), so a course copy's teacher who may not edit can read the view through the API but has no tab yet.
    • Verified by additiveGroupExhaustive.test.ts (every group of two to five cells, k = 3–6, with INS-002's share as known) and the [INS-006] property tests over the report, the CSV rows, and the API's JSON and CSV.
    • Residuals for the DPIA input (DATA-005, docs/privacy/DPIA-INPUT.md R6–R9) and the DPO (Q6): a share in INS-002 over k or more learners can give a count below k (10 % of 20 is 2) that INS-003 hides; when k or more learners each hold a cell of their own and no cell is empty, every cell is hidden yet each must be 1; the fixed periods are nested (7 ⊂ 14 ⊂ 30 days ⊂ the semester), so two views of the same day can isolate the learners active only in their difference; and a "first answer" is the first within the chosen period, while answers H5P accepts as small spelling errors are listed as wrong in INS-003.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-4 privacy review: when a period ends, 1 August, the gap rule as built, the summaries, the roster URL): Found in the privacy review of step 4: (a) every period ended at the request (end: now), so two views of the same period a few minutes apart differed only by what was stored in between, and a teacher who saw one learner play could read which cells that learner moved, below k (the residual above, and DPIA R3 and R8, named only views on different days); (b) a 7-, 14- or 30-day view opened from 2 to 30 August spanned 1 August, when the pseudonym secret changes (DATA-002), so a learner who played on both sides counted twice, under two keys, and a portal session keeps the old year's key up to 12 hours past 1 August (D-057); (c) the chart summaries named "the hardest" question and "the most common" wrong answer among the shown cells only, which a hidden cell can make false; (d) the gap rule the review built is not written here; (e) the NRPS roster URL behind the course count was not checked as D-104 checks a line item's URL. Decided:
    • Every period ends at the latest midnight in Oslo, the start of today: a view holds the data up to and including yesterday, and the tab says so («Tal til og med i går»). Two views of the same period on the same day are the same whatever is stored in between. The start is N days before that midnight (7 whole days for 7d), or for semester the start of the semester of the period's last day (yesterday), so on 1 January the view is the autumn semester and on 1 August the spring semester, never an empty one. The trade-off: a teacher sees today's plays tomorrow. The alternative, a new view only after k new learners, is open for the owner and ALU (PROGRESS Q24). SPEC-DEVIATION (spec 05 §1, already one for the fixed start): the view never holds today.
    • No period crosses 1 August. A view belongs to the academic year of its last day and starts no earlier than 1 August 00:00 Oslo of that year: a 7-, 14- or 30-day view whose days would reach back before it starts on 1 August instead (the 7-day view from 2 to 7 August, the 14-day view to 14 August, the 30-day view to 30 August), and the tab says the period is shortened and why. On 1 August itself the period ends at that midnight and lies wholly in the year that ended, so it is not shortened. The query also reads only rows whose academicYear (the year of the key, D-107) is the view's year, so the portal's 12-hour tail of old keys cannot count a learner twice; a portal play of 1 August under the old year's key is then in no view. The semester never crosses 1 August. Corrected 2026-11-04 (the workstream's skeptic): this item first said that every 7-, 14- and 30-day view from 2 to 30 August starts on 1 August; only one whose days reach back before 1 August does.
    • The mappe's semester groups read one year's keys too (added 2026-11-04, the workstream's skeptic): the mappe counts each course, version and semester as a group of its own and leaves out every group of fewer than k (D-095's amendment of 2026-11-04), and its autumn semester starts on 1 August. Read by time alone, the portal's 12-hour tail made one learner two in that group, under the old and the new key, so k − 1 learners could make a group of k that insight's semester view of the same course shows as «< k». The mappe's results source (learningDesign/mappe/storedActivityResults.ts) therefore reads, for each semester, only the rows whose academicYear is that semester's academic year, as insight's views do; a result counts only for a learner present in its group, so the old key's results of that tail are in no group either. The yearly purge's snapshots already select by the stored year (D-107).
    • The gap rule as built, in place of "a gap's right answers, listed wrong answers, other wrong answers and empty gaps" in the amendment above: a listed wrong answer, which INS-003's public rule says k or more learners gave, is always shown and is never a complement; per gap, «right», «other wrong» and «empty» are one additive group whose total is the question's learners less the listed answers' learners (insight/aggregate/gapMisconceptions.ts, insight/suppression/additiveGroupCells.ts); a task with one gap stays split into two parts, «right» (which INS-002's share gives away) and the rest.
    • Summaries say "of those that can be shown" (INS-008; «av dei som kan visast»): the hardest question, the most common wrong option or gap answer and the least answered video task are named among the shown values, and the sentence says so in nn, nb and en, so a hidden cell can never make it false. Added 2026-11-04 (the workstream's skeptic): the questions' list is headed «vanskelegast først» but sorts by shown shares only, with a question whose share cannot be shown last (so its place gives nothing away); its introduction now says so in each language, so the order is never read as the hidden questions being the easiest.
    • The course count's roster URL (the completion base, LTI-008): ltijs reads the course's learners with a token from the launch's context_memberships_url, which nothing checked. D-104's line-item URL rule (its amendment of 2026-11-04) applies to it too: the URL must parse, hold no user name or password, use https where https is required, and have an origin in CANVAS_ORIGINS or one of the platform's own; otherwise no token is asked for, the old count stays and the refusal is logged with the origin only (lti/nrps/NrpsLearnerCounter.ts, nrps.url-refused). The server passes the same rules as to the grade worker (createNrpsServices' urlRules); without them only the platform's own origins are allowed. Added 2026-11-05 (integration): main.ts and the test beds' gradeBridgeInputs now pass { origins: CANVAS_ORIGINS, requireHttps: NODE_ENV === 'production' }, so a roster on the institution's Canvas domain is read when that origin is in CANVAS_ORIGINS; and the CSV's period-end row is labelled «Til (ikkje med)» (nb «Til (ikke med)», en «Up to (not included)»), since that midnight is not part of the view.
    • Verified by, besides the tests above: additiveGroupExhaustive.test.ts's [INS-006] test that no hidden gap count can be worked out from a listed wrong answer; insightScope.test.ts (the end at midnight, every day of August); insightPeriodEnd.int.test.ts (a statement stored today never changes today's view; one learner under two years' keys counts once); NrpsLearnerCounter.test.ts (a roster URL on another origin is never read, and createNrpsServices hands the rules to the counter); storedActivityResults.int.test.ts (one learner under two years' keys is one learner in the mappe's autumn group); and the web's InsightPeriodNote.test.tsx and insightSummaries.test.ts.
    • Residuals for the DPIA input and the DPO: views of the same period on two consecutive days still differ by one day's learners (R3, R8: now day by day, never within a day); the course's NRPS count can change within a day, and with it the base of the completion rate; a learner active only on 1 August under the old key, through the portal, is in no view and no mappe group; and stored rows of earlier days still change within a day when operations erase a learner's data (D-108) or an activity is deleted, so a view taken before and after an erasure differs by that learner's rows (rare, run by operations, and nothing in the tab says that or whom it erased).
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, the step-5 privacy and security review: the mappe ends at midnight too): Found: the mappe's results source (learningDesign/mappe/storedActivityResults.ts) read every stored row up to the moment of the export, while insight's views end at the latest midnight in Oslo (the amendment above). For an activity in one course and one version, the mappe's current-semester group is insight's semester view plus today's plays, so the mappe exported at 14:00 minus that view (or two exports on the same day) gives the participants, completion rate, attempts and change of the learners who played today: with one such learner, what that learner did, below k. That is the within-day differencing the amendment above closed for insight, and it breaks learnerSummaries.ts's rule that the mappe's totals cannot be differenced against insight's views. Decided: the mappe reads, like insight, only rows stored before the latest midnight in Oslo at the moment of the export (presences and root results alike), so two exports on one day are the same and an export never holds today's plays. The trade-off: as for insight, a teacher sees today's plays in the mappe tomorrow (PROGRESS Q24 applies to both). The yearly purge's snapshots cover ended years only and are unchanged. Verified by storedResultsBeforeToday.int.test.ts (a learner who played today is in no group until the next day).
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, the S6 security review: another site cannot write the audit trail): Found (SEC-S6-01): the view and the CSV download are GETs that write insight.view and insight.export (Audit above, DATA-007), D-057 asks for the CSRF token on unsafe methods only, and the SameSite=Lax session cookie goes with another site's top-level navigation. A page on any site could send a signed-in teacher to …/insight/export: the server wrote audit events under the teacher's name that the teacher never asked for (which spec 00 §8's measure reads), saved the aggregated CSV among their downloads, and used up their 60 insight requests a minute. That site never reads the answer. The same day's re-check found a second way in that a rule against other sites misses: an author can set an H5P image path to https://<app>/api/content/<id>/insight/export (rightsOfUse.ts and Lumi accept an http(s) path, h5p.js getPath plays an absolute path as it is, the player's CSP has img-src 'self'). A teacher who opens that activity in the portal loads it as an image of our own origin, which full Chromium sends as Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin, Sec-Fetch-Mode: no-cors, Sec-Fetch-Dest: image with the session cookie, and the server wrote insight.export under that teacher's name. Decided: every insight route answers 403 error.forbidden (already in the contract) to anything but what our pages send, a script's fetch from our own origin: Sec-Fetch-Site absent or same-origin, Sec-Fetch-Mode absent, cors or same-origin, and Sec-Fetch-Dest absent or empty. That refuses a top-level navigation from any site (a typed URL too), a request from another origin of any site (cross-site, or same-site, which takes in the files origin, D-045), and an image, video, frame or prefetch that a page of our own origin loads. The check comes after the sign-in check and before View, the rate limit and any audit write. Our pages' fetches (apiRequest, apiFileRequest; also in the Canvas frame, whose fetches go to its own origin) and clients that send no fetch metadata (Node's fetch sends only Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors) are served as before. D-057 is unchanged: no CSRF token on these GETs, which the web client's apiHeaders sends on unsafe methods only. Residual: a browser that sends no fetch metadata (Safari before 16.4) is not covered; only a token on these GETs would close that, a change to D-057 left open. A script running on our own origin can still fetch these routes, as it can every route. Verified by insightForeignRequest.test.ts (no audit event and no rate-limit take for a navigation, another origin's request or our own page's image, video, frame or prefetch, with the headers full Chromium sends; our pages' fetch still audited).

D-107 · SPEC-DEVIATION DATA-003: the yearly purge runs on 31 August and deletes by a stored academic year

  • Context: DATA-003 runs the purge "on a configured date (default 15 August)" for the academic year that has ended, deleting rows "older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days", keeping only k-suppressed snapshots for the mappe, and destroying that year's pseudonym secret. The academic year ends on 31 July (privacy/academicYear.ts, D-011), so the 30 days end on 30 August, and on 15 August nothing is old enough yet. The tables keep timestamps, not years, while a learner's rows belong to the year whose secret made their learnerKey (privacy/deriveLearnerKey.ts); a cut by timestamp can split them. The secrets are an environment value (PSEUDONYM_SECRETS), which the server cannot destroy.
  • Decision:
    • When: by default on 31 August, Oslo time, for the academic year that ended on 31 July; the date is configurable, but not to a day before 31 August, so the 30 days always pass first. A leased job runs it on one node, and a CLI runs the same code by hand.
    • What: XapiStatement, H5PUserData and GradeSyncJob get an academicYear column, set when a row is written to the year of the secret that made its learnerKey. The purge deletes the ended year's rows by that column, in batched transactions; then the learner Identity rows created before that year ended; then learner User rows left without an Identity (D-034).
    • Snapshots first: before anything is deleted, it writes the year's InsightSnapshot rows per activity, context (D-103) and content version, already suppressed with the configured k (D-106). Only these outlive the purge. They are kept for the mappe (DATA-003), so the values the mappe reads from them also follow D-095's rules, the two-sided rate rule included, which D-106 leaves out of the insight views only.
    • Dry run: counts per table and deletes nothing. Every run, dry or real, writes an audit event with the counts (DATA-003, DATA-007).
    • The secret: destroying the year's pseudonym secret is an operations step in the runbook: after the real run, HVL removes it from the secret store and from PSEUDONYM_SECRETS. At start-up the server names, by year only, any secret still configured for a year the purge has completed, so a forgotten step shows.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) 15 August with a timestamp cut: it deletes nothing on that day, or splits a learner's year. (b) The server destroying secrets itself: it would need write access to HVL's secret store.
  • Consequences: SPEC-DEVIATION from DATA-003 in three points: the default date (31 August instead of 15 August), which rows go, and who destroys the pseudonym secret. The purge takes the ended year's rows by their stored year, and learner Identity rows created before 1 August, not every row "older than the academic-year boundary plus 30 days", which, read on the run date, would also take the new year's first 30 days. The 30 days after the boundary are kept, as the time before the purge may run. DATA-003 has the scheduled job destroy that year's secret; here the job cannot, so HVL operations destroy it in a runbook step after the real run, and the start-up warning shows a forgotten one. DATA-002's rule that a year's secret is destroyed when that year's data is purged still holds, through that step. academicYear on XapiStatement is a field outside DATA-012's list, so this is a SPEC-DEVIATION from DATA-012 too: it holds no statement data, only the year of the secret behind the row's learnerKey, which the key cannot reveal and a timestamp can misstate (a portal session made before 1 August can keep its learnerKey for up to 12 hours after it, D-057). D-103 (a) refused a platformId column partly for this reason; there the context string can carry the platform, while nothing else carries the year. Spec 05 gets amendment notes on DATA-003 and DATA-012. Migration s6_grade_bridge_insight adds the column, and a contentVersion to InsightSnapshot, which has none today. A learner who comes back after the purge gets new rows, as the new year's key already makes them a new pseudonym. The integration test travels through a year in time (DATA-003's Verify) and checks D-034's rule.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 3 integration): where the year comes from. A portal session stores learnerKeyYear, computed at login from the same moment as its key (a session field; the data inventory's Redis section lists it); an LTI request's key and its year come from one moment in LtiAccounts (lti/launch/ ltiAccount.ts), and principalOfLaunch puts the year on the principal, so no request at the turn of the year pairs a key with the other year. learnerKeyYearOf(principal, receivedAt) falls back to the request's year only for a principal built without one. XapiStatement rows (XapiIngest) and GradeSyncJob rows (from those statements) carry it. Still open, for step 5: H5PUserData rows are written without it (h5p/storage/learnerStateWrites.ts takes the database default, the year of the write), which is wrong for a portal session made before 1 August and used up to 12 hours after; the purge step carries learnerKeyYear through principalToH5pActor into that write.
  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 5, the purge built): how the job, the CLI and the H5P state write carry this out (apps/server/src/privacy/purge/).
    • Date: PURGE_RUN_DATE (MM-DD, default 08-31) names a day from 31 August to 31 December; an earlier day, and any day from January to July, is refused. A day in spring would keep a year's rows for most of another year, which DATA-003's retention does not allow.
