  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: hardening after step 6's security review): decided before the changes; it settles the findings the review left open (PROGRESS, step 6, «Still open»).
    • clamd's alerts are required (SEC-006). clamd answers OK for a file it did not scan in full unless it is told otherwise. Measured with the ClamAV 1.4.6 image above, its signatures and nothing else changed: with the image's defaults every one of these was OK: a ZIP and a PDF that need a password to open, an office file of 10 050 entries (over MaxFiles, 10 000; 75 s of clamd's time), one of ZIPs nested 20 deep (over MaxRecursion, 17), one that unpacks to 450 MiB (over MaxScanSize, 400 MiB) and, with MaxScanTime set to 5 s, one of 9 000 entries cut off after 5 s. With AlertExceedsMax yes and AlertEncrypted yes they were answered Heuristics.Encrypted.Zip, Heuristics.Encrypted.PDF and Heuristics.Limits.Exceeded.MaxFiles, .MaxRecursion, .MaxScanSize and .MaxScanTime (so AlertExceedsMax covers more limits than clamd.conf's comment names), also with HeuristicAlerts no; the EICAR file, a clean text, a plain PDF, a PDF with only an owner password (it opens without one) and 60 MiB of random bytes were answered as before. Both settings become required wherever HVL runs clamd for this service (AlertEncryptedArchive yes with AlertEncryptedDoc yes may stand for AlertEncrypted yes), and MaxScanTime should be no higher than CLAMAV_TIMEOUT_MS, so that a scan the server has given up on also ends in clamd. The server cannot ask clamd for its settings, so this is a deployment checklist item (runbook ↗ (opens external site) §9, clamav.md ↗ (opens external site)). The stacks that start a clamd set both through the official image's CLAMD_CONF_<option> variables, which its entrypoint writes into clamd.conf (read in its /init; measured above): deploy/compose.app.yml's clamav (the Docker smoke) and ci.yml's clamav service.
    • Accepted: such files are refused as malware. The author sees upload.file.malwareFound (a password-protected PDF or an office file too large or too deeply nested to check), and the log line's signatures names the heuristic, so support can tell the cases apart. This includes a very long, ordinary PDF: MaxFiles also counts a PDF's streams, so a plain 4 MB PDF of 12 000 pages (one content stream each) was refused as Heuristics.Limits.Exceeded.MaxFiles, while 5 000 pages and the ordinary PDFs tried passed (measured by the step's review). Not chosen: mapping Heuristics.* names to a message of their own; the scanner wrapper treats every finding alike, and a heuristic name is clamd's to choose.
    • Not closed by these settings: while measuring, further files were found that clamd answers OK without unpacking them in full, with both settings on. As security findings they go to the owner outside the repository (D-112's rule for security reports), with a proposed check of our own in the upload path.
    • The root docker-compose.yml publishes on the loopback only. It published PostgreSQL (with a fixed password), Redis (with none) and the S3 emulator on every interface, and runbook §8 runs those services on a production-like node for the full load test. Each port is now 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>. The development and test settings name localhost (.env.example, ci.yml, .devcontainer/createS3Buckets.mjs), and in the dev container docker-in-docker's daemon runs inside the container, so its loopback is the container's own. Node's clients try 127.0.0.1 when localhost also resolves to ::1 (Node 24's autoSelectFamily). Measured with a copy of the file on other ports: pg, ioredis, the S3 client and .devcontainer/createS3Buckets.mjs connect through localhost, a lookup that answers ::1 first ends on 127.0.0.1, and the host's other address is refused. Every user and process on the host can still connect, so runbook §8 warns against running the file on a node that holds real data or serves users, and the deployment checklist (§9) says so. Not chosen: a variable for the bind address, which invites 0.0.0.0; a developer who needs the services from another machine uses an SSH tunnel.
    • A name the storage refuses is "not found" on the cookie route. /h5p/content/:id/*file passed a NUL byte in the file name to PostgreSQL, which refused the query, so a signed-in person could cause a 500 and an error-level log line at will. PrismaContentStorage's requireFile and fileExists now treat a name that assertSafeObjectName refuses as missing, before the database (storableFileName.ts, a predicate that signedFileRoutes.ts' own copy of the check can share later): no stored file can have such a name, because the store refuses it when it writes. Tests: [SEC-004] in contentFiles.int.test.ts (500 before the fix), [H5P-004] in contentStorage.int.test.ts and storableFileName.test.ts. Narrowing or retiring the cookie route itself stays open.
    • frame-ancestors 'none' in the user-file policy. USER_FILE_CSP becomes sandbox; default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'none', so no page, ours or another site's, can frame a user file (frame-ancestors does not fall back to default-src). Nothing frames one: the player shows images with <img>, video and audio with <video> and <audio>, captions with <track>, and documents are downloads; the editor's image editor draws an <img> into a canvas; the web app frames only the player and editor pages. Of the 120 libraries D-078 fetches, only H5P.IFrameEmbed frames a content file (Column offers it); it is in none of the ten seed packages, so the editor does not offer it, and the HTML it would frame is refused by the allowlist (SEC-002). Should an administrator install it, its frames of content files are refused, as intended. A stricter superset of D-045's policy, so not a deviation from SEC-004.
    • Smaller items: persist-credentials: false on the checkout steps of ci.yml and docker.yml, since no later step pushes or fetches with the job's token (git diff reads only the work tree); runbook §6 keeps the local backup folder on an encrypted volume and restores from the authenticated off-server copy; clamav.md says that clamscan 2.4.0 sends no server name (SNI), so the TLS proxy must present the certificate for CLAMAV_HOST without one (D-112's amendment of today measured it). upload.file.scanUnavailable stays 400: a 503 changes the shared error mapping (h5pErrorResponse.ts), which is not the upload route's.

D-111 · An HVL language overlay in a library-storage wrapper; H5P-010's guidance through it

  • Context: S5's probe P1 found that many nn and nb defaults of the real libraries are English (MultiChoice, QuestionSet, InteractiveBook and BranchingScenario buttons and messages). Patterns set their own texts (D-084), but activities made in the editor stay English. PROGRESS suggested Lumi's alterLibraryLanguageFile hook; in 10.0.4, once that hook is set, LibraryManager.getLanguageWithoutFallback returns only { semantics } for every library's language file, so the editor libraries lose their libraryStrings, the editor's own texts. H5P-010 replaces the video upload field's description with alterLibrarySemantics, but the language/nn.json and nb.json of H5P.InteractiveVideo and H5P.Video override a description in the semantics, so that change alone never reaches a Norwegian author. D-046 already wraps the library storage for the nn → nb → en fallback.
  • Decision: a design that step 7 builds.
    • Mechanism: a library-storage wrapper after D-046's. For language/nn.json and language/nb.json of a listed library version (major.minor), it sets the default (and, for H5P-010, the description) of each field an overlay entry names by its semantics path, on a copy, never on the cached object (D-046). Each entry also states the English text it translates; when a library update changes that text, the entry is skipped and content:check reports it, so a changed field never gets a stale translation.
    • Scope: learner-facing defaults in nn and nb for the ten types and the sub-content they usually hold (about 60 texts per language). Editor labels and the editor's libraryStrings are outside S6.
    • Texts: in content/, under D-082's pipeline (loaded and checked at start-up and by npm run content:check), so that ALU and HVL's language advisers edit them without code. They are drafts until reviewed (Q2, Q17).
    • H5P-010: alterLibrarySemantics (composed with the DragQuestion filter) sets the English guidance, and the overlay the nn and nb guidance. HVL's Panopto host name and the guidance texts are for HVL and ALU to confirm (open, with Q17's review).
  • Alternatives considered: (a) Lumi's alterLibraryLanguageFile: it breaks the editor's texts. (b) Editing the libraries' language files: that changes files fetched and pinned by hash (D-078). (c) Only upstream translations: right in the long run (D-112), but slow, and the pilot needs Norwegian now.
  • Consequences: An extension of H5P-008, as D-046 was; spec 01 gets amendment notes on H5P-008 and H5P-010, and PROGRESS's mention of the hook is corrected. Only new activities and fields left at their defaults change; existing activities keep the English they stored, and pattern texts still win. A few English texts come from library code, not language files (H5P.Video's "Video source is missing.", ImageHotspots' "Missing required background image"); D-086's missing-media check reports the empty slot to the author before publishing (an error that can be acknowledged, so it warns rather than blocks). Tests that pin English on purpose (probe P1's ENGLISH_IN_NYNORSK) change where the overlay reaches them.
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: the overlay as built):
    • Files (content/h5p-tekstar/, with a README for ALU): library-texts.nn.yaml and library-texts.nb.yaml, one per language because Nynorsk and Bokmål may have different reviewers; English needs none, since the libraries' own texts are English. Each names library versions (H5P.Name major.minor) and, per version, defaults and labels by semantics path, and libraryStrings by key; every entry gives en, the library's English text it translates, and the text in its own language (nn or nb). A path is the semantics field names joined by ., with [] after a list's name for its item (the list item field's own name is left out), so it is the path probe P1 reports. video-guidance.yaml holds H5P-010's guidance once, in nn, nb and en, and the video fields it goes under. Every file has status: draft until HVL's language advisers and ALU review it (Q2, Q17). The texts are plain: < and > are refused, because the editor writes labels, descriptions and library strings into its page as HTML.
    • Scope, widened: besides the learner-facing defaults, an entry may give a field's label, so that a field the overlay translates is not labelled in English in the editor, and libraryStrings, the editor's own texts. The first are H5P.DragNBar 1.5's (the toolbar of CoursePresentation's and InteractiveVideo's editors), English in both nn.json and nb.json; its «Paste» was D-080's example of a name we could only copy. The drafts cover MultiChoice, QuestionSet, InteractiveBook and BranchingScenario first (probe P1), then InteractiveVideo, ImageHotspots and CoursePresentation and the question types the containers offer most (TrueFalse, MarkTheWords, SingleChoiceSet, Summary, Essay). A text that is already the Norwegian word («Pause», «Video») or holds no words (@score / @maxscore) gets no entry. Labels are given for the first four types; the remaining English labels are for ALU to add.
    • Mechanism: LanguageOverlayLibraryStorage wraps D-046's storage in the editor and the player. For language/nn.json and language/nb.json of a listed version it parses the file Lumi would otherwise serve (for nn, nb.json when nn.json is missing, D-046; the English file when the library has neither), sets each entry on that copy, and keeps every other key, libraryStrings included. It resolves a path against the library's own semantics.json, because a language file's fields are positional, filling a missing position with {} (which H5P's deep merge ignores) and never with null. An entry whose path no longer resolves, or whose en is no longer the library's English text (semantics.json for defaults and labels, language/en.json or .en.json for library strings), is skipped, and a file where no entry applies is served as the library ships it. Every other read is passed through, so packages, exports and installs see the library as it is. The player reads no language file in Lumi 10.0.4; it is wrapped too, so that a later Lumi that does still gets the overlay.
    • H5P-010: the editor's alterLibrarySemantics is D-006's DragQuestion filter followed by the English guidance, set as the description of the listed fields (H5P.InteractiveVideo 1.28 interactiveVideo.video.files and H5P.Video 1.6 sources); the overlay sets the nn and nb guidance on the same fields. Neither library has an English language file that would hide the English guidance; content:check refuses a listed version that has one.
    • Checks: the server's start-up and content:check load the three files with D-082's loader (strict schema, every problem with file, line and key; the folder may be absent, as the mappe's may). content:check, which has the installed libraries, also refuses a version that is not installed, a path or a library string the library does not have, a default on a field that has none, a field that is not a video field under the guidance, and an en that is not the library's English text, so that a library update that changes a text is reported, not silently skipped.
    • Loading: createH5pRuntime takes the loaded texts; without them it loads content/h5p-tekstar/ itself, so every engine the server, the seed command or a test builds has the overlay. The overlay never changes stored content: an activity keeps the texts it was saved with.
    • Tests: the wrapper and the path resolver (unit), content:check refusing a broken file and a stale or unknown entry, the editor's AJAX library data in nb with Norwegian defaults, labels and library strings and in en unchanged, the guidance in all three languages, and in the real player and editor (languageOverlay.browser.int.test.ts): a MultiChoice and a QuestionSet created in nn as the editor creates them, whose buttons a screen reader names in Nynorsk and whose QuestionSet says «Neste», «Resultat» and «Poeng», and the editor in nb showing the overlay's labels ([H5P-008], [H5P-010]). MultiChoice's visible «Sjekk» was already Nynorsk; its «Send inn» is stored but shown only where a platform marks an activity as submitted for scoring (H5P.Question's isScoringEnabled or isReportingEnabled in the content's data, which our player does not set). Probe P1's ENGLISH_IN_NYNORSK keeps only «Pause», and the editor repair test's copied DragNBar markup now reads «Lim inn».
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7 review):
    • No " in HVL's texts. Libraries also put these texts into double-quoted HTML attributes (DragNBar 1.5 builds title="' + H5PEditor.t('H5P.DragNBar', 'moreElements') + '"; CoursePresentation 1.28 builds aria-label="'+this.cp.l10n.…+'"), and the editor stores a default as it is, where it escapes what an author types (h5peditor.js sets defaults, h5peditor-text.js escapes input). So the nn and nb texts and the three guidance texts may not hold a straight double quote either (SECURITY:); «» is the Norwegian quotation mark the files already use. en may hold one, because H5P's own English labels do and en is only compared, never shown.
    • Wording kept consistent with H5P's own Norwegian in the same editor and player: MultiChoice's labels for assistive technology say «Beskriving» and «assisterande teknologi» (nb «Beskrivelse», «assisterende teknologi»), as Blanks and DragText say, not «Skildring» and «hjelpemiddel»; BranchingScenario's fullscreen name is «Fullskjerm» and CoursePresentation's slide menu heading «Sider», as their own texts and the nb files say elsewhere. InteractiveVideo 1.28's end-screen summary without a score gets an entry, because its nn.json has «and» in it and its nb.json lacks «og». Its summary with a score cannot be translated: the library passes l10n.endCardTableRowSummary, a key its semantics do not have, so its English default is always shown (UPSTREAM: H5P.InteractiveVideo, for D-112's owner and the UD-040 register).
    • Test added: every entry of the real files applies on the pinned libraries and every other value of the file H5P ships reaches the editor unchanged (overlayKeepsShippedTexts.test.ts).
    • Correction: H5P.DragNBar 1.5's nb.json already has 3 of its 13 strings in Bokmål («Transformer», «Rediger», «Fjern»); the nb entries for them repeat H5P's words, so all 13 stay together for review.

D-112 · Upstream reports drafted for the owner to file; Lumi stays at 10.0.4

  • Context: D-081 left two items for S6: ask Lumi's maintainers for a release with their unreleased file-security work, or review and pin a Lumi commit built from source; and report our fixes and the D-080 barriers upstream. npm's newest @lumieducation/h5p-server is still 10.0.4 (2025-03-08), while the repository is active (R-09). Pinning a commit changes a CLAUDE.md invariant (@lumieducation/h5p-server@10.0.4); check:pins accepts only registry versions; the sanitiser, Redis-lock and ClamAV packages would have to move with it (master changed the malware-scanner interface); and it needs a review of about 620 commits in D-022's manner and the full gate. The image-size audit exceptions (D-030, R-08) expire on 2027-01-31, and only a Lumi version with image-size 2.0.3 or later removes their cause. Filing needs a GitHub account, and H5P's reporting channel per library must be checked (verify).
  • Decision:
    • Lumi stays at 10.0.4 in S6. No commit is pinned; our adapters and our own file security stay (D-003, D-081).
    • Drafts the owner files: docs/upstream/ holds texts ready to file: a release request to Lumi naming the unreleased changes we need and the image-size advisories; Lumi issues for deleteAllContentUserDataByUser deleting the acting user's data (D-108), alterLibraryLanguageFile dropping libraryStrings (D-111), the ClamAV scanner's NotScanned being accepted (D-110), and Core 1.28 with the new Hub (the adapters of spec 01 §1); and H5P reports for the barriers in D-080's register (upstreamRegister.ts). The owner files them from an account of their choice; the agent files nothing. Each filed issue's link goes back into the register and into UD-040's report.
    • Before 2027-01-31, HVL or the bachelor students choose one of: a Lumi release with a fixed image-size; a reviewed Lumi commit pinned by its own decision; or a reviewed renewal of the exception with a new expiry (SEC-007). Until then check:audit passes; after it, CI turns red, as designed.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) Pinning a reviewed Lumi commit in S6: a long review of a security-relevant dependency, not possible before 1 November beside the MUSTs. (b) A probe build of master without switching: useful evidence, left to the students with the drafts. (c) The agent filing from the owner's account: the owner decides what is published under their name.
  • Consequences: R-09 stays open, and the hand-off index (D-101) carries the expiry date and the three choices.
  • Amendment (2026-10-30, probe P1): the drafts also hold an H5P report for QuestionSet 1.21, whose resetTask resets every .h5p-progress-dot in the document, so its «Prøv igjen» fails on a page with several sets (D-115, Q20).
  • Amendment (2026-11-05, S6 step 7: the drafts as written): decided before the drafts.
    • Where: docs/upstream/, one file per report (the H5P accessibility reports one per library, in docs/upstream/h5p-accessibility/), and a README that lists every draft with its recipient, its channel and whether it is ready or needs the owner's check, and says where each filed link goes back. The drafts are in English, name our tests by file and title without links, and carry no personal data.
    • Security reports stay out of the repository. The repository is public on GitHub (checked 2026-11-05), so a private report committed here would be published before its vendor reads it. Two drafts are security reports: to H5P Group, about H5P.AudioRecorder 1.0 and H5PEditor.AudioRecorder 1.0 writing the build machine's environment into their JavaScript (D-110's amendment of 2026-11-05); and to Lumi, at the address in Lumi's SECURITY.md (security@lumi.education, read at master 493cd3e), about findings already recorded in D-039, D-040 and D-110's ClamAV amendment. Their full text is handed to the owner outside the repository; the README names them by recipient and subject only. The owner sends them, to a security contact the owner has confirmed, never as a public issue first; a public issue or a copy in docs/upstream/ follows only once the vendor has published a fix or agreed. What D-039, D-040 and D-110 already say publicly stays as it is.
    • Checked against upstream (2026-11-05, read-only shallow clones, nothing filed): npm's newest @lumieducation/h5p-server is still 10.0.4. Lumi's master (493cd3e, 2026-10-13) still deletes the acting user's state in deleteAllContentUserDataByUser and keeps only semantics when alterLibraryLanguageFile is set, and still accepts NotScanned; it fixes F1–F3 of spec 01 §1, decides SVG sanitising by the uploaded file's own name, without regard to case, and depends on probe-image-size instead of image-size, so a release would also end D-030's audit exceptions. H5P.AudioRecorder's default branch (7c66fab, 1.0.54) and H5PEditor.AudioRecorder's (b2f6ec7) still pass the whole process.env to DefinePlugin; QuestionSet's (a961bac, 1.21.14) still resets every progress dot in the document. Of the 27 webpack configurations among the 121 library checkouts of D-078's cache, only those two pass the whole environment. clamscan 2.4.0 is still npm's newest; it opens TLS to clamd without a server name (SNI), which Node 24's tls.connect then does not send (measured), and writes socket errors to stderr without its debug mode.
    • Reproduced without secrets (2026-11-05): each AudioRecorder library, built at its pinned commit under env -i with one made-up variable, carried that variable's value twice in its built file; with 'process.env': JSON.stringify({ NODE_ENV: mode }) in its webpack configuration instead, neither the value nor any other build-machine value was left, and no bare process.env remained (the suggested fix; not played in a browser). Against the installed Lumi 10.0.4: an identity alterLibraryLanguageFile drops libraryStrings; deleteAllContentUserDataByUser('learner-1', operator) asks the storage to delete the operator's state; the ClamAV scanner reports a scan without a verdict (isInfected: null) as Clean.
    • Scope, widened: besides the drafts the Decision names, the README lists drafts for clamscan (SNI, stderr) and ltijs 7.0.7 (its launch page's unguarded localStorage.removeItem, D-050), a Lumi issue collecting small API and typing gaps that UPSTREAM: tags work around, and a Core 1.28 and new-Hub backport that is filed only if Lumi declines a release. UPSTREAM: tags that record how pinned upstream code works (D-080's V2D-5 amendment, (b)) get no report. Texts H5P lacks in nn and nb go, once HVL's language advisers have reviewed D-111's drafts, into pull requests to the libraries' language files, as H5P's contribution guide asks (h5p/.github, read at e979edf), not into issues. H5P's issues use its organisation's Bug Report form (title [Bug]: ), which the H5P drafts follow; neither that guide nor the two AudioRecorder repositories name a security contact.
    • After filing: the owner, or whoever edits the code next, puts each link where the README says: a register entry's UPSTREAM: comment (as its second link, which npm run a11y:report shows in UD-040's report), the UPSTREAM: tag of a repair in a11yRepairs.js or a11yEditorRepairs.js in place of "no issue filed yet" (D-080's DOC-13 amendment), and the UPSTREAM: tags of the Lumi workarounds.

D-113 · The S6 gate in full, run in parts; CI raised to S5; per-ID runs that select tests; a licence guard

  • Context: S5's gate took about 5 hours here, in parts of under 2 hours (the limit of a background command), and its runs under full load found three timing faults. S6 adds more tests and the Docker steps. Since PR #8, GitHub runs CI on main; the push run 41075981429 on the merge failed one e2e test (appPlayEditor.e2e: its click on «Lagre» landed in H5P's editor iframe while H5P was still growing it, so no save was sent; reproducing it also found that «Lagre» was enabled before H5P's editor could save), fixed at the start of S6. CI checks traceability only through S4 (--done-through=S4 in ci.yml, pinned by ciWorkflow.test.mjs). The per-ID runs for NFR-003 and UD-031 select no tests in the root Vitest project, because their tests are in the accessibility suite, and check:licences passed while a stray node_modules/node_modules link hid the workspaces and it counted 1 production package instead of 482 (S5 open item 8). Some MUSTs can only be checked as documents here (DATA-004, DATA-005, DATA-010, NFR-002's restore drill, UD-040), as with UD-031 and NFR-003 (D-079).
  • Decision: The owner decided on 2026-10-30 that the gate keeps its full form.
    • What it runs: every S1–S5 gate command and per-ID run (Evaluator Guide §5), plus S6's: -t "LTI-01", -t "INS-0", -t "DATA-0" and -t "NFR-00"; each S6 ID alone; npm run spec:trace -- --check --done-through=S6; the Docker build and the compose smoke; the conformance report and the DPIA input (with npm run a11y:report regenerating the automated parts unchanged); and the running server showing the insight and grade-sync views. The Evaluator Guide's S6 row is rewritten in S5's manner.
    • How: in parts of under 2 hours, each a tracked background task whose output goes into PROGRESS; the hourly restart task stays on until the gate passes (D-101).
    • IDs tested only in the accessibility suite (NFR-003, UD-031, and any S6 ID whose tests are only there) run as npm run test:a11y -- -t "\[<ID>\]", so no per-ID row selects zero tests.
    • CI: --done-through=S5 now (with ciWorkflow.test.mjs), and S6 once S6's gate passes.
    • Licence guard: check:licences fails when a workspace named in the root workspaces, or a runtime dependency declared in the root or a workspace manifest, is missing from the production set it checked; the expected set comes from the manifests, so no minimum count is needed.
    • Evidence from CI: a step this environment cannot run (the image with Chromium, the compose smoke, ClamAV) may cite GitHub CI's run on the gate commit by its run ID.
    • Document checks: tests that compare a document with its sources (for example, the DPIA input's custom fields with the developer key's) count as tested for DATA-004, DATA-005, DATA-010, NFR-002 and UD-040, as D-079 decided for UD-031 and NFR-003; the Evaluator Guide lists them as not verified until HVL acts.
    • NFR-001: a reduced-scale load smoke with the spec's p95 limits here; the 200-learner run on HVL's hardware stays open.
    • Listed as open with the output: Q2–Q8, Q13, Q15 and Q17, the confirmation against real Canvas, the 200-learner load test, the manual assistive-technology run and the DPO's review.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) Counting the S1–S5 per-ID evidence from one full run's reports, which would save about 3 hours a gate: the owner kept the full form. (b) A separate "documented" status in spec-trace: a second record of what PROGRESS tracks (D-079's reasoning).
  • Consequences: Extends D-100's gate to S6 and amends the Evaluator Guide §5. The gate output says which parts ran where.
  • Amendment (2026-10-30, probes P1 and P3): Q18–Q20 (D-115) and Q21 (D-110's P3 amendment) join the questions listed as open with the gate output. The image with Chromium and the compose smoke run here as well as in CI (D-110's P3 amendment), so the gate runs them here; Evidence from CI stays for a step that still cannot.

D-114 · New development dependencies in S6

  • Context: CLAUDE.md pins every dependency exactly, and D-029's checks allow only listed licences. INS-006 asks for a fast-check property test. NFR-001 asks for "a k6 or Artillery load test script in tools/load/" and Lighthouse CI on the player route. Here, k6's download host is refused and its container image needs Docker (probe P3).

  • Decision:

    • fast-check (MIT; one dependency, pure-rand, MIT), a development dependency pinned exactly at the version current when it is added (4.10.2 on 2026-10-30).
    • The load tool is chosen in the operations probe and recorded here by amendment, with its exact version and licence: k6 as a pinned container image (AGPL-3.0, a separate program outside the npm tree), Artillery from npm (MPL-2.0, a large development tree), or a small harness of our own in Node, which departs from NFR-001's "k6 or Artillery" and would make that amendment a SPEC-DEVIATION. Lighthouse CI (@lhci/cli, Apache-2.0), if the player timing uses it, is added the same way.

    Each passes check:pins, check:licences and check:audit. The runtime changes (tsx, the ClamAV scanner) are in D-110.

  • Alternatives considered: Hand-written random cases for INS-006: no shrinking to a smallest failing dataset, and the spec names fast-check.

  • Consequences: The property tests are titled [INS-006] and run in npm test; this is D-097's rule applied to S6.

  • Amendment (2026-10-30, probe P3): the load tool is k6, the container image grafana/k6:2.3.0@sha256:2dd4756ec6e14e62778916e1eb850108e4b499304c02df56760fa0bdb0fba0b8, AGPL-3.0, run as a separate program outside the npm tree, so check:pins, check:licences and check:audit see nothing new. Its scripts are ours, in tools/load/ as NFR-001 asks, so this is no SPEC-DEVIATION. The reasons, and why not Artillery, are in D-110's P3 amendment.

  • Amendment (2026-11-05, step 6: the load harness, NFR-001): decided before the code; what the smoke measures is added at the end of this block.

    • Files: tools/load/ (the k6 scripts in tools/load/k6/, the runner runLoad.mjs, a README and tests) and the bench apps/server/test/load/loadBench.ts, which uses the test beds' code and so lives beside them. Root scripts: load:smoke and load:full.
    • The server under load (the bench): the server as createApp builds it in one Node process, so one application node (NFR-001), through the app test bed (the mock Canvas and Feide pointed at it), in a PostgreSQL database of its own that the bench creates, migrates and drops, so a run never adds rows to the shared development database; Redis and S3 are the local services. It installs the ten real content types from the D-078 packages and publishes the QuestionSet example (four questions of three types: one of the larger player pages). It writes the mock Canvas's launch addresses for its learners to a file (addresses, no tokens), prints one ready line, and on SIGTERM prints the rows the load stored, then closes and drops its database. The mock Canvas runs in the same process; its answers are taken out of the measured time (below).
    • A virtual user is one learner in one Canvas course; one iteration is one visit: the LTI launch over HTTP as a browser makes it (the mock's login form, POST /lti/login, the mock's authorization answer, POST /lti/launch and ltijs's second post with the recovered state), the player page /lti/play?ltik=… and every script and stylesheet it names, fetched like a browser with an empty cache (at most 6 connections per host); then the root attempted batch the page sends when it opens, and rounds answers, each after a think time: one xAPI batch with one question's answered and its score, and one state save (H5P saves every 5 s while something changed, so once per answer); and at the end the root completed with the total. These are the items the bridge sends and the server stores (D-115), with the activity's real question IDs, valid under the contract's schema, with the ltik as Bearer.
    • Measured, with the spec's numbers as thresholds: hvli_player_ready, from the tool's /lti/login to the last script or stylesheet, less the mock Canvas's answer, p95 < 3 000 ms; http_req_duration{kind:api} (the xAPI batches and state saves) p95 < 300 ms; http_req_failed < 1 %; checks > 99 %. Also shown: the page alone, the launch, each API route, and the bytes a visit fetched.
    • Not measured by k6 (stays open): the browser's own work (parsing, running H5P, layout) and Fast 4G's latency and bandwidth, since k6 runs no browser and throttles nothing; the bytes per visit are reported so they can be held against Fast 4G's throughput. The in-browser half of NFR-001's Verify (Lighthouse CI on the player route with Fast 4G) is not added here (D-114's Lighthouse option waits). Content files from the files origin (images, video) are file downloads, outside the API limit, and not needed before the player answers; they are not fetched.
    • Scale: full is NFR-001's 200 learners (ramp up 60 s, hold 10 min, ramp down 30 s), thinking 5–15 s, 6 answers per visit; smoke is 20 learners for 30 s, thinking 2–4 s, 4 answers (about the request rate of 60 learners of the full model). Both use the same thresholds. The full run is HVL's, on hardware like a production node (Q5), with the command in the runbook; its output goes into PROGRESS like the smoke's.
    • k6: the image by digest above, with --network host, the caller's uid and gid, the scripts mounted read-only and one writable output folder; its only settings are HVLI_LOAD_* variables. handleSummary writes summary.json and our own short text summary, so no script loads anything at run time (k6's summary helpers are a remote module).
    • SECURITY and PRIVACY: an ltik lives only in its virtual user's memory and travels as on a real page (the landing query, the Bearer header and H5P's state URL), never in a file or an argument; every request has a fixed name tag, so no URL with an ltik becomes a metric name or a line of the summary. The learners are random sub values of the mock Canvas, gone with the bench's database. The runner gives k6 no other environment.
    • Residuals: the test bed logs every line at debug into memory, more work than production's info to a stream, so the numbers err on the slow side; there is no grade worker (the launches have no line item), so AGS sending is not under load; the in-browser time and Fast 4G above.
    • Tests: tools/load/test/ titled [NFR-001]: the thresholds and both profiles against the spec's numbers, the batch against xapiBatchSchema, the launch-form parsing against the real mock Canvas, and the docker run arguments (digest, read-only mount, no extra environment).
    • What the smoke measures (2026-11-05, built and run here): npm run load:smoke on the development sandbox (4 CPUs, PostgreSQL, Redis, the S3 emulator and k6 on the same machine): 20 learners for 30 s made 60 visits and 6 180 requests; hvli_player_ready p95 1 235 ms (median 102 ms; the slow ones are the first visits, before the server's caches are warm), the API p95 22 ms (xAPI 31 ms, state saves 14 ms), no failed request, every check passed, and 360 statements and 20 learner states stored (6 statements per visit, 1 state per learner); exit 0. An earlier run of the same code gave 1 351 ms and 38 ms. A visit fetches 1 496 KiB (the player page with its 49 scripts and 37 stylesheets, and the script of ltijs's login page), which the app sends uncompressed: at Fast 4G that transfer alone is about 1.3 s, so the reverse proxy must compress scripts and styles (the runbook's checklist). What changed from the design while building: k6 2.3.0 has no noUsageReport option, so the runner passes --no-usage-report (and --quiet); the container also gets --cap-drop ALL and no-new-privileges; url is left out of k6's system tags and the runner removes ltik=…, Bearer … and JWT-shaped values from k6's output, because k6 prints a failed request's URL; the scripts of ltijs's login and launch pages count as assets of the visit, as a browser loads them before it goes on; each question scores 0 or 1 out of 1. The bench and the runner are split into loadDatabase.ts, benchProcess.mjs and k6Container.mjs to stay within 200 lines, and tools/load/test/loadBench.test.mjs makes one visit with the same readers and builders in Node against the real bench (every asset 200, four batches 202, the state read back) and checks that the bench drops its database.
    • Skeptic review (2026-11-05), with its fixes: the smoke ran again here, and once with the API limit set to 5 ms, which printed FAIL http_req_duration{kind:api} p(95)<5 and exited 99 through npm run, so the thresholds can fail and the exit code reaches the caller. Fixed: (1) the runner redacted k6's output per pipe chunk, so a chunk boundary inside ltik=… let the rest of the token through; it now redacts whole lines (pipeRedactedLines), and a test that cuts a line inside the token fails with the old code. (2) The container's own file system was writable; it now runs with --read-only, so the output folder is the one place k6 can write, as the design says. The final smoke with both: exit 0, hvli_player_ready p95 1 506 ms (median 82 ms), the API p95 22 ms, no failed request, every check passed, 60 visits, 6 180 requests, 360 statements and 20 learner states stored (runbook section 8). Across the five smoke runs of this step the p95 lies between 1 136 and 1 506 ms while the median stays near 0.1 s, a slow tail that fits the 20 first, concurrent visits before the caches are warm (a third of the 60). Residual: where the caller is root (as in this sandbox) k6 runs as uid 0 in its container, without capabilities or new privileges; elsewhere it runs as the caller.

D-115 · xAPI capture, statement identity, attempts and gradable results (probe P1)

  • Context: Probe P1 played the ten real types (D-078) in Chromium on the production player and router, and recorded every statement with its document, timing and size (332 statements); a second agent re-ran seven types, the S5 pattern uv-module and a stand-in bridge (188 statements). D-102 left the attempt rule and the de-duplication to this probe. Observed:

    • Where: all ten types run div-embedded in the player document (playerPage.ts renders <div class="h5p-content">, although nine of the libraries declare embedTypes: ["iframe"]), and every statement arrives there exactly once. None reaches the web app's top window, which has no window.H5P. With H5P's own <iframe class="h5p-iframe"> embedding, which the production CSP allows and only our div template prevents, each statement arrives twice, in the iframe and relayed to the player document as the same event object, and a playerGlobalAssets script runs in both documents, because H5P copies H5PIntegration.core.scripts into the iframe. In that iframe H5P.externalEmbed is still undefined while scripts are evaluated (H5P sets it to false later), a set of seen events kept per window misses the other window's copy, and location.href is the player's URL in both.
    • Shape: no id and no timestamp; the actor is always {"name":"","mbox":"mailto:"}; object.id is the bare content ID or <contentId>?subContentId=<uuid>; the verbs are exactly LTI-011's five.
    • Volume: interacted and progressed are 38–76 % of all statements, and none of them carries what an INS requirement uses: BranchingScenario's choice interacted has no response, and InteractiveVideo sends no progressed at all. The peak was 43 statements a minute at automated speed, 22 without those two verbs. Statements are 681 B at the median and 1 524 B at p95, but H5P does not bound answers: one gap of 5 000 characters made a statement of 7 967 B.
    • Attempts: H5P marks none. A retry sends nothing, or only progressed (CoursePresentation, BranchingScenario). Root attempted means "the page loaded": it comes again on every reload, never on a retry, and never from Column or ImageHotspots, nor from InteractiveBook before «Les». On resume, CoursePresentation re-sends its scored completed with no learner action when it opens on the summary slide, and InteractiveBook offers the same submission again. Column sends a scored root completed after every «Sjekk» once all its tasks are answered, and InteractiveBook sends each chapter's completed twice within about 30 ms.
    • The root: no single test finds it. H5P's own (no contextActivities.parent) takes InteractiveBook's chapter completed for the root; LTI-012's (no subContentId) takes the context-less interacted that DragText sends while it restores state inside a QuestionSet, and every child of content saved without subContentIds, which POST /h5p/content accepts. InteractiveBook without a cover sends one root attempted with no context at all.
    • Scores: result.success comes at the root only from MultiChoice and QuestionSet. InteractiveBook (its «Send inn rapport» needs H5PIntegration.reportingIsEnabled, which we do not set) and InteractiveVideo (no submit screen in our example or in fa-video) send no root score, and ImageHotspots sends no statement at all. Every ending of uv-case scores 10 of 10 (read from the pattern). In uv-module, a chapter check's «Prøv igjen» throws in QuestionSet 1.21 (its resetTask walks every .h5p-progress-dot in the document, and the book holds three sets), and the results page stays.
    • Durations mean different things by type: summed across retries, reset by DragText's retry, counted from pre-rendering in nested content, or absent from a nested QuestionSet.

    Not observed: a play through the real portal page or a Canvas launch into /app/play; the code renders the same div template there.

  • Decision: binding for step 3. Where a point is ALU's or the owner's, the default below holds until they answer (Q18–Q20), so nothing waits.

    • Where the bridge runs: xapiBridge.js is the last script in playerGlobalAssets, after the theme scripts, and never in editorGlobalAssets. It is therefore evaluated after h5p.js and the x-api scripts and before the library scripts and document-ready, where H5P sends root attempted. While it is evaluated, it registers synchronously with its own document's H5P.externalDispatcher.on('xAPI', …), unless window.frameElement has the class h5p-iframe (a Core iframe, whose events the parent's bridge sees; a cross-origin parent such as Canvas gives null, and the web app's frame never carries that class). At event time it also ignores an event when H5P.isFramed && H5P.externalEmbed === false. The player page includes the script, and renders its configuration (the endpoint and the content's ID and version; no identity), only for a learner principal; for anyone else it leaves both out (D-102), and without a configuration the script does nothing. The div template stays; the guard covers a future iframe embedding. H5P.externalEmbed read at evaluation, a per-window set of seen events and location.href are not used: each failed in the probe.

    • What the bridge sends: only what the server may store: the first root attempted of the page load, every answered, and a root completed; never interacted, progressed, or a sub-content attempted or completed. Each statement is cut down to what the server reads: verb.id; object.id and object.definition.interactionType; context.contextActivities.parent and category; the extensions h5p-subContentId and h5p-local-content-id; and result.score, success, completion, duration and response, capped as below. No actor, question text, choices, feedback or other extensions. Each item carries a statementId (crypto.randomUUID(), one per dispatched event) and an attemptId.

    • Batches: every 2 s, at most 50 items and 60 000 bytes of JSON, one request in flight. A batch that fails with a network error, a 5xx or a 429 goes back to the head of the queue; one refused with any other 4xx is dropped. On pagehide, everything not yet acknowledged, the request in flight included, goes in one keepalive request, within the browser's 64 KiB and the same 50 items and 60 000 bytes, oldest first; what does not fit is lost, as D-102 accepts for a large last flush. The server skips what an earlier request already stored. A batch names its content and version once: the version the page was rendered with (D-093), which the server accepts from 1 up to the current version, so a page opened before a structural save never labels its statements with the new one.

    • What the server accepts and stores (LTI-011, DATA-012): it still accepts all five verbs. It ignores actor, since the learner comes only from the request's principal (D-102), and it accepts a bare UUID as object.id, a missing context and a numeric response (stored as text). Each item is checked on its own: an invalid one (including one about another activity) is discarded and counted in the log, without its content, so one odd statement never blocks its batch. A batch for an activity the principal may not view (in Canvas, any but the launched one), or with over 50 items or over 64 KiB, is refused with 403, 400 or 413, and the bridge drops it. Stored: a root attempted; an answered of the root or of sub-content (its subContentId from the extension, else from object.id); a root completed that is not a replay. Discarded: interacted, progressed, a sub-content attempted or completed, a sub-content statement without a subContentId, and a replay. The answer is 202, with no detail per item.

    • Identity and time: the statementId becomes XapiStatement.id, inserted so that an existing ID is skipped (the pagehide flush, a request retried after a lost answer); DATA-012 gains no field. A content hash is never an identity, since identical statements are normal (seven identical Blanks interacted within 100 ms). The stored timestamp is the server's receive time plus the item's place in the batch in milliseconds, so the batch's order survives as a strict order (D-102's receive time, within 49 ms); the browser's clock is never read.

    • The root and gradable results: a statement is root when object.id is the content ID with no ?subContentId=, it has no h5p-subContentId extension, and it has no contextActivities.parent. A root result is a root answered or completed whose category[0].id names the activity's main library (http://h5p.org/libraries/<machineName>-<major>.<minor>); it is gradable when result.score.max is above 0 and it is not a replay. Each test alone misclassifies a case above; a root attempted needs no category, since InteractiveBook's has none. The score is scaled, checked against raw / max within 0.0001 (Core rounds it to four decimals; an item outside is discarded), never success. One server module holds these tests, the bridge repeats them for its attempt counter, and both are tested on P1's fixtures.

    • Attempts: attemptId is <viewId>:<n>. viewId is a crypto.randomUUID() made once per page load, and n starts at 1 and goes up by one right after the bridge sends a root result with score.max above 0 (the bridge cannot tell a replay; the server can). An attempt therefore holds at most one result, and a retry, which H5P does not announce, becomes a new attempt at its next result; statements after the last result form an open attempt. The server checks the shape (a UUID, a colon, a positive integer) and reads the view part only for the replay rule. This keeps D-102's rule.

    • The attempt policy (LTI-012, D-104): each stored gradable result in a Canvas launch writes a GradeSyncJob per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId), with scoreGiven = scaled × 100. best sends the learner's highest job score in the placement, latest the score of the job created last (jobs are created in result order), and mastery 100 once any job's score reaches the threshold, else latest.

    • Replays and repeats: a root completed is a replay when its page load stored no answered since its previous root result (or since the load), and its scoreRaw and scoreMax equal those of the learner's latest stored root result for the same content, context and version. BranchingScenario is exempt: an end screen is reached by navigation alone, its choices are interacted, and it was not seen to replay. The rule drops CoursePresentation's completed re-sent on resume or on a revisit of the summary slide, and a re-submission of InteractiveBook or QuestionSet after a reload; it keeps a first submission after a reload (there is no earlier result) and a check after changed answers. P1's guard in the bridge (no learner activity since the page loaded) is not used: it would drop that first submission. Column's completed after each «Sjekk» follows an answered, so each is a result and an attempt, and D-104's coalescing sends one current score. InteractiveBook's double chapter completed and DragText's context-less interacted are never sent.

    • Gradable root result per type:

      TypeGradable root resultScoresuccess at root
      MultiChoice 1.16answered, at every «Sjekk»H5P'syes
      Blanks 1.14answered, at every «Sjekk»correct gapsno
      DragText 1.10answered, at every «Sjekk»correct dropsno
      QuestionSet 1.21completed, at every finish («Avslutt»)sum of the questionsyes (pass mark)
      Column 1.18, 1.22completed, at every «Sjekk» once all tasks are answeredsum of the tasksno
      CoursePresentation 1.28completed, at every arrival on the summary slidesum of the tasksno
      InteractiveBook 1.15completed, at «Send inn rapport», with reportingIsEnabled (the default, Q18)sum of the chaptersno
      InteractiveVideo 1.28completed, at «Send inn svar», only with a submit screen its author added (Q18)sum of the interactionsno
      BranchingScenario 1.10completed, at an end screen, unless its scoring is no-score (maximum 0)the end screen's or the path'sno
      ImageHotspots 1.11none: it sends no statementnonenone

    • InteractiveBook and InteractiveVideo (Q18): the player page sets reportingIsEnabled: true, H5P's switch for a platform that records results, which ours is. Of the ten types only InteractiveBook reads it (so does DocumentationTool, which is not offered). The learner then sees «Send inn rapport» on the book's summary page, and H5P's own score reaches Canvas as QuestionSet's does at its finish; the library's text after sending («Svara dine er sende inn til vurdering») can get a formative wording through D-111's overlay if ALU wants one. An InteractiveVideo is graded only when its author adds a submit screen: no validator rule and no pattern change in S6, so fa-video sends no score. Not chosen: a score the bridge computes from getScore() (a statement H5P never sent), or no grade for the main InteractiveBook pattern.

    • uv-case (Q19): unchanged. Its pattern gives every ending 10 on purpose ("the score shows that the student has worked through the case"), so Canvas gets 100 for every completed case: a completion mark, and formative like every score here (D-105). Not chosen without ALU: scores per choice (a pattern change that would grade professional judgement) or no Canvas score for it.

    • uv-module's chapter checks (Q20): the pattern sets endGame.showRetryButton: false on its three QuestionSets, so the failing «Prøv igjen» is not offered, and each question keeps its own «Prøv igjen» (override.retryButton: "on"). If the regression test shows that the book's own «Prøv igjen» fails the same way, the pattern turns that off too. A teacher's own page with two or more QuestionSets is expected to keep the fault (read from the code, not observed): an accepted limitation for the pilot, drafted as an upstream report (D-112). Not chosen now: a run-time repair of QuestionSet's resetTask, which would change library behaviour, not attributes as D-080's repairs do, and needs its own decision.

    • Activities that send no score (ImageHotspots, InteractiveVideo without a submit screen, BranchingScenario with no-score): no GradeSyncJob is ever written, and the Deep Linking picker says so when the placement is assignment_selection, in nn, nb and en.

    • What insight reads (INS-001…INS-005): a learner has started with any stored statement for the activity, so InteractiveBook without a cover counts at load, Column counts from the first answer, and no statement is made up. Completed is a stored root result, attempts are the stored root results, and time on task comes from the stored timestamps of each page load, never from durationMs. Where a type cannot send a root result, completed, the rate and attempts are shown as not available, never as 0, and ImageHotspots' tab says that it sends no learning data. INS-002 and INS-003 read answered by subContentId (correct is success, or full marks where H5P sends no success). INS-005: InteractiveVideo sends no progressed, so there is no drop-off curve, and the share of learners who answered each interaction is the measure, as INS-005 allows. INS-004 (SHOULD) is not built in S6: BranchingScenario's choices are in no dispatched statement, only in its getXAPIData() and saved state, and the last choice before an end screen sends nothing at all; building it means statements the bridge makes (a SPEC-DEVIATION), after a probe shows that retried choices are kept. The mappe's ActivityResultsSource (D-095) reads the same: attempts and completed as here, and the first and last scaled score from the learner's first and last root results with score.max above 0.

    • Answers, durations and rates: response is kept only for the interaction types choice and fill-in (INS-003). Each gap (between [,]) is cut to 100 characters, which is enough to group the answers k learners share; a response still over 1 000 characters (the column's limit) is not stored, because a shortened list would shift its gaps. The bridge applies the same caps to keep batches small; the server enforces them. durationMs is parsed from result.duration and stored, as DATA-012 lists it (null when absent, unreadable or over 24 hours), and no insight reads it. LTI-011's 120 statements a minute per learner and activity stays: the measured peak without interacted and progressed is 22, and the bridge sends fewer still, so a 429 (with Retry-After; nothing from that batch is stored, and the bridge retries after it) means misuse.

    • Missing subContentIds: creating, copying and importing content fill in each missing subContentId and keep the existing ones; a save of stored content does not, since that would change D-093's structure signature. (The pattern builder instead gives every node a new ID, since a skeleton's IDs must never be shared, D-084.) Nodes are found by shape, as learningDesign/patterns/subContentIds.ts finds them, so a sub-content group with no subContentId key still gets none until the editor adds it. A child of content without them sends statements the server does not store.

  • Alternatives considered: (a) Identity by (attemptId, seq): a field outside DATA-012, where the row's own ID does the same. (b) Sending every statement, as LTI-010 reads: 38–76 % more statements, raw statements of up to 8 KB with question text in a 64 KiB keepalive budget, and data no requirement uses. (c) A root attempted that the bridge makes on H5P's initialized event for Column, ImageHotspots and InteractiveBook before «Les»: more learners counted as started, from a statement H5P never sent. (d) One attempt per page load: a retry in the same load would replace the better result under best. (e) P1's guard in the bridge: see Replays and repeats. (f) Storing replays with a flag: a field outside DATA-012. (g) Any one of the root tests alone: each misclassifies an observed case.

  • Consequences:

    • SPEC-DEVIATION, exactly: LTI-010 ("It POSTs each statement"): the bridge sends only what the server stores, cut down, with a statementId and an attemptId. LTI-011 ("Then it stores the minimal fields"): interacted, progressed, sub-content attempted and completed, replays, and sub-content statements without a subContentId are accepted and not stored, and an invalid item is discarded on its own. LTI-012 (the root as "no subContentId"): the tests above. The code carries SPEC-DEVIATION: D-115. Not deviated: DATA-012's fields, the five verbs, the score checks and the rate limit.
    • D-102, D-104 and D-112 get amendments that point here, and D-113 lists Q18–Q20 as open. Step 3 adds amendment notes to spec 02 (LTI-010, LTI-011, LTI-012) and spec 05 (DATA-012, INS-001, INS-004, INS-005).
    • Tests: the mapper and the root tests on P1's fixtures ([DATA-012], [LTI-012]); the bridge capturing each statement once in H5P's iframe mode, and through the real portal page and a mock-platform launch into /app/play, which P1 could not run ([LTI-010]); the replay rule on CoursePresentation's resume and InteractiveBook's re-submission; and the nested QuestionSet retry in uv-module, pinned to the upstream behaviour, so that a fixed version shows.
    • Residuals, for the DPIA input and the students' checklist: INS-001's attempts count each Column re-check and each CoursePresentation summary reached after new answers; a learner who opens a Column and never checks is not counted as started; ImageHotspots gives no insight and no grade; on a teacher's page with several QuestionSets a set cannot be retried; content stored without subContentIds gives no insight per question; and time on task runs only from a page load's first to its last stored statement, so reading before the first answer of a Column and time after the last stored statement are not counted.

  • Amendment (2026-10-30, step 3): three points made concrete while building. latest: migration s6_grade_bridge_insight also adds GradeSyncJob.resultAt, the stored timestamp of the result that made the job or last updated it, and latest (and mastery below its threshold) sends the score of the job with the latest resultAt, then the highest attempt number n of <viewId>:<n>, then the attempt ID as text, so equal times still give one answer. Creation order is not used: it can differ from result order when two requests of one learner are handled at once (the pagehide flush beside the request in flight), and a job that a later result of its attempt updates (LTI-013) keeps its creation time. This replaces "the job created last" above and in D-104's P1 amendment; spec 02 §7 and the data inventory list the field. reportingIsEnabled: the player page sets it only together with the bridge, for a learner principal, so an author's preview never offers «Send inn rapport». Q20: uv-module's skeleton stores endGame.showRetryButton: false on its three QuestionSets, pending ALU's review of the patterns (Q17). Each question keeps its own «Prøv igjen» until its set is finished (override.retryButton: "on" sets its behaviour.enableRetry, the field spec 04's PED-H07 names). The S5 real-pattern tests (PROD-009) and PED-H07's implementation also read endGame.showRetryButton, which spec 04's PED-H07 does not name, and the tests report each set's stored pass mark (the library's default passPercentage) as one that cannot be retried; how they treat these switches is settled at the step's integration, by amendment.

  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 3 review): two more points. What is stored: a root answered or completed is stored only as a root result; one whose category does not name the main library is discarded, since DATA-012 stores no category and insight (completed, attempts) and the grade queue read every stored root answered and completed as a root result (spec 02 LTI-011 and spec 05 DATA-012 as amended say so). The book's «Prøv igjen» (Q20): it is no way round the hidden set button. In a scratch run (not kept as a test) a freshly loaded uv-module held six progress dots, and the book's resetTask, which its summary page's «Prøv igjen» calls, threw QuestionSet's TypeError in the first chapter check, so the book is not reset either: a finished chapter check cannot be retried in this pattern at all. The regression test listed above is not written yet; once it pins this, the rule above turns the book's retry off too (behaviour.enableRetry: false), which PED-H07 reports on a field spec 04 names. Whether the pattern then departs from PROD-009 ("Retry … enabled" for all patterns), and so needs a SPEC-DEVIATION, is the owner's call at the step's integration, together with the S5 tests above.

  • Amendment (2026-11-04, step 3 integration): the S5 tests and PED-H07, settled as the step-3 amendment asked. A QuestionSet whose results-page «Prøv igjen» is off (endGame.showRetryButton: false) while it forces each question's own «Prøv igjen» on (override.retryButton: "on") keeps retry on, in the sense of spec 04's PED-H07 (enableRetry) and PROD-009: PED-H07 gives no hint for that switch then (a hint would send the author back to a button that breaks when a page holds several sets), the real-pattern tests (realPatternSwitches.ts) accept it, and its pass mark counts as informative, since each question can be retried until the set is finished. Without the override, the hint and the tests' report stay. Fixtures PED-H07/negative-set-retry-off-questions-keep-theirs.json and positive-set-retry-off-without-override.json pin both sides. Not settled here: the book's own «Prøv igjen» in uv-module (the step-3 review amendment). Its regression test is still to be written, and whether the pattern then turns the book's retry off, and so departs from PROD-009 with a SPEC-DEVIATION, stays the owner's call (Q20); until then the book's retry stays on and the tests above require it.

  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-3 security review): The attempt policy: D-104's amendment of the same day replaces "each stored gradable result in a Canvas launch writes a GradeSyncJob per (placement, learnerKey, attemptId)" and the step-3 amendment's latest by GradeSyncJob.resultAt: there is one job per placement and learner, and the policy reads the stored gradable results themselves, in the same result order (timestamp, then the attempt number n of <viewId>:<n>, then the attempt ID as text). The attempt rule itself is unchanged.

  • Amendment (2026-11-04, the step-3 security review): the book's «Prøv igjen» (Q20), pinned. The regression test the step-3 review amendment asked for is uvModuleBookRetry.browser.int.test.ts (an upstream pin, DOC-004). It creates uv-module through the pattern route on the real content types, plays it as its author in Chromium in Nynorsk, finishes the first chapter check and presses «Prøv igjen» on the book's summary page. It pins what QuestionSet 1.21 and InteractiveBook 1.15 do today: the document holds six progress dots at load (two sets) and nine on the summary page; the check's results page offers no «Prøv igjen» (endGame.showRetryButton: false); the book's «Prøv igjen» raises one TypeError (reading classList, in toggleFilledDot of H5P.Components 1.0, which QuestionSet's reset calls for a dot that is not its own); the book stays on its summary page; and the first check keeps its results page, so a finished chapter check cannot be retried at all. An upstream fix, or a change of the pattern's retry switches, fails the pin. Not decided here: whether the pattern turns the book's retry off (behaviour.enableRetry: false), and so departs from PROD-009 with a SPEC-DEVIATION; that stays the owner's call (Q20), and until then the book's retry stays on, as the S5 tests require.

D-116 · An IT assurance pack for HVL IT and an SBOM generator, outside the specs; a request in three stages

  • Context: On 2026-11-05 the owner asked for an "IT assurance pack" for HVL IT, whose operations and security staff will want assurances from people before they host HVL Interaktiv, even for testing. No spec asks for one: the specs describe the product, and docs/ops/ (D-109, D-110) says how to run it, not whether IT should. The code, its tests and every review of them were written by the same AI (213 of the repository's 214 commits; the other is the merge of pull request #8), and no person has reviewed the code. The repository does not know HVL's infrastructure, routines or people, and no document names who at HVL owns or maintains the system. npm sbom sees only npm packages; H5P core, the editor and the content types come from GitHub at pinned commits (D-022, D-027, D-078), and the server image rests on base images pinned by digest (D-110).
  • Decision:
    • The pack: docs/assurance/, outside the specs' scope, in plain English for HVL IT, with Norwegian domain terms kept as in the glossary: README.md (start here, with a Nynorsk samandrag), architecture.md, threat-model.md (STRIDE), ros-analyse.md, human-review.md and test-environment.md. Each document is a draft for IT to correct; says that AI wrote and fact-checked it and that no person has reviewed it; cites its evidence (a path, a decision, a requirement ID or a test); marks HVL facts (IT to fill in) and its own suggestions (proposal); and names variables only, never a secret value.
    • The SBOM: npm run sbom (tools/sbom/) writes docs/assurance/sbom.cdx.json in CycloneDX 1.5: the npm packages of a production install, H5P core and the editor, the ten content types by commit, and the container images by digest. --check says whether the committed file is current. The output is deterministic (no time stamp, a serial number derived from the content), and the tool reads files and the installed tree only. Its tests are titled [SEC-007] (dependency hygiene), which does not itself ask for an SBOM; npm test runs them in CI, and CI does not run --check yet. What the SBOM leaves out is listed in its README.
    • No change to the app: nothing in apps/, packages/, deploy/, content/ or docs/specs/ changes. Where the pack finds a gap, it proposes a measure; a change to the code needs its own decision first (CLAUDE.md §1, "Deviation").
    • A request in three stages, in the same words in every document of the pack. Stage 0: students and reviewers run the app on their own machines or in Codespaces, against the mock Feide and mock Canvas (D-049), with made-up users; IT is not needed. Stage 1: an isolated test server with made-up data only, Feide test users, HVL's test Canvas, named testers and an end date. Stage 2: a pilot with real students in one or two courses, only after the DPO's approval (Q6), a human security review, the ROS-analyse in HVL's form and an operations agreement. PROGRESS.md's «Blocks» column keeps naming sessions or "the pilot"; the pilot is stage 2.
    • Who is accountable is open: Q31 asks HVL to name a system owner (systemeigar) and a maintainer (forvaltar) for HVL Interaktiv, the system owner and a contact for the test install before stage 1, the maintainer before stage 2 at the latest. Until then the repository owner makes the product decisions, as before.
  • Alternatives considered: (a) Widening docs/ops/: it says how to run the service for readers who already have IT's go-ahead, not whether to give it. (b) The SBOM from npm sbom --omit dev alone: on 2026-11-05 it kept 239 of the 477 production packages (playwright-core, tsx, react and prisma among the missing) and lists no H5P code or images. (c) The risk analysis in HVL's own template: the template is HVL's and unknown here, so the draft scores on a 5 × 5 scale with ROS-nn IDs that IT keeps when it moves the risks over. (d) Waiting for a human review before writing to IT: IT's questions come first, and the pack says where a human review should start.
  • Consequences: The pack describes the repository at 92ca2c5 on 2026-11-05; its figures (commits, test counts, the commits after main) age as the S6 gate and later work land, and are refreshed with the gate output. The SBOM is regenerated after a change to the lockfile, the H5P pins or the images (tools/sbom/README.md). Neither the pack nor the SBOM is a review, and neither changes what the code does. Q31 joins PROGRESS.md's open questions.
  • Amendment (2026-11-06, the owner's request; pull request #18): the pack gains how-it-was-built.md, at the owner's request of 2026-11-06: the method used throughout (the plan, build, test, verify cycle of CLAUDE.md §4; fixes as experiments, a fault reproduced before its fix and the same test shown passing after it; mutation and revert-run-restore checks of the tests; adversarial AI review with skeptics and fact-checkers; the session gates), how the local gate and GitHub CI differ (where they run, what runs, who vouches) and their shared limit, that the same AI wrote the tests both run, with the evidence and what people must still review and test. It follows this decision's rules for the pack: a draft for IT to correct, written and fact-checked by AI, each claim with its evidence, and no fact about HVL that the repository cannot know. The snapshot is refreshed to commit 8d4eaf0 and pull request #18's CI result: the first finished CI run on S6 (run 42166052880, on 3eeea8d) failed one test that relied on a developer apps/server/.env, which GitHub's runner does not have; it was reproduced without .env and fixed in the test helper (8d4eaf0); the Session gate then passed on 8d4eaf0 (run 42170423046, finished 06:45:23 UTC), and docker.yml passed on GitHub for the first time (runs 42166052745 and 42170423045). Commit counts, the commits after main and the review state (no review on pull request #18) are as read on 2026-11-06. This amendment changes no app code, test, spec or CI file. A green CI run is not a review, so the pack's caveats stand, and README.md lists the new document.

S6 — Grade bridge, insight, privacy, deployment ✅ (gate passed 2026-11-06; started 2026-10-30; open items below)

S6 is the last planned session: the xAPI → Canvas grade bridge, teacher insight with k-suppression, the privacy jobs, deployment and operations, and the carry-overs from S4 and S5. It is too large for the days before 1 November, when the project proposal for HVL's bachelor students in programming (spring 2027) goes to HVL; their project is to review this AI-written code with their own tools and to finish the Canvas integration against ALU's test instance. Plan approved 2026-10-30; decisions D-101…D-114.

Decided while planning S6 (owner, 2026-10-30; recorded as D-101, D-106 and D-113):

  1. Learning data first: the grade bridge, then insight, then the privacy operations; then operations and security, then the carry-overs. Before 1 November the realistic target is steps 0–4 with parts of step 5 (D-101).
  2. Insight in tabs only: an Innsikt tab on the activity page /aktivitet/[id] and in the Canvas view /app/play, one context at a time; no /innsikt page. CLAUDE.md §2, spec 05's code location and the Evaluator Guide §4.1 are amended (D-101, D-106).
  3. Running the session: the hourly restart task is on until S6's gate passes (D-101).
  4. The gate keeps its full form (every S1–S6 per-ID run), run in parts of under 2 hours as tracked background tasks (D-113).
  5. What passes to the students: what needs HVL's real Canvas, Feide or servers, and whatever S6 does not reach, as designs, seams and checklists, indexed in docs/handoff/README.md (D-101).

Signs of machine-written code to look for: comments that restate the code, checks repeated where one layer already guarantees them, generic or overlong names, boilerplate copied across files, abstractions with one user, and idioms that differ from file to file because different agents wrote them. The reviewers must tell "unfamiliar but correct" from "needlessly odd": code that is unusual because it is right (a security check, an H5P workaround, a timing guard) stays, and gets a short WHY comment a human maintainer can follow, rather than being made ordinary and wrong. An HVL developer reads a sample afterwards and has the last word. If time allows; otherwise carried to the pilot list. Reference Material (institutional inputs)

These files are the inputs a build session reads instead of guessing. The originals come from HVL (design manual, ALU documents, Feide and Canvas exports). On 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-21 the build container could not reach hvl.no, feide.no, instructure.com or h5p.org (network policy). So each input below was assembled from public sources, with every value cited and graded by confidence. Each was then checked again from different sources (see Verification in the provenance table). None of these files is an HVL original. Each says exactly what HVL still has to supply or confirm.

The studio's texts, patterns, mappe template and criteria built from these inputs go to ALU and the pilot teachers with the review packet alu-review-s5.md ↗ (opens external site) (open question Q17, D-100).

What HVL IT and TeCopp register (Session 3)

The S3 server runs and is tested against a mock Feide and a mock Canvas (D-049). These registrations connect it to HVL's real services. <PUBLIC_BASE_URL> is the server's public origin, https://interaktiv.hvl.no in production; register the same paths for any test server.

  • Feide Customer Portal (HVL IT, Q3). Redirect URI after login <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/auth/feide/callback; redirect URI for logout <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/auth/logged-out; a confidential client; the attribute groups userinfo-name, email, userid-feide, groups-org and groups-edu (never userinfo-photo or userid-nin). Send back the client ID and secret (FEIDE_CLIENT_ID, FEIDE_CLIENT_SECRET). Details: feide-values.md ↗ (opens external site), section What HVL IT registers in the Customer Portal.
  • Canvas developer key (TeCopp, Q4, Q13). Paste canvas-lti13-developer-key.json ↗ (opens external site): OIDC login <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/lti/login, launch <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/lti/launch, keyset <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/lti/keys, and on each of the three Deep Linking placements the custom fields feide_login = $Canvas.user.loginId and hvl_placement = the placement's name. Enter <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/lti/launch in the key's Redirect URIs field, deploy the key, and send back the client ID, each deployment ID (for LTI_PLATFORMS) and the Canvas origins that frame the tool (for CANVAS_ORIGINS). Account linking ("feideLinking": true in LTI_PLATFORMS) is switched on only after a test launch shows that feide_login is the Feide ID (D-063). Details: canvas-platform-values.md ↗ (opens external site) §1.1 and §1.2.

How to read the derived files

  • Confidence: high means an official source seen directly, or two independent sources that agree. medium means one credible source, often an official page read through a search-engine extract. low means inferred. Values marked (verify) must not be built on until confirmed.
  • Proposals in proposals/ are drafts for files that belong in content/ in Session 5. They are not approved by ALU.
  • Third-party material without a licence (for example a public transcription of HVL's palette) is cited by repository and commit, never copied in.

Rules for this folder

  • No secrets. Client secrets and private keys go in the environment or secret store, never here.
  • No HVL logo files without HVL's permission. The logo is a trademark and is not covered by the repository's GPL licence (D-015).
  • h5p-core-1.28-seed-packages/ must contain a SHA256SUMS file (sha256sum *.h5p > SHA256SUMS). The seed script refuses packages that do not match it.
  • When an original arrives, put it here, record it in the provenance table, and re-run the check named in the derived file (for colours: python3 -I docs/reference/tools/contrast.py).
